english: Christianity is a religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ.
kokborok: Christianity wngkha Jisu Khristo ni phwrwngmungrok tei bini langmani sakao rwgwi kaisa tongthar.

english: It is one of the world's major religions, with over 2 billion followers.
kokborok: Khorok 2 rarwjak ni slai phano kwbangkuk maninai borokrokbai, omo hayungni kaisa kotorkuk tongtharo khobjagu.

english: Christians believe that Jesus is the Son of God and that he came to earth to save people from their sins.
kokborok: Khristanrok poito khlayo Jisu wngkha kaitorni bwsla tei boh borokno bohrok ni sumsokrokni simi mwthangna bwgwi se boh oh swngcharo phayo.

english: They also believe that he rose from the dead and ascended into heaven.
kokborok: Bohrok abobo poito khlayo, boh kwthwino mechenwi chukha sakao kasakha.

english: The importance of love for Jesus is central to Christianity.
kokborok: Christianity'o Jisu ni bagwi hamjakma wngkha jottoni slai nangkukmani bwkhak.

english: Christians are called to love God with all their heart, soul, mind, and strength.
kokborok: Khristanrokno bohrokni bebak bwkha, mang, phola, tei phan bai Kaitorno hamjakdi hwnwi sajagu.

english: They are also called to love their neighbors as themselves.
kokborok: Bohrok saksakno hamjakma hai bohrokni nokarini borokno bo hamjakdi hwnwi bo sajagu.

english: This love is not just a feeling, but a way of life.
kokborok: Ah hamjakma haino kaisa muchungma simiya, phiya abo kaisa langmani tongwrwngse.

english: It is expressed through acts of kindness, compassion, and forgiveness.
kokborok: Abono khairokma, hamjakma tei nakarma bai simi se phunugwi mano.

english: When we love Jesus, we are not only showing our love for him, but we are also showing our love for God.
kokborok: Chwng Jisu no hamjakphuru, aphuru chwng bono simi chini hamjakma phunukya, phiya aphuru chwng kaitorno bo chini hamjakma phunugo.

english: This is because Jesus is the perfect expression of God's love for us.
kokborok: Tamni hwnmale chini sakao kaitorni kubui hamjakmani mari wngkha Jisu.

english: When we love Jesus, we are opening ourselves up to receive God's love into our hearts.
kokborok: Chwng Jisu no hamjakphuru, chwng chini bwkharokni bisingtwih kaitorni hamjakma manna bwkhak chini sak-sakrok khulukmani khlayo.

english: The love of Jesus is a powerful force that can transform our lives.
kokborok: Jisuni hamjakma wngkha chini langmarokno swlaimanai kaisa phankuplung phan.

english: It can give us hope, strength, and peace.
kokborok: Omo chwngno khakamung, phan, tei tongkwchang rwui manu.

english: It can help us to forgive others and to love ourselves.
kokborok: Omo chwngno buino nakarnani tei sak-sakno hamjaknani chubai manu.

english: Volcanic eruptions are a powerful and destructive force of nature.
kokborok: Horhapung phatima wngkha hapharni kaisa phangwnang tei swbaikhrupmannai phan.

english: They can cause widespread devastation, loss of life, and environmental upheaval.
kokborok: Abohrok kotorma swbaisurup khlaimanu, langma sokomorwimano, tei tongkhorokno phuisarwi mano.

english: While volcanic eruptions are often associated with danger, they can also be a source of beauty and wonder.
kokborok: Horhapung phatimung no urpatimung bai mamang gwdaljagu, phiya abohrok naithokmung tei uanamung baibo gwdalwimanu.

english: The sight of a erupting volcano is a awe-inspiring sight, and the resulting lava flows can create stunning landscapes.
kokborok: Horhapung phatimano naywi naikhe khaswrangrima uanamung hai, tei wngmatwi horkepek kochokma naithothok hakungmari bo swnamwi mano.

english: Volcanic eruptions are caused by the build-up of pressure beneath the Earth's surface.
kokborok: Horhapung ni phatimungrok ha bisingo belai swkwlwkmung khlaima bagwi se wngu.

english: When this pressure becomes too great, the magma is forced up through the crust and erupts onto the surface.
kokborok: Jephuru ah swkwlwkmung belai kotor wngwi thahngo, aphuru magma habukur gerebwi phan bai sakatwi peplai phayo.

english: The size and intensity of a volcanic eruption can vary greatly.
kokborok: Horhapung phatimung ni tormung tei phan belai phrwi manu.

english: Some eruptions are relatively small and localized, while others can be massive and have a devastating impact on entire regions.
kokborok: Baksa phatimung belai chikon tei kwrwngsa thayo simino kwrwngjak, phiya tei kubunirokkhe kotorma tei baksa-baksa bwkhakno swbaikhrubwi phano mano.

english: The most destructive volcanic eruptions can cause widespread ashfall, mudflows, and tsunamis.
kokborok: Jottonislai swbaikhrupmannai horhapung phatima kwrwngma thayo thapla pirsama, harpek kochokma, tei tsunami tubuimano.

english: They can also trigger earthquakes and landslides.
kokborok: Bohrok bangla tei ha phano kuwakrwi mano.

english: In the worst cases, volcanic eruptions can claim thousands of lives and cause billions of dollars in damage.
kokborok: Jottonislai hamya phatimungo, horhapung phatima sai-sai borokrokni langmarok naimano tei khok rarwjak-rarwjak rangno derarwimano.

english: Despite the risks, volcanic eruptions are an important part of the Earth's geological processes.
kokborok: Aswk deramung tongphano, horhapung phatima hayungni geological tangraidani bagwi kaisa nangkuma bokcho.

english: They help to recycle the Earth's crust and create new landforms.
kokborok: Bohrok hayungni habukurno swlaywi kwtal ha swnamthani chuba'o.

english: They also provide a home for a variety of plants and animals.
kokborok: Bohrok dalbidal buphang-uaphang tei malmatarokni bagwi nokrokbo thumwi rwo.

english: In a small village in India, there lived a young boy named Ram.
kokborok: India ni chikonsa kamio, Ram mungwi chwrai khoroksa tongmani.

english: Ram was a bright and curious boy, and he loved to learn about the world around him.
kokborok: Ram khoroksa siyangwnang tei khatungjak chwrai, tei boh bini yaksiyagra hayungni bagwi swrwngna belai hamjago.

english: One day, Ram was walking through the village when he saw a group of men working on a large pit.
kokborok: Salsa, Ram kami twih himwi thang tongphuru, chwlarok bodol kaisano, kotorma hakorkutugo samung tangwi tongma nugo.

english: "What are you doing?" Ram asked.
kokborok: "Norok tamo khlai tong?" hwnwi Ram swngkha.

english: "We're building a rainwater harvesting tank," one of the men said.
kokborok: "Chwng kaisa watwitwi thumjaknai twikhor swnamwi tongu," hwnwi khoroksa chwla sakha.

english: "This will help us to collect rainwater during the monsoon season, so that we can use it during the dry season."
kokborok: "Omo chwngno balsal molo watwitwi rungnani chubanai, kwran molo obono no chwng samungo phwnangwi mano."

english: Ram was fascinated.
kokborok: Ram muani chajakma hai wngwi thangkha.

english: He had never heard of rainwater harvesting before.
kokborok: Boh oboni slai swkang waisaphano watwitwi no thumwi tonnani hwnwi khwnayakhu.

english: He asked the men many questions, and they were happy to answer them.
kokborok: Boh ah chwlarokno no kwbangma kokrok swngkha, tei bohrok bo aboni twywi sanani belai khatungjak.

english: Ram learned that rainwater harvesting is a simple and effective way to collect and store rainwater.
kokborok: Ram saimankha watwitwi thummung, watwini twino rungmani tei khatiani kaisa kwlai tei sosol lama.

english: The rainwater is collected in a large pit, which is usually dug in the ground.
kokborok: Watwini twi kaisa kotorma hakorkuthugo rwngjago, amono haino hano khurwi no swnamjago.

english: The pit is lined with a waterproof material, such as clay or concrete, to prevent the water from seeping out.
kokborok: Oh hakorkuthuk kaisa twimisimanya mwnwi bai arirwjak, aroni twino kochok thangnani simi kasonani bagwi, abo harpek eba holongbwthap bai arirwjak.

english: The rainwater harvesting tank is usually located near the village well, so that the water can be easily accessed.
kokborok: Oh watwitwi thummung ni twikhor kamini kuwa ganao no manthogo, aroni twino kwlaikhe naharwi mannani bagwi.

english: The water can be used for drinking, cooking, bathing, and watering crops.
kokborok: Oh twi nwngnani, songnani, tukunani, tei maikhulrokno twi lunani bagwi samungo phwnangjagu.

english: India has a population of over 1.3 billion people, and it is the second most populous country in the world.
kokborok: India'o khorok 1.3 rarwjakni slai phano kwbangkuk borokrok tongu, tei abo hayungni bising jottnislai kwbangkuk borok bangthani nwi beremo kwlayu.

english: The government has been working to promote family planning for many years, but the issue is still a major challenge.
kokborok: Nukhung chaplainani no twywi haphang bisi kwdwkma romwi samung khlai phai tongu, phiya tabuk phano oh jwngjal kotorni kagwimanyakhu.

english: There are a number of factors that contribute to the high birth rate in India.
kokborok: India ni kwbang achaimungni ungkulugo kwbangma kokbubak tongu.

english: One factor is the lack of access to education and information about family planning.
kokborok: Kaisa kokbubak hwnkhe nukhung chaplanani bagwi aswk rwngswrwngmung tei kokpirmung kwrwi khu.

english: Many people in India do not know about the different methods of contraception, or they may be afraid to use them.
kokborok: India ni kwbangma borokrokno contraception ni juda-juda raidarokno saimanyakhu, eba bohrok abo samungo phwnangnani phano kirijagwimanu.

english: Another factor is the cultural preference for large families.
kokborok: Tei kaisa kokbubak hwnkhe kotor nukhungrokno chajakukmungni hukumu.

english: In some parts of India, it is seen as a status symbol to have many children.
kokborok: India ni baksa-baksa bwkhago, kwbangma bwsarok tongmani kaisa tongboromni mari haikhese naisikjago.

english: The government has implemented a number of programs to promote family planning.
kokborok: Nukhung chaplainani no tisana bagwi, haphang kwbangma tangbwtang naharkha.

english: These programs include providing free or subsidized contraception, offering education and counseling about family planning, and making it easier for people to get sterilized.
kokborok: Ah tangbwtangrogo magwnang eba chubachrujak contraception bakmani, nukhung chaplainani kokchana bagwi rwngswrwngmung tei kokbiti yapharmani, tei borokrokno kwlaikheno sterilized wngnanirok khobjago.

english: However, these programs have had limited success.
kokborok: Haiphano, oh tangbwtangrok aswk bwthai tubuimanliya.

english: There are a number of challenges to promoting family planning in India.
kokborok: India'o Nukhung chaplanani kokno pirnani bagwi kwbangma kasumung tongo.

english: One challenge is the high cost of the programs.
kokborok: Kaisa kasumung hwnkhe tangbwtangrokni belai kwbang morok.

english: Another challenge is the resistance to family planning from some religious groups.
kokborok: Tei kaisa kasumung hwnkhe nukhung chaplainani phasing baksa-baksa tongthar bodolrokni simi kebengmung.

english: Additionally, there is a lack of political will to address the issue.
kokborok: Teise, oh kokrokno tisanani bagwi thwngwrwng hapharni mungsa saktharmung bo kwrwi.

english: Family planning in India has been a topic of debate for many years.
kokborok: India'o bisi kwdwkma romwi no nukhung chaplainani kok kaisa kokbanglaimung ni kokhak wngwi phai tongu.

english: In 1976, the Indian government passed the controversial National Emergency Act, which imposed a forced sterilization program on men and women.
kokborok: Bisi 1976'o, Barot haphang ah kokbanglaijaknai National Emergency Act Passed khlaikha, aboni twywi chwla tei bwrwirokni sakao bohrokni muchungma kwrwi twtwi bwchwlwi bwtharma tangbwtang phwnangjakha.

english: This program was met with widespread resistance and eventually overturned by the Indian Supreme Court.
kokborok: Oh tangbwtangrok belaino sejajakha paithago abo Indian Supreme Court bai rosai naharjakha.

english: In recent years, the Indian government has taken a more progressive approach to family planning.
kokborok: Laithangnai bisirokni bising, Barot haphang nukhung chaplaimani bwkhak teibo swkangnainai yaprirok naharkha.

english: In 2010, the government launched the National Family Planning Program, which provides free contraception and sterilization services to all Indian citizens.
kokborok: Bisi 2010'o, haphang National Family Planning tangbwtang chengkha, aboni bisingtwi jotto barot haniborokrokno magwnang suta oknangya khlaima tei bwchwlwi bwtharma sebukrok bakjakha.

english: The program has been successful in reducing the fertility rate in India, but it still faces challenges, such as a lack of awareness and access to services.
kokborok: Ah tangbwtangni bisingtwi Barot haktorni bwsa chuwi manmungni wngmarino khaithani bwthai kahamno mankha, haiphano tabukbo obo jwngjal bai kwrangjakhu, sana thangkhe omoni twywi awaimung tei seb-sab mannani lamarok aswk kwrwi.

english: One of the most important challenges to family planning in India is the lack of awareness about the benefits of family planning.
kokborok: Baroto nukhung chaplainani no twywi jottonislai sosol kebengmungrok hwnkhe nukhung chaplaiani hamkraino twywi aswk awaimungrok kwrwikhu .

english: Many Indian couples believe that it is their duty to have as many children as possible.
kokborok: Barot ni kwbangma hiksainwirok poito khlayo jeswk mansak chwrai khlainani abo borokni khlaithaise hwnwi.

english: This belief is often reinforced by cultural and religious norms.
kokborok: Oh poitorok hukumu tei tongtharni raidarok bai teibo rakrwjagu.

english: Another challenge to family planning is the lack of access to services.
kokborok: Nukhung chaplainani thangthani tei kaisa kebengmung hwnkhe seb-sab mannani lamarok aswk kwrwi.

english: In rural areas, there are often few or no family planning clinics.
kokborok: Kami amchairogo, nukhung chaplainani sakhamnokrok kaisa-kusu eba kwrwi swchwkno hwnwi manu.

english: This makes it difficult for couples to access the services they need.
kokborok: Obo hiksainwirokno nangwi tongmani seb-sab naharnani thani jwngjalo khiklayu.

english: Despite these challenges, the Indian government is committed to providing family planning services to all its citizens.
kokborok: Oh jwngjalrokni bisingo bo Barot haphang barotni haniborokrokno nukhung chaplainani seb-sabrokno manthokrwnani bwkhak kwrakhe saktharjak.

english: On the ninth day of Navratri, a young woman named Parvati was told that she would give birth to a son who would become a great king.
kokborok: Navratri ni salchuku'o, Parvati mungwi khoroksa bwrwi sikli hai hwnwi sajakha je boh khorok chwla bwsa no bahnai, ah chwla ulo khoroksa mungkotor bubagra wngnai.

english: She was overjoyed, and she began to prepare for her delivery.
kokborok: Boh belai tongthokjakha, tei boh bwsa bahna bagwi jugalina chengkha.

english: On the tenth day of Navratri, Parvati went into labor.
kokborok: Navratri ni salchi'o, Parvati bwsa bahmungo thangkha.

english: She labored for many hours, and finally, she gave birth to a beautiful baby boy.
kokborok: Boh kwbangma dar romwi bwsa bahmungo tongkha, paithago, boh khoroksa naithok chwla kwlwibwsa no bahkha.

english: She named him Shiva, and she knew that he would fulfill his destiny to become a great king.
kokborok: Boh bono Shiva hwnwi mung pharkha, tei boh saimano ulo boh khoroksa mungkotor bubagra wngwi bini talikha'o swijakno no supungnai.

english: Shiva grew up to be a strong and courageous young man.
kokborok: Shiva khoroksa kwrak tei kiriya chwla sikla wngwi torwi phaikha.

english: He was always willing to help others, and he was known for his fairness and compassion.
kokborok: Boh homnino kubuni borokrokno chubana bwkhak tiyar tongu, tei boh bini sosolmung tei khairokmung ni bagwi sinijagu.

english: He quickly became a popular figure among the people, and they looked to him for guidance and leadership.
kokborok: Boh daktino lukurokni bisingo sinijaknani chengkha, lukurokbo bini thani twidulmung tei twiphangni bagwi naichomlaikha.

english: One day, Shiva was walking through the forest when he came across a group of bandits who were attacking a village.
kokborok: Salsa, Shiva bolong bisingtwi himwi thangwi tongphuru bo kaisa dagaitrokni bodolrok kami'o choprobwi tongma nukha.

english: Shiva quickly jumped into action, and he fought off the bandits.
kokborok: Shiva daktino samungo bakhwlaikha, tei bo ah dagaitrok bai bulaikha.

english: The villagers were grateful to Shiva for saving them, and they asked him to become their king.
kokborok: Kamini lukurok belai khaphurjakha Shiva bohrokno mwthangmani bagwi, tei bohrok bono swngkha bohrokni bubagra wngdi hwnwi.

english: Shiva agreed to become king, and he ruled the kingdom wisely and justly for many years.
kokborok: Shiva bubagra wngna bagwi gosi naharkha, tei bo ah ha no bisi kwdwkma romwi elem tei kubuima bai naikolkha.

english: He was a kind and compassionate ruler, and he always put the needs of his people first.
kokborok: Boh khoroksa khakaham tei khairokma gwnang bubagra wngkha, tei boh homnino bini borokni nangkukmarok bwskango puila tonikha.

english: Indira Gandhi was the first and only woman to serve as Prime Minister of India.
kokborok: Indira Gandhino puila tei tabukswk jora bwrwirokni bisingo baraot hani montri bokhorok chalangnai.

english: She was born in 1917 into a prominent political family, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Prime Minister of India.
kokborok: Bo 1917 bisio kaisa munggwnang thwnggwrwng nukhungo achaikha, tei bupha Jawaharlal Nehru, bono Barot hani puila Montri Bokhorok.

english: Indira Gandhi was educated in India and England, and she married Feroze Gandhi in 1942.
kokborok: Indira Gandhi Barot tei England hao rwngswrwngkha tei bisi 1942'o Feroze Gandhi bai kaijakha.

english: They had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay.
kokborok: Bohrokni khoroknwi bwsa chwla wngjakha, Rajiv tei Sanjay.

english: Gandhi began her political career in 1955, when she was elected to the Indian Parliament.
kokborok: Gandhi bini thwngkwrwngni langma bisi 1955 ni simi chengkha, aphuruno bo Barotni kerongchapnogo chongjago.

english: She served in various ministerial positions in the government of her father, and in 1966 she became Prime Minister after his death.
kokborok: Bini buphani haphango boh dalbidal bedego montrirokbo chalangkha, tei bisi 1966'o bini bupha thwimani yagulo boh montri bokhorok wngkha.

english: Gandhi was a controversial figure, and her policies were often criticized.
kokborok: Gandhi khoroksa belaikhe kok cherjaknai borok tongmani, bini tangbitirok homanino sejajago.

english: She was accused of being authoritarian and of suppressing dissent.
kokborok: Boh saksakni phanno simi phwnango tei batainairokno swkwlwgu hwnwi koksilchamung bo rwjago.

english: However, she was also a popular leader, and she is credited with modernizing India and improving the lives of its people.
kokborok: Haiphano, bo khoroksa bumung gwnang ojama bo hwnjagu tei Barot hano kwtalkhe swnamnani tei oh hani borokrokni langmano hamsarwmani bagwi borombo rwjago.

english: Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.
kokborok: Gandhi bisi 1984'o bini sakmwrwknairokbaino bwtharjakha.

english: She was succeeded by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.
kokborok: Bini achukthaino bini bwsla Rajiv Gandhi naharkha .

english: Gandhi's life and career were marked by many challenges, but she never gave up on her dream of a better India.
kokborok: Gandhini langma tei samungbwtang belaino jwngjal tei kebengmungbai kupulwng, phiya boh bini kahamkuk ni imang yakarliya.

english: In the small town of Malgudi, there was a corrupt police inspector named Ramasamy.
kokborok: Malgudi mungwi kaisa chikonsa aoli'o, Ramasamy mungwi khoroksa rangchakwrak Police inspector tongmani.

english: He would often take bribes from the people he arrested, and he would also use his power to harass and intimidate people.
kokborok: Boh homnino boh rommani borokrokni thani yaksak naharu, tei boh bini phan no borok rokno sikirinani tei chekeleknani bagwi bo phwnangu.

english: One day, Ramasamy arrested a young man named Krishnan for a crime he did not commit.
kokborok: Salsa, Krishnan mungwi khoroksa chwla sikla no bini chayakhlaima kwrwi twtwino bono Ramamsamy romkha.

english: Krishnan was innocent, but Ramasamy refused to listen to him.
kokborok: Krishnan majra kwrwi se, haiphano Ramasamy bono khwnana se gosiliya.

english: He demanded a bribe from Krishnan, and when Krishnan refused to pay, Ramasamy threw him in jail.
kokborok: Boh Krishnan ni thani yakbara rwui rang sankha, Krishan jephuru bono rinani gosiliya, Ramasamy bono aphuru alongo daui rwkha.

english: Krishnan's father, a poor farmer, was desperate to get his son out of jail.
kokborok: Krishnan ni bupha khoroksa bigra chuwainaisa, boh bwsla no alongnokni karinani bagwi belai muchungsukjakha.

english: He went to see Ramasamy and begged him to release Krishnan, but Ramasamy refused.
kokborok: Boh Ramasamy bai malainani thangkha tei bono Krishnan no phiyokdi hwnwi koikha, haiphano Ramasamy gosiliya.

english: The farmer then went to the local temple and prayed to God for help.
kokborok: Hwnkhe ah chuwainaisa aroni kaisa mwtainogo thangkha tei mwtai no chubajadi hwnwi surikha.

english: The next day, the farmer was walking home from the temple when he saw a large snake crossing the road.
kokborok: Teini salo, ah chuwainaisa mwtainok ni simi himwi thangphuru bo kaisa chibuk kotorma no lama laisutongmani nukha .

english: The farmer was afraid of snakes, but he knew that he had to do something to help his son.
kokborok: Ah chuwainaisa chibukno belai kirijagu, phiya boh saimano boh bini bwsla no chubana bagwi mungsaswk khaina nangnai hwnwi.

english: He picked up the snake and carried it to the police station.
kokborok: Boh chibukno khochakha tei police station'o twlang thangkha.

english: When Ramasamy saw the snake, he was terrified.
kokborok: Jephuru Ramasamy chibukno nukha, bo kirijakha.

english: Dear [Recipient Name], I hope this letter finds you well.
kokborok: Khajani [yachaksoknai ni mung], ang kha khwlayo nini kaham kwrwng jorao no o koktun sogwi khana hwnwi.

english: I am writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been good this year.
kokborok: Ang nono chini khamparni simi suihoro, taklai bisi o maithai belaino kwbang mankha.

english: We are grateful for the bountiful crops that we have been able to grow, and we are looking forward to a successful year ahead.
kokborok: Chwng belai khasrangjak amoswk kwbang maithai mwithai kaiwi manmani bagwi, tei bwskang bisi o amo haino khwlaiphinai hwnwi uansogo.

english: I am writing to you today to tell you about my experience with the Clean India campaign.
kokborok: Ang tini nono suihorma khe clean India Campaign ni samung khwlaimano twywi sana bagwise.

english: As you know, the Clean India campaign is a nationwide effort to promote cleanliness and sanitation in India.
kokborok: Nwngbo sio, Clean India Campaign khwlai mani abo India ha gwnangwi kwchwng khe tongnani tei khithairogno kwchwng khe tongnani abono twywise samung khwlai jago.

english: I have been involved in this campaign since its inception, and I have seen firsthand the positive impact that it has had on our community.
kokborok: O pirmungo chengphuru ni simino ang kubuljak, tei chini hodao puila kaham swlaijakmung nukha.

english: One of the most important things that the Clean India campaign has done is to raise awareness of the importance of cleanliness.
kokborok: Bebakni slai hamkuk mani Clean India Campaign song samung khwlai ma khe kwchwng khe tongmani abo bwswk joratwi nang abono simung rwna naima se.

english: People are now more aware of the need to dispose of waste properly, and they are more willing to take action to keep their communities clean.
kokborok: Lukurok tabuk teibo sikha hamya manwino boro khibinai, tei bohrok sakni kamino kwchwng khwlaina bagwi bohrok teibo sakthar kha.

english: Another important thing that the Clean India campaign has done is to provide resources to help people clean up their communities.
kokborok: Tei kaisa Clean India Campaign song samung khwlai ma khe bohrok manwi hamya tonijaknai bago bohrokni kamino kwchwng khwlai thanio chukthwng hwnwi.

english: The government has provided funding for new garbage collection and recycling programs, and it has also provided training for people who want to become sanitation workers.
kokborok: Haphang song manwi hamya thumwi khibijaknai tei recycling programrokni bagwi rang bo rwi tongo, tei khithaini samung khwlaina muchungnairogno bo phwrwngjagwi tongo.

english: As a result of the Clean India campaign, our community is cleaner and more sanitary than ever before.
kokborok: Clean India Campaign khwlai mani bwthai wng kha, chini kamirok tei khithairok swkang ni slai chwngkuk kha.

english: Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian state of Kerala.
kokborok: Onam Barot haktorni Kerala haste'o palaijaknai kaisa maital tisama ter.

english: It is a time for family and friends to come together and celebrate the good harvest.
kokborok: Oh jorao nukhung kaisa tei bayapchari rokbai malaywi kaham maitalno twywi tongthoklaimani jora.

english: The festival lasts for ten days, and each day is filled with different activities and traditions.
kokborok: Oh ter salchi romwi khwlaijago tei kaisa-kaisa salo dalbidal samung tei hukumu raidarok bai palaijagu.

english: One of the most important traditions of Onam is the Vallamkali, or snake boat race.
kokborok: Onamni kaisa nangkukmani hukumu wngkha Vallamkali eba chibuk rung bataimung.

english: This is a boat race that takes place on the River Pampa.
kokborok: Oh rung bataimung Pampa twimao khwlaijagu.

english: The boats are long and narrow, and they are decorated with flowers and leaves.
kokborok: Oh rung belai kolok tei khochor, tei dalbidal khumbwlairokbai sajukjak.

english: The race is very competitive, and it is a lot of fun to watch.
kokborok: Oh rung bataimung belaino kutuk bataimung, tei naywi naikhe belai tongthothokbo wngo.

english: Another important tradition of Onam is the Pookalam, or flower rangoli.
kokborok: Onamni tei dalsa nangkukmani hukumu wngkha Pookalam eba khumbarni dalbidal naithok swnamung.

english: This is a beautiful design made out of flowers that is placed in front of the house.
kokborok: Oh khumni rikmung belaino naithokthok wngo tei nok bwskango obo swnamjago.

english: The Pookalam is a way to welcome the gods and goddesses, and it is also a way to show respect to the elders.
kokborok: Pookalamni bisingtwino mwtai tei mwtaijwkrokno lamsogo tei oboni bisingtwino okra-chakra roknobo borom rwjago.

english: Onam is a time for feasting and celebration.
kokborok: Onam ter phuru chalaimung tei tongthoklaimung wngo.

english: There are many traditional dishes that are eaten during the festival, such as rice, fish, and vegetables.
kokborok: Oh tero dalbidal chamung chajago romdi mai, ah tei dalokrok.

english: There is also a lot of singing and dancing.
kokborok: Oro rwchapmung tei mwsamungbo wngo.

english: The influences of religion on music are vast and varied.
kokborok: Ah tongkwthar kobolmungrok ah rwchapmung sakao wngkha kuar tei dalkwbang.

english: From the chanting of hymns in ancient temples to the soaring melodies of gospel songs, music has long been used to express religious beliefs and emotions.
kokborok: Ah diyaimung rwchapma simi kwcham mwtainokrok ah birsama khorangkahamrok gospel rwchapmungrok bwkhak, rwchapmung kaisa kwdwkma tongkwtahr poitotok tei khanangjakrok swbaikhrubwi sama bwkhak.

english: In many religions, music is seen as a way to connect with the divine.
kokborok: Kwbangma tongkwtharrokni bising, rwchaomung kaisa ah chukhani kok bai kwrwngna bwkhka kaisa lama haikhe nukjakha.

english: The sounds and rhythms of music can create a sense of awe and reverence, and can help to transport the listener to a higher plane of consciousness.
kokborok: Ah khorangrok tei kokyaprirok rwchapmung kaisa sinai simanwi kirima tei khlumjaknai swnam mano, tei ah khwnanai rokno kaisa kuchuk milik sichajak rwkamung bwkhak chubai mano.

english: For example, in Hinduism, music is considered to be a form of yoga.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, Hinduism bising, yoga wngkha kaisa sakmang bwkhak rwchapmung wansukukma wngkha.

english: The practice of kirtan, or devotional chanting, is said to help to purify the mind and open the heart to the divine.
kokborok: Ah kirtan loi khlaimung bai, eba tongkwthar rwchapmung, ah khorokno kwthar khai chubma bwkhak sajakha tei ah chukhani kok bwkhak bwkha khulukma.

english: In Buddhism, music is often used as a form of meditation, helping to focus the mind and bring about a state of calm and tranquility.
kokborok: Buddhism bising, rwchapmung uramuram phwnangjak wngkha iko kaisa asonkhaimani tomung, ah khorokno naisikma bwkhak chubamani tei kaisa tongrem kwchang tei shanti bagwi tubumani.

english: In addition to its spiritual role, music can also be used to address social and political issues.
kokborok: Jora rwmani bising omo pholagwdaljak tangmung bwkhak, rwchapmung hodarwk tei thwngrwngrwk swimarirok nikuma bwkhak phwnangjak bo wngmano.

english: In the civil rights movement, for example, music played a powerful role in mobilizing people and inspiring them to fight for justice.
kokborok: Ah luku manthai ninangrimung bising, phunukmari karwi, kaisa phangwnang tangmung rwchapmung tamjakha borokno samungo thepama bising tei bohrokno mankubuini bagwi bulaina bwkhak khasrangrwkha.

english: The songs of Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, and others helped to give voice to the hopes and dreams of African Americans, and helped to bring about a more just and equitable society.
kokborok: Ah Martin Luther King Jr, Mahjalia jacksongni rwchapmungrok, tei kubunrok khorang rwma bwkhak chubakha ah khajamungrok tei African Americans ni imangrok, tei kaisa teibo haino tei makubui dopha bagwi tubuna bwkhak chubakha.

english: "I can't believe we're going to be learning how to cook Indian food today," said 10-year-old Priya excitedly.
kokborok: "Ang poito khwlaywi manya chwng tini India ni chamungrokno songnani maswrwngnai" hwnwi bisi 10 omorni Priya tongthokjagwi sakha.

english: She had been looking forward to this day ever since her teacher, Ms. Singh, had announced that they would be doing a unit on different cultures. "I've never had Indian food before," said Priya's friend, Sam. "What's it like?"
kokborok: Oh salno boh belaino khatungkhajakhe naisingjak bono phwrwngnai, Ms. Singh, bohrokno dalbidal hukumu bodolni chamung swrwnglainai hwnwi sakhlaimani yagulo. "Ang Indiani chamungrogrokno waisa phano chajakya kho, " hwnwi Priyani kiching, Sam sakha. "Abo bahai?"

english: "It's delicious," said Priya "It's usually very flavorful, with a lot of spices. And there are so many different dishes to choose from."
kokborok: "Abo belaino kothok, " hwnwi Priya sakha "abo belaino thogu, moso yokma bo kwbang. Tei aro kwbangma dalbidalni mii swngjaknai tongo aroni bisingo saiwi naimano."

english: The class arrived at the kitchen, and Ms. Singh began to set up.
kokborok: Rwngremrok nokganti'o sokkha, hake Ms. Singh bo jugalnani chengkha.

english: "Today, we're going to be making a simple dish called dal makhani," she said.
kokborok: "Tini chwng kaisa kwlai mui dal makhani no swnamlainai, " hwnwi boh sakha.

english: "It's a type of lentil soup that's very popular in India."
kokborok: "Abo kaisa mwibwtwi haise India'o belai chajago."

english: Ms. Singh showed the class how to measure out the ingredients and cook the lentils.
kokborok: Ms. Singh class no phunukha bahaikhe manwi-khwnwirok suh'ui oh muibwtwi songnai.

english: The students helped each other chop vegetables and stir the pot.
kokborok: Swrwngnairok bohrok kiching mui helep thani tei mwitwk kollai thani chubalaikha.

english: As they worked, they chatted about their favorite foods and what they were looking forward to trying in India.
kokborok: Bohrok samung khwlai twtwi, bohrokni thokjakukmani chamungrogno twywi tei India ni chamungno bo chanai nayano hwnwi salaikha.

english: When the dal makhani was finished, the students sat down to eat.
kokborok: Dal makhani song baikha hwnkhe, bohrok chalaina bagwi achuklaikha.

english: Reservation in India is a system of positive discrimination that aims to provide opportunities to historically disadvantaged groups.
kokborok: Manthaini khatimung wngkha belai raida kaham aboni naharmung wngkha laibuma rwgwi swkwlwkjagwi phainai dopharokno kuchugo tisanani.

english: It is based on the idea that these groups have been discriminated against in the past, and that they need special help in order to achieve equality.
kokborok: Omo kaisa uansokmungni sakao je oh dopharok agi phuru swkwlwkjagwi phaima bagwi, bui bai baksa bohrokno tisana bagwi juda chubamung nango.

english: Reservations are used in a number of areas, including education, employment, and government.
kokborok: Kwbangma thayono manthaini khatimung khwlaijago, aro swrwngmungo, haba tangthanio, tei haphango bo abo khobjago.

english: They can take the form of quotas, which set aside a certain number of places for members of a particular group, or of preferences, which give members of a particular group an advantage in selection.
kokborok: Bohrokni manthaini sinimung bwlai nauimanno, aro kaisa bodolni borokrok simino manwi mano, bohrokni bodolno simino judakhe chongwi naharjago.

english: Reservations are controversial, and there are a number of arguments for and against them.
kokborok: Manthai khatimungrokno twywi belai kokbanglaimung tongu, abono twywi kwbangma kaham tei hamya kwbangma kokrok sajaklayu.

english: Some people argue that they are necessary to correct the effects of past discrimination, and that they provide an important opportunity for members of disadvantaged groups to improve their lives.
kokborok: Baksa borok kheba sao abono teisa swnamna nangphinai hwnwi, tei manthaino manyarokni bagwi jora kaham rwna nangnai hakhese bohrok kuchugo kauimanai hwnwi sajago.

english: Others argue that reservations are unfair to other groups, and that they create a sense of entitlement among the beneficiaries.
kokborok: Baksa ba sao manthaino khatimani abo kubun bodolrokni bagwi chaya hwnwi, tei bohrok manthaino manwi mangse tongna muichungo hwnwi.

english: The debate over reservations is likely to continue for many years to come.
kokborok: Manthai khatimungno twywi kokbanglai mani abo phainai bisirogo bo banglaiwi no thangnai.

english: However, there is a growing consensus that reservations are an important tool for achieving equality in India.
kokborok: Abobaino, bangrwrwk wngmabai manthaini khatimung nangsogo India o bebakno baksa khwlaina bagwi.

english: The Indian Constitution guarantees the right to equality for all citizens, regardless of their caste, religion, or gender.
kokborok: India ni tongraida bebak borokno no tongbaksa khwlayo, bohrokni dopha, tongk'thar, eba sir no naiya.

english: As a young man, I was always fascinated by the stories that my grandmother used to tell me.
kokborok: Chwla sikla wngwi, ang homni no kothomarok bai muani kwlaima je ani nanan ano sama hai.

english: She had a wonderful gift for storytelling, and her tales always seemed to transport me to another world.
kokborok: Bo kothomasawui uanamasingsa rwmung kwlayo, tei bini khothoma homnino kubuni swngcharo ano rwkai twlango.

english: One of my favorite stories was about a man named Srinivasa, who was a great scholar and philosopher.
kokborok: Ani kaisa chajakmani kothoma hwnkhe khoroksa Srinivasa mungwi, bo kotorkuar swrwngnai tei nukuansuksinai.

english: Srinivasa was so wise that he could answer any question that was put to him.
kokborok: Srinivasa belai sijak je bono swngmung rwjakmani bo abono kokphirokwi mano.

english: One day, a king came to Srinivasa and asked him a question that no one had ever been able to answer: "What is the meaning of life" Srinivasa thought for a moment, and then he said, "The meaning of life is to find your gift.
kokborok: Salsa, bubagra Srinivasa ni ro phaikha tei bono mohai swngmung swngkha je tak sak jora kebo Kokphirok manyakhu: "langma ni kokmung tamo" Srivasa swrapsa wansukgrakha, tei bo sakha, "langma ni kokmung wng nini rwmungno naituknani.

english: The purpose of life is to give it away" The king was so impressed with Srinivasa's answer that he gave him a large reward.
kokborok: Langma ni naimung hwnkhe bagwi rohornani" bubagra Srinivasa ni kokphirokma no aswk khe chajakha je bo bono kotorma yakpai rwkha.

english: But Srinivasa refused the reward, saying that he had already been rewarded enough by the knowledge that he had helped someone else.
kokborok: Phiya Srinivasa yakpai no nana soiliya, bo sakha je bo agino elem bai belai yakpaijak je bo buino chubachu khai mankha hwnwi.

english: This story taught me that the most important thing in life is not to seek material possessions, but to find your gift and share it with others.
kokborok: Oh kothoma ano phwrwngkha je oh langma ni belai nangkukma manwi hwnkhe manwi-khwnwi sasokmani naitukma simiya, phiya nini rwmung naitukna se tei kubun bai baknani.

english: I was once walking through the streets of Mysore when I saw a young boy sitting on the steps of a temple.
kokborok: Ang salsa Mysoreni lamtwi himwi thang phuru jephuru ang chwrai khoroksano noktharni lamani theken o achukjak nukphu.

english: He was crying bitterly, and when I asked him what was wrong, he told me that he had lost his way.
kokborok: Bo kabui tongo swlwgwi, tei ang bono jephuru tamo wngkha hwnwi swngkha, bo bini lama koro kha hwnwi ano sakha.

english: I took pity on him and offered to help him find his way home.
kokborok: Ang bono Khairok kha tei bono chubakha bini nokni lama naitukthani.

english: We walked together for a while, and I asked him about his life.
kokborok: Chwng baksa khe swrapsani bagwi himkha, tei ang bono bini langmani twi swngkha.

english: He told me that he lived with his parents and siblings in a small village outside of Mysore.
kokborok: Bo ano sakha bo bini buma-bupha tei dagisong bai mysore ni phataro chikonsa kamio tongo hwnwi.

english: He said that he loved to play cricket and that he dreamed of one day becoming a professional cricketer.
kokborok: Bo cricket thwngna hamjago hwnwi sakha tei bini imang khe salsa kaham cricket thwngkwrwng wngnani.

english: I told him that I was sure he would achieve his dream if he worked hard and never gave up.
kokborok: Ang bono sakha bo bini imangno mannai tumung bo samung kwrak tei yakarya'ui khlai tongkhe.

english: We eventually found his way home, and I was glad to see that his parents were so relieved to see him.
kokborok: Chwng ulokhe bini nok mankha, tei ang tongthok kha bini buma-bupha songno bono nugui khakchangma manmano nugwi.

english: Ambedkar Jayanti is a day of celebration in India and other countries around the world to honor the memory of Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, a social reformer, jurist, and political leader who was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and the architect of the Constitution of India.
kokborok: Ambedkar Jayanti wngkha mohai sal India o terkhlaima tei kubun hakotorrokni hayung yaksiyagra Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar ni mukumu no borom rwi, khoroksa hodarwk swnamnai, raidakwrwng, tei thwngrwngrwk ojama je Indian ni yohkmung ninangrimung ni kaisa lekhathaih berepkong tei Inda ni raidabwchcap tangrwbai.

english: Ambedkar was born into a Dalit family, a group of people who were considered to be untouchables in the caste system of India.
kokborok: Ambedkar kaisa Dalit ni nukhungo achayo, kaisa borok bodol je tangwimanya hwnwi wansukjago India ni khil lam bai.

english: He faced discrimination and hardship throughout his life, but he never gave up on his dream of equality for all Indians.
kokborok: Bo phermung malaikha tei bini langma o kwrwngwi bo belai biyal manjakha, phiya bo bini imang no jesaphano wngthwng yakaliya je Indians no homan khainani.

english: Ambedkar was a brilliant student and went on to earn a doctorate in law from Columbia University in the United States.
kokborok: Ambedkar wngkha bomtomgwnang rwngswrwngnai tei bo United States o thangwi Kerong doctrate ajikha Colombia University o.

english: He also studied at the London School of Economics and became a barrister.
kokborok: Bo London rangthong rwngnogo porijak tei khoroksa barrister bo wngkha.

english: After returning to India, Ambedkar became a leading figure in the Indian independence movement.
kokborok: India o phirokma olo, Ambedkar khoroksa lekhathaih dagimung wngkha Indian yokmung ninangrimung thayo.

english: He was a member of the Indian National Congress, but he eventually broke away from the party and formed his own political organization, the Scheduled Castes Federation.
kokborok: Bo khoroksa Indian National Congress ni adong wngjak, phiya paithago bodol bai kagwi thangpaikha tei bini sakni thwngrwngrwk motha swnamkha, Scheduled Castes Federation.

english: Ambedkar was also a key figure in the drafting of the Constitution of India.
kokborok: Ambedkar wngkha khoroksa berepkhong lekhathaih India ni raidabwchap koksongsagramung khai thani.

english: Casteism is a social system in India in which people are divided into rigid social classes, called castes.
kokborok: Khil wngkha kaisa hodarwk lam India bising boro borokrok kwrak hodarwk rwngremrok bising bakjakha, khilrok hwnwi ringjakha.

english: The caste system is based on the belief that people are born into a certain caste and that their caste determines their social status, occupation, and marriage prospects.
kokborok: Ah khil lam yapahang wngkha poitoni sakao je borok kaisa khatharjak khil bising achaikha tei je bohrokni khil kahthonmarok borokni hodarwk tongborom, occupation, tei khailaimung naiphunukmungrok.

english: Casteism has been a part of Indian society for centuries and has had a profound impact on Indian culture and society.
kokborok: Khil bisirarok karwi Indian dophani kaisa bokcho wngkha tei kaisa kuthukuk sekrupma tongo Indian hukumu tei dopha sakao.

english: The caste system has led to discrimination against lower castes, who have been denied access to education, jobs, and other opportunities.
kokborok: Ah khil lam tola khilrok kwthaiya khakjakmani bwkhak twlangkha, je rwng bwkhak sogwima, samungrok, tei kubun seprok gosiya wngkha.

english: In recent years, there have been efforts to abolish the caste system, but it remains a serious problem in India.
kokborok: Laithangjak bisirok bising, ah khil lam sokomorna bwkhak chaitokmarok aro wngkha, phiya amo kaisa India bising kubui kebengmung torwkma.

english: In 2018, the National Crime Records Bureau reported that there were over 40,000 cases of caste-based violence in India.
kokborok: 2018 bising, ah hodapharwk tangsitra tongmarirok haphangtang saimarikha je aro 40,000 sakao dorbkamung khil-yaphang bulaimamung wngkha Indiani bising.

english: Casteism is a complex and multifaceted issue.
kokborok: Khil wngkha kaisa kutuk tei jadrepodjak ongkhorma.

english: There is no easy solution to the problem, but it is important to continue to raise awareness of the issue and work towards eliminating caste discrimination.
kokborok: Aro ah kebengmung bwkhak mungsa solution kwrwi, phiya omo wngkha nangkukma bwkhak choyai oh ongkhorma sirwmarok kasama bwkhak tei ganarwk samung khil khajakmani normani.

english: It’s coming from the kitchen, so I get up to investigate.
kokborok: Obo nokgantini simi phaiui tongo, haini bagwi ang naitukphinani bachakha.

english: I creep down the hallway, careful not to make a sound.
kokborok: Ang khotol kotoro twrwk twrwk makhwganw, hojak tongdi mungsa khorang khwlaiyatwi

english: The clacking is getting louder.
kokborok: Kechemeche khorang teibo torrwk

english: I peer around the corner into the kitchen and see Mum standing at the sink, staring out the window.
kokborok: Ang nokgantini bwsup ganatwi naison naikha tei nukha ama sink ganao bwchaui phataro naisik tongo.

english: She looks pale and shaken. “Mum?” I ask.
kokborok: Boh saktwi kajak tei kwlwijak. "Ama?" Ang swngkha.

english: She doesn’t turn around.
kokborok: Boh yaksi yagra uphilya wng tongkha.

english: “Mum, what’s wrong?” She takes a deep breath and turns to face me.
kokborok: “Ama, tamo wngkha?” Boh hama kolok uaisa nasakha tei ani mwkhang phasing uphilkha.

english: Her eyes are wide and filled with fear.
kokborok: Bini mokol kotor kotor tei kirima gwnang wngjak.

english: “There’s something outside,” she says. “Something big.”
kokborok: “Phataro mungsaswk tongo, ” boh sao. “mungsaswk kotor.”

english: I follow her gaze out the window.
kokborok: Ang tailam phataro bini naisikmano rwgwi naisik naikha.

english: At first, I don’t see anything.
kokborok: Puilao, Ang mwgnsa nugwi manya wngmani.

english: But then, I notice a movement in the shadows.
kokborok: Phiya ulo, ang sampili kaisa lorimano nukha.

english: It’s a large, dark shape, and it’s moving towards the house.
kokborok: Obo kaisa kotor, kosom mang tei obo nok phaising agogui tongo.

english: “What is it?” I ask. “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But I don’t think it’s friendly.”
kokborok: “Obo tamo?” Ang swngkha. Ama sao “Ang saimanya, ”. “Phaia obo kichinghai hwnwi ang khakaya.”

english: The creature gets closer.
kokborok: O mal manwi ganao sokphayo.

english: It’s tall and slender, with long, spindly legs.
kokborok: Obo kuchuk tei keram, yakung kolok, kwsagwnang.

english: Its body is covered in black fur, and its head is a smooth, round ball.
kokborok: Bini bwsak buikhumu kosombai kupulung, tei bini khorok kepher, ball kitinghai

english: It has no eyes, but I can see two large, pointed ears.
kokborok: Oboni mokol kwrwi, phiya ang kotor, kwplap khunji kainwi nugwi tongo.

english: “What are we going to do?” I ask.
kokborok: “Chwng tamo khwlainani naiui tong?” Ang swngkha.

english: “We need to get out of here,” Mum says. “Now.”
kokborok: “Chwng oroni nokhornani nangnai, ” ama sao. “Tabuk”

english: We run out of the kitchen and into the living room.
kokborok: Chwng nokgantini kharwi achukjaknai khotolo phaiui paikha.

english: “Mum! Dad!” I cry. “There’s something outside!”
kokborok: “Ama! Apha!” ang kabo, “phataro mungsa tongo!”

english: Dad looks up from the TV. “What is it?” he asks.
kokborok: Apha TV ni simi nasikhoro. “Obo tamo?” Boh swngkha.

english: “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But it’s big and it’s coming this way.”
kokborok: “Ang saimanya, ” ama sao. “Phiya obo kotor tei yango phaiui tongo.

english: Dad gets up from the couch.
kokborok: Apha sofani simi bwchakha.

english: “We need to get out of here,” he says.
kokborok: “Chwng oroni nokhorwi thangnani nangnai, ” boh sao.

english: We all run for the front door.
kokborok: Chwng jottono bwskangni dogar phasing khachiklaikha.

english: Mum unlocks it and we rush outside.
kokborok: Ama doga phiyogwi rwkha tei chwng phatar phaising dolaikha.

english: The creature is right behind us.
kokborok: Oh mal manwi chinisai kisa ukologo

english: It’s so close I can feel its hot breath on the back of my neck.
kokborok: Obo aswkkhe ganao je ang ani gwdwna ukologo bini hama kutungno chongwimanw.

english: We run to the car and get in.
kokborok: Chwng malkhung phaising kharlaikha tei bisingo haplaikha.

english: Dad starts the engine and we peel out of the driveway.
kokborok: Apha engine chengkha tei chwng lahartwi nokhorwi phaikha.

english: The creature chases after us, but we’re too fast.
kokborok: Oh mal manwi chini ukolok rwktharo, phiya chwng belai dojak.

english: This is because they do not feed on blood.
kokborok: Omo tamni hinba bohrok thwi nwngya.

english: Instead, they feed on nectar from flowers.
kokborok: Boni slai, bohrok khumrokni simi twikwtwi nwngo.

english: Female mosquitoes, on the other hand, do feed on blood.
kokborok: Bwrwi thampuirok, tei kubun digi, bohrok thwi nwngo.

english: They need blood in order to produce eggs.
kokborok: Bwtwirok twihna bagwi bohrok thwi nango.

english: Male mosquitoes are attracted to light, so they are often found near windows and doors.
kokborok: Chwla thampurirok pohor bwkhak sotonjak wngkha, aswkno bohrok uramuramwi tailamrok tei duklamrok gana mano.

english: They are also attracted to the smell of sweat and CO2.
kokborok: Bohrok kolomtwi bahai tei C02 bwkhak khasotonma bo wngkha.

english: Female mosquitoes are attracted to the same things, but they are also attracted to the smell of certain chemicals in human blood.
kokborok: Bwrwi thampuirok wngkha ah sollai manwirok bwkhak khasotonjakha, phiya bohrok borok thwi bising khatharjak sapulswnamjakrok bahai bwkhak bo sotonjakha.

english: When a female mosquito bites a human, she injects saliva into the skin.
kokborok: Jephuru khoroska borokno kaisa bwrwi thampui uaro, bo ah bukur bising khuktwi sitogo.

english: This saliva contains anticoagulants, which prevent the blood from clotting.
kokborok: Oh khuktwi anticoagulants tonio, bomo ah thwi buthupmani simi kasogra khayo.

english: The mosquito then sucks up the blood.
kokborok: Ah thampui hwnkhe ah thwi kusupbo.

english: Mosquito bites can cause itching and swelling.
kokborok: Thampui warna motokmani tei torrwmani pher mano.

english: In some cases, they can also cause an allergic reaction.
kokborok: Baksa tanghalokrok bisingm borok kaisa allergic wngmani pher bo mano.

english: The most common type of allergic reaction to mosquito bites is hives.
kokborok: Ah jottoni slai manthok allergic wngmani sapokthaih thampui uarmarok bwkhak wngkha bothrairok wngo.

english: Hives are red, raised bumps that appear on the skin.
kokborok: Ah bothrairok wngkha kwchak, tisajak thaihmarok je ah bukur sakao peplao.

english: They can be itchy or painful.
kokborok: Bohrok motokma eba belai sah'ui mano.

english: In rare cases, mosquito bites can cause more serious problems.
kokborok: Manthokya tonghalok bising, thampui uarmarok teibo uansukrak kebengmungrok pher mano.

english: For example, some people can develop an infection at the site of the bite.
kokborok: Phunukmari kari, baksa borok kaisa bemar tubumani hamkrai mano ah uarma thayo.

english: In some cases, mosquito bites can even lead to death.
kokborok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, thampui uarma thwimung bwkhak haino dagi mano.

english: The best way to avoid mosquito bites is to wear long sleeves and pants when you are outdoors.
kokborok: Ah kaham lama thampui uarmarok katina bwkhak wngkha kolok yaktwkrok tei pants jephuru nwng phataro thangkhe.

english: You should also use insect repellent.
kokborok: Nwng yong kosorwma bo phwnangna nango.

english: If you do get bitten by a mosquito, you can apply a cold compress to the bite to relieve the itching and swelling.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng thampui bai uarjakha, nwng uarma thayo kaisa kwchang sinna thepai mano ah motokmani tei torrwmani holirwi mano.

english: You can also take an over-the-counter antihistamine to relieve the symptoms of an allergic reaction.
kokborok: Nwng kaisa kaisa allergic wngmani nukswkangmari holirwm bakhak kaisa ah-counter-sakao antihistamine bo nai mano.

english: Mosquitoes are important carriers of disease.
kokborok: Thampuirok wngkha bemar twinai nangkukma wngkha.

english: They can transmit a variety of diseases, including malaria, dengue fever, and yellow fever.
kokborok: Bohrok kaisa dalbidal bermarok, malaria khobmani, dengue kulum, tei kormo kulum rohor mano.

english: Mosquitoes are responsible for the deaths of millions of people each year.
kokborok: Ah chirasairok borok bisi thwgwi thwimungrok bagwi thampuirok bokjak wngkha.

english: There are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je ah thampui bangmanirok mwthakmung bwkhak khlaijak mano.

english: One way is to reduce the number of places where mosquitoes can breed.
kokborok: Kaisa lama wngkha ah lombor thairok khairwnani boro thampuirok achai mano.

english: This can be done by draining standing water and clearing away vegetation.
kokborok: Omo twi bathajakmani sokornani tei mwikhwtwng phang sapsutra hakchalo khaimani bai khlaijak mano.

english: Another way to control mosquito populations is to use insecticides.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lama thaimpui bangmani mwthakmung wngkha yongkuk thwithirok phwnangma.

english: Insecticides can be used to kill mosquitoes both indoors and outdoors.
kokborok: Yongkuk thwithirok thampui bwtharna bwkhak phwnangjak mano kanwi nokbisingrok tei patharok bai.

english: Mosquitoes are a major public health problem.
kokborok: Thampuirok wngkha kaisa kotor luku sakduk kebengmung.

english: However, there are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations and reduce the risk of mosquito-borne diseases.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro wngkha kwbangma manwirok je thampui bangmanirok mwkthakmung bwkhak khlaijak mano tei ah thampui- achaijak bemarok khairwi mano.

english: When tissue is injured, the body’s immune system sends white blood cells to the area.
kokborok: Jephuru sakhan dukhu manjak wngkhak, ah sak phiyokjak lam thwi kuphur khotolste homarok ah ari bwkhak.

english: These cells release chemicals that cause blood vessels to dilate and become more permeable.
kokborok: Oh khotolsterok sapulswnamjakrok yakaro je thwi twkrok pher phuarma bwkhka tei teibo hapmanjak wngkha.

english: This allows fluid and white blood cells to leak out of the blood vessels and into the injured tissue.
kokborok: Omo bwtwi tei thwi kuphur khotolste bwkhak kwpla ongkhorma ah thwi twkrok tei ah sakhan dukhu manjak bisingo wngo.

english: The fluid forms a clear, watery swelling called edema.
kokborok: Ah bwtwi sakmangrok kaisa sraisrai, twima torrwmani edema hwnwi ringjago.

english: The white blood cells help to fight infection and to remove damaged tissue.
kokborok: Ah thwi kuphur khotolsterok solomani bulaima bwkhak chubao tei bo sakhan piyakjak ongkhorma bwkhak.

english: They also release chemicals that stimulate the growth of new tissue.
kokborok: Bohrok sapulswnamjak bo yakarkha je ah kwtal sakhan torrwma jolirwma bai.

english: The classic signs of acute inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain.
kokborok: Oh kwcham marirok chiring robomsamung chaksama, kutung, torrwmani, tei kiyorma wngkha

english: These signs are caused by the increased blood flow and the release of chemicals in the injured tissue.
kokborok: Oh marirok thwi kochokma bangma bai pherjak tongo tei ah sakhan dukhu manjak bising sapulswnamjak yakarma tongo.

english: Redness is caused by the dilation of blood vessels.
kokborok: Chaksamarok ah thwi twkrok phuarma bai pherjak wngkha.

english: Heat is caused by the increased blood flow and the release of inflammatory chemicals.
kokborok: Tungma wngkha thwi kochokma bangma bai tei ah robomsama sapulswnamjakrok yakarma bai wngo.

english: Swelling is caused by the leakage of fluid from blood vessels into the injured tissue.
kokborok: Torrwmani wngkha ah bwtwi kwpla thwi twkrok ah sakhan dukhu manma simi pherjak wngkha.

english: Pain is caused by the release of inflammatory chemicals and the pressure of the swelling.
kokborok: Kiyorma wngkha pherjak ah yakarma bai robomsama sapulswnamjakrok tei ah torrwmani sepmung.

english: Acute inflammation is a normal part of the healing process.
kokborok: Chiring robomsamung wngkha kaisa kosong bokcho ah hammani tangsep.

english: However, if it is severe or prolonged, it can damage healthy tissue.
kokborok: Haiphano, tumungno omo kwrak eba kokphang, omo sakdukma sakhan paiyakmung mano.

english: In some cases, acute inflammation can lead to chronic inflammation, which is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
kokborok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, chiring robomsamung kwdwk bemar bwkhak dagi mano, bomo kaisa kolok-joraari tonghalok je kiyorma, manjuya, tei haino thwimung pher mano.

english: There are a number of things that can cause acute inflammation, including infection, injury, and autoimmune diseases.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je chiring robomsamung, solomani khobmani, dukhu manma, tei sakphiyokjak beramrok pher mano.

english: Infections are caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.
kokborok: Solomanirok bacteria, solobermarok, eba fungi bai pherjak mano.

english: When these organisms enter the body, they can trigger an immune response that leads to inflammation.
kokborok: Jephuru oh malmatarok sak oh habo, boro kaisa phiyokjak khophirokmarok lorki je robomsamung bwkhak dagimarok mano.

english: Injuries can also cause inflammation.
kokborok: Dukhumanmarok robomsamung pher bo mano.

english: When tissue is damaged, it releases chemicals that attract white blood cells and other immune cells to the area.
kokborok: Jephuru sakhan paiyakmung wngkha, omo sapulswnamjakrok yakarmarok je thwi kuphur khotolsterok tei kubun phiyokjak khotolsterok ah ari bwkhak khasotonma mano.

english: These cells release chemicals that cause inflammation.
kokborok: Oh khotolsterok sapulswnamjakrok yakaro je pher robomsamung bai.

english: Autoimmune diseases are caused by the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues.
kokborok: Sakphiyojka bemar wngkha ah sak phiyokjak lam choprobmani sakni sakhanrok bai pherjak wngkha.

english: This can lead to inflammation in the affected tissues.
kokborok: Omo ah sago kwlaijak sakhan bising robomsamung bwkhak dagi mano.

english: Acute inflammation is usually treated with pain relievers, such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen.
kokborok: Chiring robomsamung wngkha nangnungya kiyor holirwmarok bai saknaijak, ahaino ibuprofen eba acetaminophen.

english: In some cases, corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation.
kokborok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, corticosteriods robomsamung khaina bwkhak bo phwnangjak mano.

english: If the inflammation is caused by an infection, antibiotics may be prescribed.
kokborok: Tumungno robomsamung kaisa solomani, antibiotics bithini-kok sama bai pherjak mano.

english: Chronic inflammation is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
kokborok: Kwdwk bemar robomsamung wngkha kaisa kolok- joraaro tonghalok je kiyorma, manjuya, tei ahaino thwimung.

english: It is often caused by autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease.
kokborok: Omo uramuram sakphiyokjak bemarok bai pherjak wngkha, ahaino rheumatoid arthristis tei kwdwk bemarrok.

english: Chronic inflammation can also be caused by obesity, smoking, and air pollution.
kokborok: Kwdwk bemar khammani kuphungm hoku nwngmani, tei nokbar sitramung bai bo pherjak mano.

english: There is no cure for chronic inflammation, but it can be managed with medication, lifestyle changes, and physical therapy.

english: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
kokborok: Morokmung wngkha manwi morokmani tei kwlai wngma no sao.
