english: Texture can be created by using flowers with different types of petals, leaves, and stems.
kokborok: Taknai khumrokbai bai judajuda sapokthaih bai halok bubarlaih, bwlairok, tei bosongrok swnamjak mano.

english: When arranging flowers, it is important to consider the overall effect that you want to create.
kokborok: Jephuru khumrok thepjago, omo belai nanagkumani jottomiliwui amjokthai bwkhak wansukukma, je nwng swnamna nang jakmani.

english: Do you want a formal or informal arrangement?
kokborok: Nwng raidatwi eba raidayatwi thepajakma nang?

english: A romantic or modern arrangement?
kokborok: Kaisa wansuk khapang eba kwtal thepjakma nang?

english: Once you know what you want, you can start to choose the flowers and arrange them in a way that will achieve your desired effect.
kokborok: Waisa jodi nwng saimankha je nwng tamo nang, nwg saina chengwi manoo khumrok tei bohrokno thepama lamago je nwng muchungmarok amjokthai manwi mano.

english: Flower arranging is a creative art form that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.
kokborok: Khum thepamani hwnkhe kaisa swnamjakma rikmung sakmang, je jotto omorni borok tongthotogwi mano.

english: It is a great way to express your creativity and to bring beauty into your home.
kokborok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama nini swnammarok sraisrai khai sama tei nini nogo bisingo naithotok khe tubuimano.

english: In addition to their aesthetic appeal, flowers can also be used to communicate messages.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bwkhak bohrokni aethetic koima, khumrokno kokkwrwnglaima koktungrogo phwnangwi mano.

english: For example, red roses are often given to express love, while white lilies are often given to express sympathy.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, kwchak khutlairok wngkha hamjakmano sraisrai khai sama uramuram bwkhak rijago, jephuru kuphur kongcharirok khe khairokmung sraisrai khai sama uramuram bwkhak rijago.

english: The meaning of flowers can vary depending on the culture and the context in which they are given.
kokborok: Khumrokni kokmung dalbidal khlaima sakbokmani hukumu tei jeba swkangnikok bising bohrok rijago.

english: For example, in some cultures, the color purple is associated with royalty, while in other cultures, it is associated with mourning.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, baksa hukumurogo, pali phantok gap bugrasong bai gwdaljak, tei kubuni hukumurok, amo khe dukhu nangmani bai gwdaljak.

english: If you are not sure what the meaning of a particular flower is, it is always best to ask the person who gave it to you.
kokborok: Nwng jodi kaisa chongjak khum kokmung tamo wngkubui hwnwi siya khai, omo homnino kaham bwkhak je borok nono rinai no swngwi mano.

english: Flower arranging is a beautiful and meaningful art form that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.
kokborok: Khum thepamani wngkha kaisa naithokma tei kokmungkuplung rikmung sakmang je jotto omorni borok tongthokjak mano.

english: It is a great way to express your creativity and to bring beauty into your home.
kokborok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama bwkhak nini swnamjakma srai srai khai sama tei nini no bisingo naithok bwwkhak tubunani.

english: As a member of society, we have a responsibility to uphold the values and norms that make our community a better place to live.
kokborok: Khorosa dopha ni adong wngwi, chini thani kaisa bokjakmung tongo ah swkrok tei norms je chini hodano kaisa kaham tongna thai bwkhak sakatisama.

english: Stealing is wrong because it deprives others of their property and belongings, and it can have a negative impact on the community as a whole.
kokborok: Khokmani wngkha chaya tamhinba omo bohrokni manwiphan tei manwikhwnwirok kubunrokno sinkwlwkmarok, tei omo kaisa jotto hoda sakao kaisa chaya sekrupma tongwi mano.

english: When people steal, it can create an atmosphere of fear and distrust.
kokborok: Jephuru borok khogo, omo kaisa kirima habar tei poitochaya swnam mano.

english: It can also make it difficult for businesses to operate and for people to feel safe in their homes and neighborhoods.
kokborok: Omo bagwi beparirok bwkhak chalukna tei borokno bohrokni nokrok tei nokganarok bising katijak wansukma bwkha bo omo swnam mano.

english: In addition, stealing can lead to increased crime rates and social unrest.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising, khokmani tangsitra swkrok tei hodrwk oroiproi bangma bwkhak dagi mano.

english: If we want to create a society where everyone feels safe and respected, then we need to do everything we can to discourage and prevent theft.
kokborok: Tumungno chwng kaisa dopha swnamna muchungkhe boro jottono katijak wansukmarok tei boromjak wngkhe, hwnkhe chwng jottomanwi khai mansak khaina nangnai khaswbaima tei khokma kasogra.

english: We can do this by teaching our children about the importance of honesty and respect for others, and by working to create strong social and economic conditions that make people less likely to turn to crime.
kokborok: Chwng chini chwrairokno phwrwngmani bai khlaimano ah tongkwthar nangkukma tei kubunrokno kwrwi borom rwma bagwi, tei samung khaimani bai kwkrak hodarwl tei rangthog tonghalokrok swnamma bwkhak abo borokno haino kisa tangsitra bwkhak philma bwkhak swnamo.

english: As a socially sensible citizen, we should all do our part to make our community a better place.
kokborok: Kaisa hodarwkma simanwi habohrok wngkha, chwng jotto chini bokcho khaina nango chini hoda no kaisa kaham thai swnammaa bwkhak.

english: We should be vigilant about reporting suspicious activity and we should never hesitate to help someone who is in need.
kokborok: Chwng kaichomjak wngna nango chathaya samung-humung saimanrimani bagwi tei chwng jesaphuru phano kwmamma tawngthwng khoroksaswkno chubana bwkhak je nangwi tongkhe.

english: We should also be mindful of our own behavior and make sure that we are not doing anything that could put others at risk.
kokborok: Chwng chini saksakni tongmung no bwkhakuplung bo wngna nango tei wngkubui swnamdi je chwng mungsaphano khaiya twi je kubunrokno tangkiri thepai mano.

english: By working together, we can create a society where everyone can feel safe and respected.
kokborok: Thansa khe samung khaimani bai, chwng kaisa dopha swnam mano boro jottono katijak wansukma tei boromjak mano.

english: We can make it a place where everyone has the opportunity to succeed, and where everyone can contribute to making the world a better place.
kokborok: Chwng omono kaisa thai swnam mano boro jottono thani ah sep tonganw khalimanma bwkhak, tei boro jottono thumlai kaisa kaham thai hayung swnammani bwkhak.

english: Here are some additional thoughts on the importance of being a socially sensible citizen:
kokborok: Oro wngkha baksa jora rwjak wansukmarok kaisa hodarwkma simanwi habohrok wngjak ah nangkukma sakao:

english: * Socially sensible citizens are aware of the impact of their actions on others.
kokborok: * Hodarwkma simanwi habohrokrok wngkha ah sekrupmao sijak kubunrokni sakao bohrokni samungrok.

english: They think about how their behavior affects the community as a whole, and they make choices that benefit everyone.
kokborok: Bohrok wansukha bahaikhe bohrokni tongmung ah hoda khobwi nwngarwmarok, tei bohrok saimungrok swnamo je jottoni bagwi manmari khayo.

english: * Socially sensible citizens are willing to help others.
kokborok: * Hodarwkma simanwi habohrokrok wngkha kubunrokno chubana bwkhak gosimani.

english: They are not afraid to get involved in their community and make a difference.
kokborok: Bohrok bohrokni hoda bising kubuljak manna bwkhak kiriya wngkha tei kaisa pherlaima swnamnani.

english: * Socially sensible citizens are respectful of others.
kokborok: * Hodarwkma simanwi habohrokrok wngkha kubunrokno boromkuplung wngkha.

english: They treat everyone with dignity and respect, regardless of their race, religion, gender, or socioeconomic status.
kokborok: Bohrok jottono borom tei borom rwma bai bebohar khayo, bohrokni bosong khauarya, tpngkwthar, sir, eba hodarangthong tongborom.

english: * Socially sensible citizens are responsible.
kokborok: * Hodarwkma simanwi habohrokrok wngkha bokjak.

english: They take responsibility for their actions and they are accountable for the impact they have on the world.
kokborok: Bohrok bojakmung nao bohrokni samungrokni bagwi tei bohrok wngkha thikejak ah sekrupma karwi bohrok ah hayung saka tongo.

english: If we all strive to be socially sensible citizens, we can create a better world for ourselves and for future generations.
kokborok: Tumungno chwng jotto hodarwkma simanwi habohrokrok chaitoksukma khaikhe, chwng kaisa kaham hayung chini saksakni bagwi tei chini thinangni achaisongrok bagwi swnam mano.

english: A: Did you know that deforestation is one of the leading causes of climate change?
kokborok: A: Nwng saideman je bolong tanmani wngkha kaisa nokbartwibar swlaijakmani dagimani twmwirok?

english: B: No, I didn't.
kokborok: B: Ihin', ang siya.

english: How does that work?
kokborok: Abo bahai khe samung khai?

english: A: Well, when we cut down trees, we're not just destroying the trees themselves.
kokborok: A: Akon, chwng jephuru buphang rok raphaiyo, chwng haino buphangrokno baikhruptongmani khaiya phiya bohroksaksakno.

english: We're also destroying the habitats of countless animals and plants.
kokborok: Chwng lekhabaiya malamatarok tei buphang-uaphangrok tongma thai bo baikhruptongmani khayo.

english: And when we lose these habitats, we also lose the benefits that they provide us.
kokborok: Tei jephuru chwng oh tongma thairok kwmajago, chwng ah manmarrok bo kwmajago je bohrok chwngno swnamtonio.

english: B: Like what?
kokborok: B: Bahaikhe?

english: A: Well, for example, trees help to regulate the climate.
kokborok: A: Kahamno, phunukmari karwi, buphangrok nokbartwibar no cholirinani chubao.

english: They absorb carbon dioxide from the air and release oxygen.
kokborok: Bohrok carbon dioxide bo surupbo ah nokbar ni simi tei oxygen phiyogo.

english: They also help to prevent soil erosion and flooding.
kokborok: Bohrok haching kochokma tei twi lomani bo kasogra bwkha chubachu khayo.

english: And they provide food and shelter for animals.
kokborok: Tei bohrok chahthai tei malmatarokni bagwi tongthai swnamtonio.

english: B: So deforestation has a lot of negative effects.
kokborok: B: Aswkno bolong hokmani kaisa kwbang chaya sago kwlaimarok tongo.

english: A: It does.
kokborok: A: Omo hai wngo.

english: And it's a problem that's only getting worse.
kokborok: Tei omo kaisa kebengmung je omo hamsukya wngwi tongo.

english: Every year, we lose millions of acres of forest to deforestation.
kokborok: Bisi thwgwi, chwng chirasai bolong kanirok kwmjak tongo bolong hokmani bwkhak.

english: And if we don't do something to stop it, the consequences will be devastating.
kokborok: Tei tumungno chwng mwthakna bagwi mungsaswk khaiya khe, ah bwthaih rok swbaimani wngna i.

english: B: What can we do to stop it?
kokborok: B: Tamo chwng omono mwthakna bagwi tamo khainai?

english: A: There are a number of things we can do.
kokborok: A: Arao wngkha kwbangma manwirok chwng khai mano.

english: We can reduce our demand for wood products.
kokborok: Chwng chini bophang wngmanwi sanma khairwi mano.

english: We can plant trees.
kokborok: Chwng buphanagrok kaimano.

english: Chess is a game of strategy and tactics.
kokborok: Chess kaisa chapmung tei tang kwrwng ni thwngmung.

english: Players must be able to think several moves ahead and anticipate their opponent's moves.
kokborok: Thwngnairok dalbidal lorimarok wansukna kwrwng wngna nango tei bohrokni batainai rokni lorimarok khathaima wngna nango.

english: They must also be able to recognize patterns in the game and exploit them to their advantage.
kokborok: Bohrok thwngmung ni naidal rok siniwui narakna nango tei bohrokno samung phwnangma bwkhak bohrokni tangsrai khainani.

english: Pattern recognition is a key skill for chess players.
kokborok: Naidalrok sinijakmanai kaisa berepkhong yaksrai chess thwngnairokn bagwi.

english: It allows them to see the big picture and understand how the different pieces on the board interact with each other.
kokborok: Omo bohrokno kotor mangpili naina rwo tei juda juda bokchorok buohangbwlap sakao bahaikhe khoroksa tei khoroksa bai kwrwnglai bahai khe buchinani.

english: It also helps them to spot opportunities and threats early on, so that they can make the best possible moves.
kokborok: Omo bohrokno mari sep manna chubawo tei swkang skrimung sakao, je bohrok kahamkuk khe lorimanirok wngwimanma swnam mano.

english: Intuition is another important skill for chess players.
kokborok: Buchimani wngkha teikaisa nangkukmani yaksrai chess thwngnairokni bagwi.

english: It allows them to make decisions quickly and decisively, even when there is not enough time to think through all of the possible options.
kokborok: Omo borokno dakti chapmungrok tei kokthakjak swnamma bwkhak gosirio, jephuru aro aswk wansukna jora manya jotto wngwi manai saimungrokno twih.

english: Intuition is often developed through experience, but it can also be learned through training.
kokborok: Buchimani uramuraam saimanjak twih hamrai wngo, phiya omo swrwngmani twih swrwngjak wngwi mano.

english: Of course, there are many other skills that are important for chess players, such as calculation, memory, and concentration.
kokborok: Kubuino, aro kwbangma juda yaksrairok tongo je chess thwngrokni bagwi nangkukmani, ahaino lekhamani, muituphan, tei bwkharwmani.

english: However, pattern recognition and intuition are two of the most essential skills that all good chess players have.
kokborok: Haiphano, naidal sinijkamani tei buchimani wngkha kanwi jotto nangnai yaksrairok je jotto chess thwngnairokni oro tongo.

english: Here are some examples of how pattern recognition and intuition can be used in chess:
kokborok: Oro wngkha baksa phunukmari bahaikhe naidal sinijakmani tei buchimani chess o phwnangwi mano:

english: * A player may recognize that their opponent is trying to set up a particular trap.
kokborok: * Kaisa thwngnai sinijak mano je borokni batainai kaisa chongjak khwih kaihnani chaitogwi tongo.

english: By anticipating the trap, the player can avoid it and gain an advantage.
kokborok: Khwih no khathaima bai, thwngnairok katiwui mano tei omo tangsrai aji mano.

english: * A player may see that their opponent is weak on one side of the board.
kokborok: * Kaisa thwngnai bohrokni batainai no buphangbwlap kaisa digi kebel khe nugwi mano.

english: By exploiting this weakness, the player can gain control of the game.
kokborok: Oh beljak no samungkhaima bai, thwngnairok thwngmungno kaswkma aji mano.

english: * A player may have a gut feeling that a certain move is the best one to make.
kokborok: * Kaisa thwngnai kaisa kiryai wansukmani tongwi mano je kaisa khathrjak lormani kaisa kahamuk bwkha swnmam mano.

english: Even if they cannot explain why they feel this way, they may be right.
kokborok: Tumung borok baksa kok sukrubwi saimanya tangwiwi ang omtwi khe wansukma phai, bohrok kubui wngwi mano.

english: Pattern recognition and intuition are not easy skills to develop.
kokborok: Naidal sinimani tei buchimani wngkha yaksrairok hamkrai bwkhak wngya.

english: However, they are essential for anyone who wants to become a good chess player.
kokborok: Haiphano, bohrok jeba kaisa ni bagwi nangnai sabo kaham chess thwngnai wngna muchungjago.

english: With practice, these skills can be honed to a razor's edge, and a player will be able to see the game in a whole new way.
kokborok: Loi khlaimung bai, oh yaksrairok sengsa buchuk hulwi mano, tei kaisa thwngnai thwngmungno jotto kwtal lama twi nugwi mananw.

english: Children are constantly learning and growing, and it is important to teach them about appropriate and safe behavior.
kokborok: Chwrairok amtwinoamtwi swrwngmani tei tormani wngkha, tei omo wngkha kaisa nangkukma bohrokno phwrwngna bwkhak gothokma tei katijak tongmungni bagwi.

english: This includes teaching them about the difference between right and wrong, how to respect others, and how to stay safe.
kokborok: Omo bohrokno chajak tei chayani kwcharo ah pherlaima phwrwngmani khobmarokni bagwi, kubunrokno bahai khe borom rinai, tei bhaikhe kaitjak tongna.

english: One of the best ways to teach children about appropriate and safe behavior is by setting a good example.
kokborok: Kaisa ah kahamkuk lamarok chwrairokno phwrwngma bwkhak gothokma tei katijak tongmungni bagwi wngkha kaisa kaham phunukmari tangbwtang bai.

english: Children learn by watching the adults in their lives, so it is important to model the behavior that you want to see in them.
kokborok: Chwrairok bohrokni langmarogo ah okrarokno naiwui swrwngo, asswkno omo wngkha nangkukma naidal ah tongmung bwkhak je nwng bohrokni bising naina muchungmani.

english: For example, if you want your child to be honest, then you need to be honest with them.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, tumungno nwng nini chwraino tongkwthar khaina muchungkhe, hwnkhe nwng bohrok bai tongkwthar wngna nanganw.

english: If you want your child to be respectful, then you need to be respectful of them.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng nini chwraino boromjakma khaina muchungkhe, nwng borokno bomromjakma wngna nanganw.

english: Another important way to teach children about appropriate and safe behavior is to talk to them about it.
kokborok: Tei kaisa nangkukma lama chwrairokno phwrwngma bwkhak wngkha gothokma tei katijak tongmung wngkha omoni bagwi bohrok bai koksama.

english: Explain to them what is right and wrong, and why it is important to behave in a certain way.
kokborok: Borokno tamo chajak tei chaya, te bahai omo wngkha kaisa nangkukma kaisa khatharjak lama bising tongraida bwkhak.

english: Talk to them about the consequences of their actions, both good and bad.
kokborok: Bohrok bai kok sadi borokni samungrok ah parinamrok bagwi, kainwino kaham tei hamya.

english: It is also important to give children opportunities to practice appropriate and safe behavior.
kokborok: Omo chwrairokno seprok rwma bwkhak bo nangkukma wngkha gothokma loi khlaimung tei katijak tongmung.

english: This can be done through games, role-playing, and other activities.
kokborok: Omo thwngmungrokni bising twih khlaimano, thangthai-thwngmani, tei kubun samung-humungrok.

english: For example, you can play a game of "What would you do?" with your child and ask them how they would respond to different situations.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, nwng kaisa thwngmung thwngwi mano "nwng tamo khainai?" nini chwrai bai tei bohrokno swngma bohrok omono bahai kokphiroknai juda juda tonghalokrok bwkhak.

english: You can also role-play different scenarios, such as how to talk to a stranger or how to cross the street safely.
kokborok: Nwng bo juda juda nukmarirok tangthai-thwng mano, ahaino siniya bai bahaikhe kok sanai eba lamao kaitwui bahai khe laisunai.

english: By teaching children about appropriate and safe behavior, you can help them to become responsible and well-rounded individuals.
kokborok: Chwrairokno gothokma tei katijak tongmung bagwi phwrwngmani bai, nwng borokno bokjak tei kaham-kitingjak saksaknirok bwkhak chubai mano.

english: You can also help them to avoid dangerous situations and make good choices.
kokborok: Nwng bohrokno sakkati akochokma tonghalokrok tei kaham saimarok swnamma bwkhak bo chubai mano.

english: In addition to teaching children about appropriate and safe behavior, it is also important to provide them with a safe and secure environment.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising chwrairokno gothokma tei kaitjak tongmung bagwi phwrwngmani bwkhak, omo bo nangkukma bohrokno kaisa katijak tei naimwthangjak habar bwkhak bago.

english: This means making sure that your home is safe, that your child is supervised when they are playing outside, and that they are not exposed to violence or other harmful situations.
kokborok: Omoni kokmarok wngkubui swnammani je nini nok kaitjak wngma, jephuru bohrok phatardigi thwngwi tongphuru je nini chwraino naikoljakma wngkha, tei je bohrok bulaimani bwkhak phiyokjakma tawngthwng eba kubun hamyakuplung tonghalokrok.

english: By providing your child with a safe and secure environment, you can help them to feel safe and loved.
kokborok: Nini chwrai no kaisa katijak tei naimwthangjak habar bakmani bai, nwng bohrok wansukma katijak tei hamjakma bwkhak chubai mano.

english: This will help them to develop a healthy self-esteem and to make good choices.
kokborok: Omo bohrokno hamkrai bwkhak chubai mano kaisa sakdukma sak-boromrwma tei kaham saiamanrok swnamma bwkhak.

english: Teaching children about appropriate and safe behavior is an important part of parenting.
kokborok: Chwrairokno phwrwngmani gothokma tei katijak tongmung wngkha kaisa nangkukma bokcho parentingni bagwi.

english: By setting a good example, talking to your child about behavior, and providing them with a safe and secure environment, you can help them to become responsible and well-rounded individuals.
kokborok: Kaisa kaham phunukmari tangbwtang bai, nini chwraino tongmungni bagwi kok samani bwkhak, tei bohrokno kaisa katijak naimwthangjak habar bakmani, nwng borokno bokjak tei kaham-kitingjak saksaknirok bwkhak chubai mano.

english: When you are in a difficult situation, it is important to stay calm and collected.
kokborok: Nini jora hamya phuru, kwchang kwchang khe tongmani tei borok pal bai gwdalwi tongnani belai nango.

english: This will help you to think clearly and make good decisions.
kokborok: Omo hai khwlai khe nwng kaham uansokmung uansogwi manai tei kaham yapri seb thani chukrw nai.

english: It is also important to seek out the advice of someone who can help you to understand your situation and make the best decisions for yourself.
kokborok: Nono chuba'ui manai abotwi borokrokni kokno no bo khwna nangnai hakese nwng yapri kaham se wi manai.

english: There are many resources available to you, such as friends, family, counselors, and mental health professionals.
kokborok: Nini gana gini o kwbangma no manthogo, nini dolrog, nukhungni borokrog, kokbiti kwrwngrog, tei mental healthni professionalrog.

english: If you are struggling to cope with a difficult situation, please reach out for help.
kokborok: Omo hai jorarok bai gwdalna tukjagwi tong khe, chubamung ni bagwi rutuk jadi.

english: There is no shame in asking for help.
kokborok: Chubamung san thani lachimung kwrwi.

english: Here are some tips for staying calm and collected in a difficult situation:
kokborok: Kwchang kwchang khe tongjaknai tei pal bai gwdalwi tongjaknai abotwirokni kisaswk kaidarok wngkha:

english: * Take a few deep breaths.
kokborok: * Hama kolok khe nagra di.

english: This will help to slow your heart rate and breathing, which will make you feel calmer.
kokborok: Omo hai khwlai khe nini bwkha kodoma khe kwlwi marok tei hama sosa marok twrwk twrwk wngwi thangnai, omo hai kheno nono khakchang rw drop le wngnai.

english: * Focus on something positive.

english: * 1 large egg
kokborok: * 1 toktwi kotor

english: * 1 large egg yolk
kokborok: * 1 kotor toktwi bokhiri

kokborok: * Badam sepjak 1 tharukbwsa

english: * 1/2 cup milk
kokborok: * Dut cup 1/2

english: Instructions:
kokborok: Phunukmani:

english: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour an 8-inch round cake pan.
kokborok: 1. 350 degrees F'o (175 degrees C) thapa swkang muthungradi. Tok tei moida 8-inchi kiting kek pan.

english: 2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flours, granulated sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
kokborok: 2. Majar khurio, moida, pherekjak chini, somchak chini, baking powder, baking soda, tei somno baksakhe sapulwi.

english: 3. In a large bowl, cream together the butter and egg until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
kokborok: 3. Kotorma khurio, baksa khai makhon bai toktwino heleng tei lophung-lophung wngyasak sapuldi khlaidi. Toktwi bokhiri tei badam bwtwino sapuldi.

english: 4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk. Mix until just combined.
kokborok: 4. Remrem khai thumdi kwran bokobomrok kisi bokobomrokni saka rwdi, dutno khobwi. Sapuldi manjubaya sak.

english: 5. Fold in the almond flour until evenly distributed.
kokborok: 5. Badamni moidano thapdi baksakhe bakjana wngya sak.

english: I was worried that I might have contracted Lyme disease, but I went to the doctor and he said that I didn't have anything to worry about.

english: He told me that the rash was probably just a reaction to the tick's saliva.
kokborok: Bo ano sakha je ah bothrai guri wngkha unngthokma haino ah swkrani khutwi bwkhak wngphimani.

english: I was relieved to hear that I didn't have Lyme disease, but I was still a little bit concerned about the rash.

english: The doctor told me that it would go away on its own, but it took a few weeks for it to completely disappear.

english: In the meantime, I tried to keep the rash clean and dry.

english: I also applied some over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream to help relieve the itching.
kokborok: Baksa sakao-ah-bokhok hydrocortisone bithi bwthap ah motokmani holirwna bwkhak chubao.

kokborok: Ah bothrai guri motokma tei naithokya wngkha, phiya omo ano jesa kubun kebengmungrok pherjakya.

english: I'm just glad that I didn't have Lyme disease.
kokborok: Ang haino khatung kha je ang thani mungsa Lyme bemar kwrwi.

english: If you find a tick attached to your body, it's important to remove it as soon as possible.
kokborok: Tumungmo nwng kaisa swkra nini sago kwphajak mankha, omo jeswk daitono karina bwkhha omo nangkukma.

english: You can use a pair of tweezers to grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull it straight out.

english: Don't twist or jerk the tick, as this could cause the head to break off and remain in your skin.

english: Once you've removed the tick, wash the area with soap and water.
kokborok: Waisa nwng ah swkra swkakkha, ah kholano twi tei sapan bai sudi.

english: You can also apply a topical antibiotic ointment to help prevent infection.
kokborok: Nwng kaisa tropical antibiotic lepamabithi bo phulwi mano solomani kasogra chubama bwkhak.

english: It's important to watch for signs of Lyme disease after being bitten by a tick.
kokborok: Omo mwrwkna bwkhak nangkukma Lyme bemar marirokni bagwi kaisa swkra bai warjakma wngjak olo.

english: These symptoms can include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle aches, and a characteristic rash.
kokborok: Oh nukswkangmarirok kulum, khorokmihima, sak hoi hoi, bahan samarok, tei kaisa gwrwngjakma bothrai guri khobwi mano.

english: If you develop any of these symptoms, see your doctor right away.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng oh nukswkangmarirok babai jesa hamrwk wngkha, daktino nini saknainai bai malaidi.

english: Lyme disease is a serious illness, but it can be treated with antibiotics.
kokborok: Lyme bemar wngkha kaisa wansukrak kulum, phiya omo antibiotics bai saknaijakma wngwi mano.

english: Early diagnosis and treatment is important to prevent serious complications.
kokborok: Dakti hamyaungmarok tei saknaimung wamsukrak hamthayamarok kasogra bwkhak nangkukma wngkha.

english: If you have any questions about ticks or Lyme disease, talk to your doctor.
kokborok: Tumungno nini thani jesa swngmungrok tongkhe swrakrok eba Lyme bemar bagwi, nini saknainai bai kok sadi.

english: You can also review your notes after class to help solidify your understanding of the material.

english: For example, a person who is angry at their boss may take it out on their spouse or children.

english: This is because wrath is often a secondary emotion, meaning that it is triggered by another emotion, such as fear, sadness, or anxiety.
kokborok: Tamni hwnba jolima wngkha uramuram kaisa majarni khanangmung, oboni kokmang hwnkhe obo kirima, bwkha hamya wngma, eba khaching-khaching wngma hai kubun khanangmung bai khilijak.

english: When we are feeling these emotions, we may lash out in anger in order to protect ourselves or to feel a sense of control.
kokborok: Chwng jephuru oh khanangmarokno matongo, chwng amo jolimabai kutuk kari mano, chini sakno kartina bagwi eba sak-sakno kaisa sinai simanwi hai matongna bagwi.

english: Wrath can also be a destructive emotion.
kokborok: Jolimung kaisa sokomorthok khanangmung wngwi manu.

english: It can lead to violence, abuse, and other harmful behaviors.
kokborok: Omo bulaimung, satokmung, tei kubun chayakuplung tongmungrokni bwkhak dagimano.

english: When we are angry, we may not be thinking clearly and we may make decisions that we later regret.

english: We may also say or do things that hurt others, which can damage relationships and make it difficult to repair them.

english: It is important to be able to recognize and manage wrath.
kokborok: Jolimungno saimannani tei naikolnani nangsugu.

english: If we can do this, we can avoid the negative consequences of this emotion.
kokborok: Tumungno chwng amo khlaywi mankha hwnkhe, chwng ah khanangmungni chaya thaimungrokno sakpherwi manu.

english: There are a number of things we can do to manage wrath, such as:
kokborok: Chwng jolimano chorwi tonna bagwi kwbangma manwi khlaywi manu, aborok wngkha:

english: * Identifying the triggers for our anger.

kokborok: Bohrok kisa kahai sakderakha eba siniyarokbai chaya khaima eba akabikarok bai tongo.

english: On the other hand, it has also made children less independent.
kokborok: Tei kaisa yago, omo chwrairokno kisa yohkjak bo swnam tongo.

english: They are less likely to be able to take care of themselves or to make their own decisions.
kokborok: Bohrok kisa ahaino bohroksaksakno nakani khai nama bwkhak khlaimana tongo eba bohrokni sakni chongmarokno swnamma bwkhak.

english: In addition to increased supervision, children are also more likely to be involved in structured activities than they were in the past.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising naikoljakma phuwarkha, bohrok wngthangjak bisingni slai chwrairokbo teibo ahaino swnamarikha samung-humung bising kubulma tongo.

english: This is due in part to the rise of the "activity culture," which emphasizes the importance of children being involved in a variety of extracurricular activities.
kokborok: Omo sakmwchang bokchoni bising ah "hukumu tangma," kasamung bwkhak wngo, bomo khakrakokrok ah charairokni nangkukma kaisa dalbidal yakbahrasaklaima samung-humung bising kubulma wngjak.

english: Activity culture has been driven by a number of factors, including the increasing competitiveness of the job market and the belief that children who are involved in extracurricular activities will be more successful in life.
kokborok: Hukumu tangma wngkha kwbangma kusunchwlwi bai chalukjak tongo, ah tangsamung hatio batailaimung bangmani bising khobmani bai tei ah poito je chwrairok je yakbahrasaklaima samung-humung bising kubulma tongo bohrok teibo khlaimanjak langmani bising wngnai.

english: The rise of the activity culture has had a number of consequences for children.
kokborok: Ah hukumu tangma kasamung chwrairokni bagwi kwbangma bwthaihrok tongo.

english: On the one hand, it has given children more opportunities to develop their skills and talents.
kokborok: Tei kaisa yago, omo chwrairokno teibo seprok rwkha bohrokni yaksrairok tei suargangrok hamkrai bwkhak.

english: On the other hand, it has also added to the pressure that children feel to succeed.
kokborok: Tei kaisa yago, omo ah sinmung bwkhak bo thepakha je chwrairokno khlaimanma bwkhak wansukrio.

english: Children who are not involved in a variety of extracurricular activities may feel like they are not measuring up.
kokborok: Chwrairok je kaisa dalbidal yakbahrasaklaima samung-humung bising kubulya tongma kahai wansuk mano bohrok saka sumung khaiya.

english: The worries about childhood that have emerged in recent years have had a profound impact on the way that children are raised today.
kokborok: Ah unnarwmarok chwrairokni bagwi je laithangjak bisirokni bising ongkhorma tongo kaisa kuthukuk sekrupma tongkha ah lama sakao je chwngrairok tini torrwma wngkha..

english: These worries have led to a number of changes in the way that children are supervised and the activities that they are involved in.
kokborok: Oh uanarwmarok kwbangma swlaimarok bwkhak twlang tongo ah lama bising je chwrairok naikolma tei samung-humung je bohrok kubulma bising tongo.

english: These changes have had both positive and negative consequences for children.
kokborok: Oh swlaimarok kainwi kaham tei hamya bwthaihrok tongo chwrairokni bagwi.

kokborok: Phiya Jack ni thani mungsaswk tongo abono nugwi Josephin ma chajak kha.

kokborok: Jack bai Josephin malaina chenglai kha, tei borok dakti no hamjak bo pailai kha.

kokborok: Bohrok kwnwi bars o mwsawino sal haprwo tei horo khe kok salaiwi no dam pairwlayo.

english: Online shopping is the process of buying goods or services from a retailer over the Internet.
kokborok: Online shopping wngkha ah tangsep manwirok paimani eba samungrok kaisa swbai phalnai ah internet sakao.

english: It is different from traditional shopping in that the consumer does not physically visit a store to purchase the product.
kokborok: Omo wngkha juda juda mukumu shopping bising je ah painai ahaino sakno twi kaisa khatinogo ah duna bwthaih no paina bwkhak naina thangya.

english: Instead, the consumer browses through products and makes purchases online.
kokborok: Aboni bade, ah painai duna bwthaih twih browses khayo tei onlinen twi paimarok khayo.

english: The consumer then receives the product at their home address.
kokborok: Ah painai hwnkhe ah duna bwthaih bohrokni nok ni nikumao manphaiyo.

kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmarirok tongo online shopping khaima bwkhak.

kokborok: Puila, omo uramuram teibo chajak mukumu shopping ni slai.

kokborok: Painairok bohrokni sakni nogni simi aram khai pai mano, jesa jora phano hor eba sal wngthwng.

english: They can also compare prices from different retailers and read reviews of products before making a purchase.
kokborok: Bohrok morokmarokbo suwui mano juda juda swbai phalnairok simi tei duna bwthaih naikolmungrok poriwui paina swkang.

english: Second, online shopping can be more affordable than traditional shopping.
kokborok: Nwirem, online shopping mukumu shopping ni slai teibo painani phan tongwi mano.

english: Many retailers offer discounts and promotions on their online products.
kokborok: Kwbangma swbai phalnairok khaihmarok tei remsitamungrok bohrokni online duna bwthaihrok sakao yapharo.

english: Third, online shopping can be more environmentally friendly than traditional shopping.
kokborok: Thamrem, online shopping teibo mukumu shoppingni slai habarjak bayapsong wngwi mano.

english: Consumers do not have to drive to the store, which reduces emissions.
kokborok: Painairok khatinogo chalugwi thangna nangya, obo emissions khairio.

english: However, there are also some drawbacks to online shopping.
kokborok: Haiaphano, aro baksa kebengjak tongo online shoppingo tongo.

english: First, consumers cannot try on clothes or test out products before they buy them.
kokborok: Puila, painairok reerok kanna chaitok many eba duna bwthaiih rokno kari amjok manya bohrokno bohrok paina swkang.

english: This can lead to disappointment if the product does not fit or meet the consumer's expectations.
kokborok: Omo chajakya bwkhak dagi twlang mano tumungno ah dunaa bwthaih painaini khchongmarok bai malaiya eba chakya hwkhe.

english: Second, online shopping can be more risky than traditional shopping.
kokborok: Nwirem, online shopping mukumu shopping ni slai teibo khapharjak wngwi mano.

english: Consumers need to be careful about providing their credit card information online.
kokborok: Consumers kisa naikani wngna nango bohrokni credit card ni sakhlaimung online o thumnani swkang.

english: The forest was a place of peace and tranquility.
kokborok: Bolong wngkha kaisa thai kwchangtotok tei kwchangtotok.

kokborok: Buphangrok kuchuk tei bolaijak khe bachajak, bohrokni bedekrok nokha saka sogwinaikha.

kokborok: Omo wngkha mohai thai boro khoroksaswk yoknai bagwi phaimano dagachopa tei dosidopra sal brumbrum langmao.

english: One day, a young woman named Diana was walking through the forest.

english: As she walked, she heard a noise.
kokborok: Bo himwi tongphuru, bo kaisa khorang khwnakha.

kokborok: Abo kaisa lengjak khorang, phiya bini saktongma romna bagwi nangmaswk wngkha.

english: She stopped and listened, and she heard the sound again.
kokborok: Bo bathagwi tei khwnakha, tei bo teiwaisa khorang khwnaphikha.

english: It was the sound of crying.
kokborok: Obo wngkha kabmani khorang.

english: Diana followed the sound, and she came to a clearing.
kokborok: Diana khorangno rwtharwi thangkha, tei bo sraisrai khaima bwkhak phaikha.

english: In the middle of the clearing was a small girl, sitting on a rock and crying.
kokborok: Sraisraini kwcharo khoroksa bwrwi chikonsa wngkha, holong sakao achugwi tei kabwi tongo.

english: Diana walked over to the girl and asked her what was wrong.
kokborok: Diana bwrwino oro himwi thangkha tei bono swngkha tamo chaya wngkha hwnwi.

english: The girl told Diana that she was lost.
kokborok: Bwrwi Dainano sakha je bo kwmakha hwnwi.

kokborok: Daina bwrwino sakha tawanadi hwnwi, tei bo swmai tangkha bono chubana hwnwi bini nok lama naituk thani.

english: "I stood before the sculpture, my heart filled with both awe and sadness.

english: But they were not.

english: I turned to the artist, a young man named Ram. "You must stop sculpting," I said.
kokborok: Ang ah rikwrwng bwkhak gurikha, khoroksa chwla sikla ram mungwi, "nwng takmani mase ma mwthaknai," ang sakha.

english: You are seeing the world as you wish it to be. That is not real art.
kokborok: Nwng ah hayungno naimani nini amo mucungma bwkhak twi. Abo kubui rikmung wngmaya.

english: Real art is about showing the world as it is, warts and all.

english: It is about making people feel something.

english: Your sculptures don't make people feel anything.

english: They just make them feel sad."
kokborok: Bohrok haino borokno bwkha hamya wansukrio."

english: Ram was silent for a long time.

english: I was driving home from work one day when I got cut off by another driver.

english: Finally, I couldn't take it anymore.

kokborok: Ang saka tisai bini gana bachakha tei bono chirikna chengkha.

kokborok: Bo bini tailam tola khikwlaikha tei ano ukuluk chiroknani chengkha.

english: We were both so angry that we were shaking.
kokborok: Chwng khoroknwino aswkno thamsi wngjak chwng kwlwijak wngkha.

kokborok: Ah kubun chaluknai ah lama kinar bwkhak saka sotonkha, tei ang bono rwtharkha.

kokborok: Chwng nini malkhungni phatar ongkhorkha tei khoroksa tei khoroksa no chiriklainani chengkha teibo sotonwi.

english: I was so close to hitting him that I could smell his breath.
kokborok: Ang aswko gana wngkha bono bunani phiya ang bini hamanio bahai manwi tongo.

english: Just when I thought it couldn't get any worse, a police car pulled up.
kokborok: Haino jephuru ang wansukha omoni slai mungsa hamya wngya hwnwi, khoroksa police malkhung saka sotonkha.

english: The officer got out of his car and asked us what was going on.
kokborok: Ah habaphang nini malkhungni phatar ongkhorkha tei chwngno swngkha tamo wngwi tong.

english: We both told him our sides of the story, and he started writing us a ticket.
kokborok: Chwng khoroknwino bono chini digirokni kothoma saka, tei bo chwngno kaisa nanglaih swinani chengkha.

english: As I was walking back to my car, I realized that I had learned my lesson.
kokborok: Iko ang ani malkhung bwkhak phirok himwi thangmani, ang saimankha je ang nai phwrwng bwchap swrwngkha.

english: The flowers were expensive, but I didn't care.
kokborok: Khumrok belai morojak, phiya ang naikani khailiya.

kokborok: Ang bohrokno manna nango.

kokborok: Aborok belai naithokmani khumrok ang kumphru nukmani, tei ang saimano bohrok bono tongthokrwi mano.

english: I bought a dozen roses, all different colors.
kokborok: Ang kaisa chwnwi khutlairok painakha, jotto juda juda palitwi.

english: She smiled when she saw them. "They're beautiful," she said. "Thank you."

kokborok: "Angbo nono hamjago," ang sakha.

english: Crops and seeds are essential to life.
kokborok: Mwithaih bwthaihraok tei bwchwlwirok wngkha langma bwkhak nangnai.

english: They provide us with food, clothing, and shelter.
kokborok: Bohrok chwngbai chathaih, richum, tei lenglama bago.

english: In order to grow healthy crops, we need to select the right seeds for our climate and soil conditions.

english: We also need to take care of our crops by watering them, fertilizing them, and protecting them from pests.

english: Farmers have been selecting and breeding crops for thousands of years.
kokborok: Chuwainairok sai bisirok karwi saimani tei mwithaih bwthaih thaihrwmani wngkha.

english: They have learned how to grow crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, and that produce high yields.
kokborok: Bohrok bahaikhe mwithaih bwthairok torwna bwkhak swrwngjak tongo je pests tei bemarrok kasojak bwkhak wngkha, tei je kuchuk achairwi achairwmarok thairwma.

english: In recent years, farmers have also begun to use genetic engineering to improve crop yields and resistance to pests.
kokborok: Laithangnai bisirok bising, chuwairok genetic engineerig phangma bwkhak mwithaih bwthaih achairwmarok tei pests kasojak bwkhak bo chengjakma wngkha.

english: The process of growing crops is not without its challenges.
kokborok: Mwithaih bwthaih torwmani wngkha ah tansep bataimarok kwrwi wngya.

english: Farmers often have to deal with unpredictable weather conditions, pests, and diseases.
kokborok: Chuwainairok uramuram sasokmaya salbar tonghalokrok, pests tei bemarok bai naimung bwkhak tongo.

english: However, the rewards of growing crops can be great.
kokborok: Haiphano, ah yakpairok mwithaih bwthairok torimani kotorokuar wngwi mano.

english: Farmers can provide food for their families and communities, and they can also earn a living from their work.
kokborok: Chuwainairok bohrokni nukhungrok tei hodarokni bagwi chaithaih bagwi mano, tei bohrok bohrokni samungni simi kaisa tongmani bo aji mano.

english: In addition to providing food, crops can also be used to create other products.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising bakmani bwkhak chathaih, mwithaih bwthaihrok kubun duna bwthaihrok swnamma bwkhak bo chubai mano.

english: For example, cotton can be used to make clothing, and corn can be used to make ethanol.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, khulno richum swnamma bwkhak phwnangjak mano, tei mogodamno ethanol swnamma bwkhak phwnangjak mano.

english: Crops can also be used to create biofuels, which can help to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels.
kokborok: Mwithai bwithaihrok biofuels swnamma bwkhak bo phwnangjak mano, omo fossils fuels ni sakao chini khatharjak khaina bwkha chubai mano.

english: The importance of crops and seeds is undeniable.
kokborok: Ah mwithaih bwthaihrok tei bwchwlwirok wngkha undeniable nangkukma.

english: My first day of school was a day I will never forget.
kokborok: Ani puila sal rwngnogo wngkha amtwi sal ang tei abo pokgwlak.

english: I was both excited and nervous, not knowing what to expect.
kokborok: Ang aphuru kainwino tongthokjak tei kirijak, saimanjaya tamno khachongjak.

english: When I woke up that morning, I got dressed quickly and ate a quick breakfast.
kokborok: Jephuru ang phungo bachao, ang dakti no ri chumkha tei dakti no chamung chakha.

english: Then, my mom drove me to school and walked me to my classroom.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, ani maa ano rwngnogo twlangkha tei rwngrem bising himrwi tunuikha.

english: When I walked into the classroom, I was immediately greeted by my teacher, Ms. Smith.
kokborok: Ang jephuru rwngrem bising himiw thangkha, ang daktino ani rwngphwrwngnai, Ms. Smith bai lamsukjakha.

english: She was a kind-looking woman with a warm smile.
kokborok: Bo belai kaham-naima brwi tunglulu mwmwima bai.

english: She introduced herself to me and then showed me to my seat.
kokborok: Bo ano bini sinimung rwkha ano tei ani achukthai boro phunukha.

english: I sat down next to a girl named Sarah.
kokborok: Ang khoroksa bwrwi mung Sarah ni gana achukha.

english: She smiled at me and said, "Hi, I'm Sarah."
kokborok: Bo ano mwmwikha tei sakha, "Hi, ang Sarah."

english: I smiled back and said, "Hi, I'm Vera."
kokborok: Ang kiphilwi mwnwikha tei sakha, "Hi, ang Vera."

english: We talked for a few minutes before the bell rang for class to start.
kokborok: Chwng jora kisa romwi kok salaikha gonta togwi rwng chengna swkang.

english: Ms. Smith began by introducing herself and telling us about the rules of the classroom.
kokborok: Ms. Smith bini bagwi sinimung rina chengkha tei chwngno rwngrem raidarokni bagwi sakha.

english: Then, she started teaching us about math.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, bo chwngno ongko phwrwngna chengkha.

english: I was a little bit confused at first, but Ms. Smith explained everything clearly.
kokborok: Ang puila wo kisa bujimanya wngkha, haiphano Ms. Smith kahamma khe bebak sukurubwi sakha.

english: After math class, we had a break.
kokborok: Ongko rem ni olo, chwng bathakjakna mankha.

english: Sarah and I went outside to play on the playground.
kokborok: Sarah bai ang phatarni nokhwlao thwngna thangkha.

english: We played on the swings and the slide for a while, then we went back inside for lunch.
kokborok: Chwng swrapsa khitarjakna tei sorojaknai thwngkha, hwnkhe chwng phirogwi bisingo chana thangkha.

english: These are just a few of the issues that can plague a car that has been in a minor accident.
kokborok: Oh kisasa jwngjal baino malkhungno chikonsa accident wngwi thangkha.

english: While the damage may not seem significant, it can still be dangerous and expensive to fix.
kokborok: Deramarok sijaklia phano, tabukbo kirimasingsa tei thepaphinani morok.

english: In the case of worn or falling apart rubber pieces, this can be a safety hazard.
kokborok: Rubber bwkaprok kwphai tongkhe ba, kisale sak katima hai wngwi mano.

english: Rubber is used in a variety of places on a car, including the tires, brake pads, and seals.
kokborok: Rubber malkhungni dal bidal thayo thepajago, tyre, brake pad tei seal rogo.

english: When rubber becomes worn, it can crack, split, or otherwise deteriorate.
kokborok: Jephuru rubber chamwi ransao aphru phatiui mano ebakhe hamsukya wngwi thangnai.

english: This can lead to a number of problems, such as reduced traction, decreased braking performance, and leaks.
kokborok: Oboni bisingtwi brung brung jwngjalrok phaiwi mano, romdi sochol malma khochornai, braking romma bo khainai, tei kwplabo wngwi mano.

english: Missing roof rail pieces can also be a safety hazard.
kokborok: Nukhung sakao bwkap tongkhebo atomsa patimungni sak kati wngo.

english: Roof rails are designed to help protect passengers in the event of a rollover accident.
kokborok: Malkhung nukhungni bokong swnamjakma hwnkhe jephuru malkhung goirogwi accident o philjago aphuru aphuru kanaino dukhu manna katirwo.

english: If the roof rails are missing, the roof of the car is more likely to collapse in a rollover, which can cause serious injuries or death.
kokborok: Tumung malkhung nukhungni bokong kwrwi hwnkhe, malkhung nukhung teibo bainani kwlai wngo jephuru malkhung ukuluk philjakhe abo kirimasingcha khe dukhu mannai eba thwinai.

english: A broken fuel tank door lock can also be dangerous.
kokborok: Thok tengki ni khapremung kwbai hwnkhe bo bini akocho kirimasingsa.

english: If the fuel tank door cannot be locked, it could come open while the car is moving.
kokborok: Tumung thokni bokhok tala khajakya hwnkhe malkhung malwi tongphuru phiyokjagwi mano.

english: This could spill fuel onto the road, which could cause a fire or explosion.
kokborok: Haikhe lamao thok kwsarwi mano, abobai hor khamwi mano eba phatiui mano.

english: In addition to the safety risks, these types of damage can also be expensive to fix.
kokborok: Sak kati marino naikhe, obohai deramungno swnamphi nani belai morok.

english: Rubber pieces can be difficult to replace, and roof rails and fuel tank door locks can be expensive to repair or replace.
kokborok: Rubber bwkap rokno thepaui swlai rwi mano malkhungni nukhung sakaobo, tei thok tonma bokhokbo swmanna hwnkhe belaino morok wngo.

english: In some cases, it may be more cost-effective to total the car and buy a new one.
kokborok: Babaisa naikhe, aswk morokya bo wngwi mano jotto thumui malkhungni morokma tei kwtal paina no wansuk naikhe.

english: If you are considering buying a used car that has been in a minor accident, be sure to have it inspected by a qualified mechanic.
kokborok: Nwng tumung malkhung chalukjak no painani wansugwi tongkhe, abo kisisa accident wngjak phano, siniui nadi je abo elem gwnng malkhung naikwrwngbai naijak wngthung.

english: They will be able to identify any damage that may not be visible to the naked eye, and they can advise you on whether or not the car is safe to buy.
kokborok: Bohrok derajak manwino sinina rwngo mokolbai nukya manwino phano, tei bohrok nono kok khoraiwi mano ah malkhungno paiwi kaham da wngno wngya.

english: My colleague was a hard worker, but she was always getting passed over for promotions.
kokborok: Ani tangsong belai samung kwrak khainai, phiya bo homnino remtisamung manmarogo lairwi hojago.

english: She was told that she needed to "work harder" or "be more visible," but it seemed like no matter what she did, she couldn't get ahead.
kokborok: Bo sajakha je bo "samung kwrak" eba "teibo naimanmung wngdi," bwkhak nanganw phiya omo naina thangkhe bo tamo sakha samung nangjakyaa, bo bwskango maanwi manliya.

english: The manager was also a problem.
kokborok: Ah manager bo kaisa kebengmung.

english: He was always micromanaging everyone, and he was quick to criticize.
kokborok: Bo homnino jottono micromanaging khayo, tei bo dakti no kokchirmung khayo.

english: He didn't seem to care about the employees' work-life balance, and he expected them to be available 24/7.
kokborok: Bo aswk samungkhainai rokni langma-samung ojon bwkhak naikini khaima nukjakya, tei bo bohrokno 24/7 manthoknai hwnwi khajajak.

english: My colleague eventually reached her breaking point.
kokborok: Ani tangsong paithago bini baimani buchugo sogwikha.

english: She couldn't take the stress of the job anymore, and she knew that she wouldn't be able to advance her career there.
kokborok: Bo samung ni sekrupma tei naimanliya, tei bo saimano je bo aro bini tangmung swkangkolok manliya.

english: She gave her two weeks' notice and started looking for a new job.
kokborok: Bo bono hatinwi rok rwkha' sakhlaimung tei kwtal samung naitukna chengkha.

english: She found a new job that was a much better fit for her.
kokborok: Bo kaisa kwtal samung mankha je teisa kahamkuk bini bagwi chukjak.

english: The pay was better, the hours were more reasonable, and the manager was supportive and understanding.
kokborok: Aro rwma tei sa kaham, damrwi rok teibo reasonable, tei manager twichurunai tei buchinai.

english: She's much happier now, and she's glad that she made the decision to leave her old job.
kokborok: Bo tabuk teisa tongthokjak, te bo khatung khajak je bo bini kwcham samungno chongwi yakarmani.

english: I'm not sure what the manager is doing now, but I hope that he's learned his lesson.
kokborok: Ang aswk wngkubui rwi mnay tabuk manager tamo kha tong, phiya ang khajamung khayo je bo bini phwrwng bwchap swrwngkhwna.

english: He can't treat his employees like that and expect them to stay.
kokborok: Bo bini samungkhainai rokno naikol manya haino je bohrokno tongdi hwnwi khajama khai tongdi hwnwi manya.

english: If he wants to keep good people, he needs to change his ways.
kokborok: Bo jodi borok kaham rokno tonina muchungkhe, bo bini lamarok swlaina nanganw.

english: As for my colleague, she's doing great in her new job.
kokborok: iko ani tangsongno karwi, bo bini kwtal samungo kotorkuar khaitongo.

english: She's getting the recognition that she deserves, and she's finally able to advance her career.
kokborok: Bo sinimung manwi tongkha je bo yakpai manmani, tei bo paithago bini tangmung swkangkolok khaimanani.

english: She's a great example of what happens when you stand up for yourself and refuse to put up with a bad situation.
kokborok: Bo kaisa kotorkuar phunukmari jephuru nwng nini nagwi bachao aphuru tamo wngno tei soiyawui saka tonima bai hamya jorao.

english: In a Google spreadsheet, an absolute reference will always refer to the same cell, regardless of where it is copied or moved to.
kokborok: Kaisa Google spreadsheet bising, kaisa soidom yasikaihjakma homnino ah solai kotagera bwkhak yasikaihma, khauarya boro amo kosoljak eba norjak bwkhak wngkha.

english: Absolute references are useful for cells that contain data that you do not want to change when you copy or move the formula.
kokborok: Belai yasikhaihjakma kotagerarokni bagwi doro wngkha je sijakrwnai tongo je nwng swlaina muchungjakya jephuru nwng kosol eba ah karilam norma.

english: For example, if you have a formula that calculates the total sales for each month, you would want to use an absolute reference for the cell that contains the starting date.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, tumungno nini thani kaisa karilam tongkha je tal thwgwi ah bebak phalmarokni bagwi gonimarok, nwng ah kotagerani bagwi kaisa kubui yasikaihjakma phwnangma bwkhak muchung mano je ah chengmani sal tongmarok.

english: This way, the formula will always refer to the same cell, even if you copy it to a different row or column.
kokborok: Omo haikheno, ah karilam homino ah solai kotagera bwkhak yasikaihnai, ahaino tumungno nwng ahaino omo juda juda bwtang eba thong bwkhak kosol khayo.

english: You can create an absolute reference by adding a dollar sign ($) to the row number and column letter of the cell reference.
kokborok: Nwng kaisa kubui yasikaihjakma swnam mano kaisa kaisa dollar mari ($) jora rwmani bai ah lombor bwtang bai thong swithaih kotagera yasikaihjakma bwkhak.

english: For example, the absolute reference for the cell A1 would be $A$1.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, ah kubui yasikaihjakma ah kotagera A1 bagwi $A$1 wngwi mano.

english: You can also use absolute references to reference a range of cells.
kokborok: Nwng kubui yasikaijakmarok kaisa bwtrang kotagerarok yasikaijakma bwkhak bo phwnangjak mano.

english: To do this, add a dollar sign to the row number and column letter of each cell in the range.
kokborok: Omo khaina thangkhe, kaisa dollar mari jora rwma bwkhak ah lombor bwtang tei thong swithaih kotagera thwgwi ah bwtrang bising wngo.

english: For example, the absolute reference for the range A1:B1 would be $A$1:$B$1.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, ah kubui yasikaihjakma ah bwtrang A1:B1 bagwi $A$1:$B$1 wngmano.

english: Absolute references are a powerful tool that can be used to make your formulas more flexible and easier to use.
kokborok: Kubui yasikaihjakmarok wngkha kaisa phangwnang kol je nini karilamrok swnamna bwkhak phwnangjak wngmano teibo khongkwlai tei kwlaikuk phwnangma bwkhak.

english: By understanding how to use absolute references, you can create formulas that will work even when you copy or move them to different locations.
kokborok: Bahaikhe kubui yasikaihmarok phwnangma bwkhak buchimani bai, nwng karimarok swnam mano je ahaino samung khainai jephuru nwng kosol eba bohrokno juda juda tongma thairokni bwkhak norwi twlango.

english: Here are some additional tips for using absolute references:
kokborok: Oro wngkha baska dagiphang rwmarok kubui yasikaihmarok phwnangmani bagwi:

english: * Use absolute references for cells that contain data that you do not want to change.
kokborok: * Kotagerani bagwi kubui yasikaihmarok phwnangdi je sijakrwnai tongma je nwng swlaina muchungjakya.

english: * Use relative references for cells that contain data that you do want to change.
kokborok: * Kotagerani bagwi halok gnang yasikaihmarok phwnangma je sijakmari tongma je nnwg swlaina muchungjakya.

english: * Be careful when using mixed references, which are references that contain both absolute and relative references.
kokborok: * Hush wngdi jephuru yasikaihmarok dalukjak phwnangmani dalujago, omo kubui kainwi tei halok gnang yasikaihmarok tongma wngo.

english: * Use the F4 key to toggle between absolute, relative, and mixed references.
kokborok: * Ah F4 berepkhong phwangdi kubui, halol gnang, tei dalukjak yaskikaihmarok kwcharo toggle khaima bwkhak.

english: By following these tips, you can use absolute references to create powerful and flexible formulas that will make your work in Excel easier and more efficient.
kokborok: Oh rwmarok rwktharmani bai, nwng kubui yasikaihmarok phwnang mano phangwnang tei khongkwlai karilamrok bwkhak swnamo je nini samung Excel bising kwlaikuk tei teibo chukma swnammanai.

english: Esteban was a concerned father.
kokborok: Esteban wngkha kaisa wanajak bupha.

english: His daughter, Marcela, was listening to music that he didn't approve of.
kokborok: Bini bwsajwk, Marcela, rwchapmung khwnai tongmani je bo khasoiya wngmani.

english: The lyrics were explicit and violent, and he didn't want his daughter exposed to that kind of material.
kokborok: Ah kokthuprok wngkha sraisrai tei kikhri, tei bo bini bwsajwk no je omo hai manwi-khwnwi bai phunukna muchungjakya.

english: He tried to talk to her about it, but she just shrugged him off.
kokborok: Abo omo ni bagwi kok sana chaitokkha, phiya bo haino bono bangra norwi rwkha.

english: He didn't know what else to do.
kokborok: Bo saimanliya tei tamo khaisinai.

english: One day, Esteban was listening to the radio when he heard a song that he thought Marcela would like.
kokborok: Salsa, Esteban auaikhok khwnai tongphuru aphuru bo kaisa rwchapmung khwnakha je bo wansukha Marcela chajakganw hwnwi.

english: It was a catchy tune with a positive message.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa rommanai khorang kaisa kubui koktun bai.

english: He decided to burn a copy of the song and give it to her.
kokborok: Bo chongwi nakha kaisa rwchapmungno copy burn khaima bwkhak bono rina hinkha.

english: When she got home from school, he gave her the CD and told her to listen to it.
kokborok: Jephuru bo rwngnokni simi nogo sokphaikha, bo bono CD rwkha te bono sakha khwnadi omono hwnwi.

english: Marcela was surprised by the gift, but she was also intrigued.
kokborok: Marcela yakpai manma bai belai wanamasingsa wngkha, phiya bo khwithonjak wngkha.

english: She put the CD in her stereo and listened to the song.
kokborok: Bo CD no bini stereo thepakha tei rwchapmungno khwnakha.

english: She liked it so much that she listened to it over and over again.
kokborok: Bo omo aswkhe chajakha je bo omono bar-bar khwnakha.

english: The next day, Esteban asked Marcela what she thought of the song.
kokborok: Ah teini salo, Esteban Marcelano swngkha bo ah rwchapmungni bagwi tamo wansukkha.

english: She told him that she loved it and that it had made her think about things in a new way.
kokborok: Bo bono sakha je bo omono hamjakha hwnwi tei je omo bono kaisa kwtal lama bisingtwi wansukna rwkha manwirokni bagwi.

english: Esteban was thrilled.
kokborok: Esteban saktwikarjak wngkha.

english: He knew that he had made a difference in his daughter's life.
kokborok: Bo saimano je bo kaisa pherlaima swnamkha bini bwsajwkni langmao.

english: From that day on, Marcela listened to more positive music.
kokborok: Je ah salni simi, Marcela teibo kubui rwchapmung khwnankha.

english: Assertiveness is the ability to stand up for your rights in a confident and direct way, without being aggressive or passive-aggressive.
kokborok: Sakhlaimani wngkha ah khlaimanma bwkhak bachama nini manthairok bagwi kaisa khakrak tei kepleng lama, choprobnai eba lem-choprobnai wngjak karwi.

english: When you are assertive, you are able to express your thoughts and feelings clearly and respectfully, and you are able to set boundaries and say no when necessary.
kokborok: Jephhuru nwng sakhlaima wngkha, nwng nini wansukmungrok tei sraisrai khai wasukmani tei borom rwmani swbaikhrubwi sama bwkhak khapima wngo, tei nwng arirok kaihma bwkhak khapima wngkha tei jephuru nangphuru ehe hwnwi sadi.

english: Aggressiveness, on the other hand, is the tendency to be forceful or hostile in a way that is intended to intimidate or hurt others.
kokborok: Choprobnairok, tei kubun digi, ah wngmuchung wngkha phankhlaima bwkhak eba ualaijak kaisa lama bising je sikrima phunukma bwkhak khatharjak wngkha eba kubunrokno dukhu manrwma.

english: When you are aggressive, you may try to control others through intimidation or threats, and you may be quick to anger and lash out.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng choprobnai wngkham nwng kubunrokno makthakmung bwkhak chaitok mano sikrimmung phunukma twih eba sikrimarok, tei nwng daktino jolima tei thamsi karima bwkhak wngwi mano.

english: Arrogant behavior is characterized by a feeling of superiority and a lack of respect for others.
kokborok: Saktormung tomung wngkha kaisa kahamkukma wansukmani bai gwrwngjakma wngkha tei kubunrokni bagwi borom rwma kwrwi.

english: When you are arrogant, you may brag about your accomplishments, put others down, or act entitled.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng saktormung wngo, nwng nini khlaimanmarok bagwi nwng baolaima mano, kubunrokno tola tonima, eba samung mathai rwjak.

english: It is important to be able to distinguish between assertiveness, aggressiveness, and arrogance, as each behavior has its own set of consequences.
kokborok: Omoni kwcharo pherrwma bwkhak chujak wngma bwhak nangkukma wngkha Sakhlaimani, choprobmani, tei saktormung, omo sakni kaihma thaihmungrok tongo tongmung thwgwi.

english: Assertiveness is generally seen as a positive trait, while aggressiveness and arrogance are often seen as negative traits.
kokborok: Sakhlaimani wngkha jottonokhobwi kaisa kubui tongdal haikhe nukha, jephuru Sakhlaimani tei saktormung uramauram iko chaya tongdalrok nukha.

english: Assertive people are more likely to be successful in their personal and professional lives, as they are able to stand up for themselves and get their needs met.
kokborok: Sakhlaima borok wngkha teibo haino khlaimanmung wngma bwkhak bohrokni sakbaithang bising tei tangsamung langmarok, bohrok bohroksaksakni bagwi bachama bwkhak chukjak wngkha tei bohrokni nangmarok malaima mankha.

english: Aggressive people, on the other hand, are more likely to alienate others and have difficulty forming healthy relationships.
kokborok: Choprobnai borok, tei kubun yago, wngkha teibo ahaino kubunrokbai khakjakma tei sakdukma runghalokrok swnammani tongma bwkhak.

english: And arrogant people are often seen as conceited and unlikable.
kokborok: Tei saktormung borok ahaino bolaijk tei chajakya nukjago uramuram tongo.

english: If you are struggling to be assertive, there are a few things you can do to improve your assertiveness skills.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng kaphramani wngkha sakhlaima bwkhak, aro wngkha kaisa kisa manwirok nwng khlaimano nini sakhlaimani yaksrairok charwma bwkhak.

english: First, it is important to be aware of your own feelings and needs.
kokborok: Puila, omo nini sakni wansukamrok tei nangmarok sijak wngma bwkhak nangkukma wngkha.

english: Once you know what you want, you can start to express yourself more clearly and directly.
kokborok: Waisa nwng saimankha nwng tamo muchungma nwng ninisaksakno swbaikhrubwi sama bwkhak chengwi mano teibo sraisrai tei kepleng khai.

english: It is also important to be respectful of others, even when you are disagreeing with them.
kokborok: Omo bo kubunrokno borom rwma bwkhak nangkukma wngkha, ahaino jephuru nwng bohrok bai gosiya wngkha.

english: And finally, it is important to be confident in yourself and your abilities.
kokborok: Tei paithago, omo ninisaksak sakno poitokhaima tei nini khlaimanmarok wngma bwkhak nangkukma wngkha.

english: When you believe in yourself, others are more likely to believe in you too.

kokborok: Kwbangma motharok aoli dikholo buphang kainani samung khai tongo, nokbar dal khai hamrinani tei kwkhwrang haari swnamo.

english: Trees are also important for gardens.
kokborok: Buphang rok bari ni bagwi nangkukma manwi.

english: They can provide shade, shelter, and food for plants and animals.
kokborok: Borok saklom, lenglama, tei buphang-uaphang tei malmatarokni bagwi chamung swnamtonimano.

english: They can also help to improve the soil and water quality.
kokborok: Bohrok hasing tei twini dal no charwi chubachu khaimano.

english: If you are planning to plant a garden, it is important to consider the type of trees that you will plant.
kokborok: Nwng bari kainani hwnwi muchung tongkhe, nwng uansugwi mohai nangkukmani buphangno sapokthai je nwng nai kaimannai.

english: Some trees are better suited for gardens than others.
kokborok: Baksa buphang rok kubuni slai bari khainani kerong kaham wngo.

english: If you are interested in planting trees, there are many resources available to help you.
kokborok: Nwng khaswrangwi buphang kainani wngkha, aro kwbangma tanglam manthogo je nono chubai mano.

english: You can find information on tree planting from your local government, gardening centers, and environmental organizations.
kokborok: Nwng buphang kainani kokthumwi mano nini oroni haphang thani, barini kwcharo, tei tongkhorni mothani thani.

english: You can also find helpful information online.
kokborok: Nwng online twi bo kokthumni chubachu naimano.

english: Tree planting is a great way to make a difference in your community and the world.
kokborok: Nini hoda tei hayung ni bagwi nwng pherlai buphang kainani kotokuar lama swmandi.

english: By planting trees, you can help to improve the environment and create a more sustainable future.
kokborok: Buphang kaimabai, nwng tongkhor ni bagwi charwi mano tei thinango teibo rujuwi swnamano.

english: Dear [Name], I hope this letter finds you well.
kokborok: Khapangni [mung], ani khajamung oh kokduk nono kahamkhai khai naituk mano.

english: I'm writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been going well this year.
kokborok: Ang nono chini nukhung habani simi swimani, boro ah thummung oh bisio kaham thangwi tongo.

english: We're expecting a bumper crop of sugarcane, which is used to make rum.
kokborok: Chwng khakamani kuruk kaisa kupulung bwthaih, boro rum swnamma bwkhak phwnangkha.

english: Rum is a distilled spirit made from sugarcane molasses or sugarcane juice.
kokborok: Rum wngkha kaisa rairai khwlaijakma arak kuruk kwtwi eba kuruk bwtwi simi swnamma.

english: It's typically aged in wooden barrels, which gives it its characteristic flavor.
kokborok: Omo hainohai buphang uahsongrok bising omor wngkha, bomo omono gwrwngma thokmung rwkha.

english: Rum can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or mixed in cocktails.
kokborok: Rum sapsutra tongthokma wngmano, on the rocks, eba cocktails bising sapuljak.

english: There are many different types of rum, each with its own unique flavor profile.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma juda juda rum sapokthaihrok tongo, omoni sakni manthokya thokmung profile bai thwgwi.

english: Some of the most popular types of rum include light rum, dark rum, and spiced rum.
kokborok: Baksa ah jottoni slai luku hamjakjak rum sapokthaihrok kwchwng rum khobwi, mwnak rum, tei muithok rum.

english: Light rum is typically made from molasses and has a light, sweet flavor.
kokborok: Kwchwng rum wngkha hainohai rairai khwlaijakma simi swnamma tei kaisa kwchwng, kwtwi thokmung tongo.

english: Dark rum is made from sugarcane juice and has a richer, more complex flavor.
kokborok: Kosom rum kuruk bwtwini simi swnammo tei kaisa gnangma, teibo kutuk thokmung tongo.

english: Spiced rum is made with added spices, such as cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
kokborok: Muithok rum muithokrok thepakha, ahaino bukur kwtwi, thaihmotom, tei long bai swnamma wngkha.

english: Rum is a versatile spirit that can be used in a variety of cocktails.
kokborok: Rum wngkha kaisa kwbang sini spirit je kaisa dalbidal cokctails bising phwnangjak mano.

english: Some classic rum cocktails include the daiquiri, the mojito, and the pina colada.
kokborok: Baksa kwcham rum cocktails ah daiquiri, mojito, tei pina colada khobwi.

english: Rum can also be used in more creative cocktails, such as the Hemingway Daiquiri or the Painkiller.
kokborok: Rum teibo cocktails swnamjak bsing phwnangjak mano, ahaino ah Heminway Daiquiri eba ah Painkiller.

english: "Complete your Amazon shopping experience with our new and improved ad service!" the ad read.
kokborok: Nwng amazon o paimani bobohai wngkha chini kwtal ad sebani bisingtwi.

kokborok: Chini sebani bisingwi nwng mungsa wanana kwrwi chini mwchangjak deal manphinai.

kokborok: Achukthayo achugwi simi tongsidi tei leladi.

kokborok: Chini seba completely magwnang tei obo kaisa chengwi mannai.
