kokborok: Sign up khwlaiwi account simi swnamdi tei cart khwlainani chengdi.

english: When you're ready to check out, our service will automatically find the best deals for you and apply them to your order.
kokborok: Nwng jephuru jotto naikolwi naibaikha hamjakmani manwirokno chini aphuru saksakno nini bagwi jottoni deal kaham swnamwi rwnai tei order khwlai mannai.

english: So what are you waiting for?
kokborok: Hwnkhe tei twmano naisingwi tong?

english: Sign up for our service today and start saving money on all your Amazon purchases!"
kokborok: Tinini bisingono sign up khwlaidi tei rang khatinani naidi amazon o jotto manwi khwnwi paithani.

english: As the customer clicked on the ad, they were whisked away to a new website.
kokborok: Painairok jephuru ads o click khwlai togwi rwo aphuru kwtal website o twlang thango.

english: The website was full of ads for all sorts of products, all of which were supposedly on sale.
kokborok: Ah website o tongnai ads bai kupulung dal bidal manwi phunukjak wngnai phalnani bagwi.

english: The customer was tempted to buy a few things, but they hesitated.
kokborok: Painairok kisa kisa manwirokno painale muchungjao phiya bohrok yak korojago.

english: They had heard stories about people getting scammed by online ads, and they didn't want to be one of them.
kokborok: Bohrok khwnamakhe scam eba thokairok wngo hwnwi ads ni bisingtwi manwi paimano, tei bohrok abohai thokaimungo kwlaina muchungjakya.

english: The customer decided to do some research on the company that was running the ad.
kokborok: Painairok tabuk naituknayo tei swrwngnayo company soisoide ads phunukmani kaham da hamya jachai khwlai nayo.

english: They found a few negative reviews, but most of the reviews were positive.
kokborok: Bohrok mankha je aro chaya kok kiphirokmung phiyaba kwbangkukno chama kokno kok phirokmung rwkha.

english: The title of the story is "The Basketball Game".
kokborok: Ah kothomani swimung wngkha "ah langabol thwngmung".

english: It is about a group of students who are playing basketball in the school gym.
kokborok: Obo rwngnokni gym'o basketball thwngwi tongnai rwngswrwngnairokni kaisa bodol no twywi.

english: They are all having a lot of fun, and they are working together as a team.
kokborok: Bohrok jotto tongthogwi tongmani, tei bohrok kaisa thwngdol haikhe thansa samung khaimani tongo.

english: One of the students, named Ayanda, is new to the school, and she is not very good at basketball.
kokborok: Khoroksa swrwngnai, mung Ayanda, wngkha ah rwngnogo kwtal, tei bo basketball bwkhak belai kaham wngya.

english: But she is trying her best, and her teammates are encouraging her.
kokborok: Phiya bo bini kahamkuk chaitokmani wngkha, tei bini thwngdol logisongrok bono khatungrimung wngkha.

english: One of the students, named Christian, is the best player on the team.
kokborok: Khoroksa swrwngnai, mung Christian, wngkha kahamkuk thwngkwrwng ah thwngdol sakao.

english: He is very talented, and he is always willing to help his teammates.
kokborok: Bo belai suargnang wngkha, tei bo homnino bini thwngdol longisongrokno chubana bwkhak muchungjago.

english: He is a good leader, and he sets a good example for the other students.
kokborok: Bo wngkha khoroksa kaham ojama, tei bo kaisa kaham phunukmari thepakha ah kubun swrwngnairokni bagwi.

english: The students are all playing hard, and they are all very excited.
kokborok: Ah swrwngnai wngkha jotto kwrak thwngmani, tei bohrok jotto belai tongthokjak wngkha.

english: They are all hoping to win the game.
kokborok: Bohrok jotto ah thwngmung kwplai wngna bwkhak khajamani wngkha.

english: The game is close, and it is going down to the wire.
kokborok: Ah thwngmung wngkha gana, tei abo ah duk bwkhak thangwi tongo.

english: In the final seconds, Christian makes a basket to win the game for his team.
kokborok: Ah paithak nwiremrokni bising, Christian kaisa langa swnammarok bwkhak ah thwngmung jitina bini thwngdolni bagwi.

english: The students all celebrate, and they are all very happy.
kokborok: Ah swrwngnairok jotto terkhlaikha, tei bohrok jotto belai tongthokjak wngkha.

english: They have all learned a lot about teamwork and sportsmanship, and they have all had a lot of fun.
kokborok: Bohrok jotto tangthansa tei rungthwngkwrwng bagwi kwbang jotto swrwngkha.

english: The hotel was busy, as it always was during the summer months.
kokborok: Ah lenanok wngkha paihlaya, aswkno amo homnino talbung talrogo wngjora wngkha.

english: People came from all over the world to stay in its luxurious rooms and enjoy its many amenities.
kokborok: Omoni phutani nokrok bising tei omoni kwbangma suksuvidharok tongthok bising jotto hayung sakani simi borok tongna bwkhak phaiyo.

english: One of the guests was a young woman named Sarah.
kokborok: Khoroksa ah naruwairok wngkha kaisa bwrwima sikli Sarah mungwi.

english: She had been struggling with mental health issues for some time, and she had come to the hotel in hopes of finding peace and quiet.
kokborok: Bo kisa jora romwi khapang sakdukma wngma bai bo khapharmani wngwi tongkha, tei bo ah lenanok khajamungrok bising bwkhak phaikha kwchangtotok naituknani tei siring mannani.

english: Sarah's room was on the top floor of the hotel, and it had a beautiful view of the city.
kokborok: Sarah's tongar wngkha ah lenanok ah kuchuk noksing ha sakao, tei omo kaisa naithok nukthok ah doyung tongo.

english: She spent her days sitting by the window, watching the people go by.
kokborok: Bo bini salrok tailam gana achugwi katiwo, ah borok thangmano naimani bai.

english: She found it calming to watch the hustle and bustle of the city below, and it helped her to forget her troubles.
kokborok: Bo amo dagachopa tei dosidopra ah doyung tola naima bwkhak kwchangtotokmani wngjago, tei amo bono bini suprunarok pokna bwkhak bono chubakha.

english: One day, Sarah was sitting by the window when she saw a man sitting on a bench in the park below.
kokborok: Salsa, Sarah ah tailam gana achugwi tongmani jephuru bo khoroksa chwla no kaisa achukthai sakao ah aolikhumbari hachero achukmani nukha.

english: He was crying, and he looked very sad.
kokborok: Bo kabwi tongo, tei bo belai mokjak khe nukjak kha.

english: Sarah felt sorry for him, and she decided to go down and talk to him.
kokborok: Sarah bini bagwi khanang wasukha, tei bo chongkha je tola thangwi tei bobai koksana hwnwi.

english: When Sarah got to the park, the man was still sitting on the bench.
kokborok: Jephuru Sarah ah aolikhumbari thangkha, ah chwla tabukbo ah achukthayo achugwi tongkhu.

english: He looked up at her and smiled.
kokborok: Bo bono saka naisikha tei mwnwikha.

english: "Hello," he said. "My name is Tom."
kokborok: "Khulumkha, " bo sakha. "ang mung wngkha Tom."

english: Sarah introduced herself, and they sat down together.
kokborok: Sarah sakno sinimung rwkha, tei bohrok thansa khe achuklaikha.

english: Action speaks louder than words, and this is especially true in the world of adventure.
kokborok: Samung chirikgwi koksao kokthairokni slai, tei omo kahamkhai kubui hayungni saktwikarjak karwi.

english: When you're out in the wilderness, you need to be able to rely on your own skills and abilities to get you through.
kokborok: Nwng jephuru hachingma ni phatar phuru, nwng nini sak yaksrai rogo khajakma bwkhak khai manna nango tei nwng pharimung twih manna bwkhak thango.

english: Words won't help you if you're lost, or if you're injured.
kokborok: Nwng jodi kwmai thangkhe kothairok nono chubai mangwlak, eba jodi nwng sakderakhe.

english: Only action will.
kokborok: Samung simi naimano.

english: I've seen this principle in action time and time again.
kokborok: Ang oh samung jora tei jora teiwaisa kahamkhai nukha.

english: On one of my early adventures, I was hiking with a group of friends when we got lost.
kokborok: Ani swkangni kaisa saktwikarjakrok, ang ani bayaprok bodol bai hiking phuru aphuru chwng kwmakha.

english: We wandered around for hours, trying to find our way back to the trail.
kokborok: Chwng damrwi lamkorowui yaksiyagra wng tonglaikha, chin lama phirogwi trail bwkhak naitukna chaitoklaikha.

english: But no matter what we said or did, we just couldn't seem to find our way.
kokborok: Phiya chwng tamo sakha eba khaikha abo manwi wngya, chwng haino chini lama naituk kari manya wng tongkha.

english: Finally, one of our friends decided to take action.
kokborok: Paithago, chini khoroksa bayapsong kokchapkha samung nana bwkhak.

english: He started walking in a particular direction, and we all followed him.
kokborok: Bo kaisa chongjak digi himani chengkha, tei chwng jotto bono rwtharkha.

english: After a few hours, we came to a road, and we were able to find our way back to the trailhead.
kokborok: Kisa damrwi ni olo, chwng lama wo sokphaikha, tei chwng chini lama trailhead bwkhak naituk manphikha.

english: If we had just sat around and talked about what to do, we would never have found our way back.
kokborok: Chwng haino jodi yaksiyagra achugwi tongkhe tei tamo khaina hwnwi koksalai tongkhe, chwng jesakhe phano chini lama phirogwi naitugwi mangwlak khamu.

english: But because one of us took action, we were able to get out of a dangerous situation.
kokborok: Phiya tamni hinmale chini bising khoroksa samung nakha, chwng kirimasinga jora hamya ni ongkhorwi mangwlakhamu.

english: This is just one example of how action can save the day.
kokborok: Omo haino kaisa phunukmari bahaikhe samung sal bachiriwui man.

english: Imagine being able to enjoy your life without the constant fear of these debilitating conditions.
kokborok: Chongwi nadi nini langmano nwng belai tonthogwi tongwi mano bebak bemarokni yakni katewi.

english: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are a common problem, especially for women.
kokborok: Swtwilam ni bemarno bebak borokno manjago, abono manjakuknairok wngkha bwrwirog.

english: They can cause a variety of symptoms, including pain, burning, and frequent urination.
kokborok: O bemar sago dalbidal bemar manjak rwo, samani, khamma hairok wngo, tei kwrwngwi ma swtwi o.

english: In some cases, UTIs can lead to more serious problems, such as kidney infections.
kokborok: Waisa wuisu khe, swtwi lama ni bemar teibo jwngjal kotor wngwi mano, abo swtwikhok no hamya khwlayo.

english: Bladder stones are another common problem.
kokborok: Bladder o holong wngmani abo bo tei kaisa borokrok majakuk mani jwngjal.

english: They can cause pain, difficulty urinating, and blood in the urine.
kokborok: Abohrok nono bwsak sarwo, nwng swtwi phuru, tei swtwi o thwi bo wngwi mano.

english: In some cases, bladder stones can block the urethra, which can lead to a life-threatening emergency.
kokborok: Jora juru o khe, bladder o holong wngmani abo swtwi lama no kasowi mano, abo hai wngmani langmano derarw wi mano.

english: Kidney diseases are a serious problem that can affect people of all ages.
kokborok: Swtwikhok ni bemar wngkha belai jwngjal kotor abo bebak borokrok no manjago.

english: They can cause a variety of symptoms, including fatigue, nausea, and vomiting.
kokborok: Abohrok dalbidal ni bisingtwi sago hamya khwlayo, lengrw o, sak tongthokya khwlayo, tei ma kwba o.

english: In some cases, kidney diseases can lead to kidney failure, which is a fatal condition.
kokborok: Jora juru o khe, kidney ni bemar swtwikhok no hamya khwlai wi mano, abo bwtharwi bo mano.

english: If you are suffering from any of these conditions, there is help available.
kokborok: Tumung nwng obo hairokni jesa kaisa bemarok bai manjagwi tong khe, chubamung manthogo.

english: Talk to your doctor about your symptoms and treatment options.
kokborok: Nini doctor bai kok salai di nini sak hamya no twywi tei bahai khe hamwi mannai abotwi lamarok no twywi.

english: There are a variety of treatments available for UTIs, bladder stones, and kidney diseases.
kokborok: Swtwi lam dera mano twywi swnamjaknai kwbangma lama tongo, bladder o holong wngmarog, tei swtwikhok ni bema wngmarok bo tongo.

english: With proper treatment, you can get relief from your symptoms and prevent further complications.
kokborok: Kaham khe naijak khe, sak hamya wngmarok hamwi mannai tei teibo kwbang derana thangwi tongmanirogno kasowi mannai.

english: Don't let these conditions control your life.
kokborok: Nini langmano omo hai jora hamayarok bai mechengna takhwlaidi.

english: Talk to your doctor today and start on the path to recovery.
kokborok: Nini doctor bai kok salai di tei hamnani lamano romna chengsidi.

english: The elephants can roam freely without fear of being hunted, and the farmers can be sure that their crops will not be destroyed.
kokborok: Mayungrok sikar khaijakna kiriya karwi phiyokjak khe beraimano, tei chuainairok wngkubui mano je bohrokni bwthai-maithai rok swbaimanya wngtwi.

english: Radio collars are small devices that are attached to an animal's neck.
kokborok: Auaikhok collar rok wngkha chikonsa devices je malmatani gwdwna thepajak.

english: They emit a signal that can be tracked by a receiver.
kokborok: Bohrok je khitarsama thar yaprimari yachaknai rokbai mano.

english: This allows scientists to track the animal's movements over time.
kokborok: Omo soisikwrwng rokno jora rwgwi malmatarokni lorimano twi naikol mano.

english: In the case of elephants, this information can be used to create maps of their home ranges and to identify areas where they are most likely to come into conflict with humans.
kokborok: Mayungrokni tanghalok hwnkhe, oh sakhlaimung bai bohrokni nok bwtrango maps swnamwi phwnangwi mano tei babai amchaino siniwui narakdi jephuru borok munuishu bai nanglainani majaro bohrok jottoni swlai phaina hwnwi wansugwinao.

english: Farmers can use this information to take steps to protect their crops from elephants.
kokborok: Chuainairok oh sakhlaimungno phwnangwi mano yapri sehwui bohrokni bwthaih-maithai rokno mayungrokni simi katirwma babai.

english: They can build fences, plant thorny bushes, or use other methods to deter elephants from entering their fields.
kokborok: Bohrok bera dumwi mano, bushu jabra kaimano, eba kubuni raida phwnangwi mayungrokno kasuma simi bohrok kheto habnani twi.

english: By working together, scientists and farmers can help to keep both elephants and humans safe.
kokborok: Thansakhe samung khailai, Soisikwrwng tei chuainai chubai mano babai mayungrok tei borok munuishu khoroknwi kati tonimano.

english: Here is an example of how radio collars have been used to help elephants and farmers.
kokborok: iko kaisa phunukmari bahaikhe auaikhok collars chauinai tei mayungrokno chubama'o phwnangjago.

english: In Kenya, scientists from the University of Cambridge have been working with local communities to track the movements of elephants.
kokborok: Kenya o, soisikwrwng University of Cambridge oroni hodarokbai samung khai phayo babai mayungrokni yapri semano twi.

english: This information has been used to create maps of the elephants' home ranges.
kokborok: Oh sakhlaimung maps swnama'o phwnangjago mayungrokni' nok bwtrango.

english: The maps have been shared with farmers, who have used them to build fences around their fields.
kokborok: Maps chuainai rokbai bakjago, jara bohrokni kheto o bera guriwi dumwi tisaui bohrokno phwnangwi khaimani.

english: This has helped to reduce the number of conflicts between elephants and humans.
kokborok: Omo mayung tei borok munuishu bising nanglaimani lombor khairina chubakha.

english: Radio collars are a valuable tool for studying elephants and for helping to reduce human-elephant conflict.
kokborok: Auaikhok collars wngkha morojak kol mayungno porina bagwi tei mayung-borok bai nanglaimano chubachukhai khaina bagwi.

english: They provide scientists with valuable information about elephant behavior, and they can help farmers to protect their crops.
kokborok: Bohrok soisikwrwng bago morjak sakhlaimung mayungni tongmung chamungno twi, tei bohrok chuairokno chubai mano bohrokni bwthai mwithai no katirina bagwi.

english: By working together, scientists and farmers can help to create a future where elephants and humans can live together in harmony.
kokborok: Thansa khe samung khwlai, soisikwrwng tei chuainai thinango twi chubama swnamano jethayo mayung tei borok rok thansa kwthai tongwimano.

english: She had always been a talented painter, but after her loss, she found that she was no longer interested in painting pretty landscapes or still lifes.
kokborok: Bo agini simino khoroksa suargnang lepanai, phiya bini kwmama olo, bo mankha je bo tabuk naithok hakung marirok eba sringsiring langmarok lepanani biisng ol manjakliya wngkha.

english: Instead, she began to create dark, brooding works of art that reflected her inner turmoil.
kokborok: Aboni slai, bo mwnak swnamna bwkhak chwngkha, rikmung samungrok wansukmani je bini bisingni tongthokya kiphilphima.

english: One of her most famous paintings, "The Death of My Son," is a stark and disturbing image of a young boy lying in a coffin.
kokborok: Kaisa bini jottoni slai mungkoto lepamanirok wngkha. "ani bwslani thwimung, " uangkha kaisa kuplung tei kebangmani mangili khoroksa sikal chwla phopkhok bising rokoma.

english: The boy's face is peaceful, but his body is twisted and contorted in pain.
kokborok: Aha chwlani mwkhang wngkha khajamungjak, phiya bini sak wngkha mothorjak tei samani bising khwrangjak.

english: The painting is full of symbolism, and it is clear that Mary is using her art to process her grief and anger.
kokborok: Ah lepamani wngkha mangthongni kuplung, tei omo wngkha kwchwng je Mary bini rikmung phwnangmani bini khanang tei jolima bwkhak tangsep unkha.

english: Mary's shift in artistic style was not without its critics.
kokborok: Rikmung tongdal bising Maryni shehma kokchirnairok karwi wngya.

english: Some people accused her of being exploitative and insensitive.
kokborok: Baksa borok bono kok silchakha shoshanjak wngjak tei bormanjakya.

english: Others said that her paintings were too depressing and that they should not be shown in public.
kokborok: Kubunrok sakha bini lepamanirok belai khakwbaimung tei je bohrokno lukuni bising phunukjakna tawngthwng.

english: However, Mary refused to back down.
kokborok: Haiphano, Mary yakarna bwkhak gosiya.

english: She believed that her art was important, and she wanted to share it with the world.
kokborok: Bo poitokhaikha je bini rikmung wngkha nangkukma, tei bo amono bakna muchungjago ah hayung bai.

english: Mary's work eventually found an audience, and she became one of the most respected artists of her time.
kokborok: Maryni samung paithago khiroksa nainai mankha, tei bo khoroksa jottoni slai borom rwjak rikkwrwng bini jorani wngkha.

english: Her paintings are now considered to be masterpieces, and they are still studied and admired by people all over the world.
kokborok: Bini lepamanirok tabuk hamkuk manwirok bwkhak wansukukma wngkha, tei bohrok tabukbo porijak tongo tei jotto ah hayung sakani borok bai lopjago.

english: Mary's story is a reminder that art can be a powerful tool for expression.
kokborok: Maryni kothoma wngkha kaisa muito narwkna je rikmung kaisa phangwnang manwi wngwi mano kokmwkhangni bagwi.

english: It can be used to process grief, anger, and other difficult emotions.
kokborok: Omo tansep khanang, jolima, tei kubun 3 khanangjakrok bwkhak phwnangjak bo mano.

english: It can also be used to communicate important messages about the human condition.
kokborok: Omo koktunrok nangkukma gwdallaima bwkhak phwnangjak bo mano ah borok tonghalok bagwi.

english: Mary's paintings are a testament to the power of art, and they continue to inspire people to this day.
kokborok: Maryni lepamanirok wngkha kaisa thwiswimung ah phan rikmung bwkhak, tei bohrok choyai tini bo borokno khasrangrwma bwkhak khayo.

kokborok: [Scene: Coffee phalnok. Kiching kwnwirog, Namrata bai Tudor, bohrok table o achoklai tongo, coffee nungtwtwi kok salayo.]

kokborok: Namrata: hwnkhe, ang khwnao Apple song bwskang tal kwtal phone karinai khapho hwnwi.

kokborok: Tudor: Kwbwi da? Belai chasukha!

english: I was on the fence about switching to the iPhone for a long time, but I finally took the plunge a few months ago, and I'm really glad I did.
kokborok: Ang iphone no nana bagwi kwdwkma uansokjak, phiya paithago talnwi taltham swkang chapwi naiman kha, tei ang belai chajaksok kha.

english: It's a great phone.
kokborok: Belai phone kaham.

english: If you don't like it, you can always switch back to your Android.
kokborok: Tumung nwng chajakya wngwi tong khe, nini Android o habwi nai phi mano.

kokborok: Namrata: Abo belai uansokmung kaham.

english: Punctuality is the quality of being on time or early.
kokborok: Koklenamung wngkha ah dal wngjak jora eba swkang sakao.

english: It is an important skill in both personal and professional life.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa nangkukma yaksrai kanwi sakbaithang tei tangsamung langmani bising.

english: Being punctual shows that you respect other people's time and that you are reliable.
kokborok: Koklena wngjak phunukmarok je nwng kubun borokrokni jorano borom rwma tei je nwng poitogwnang wngkha.

english: There are many benefits to being punctual.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmarirok tongo koklena wngjak bwkhak.

english: For example, you are less likely to miss appointments or important events.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, nwng haino kisa chongberamungrok koroma eba nangkukma wngmungrok bwkhak tongo.

english: You will also be more productive, as you will not have to rush to get to places.
kokborok: Nwng teibo duna bwthaihma wngnai, haino nwng thairogo bwkhak thangna bagwi dona nangwlak.

english: Additionally, being punctual can help you build a positive reputation at work.
kokborok: Jora rwmani, koklena wngjak nono kaisa kaham borom samungo tangma bai chubai mano.

english: If you are known for being punctual, your coworkers and clients will be more likely to trust and respect you.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng koklena wngjak bagwi sinijak tongo, nini logisamung khlainairok tei painai bohrokrok nono borom rwma tei poito bwkhak teibo haino wngmano.

english: There are a few things you can do to become more punctual.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kisa manwirok nwng khlaimano teibo koklena wngna bwkhak.

english: First, set realistic goals for yourself.
kokborok: Puila, ninisaksakni bagwi kubuijak sokthairok kaihma.

english: If you are not used to being on time, start by setting small goals, such as arriving 5 minutes early to appointments.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng jora saka wngjak bwkhak phwnangjakya wngkha, chikon sokthairok tangbwtang bai chengdi, ahaino chongberamungrok bwkhak 5 sotirok dakti sowgwimani.

english: Once you are able to consistently meet these goals, you can gradually increase the amount of time you allow yourself.
kokborok: Waisa nwng oh sokthairok malaina kwthajak bwkhak mankha, nwng remrem khai ah jora thikemung bangwi mano nwng saksakno gosima bai.

english: Another helpful tip is to plan ahead.
kokborok: Teikaisa chubamung buchuk wngkha swkang bereh chapma bwkhak.

english: This means leaving plenty of time to get ready and to travel to your destination.
kokborok: Oh komrarok jora kwbangma yakarmani bwkhak tiyar wngma tei nini sogwina thai bwkhak beraima.

english: It also means being prepared for unexpected delays, such as traffic or bad weather.
kokborok: Omo kokmarok bo wansukmaya lererwmarok karwi tiyar khalima wngjak, ahaino tahnglaiso eba hamya salbar.

english: Finally, it is important to be mindful of the time.
kokborok: Paithago, omo wngkha nangkukma ah jora wansukuplung wngna.

english: Balance is the ability to maintain equilibrium.
kokborok: Bakhara wngkha pharimung bwkhak kaham tonima equilibrium.

english: It is essential for all living things, as it allows them to stay upright and move without falling over.
kokborok: Omo jotto thangnai manwirokni bagwi nangnai, omo bohrokno gosimarok bwkhak kepeleng tongna tei sakao kwlaiya karwi lorimani.

english: Balance is also important for coordination and motor skills.
kokborok: Bakhara belai nangkukmani coordination tei lorirwnai kol yaksrairokni bagwi.

english: There are many ways to improve balance.
kokborok: Borok wngkha kwbangma lama bwkhak bakhara charwma.

english: One way is to exercise regularly.
kokborok: Kaisa lama hwnkhe salbrum-brum no sakswnamdi.

english: Exercise helps to strengthen the muscles and joints that are involved in balance, and it also helps to improve coordination.
kokborok: Sakswnam sakphanrokno tei bothor rokno rakrinani chubchu khayo je bakhara bai gwdaljak, tei coordination charwma bwkhak bo chubachu khayo.

english: Another way to improve balance is to practice yoga or tai chi.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lama bakhara charwma hnwkhe yoga eba taichi loi khlaimung.

english: These exercises focus on body awareness and coordination, and they can help to improve balance in a gentle and effective way.
kokborok: Aro sakswnamrok sago sijakmani tei coordination naisikma, tei bohrok bakhara charwma bising kaisa kwchang tei amjokthaini lama.

english: Balance is important for people of all ages.
kokborok: Bakhara belai nangkukmani jotto omorni borokni bagwi.

english: Children need good balance in order to learn to walk and run.
kokborok: Chwrairok kaham bakhara nango swrwngna tholmung bwkhak himani tei kharnani.

english: Adults need good balance to avoid falls, which can be a serious health risk.
kokborok: Siklarok kaham bakhara nango kwlainarok katima, obo kaisa sosol sakduk khapharmung wngwi mano.

english: The elderly are especially at risk for falls, and balance exercises can help to reduce their risk.
kokborok: Okrarok sago kwlaina bagwi kahamkhai khapharmung wngkha, tei bakhara sakswnamrok khapharmung khairithani chubaimano.

english: There are many benefits to having good balance.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmari kaham bakhara tongmani.

english: Improved balance can help to reduce the risk of falls, it can improve coordination and motor skills, and it can also help to prevent injuries.
kokborok: Chasajak bakhara kwlainani khapharmung khaina bwkhak chubaimano, omo charwma coordination tei lorinai kolyaksrairok, tei tektoni kasogra bwkhak bo chubaimano.

english: If you want to improve your balance, there are many exercises and activities that you can do.
kokborok: Nwng jodi nini bakhara no charwna nangkhe, aro kwbangma sakswnammungrok tei dalbidal rok je nwng khai mantwi wngo.

english: Talk to your doctor or a physical therapist to learn more about how to improve your balance.
kokborok: Nini saknainai eba sakni kok haya nainai bwkhak teibo swrwngwi bahai khe nini bakhara no charwmanai.

english: It is a time to spend with loved ones, give thanks for the year that has passed, and look forward to the year ahead.
kokborok: Omo hamajakma borokrok bai kaisa jora larirwna bwkhak, je bisi laithangma bagwi hambairok rwma, tei bwskango phainai bisi bwkhak bwskang naisikma.

english: For some, December can also be a time of stress and anxiety.
kokborok: Baksani bagwi, talhing kaisa mothokma jora tei kachuk-buchhuk bo wngwi mano.

english: With the hustle and bustle of the holiday season, it can be easy to feel overwhelmed.
kokborok: Ah lelanasal mol bai dagachopa tei dosidopra wngma bai, omo 1 khamunsukma bwkhak wansukmung wngmano.

english: But it is important to remember that December is a time for joy and peace.
kokborok: Phiya omo muito narakwna bwkhak nangkukma wngkha je talhing wngkha kaisa jora tongthok tei kwchangtoktokni bagwi.

english: There are many ways to enjoy the month, even if you are busy or on vacation.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kwbangma lamarok tongo ah tal tongthokma bwkhak, tumungno nwng paihlaiya eba lelanasalo.

english: One way to enjoy December is to spend time with loved ones.
kokborok: Kaisa lama talhing tongthokma bwkhak kaisa lama wngkha hamajakma borokrok bai jora lairwma bwkhak.

english: Whether you are gathering for a big holiday meal or simply taking a walk around the block with your family, spending time with loved ones is a great way to relax and de-stress.
kokborok: Jebasa nwng kaisa kotor lelasal chahmung bagwi kuthumlaimani wng tongo eba ahaino nini nukghungni borok bai ah blockni yaksiyagra himwi namani, hamjakma borokrok bai jora lairwmani wngkha kaisa kotor lama mothokma tei lengrwma bwkhak.

english: It is also a good opportunity to reflect on the year that has passed and to look forward to the year ahead.
kokborok: Omo bo kaisa kaham sep wngkha ah bisi sakao kiphilphima bwkhak je laithangkha tei ah bisi bwskango bwskang naisikma bwkhak.

english: Another way to enjoy December is to give back to your community.
kokborok: Teikaisa lama Talhing tongthokma bwkhak wngkha nini hodani bwkhak phirok rwmani.

english: There are many ways to do this, such as volunteering at a local soup kitchen or donating to a charity.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma lamarok tongo omo khainani, ahaino kaisa oroni muibwtwi gantinok eba kaisa hamari samung bwkhak yakchubamani bai santuamani.

english: Giving back is a great way to make a difference in the world and to feel good about yourself.
kokborok: Phirok rwmani wngkha kaisa kotor lama ah hayung pherlaimungni bising swnamma bwkhak tei ninisaksakni bagwi kaham wansukmung.

english: If you are feeling overwhelmed by the hustle and bustle of the holiday season, it is important to take some time for yourself.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng ah lelanasal molo dagachopa tei dosidopra bai khamunsukma wansukmani wngkha, ninisaksakni bagwi kisasa jora nama bwkhak nangkukma wngkha.

english: This could mean taking a warm bath, reading a book, or simply spending some time in nature.
kokborok: Omo kaisa kutung tukuma, kaisa bijap porimani, eba ahaino habarni bising kisasa jora lairwmani wngwi mano.

english: Taking some time for yourself will help you to relax and de-stress.
kokborok: Ninisaksakni bagwi kisasa jora namani nono mokthokma tei lengrwma bwkhak chubai mano.

english: December is a month of joy and peace.
kokborok: Talhing tongthokmung tei kwchangtotok tal wngkha.

english: By spending time with loved ones, giving back to your community, and taking some time for yourself, you can make the most of this special time of year.
kokborok: Hamjakma borokrok bai jora lairwmani ganao, nini hoda no phirok rwmani, tei nini saksakni bagwi kisasa jora namani, nwng ah jottoni slai oh bisini jora mahmlai swnam mano.

english: Democracy and dictatorship are two very different forms of government.
kokborok: Luku haphang bai Baithangni haphang a kainwi haphangrok pherlayo.

english: In a democracy, the people have the power to choose their leaders and make decisions about how the country is run.
kokborok: Luku haphango khe, lukurok bohrokni twiphangno saiwi nanani phan tongo tei bohrok hakotor no bahai khe twidulnani abotwirok bo sa'ui mano.

english: In a dictatorship, one person or a small group of people has all the power and makes all the decisions.
kokborok: Baithangni haphango khe, khoroksa eba kaisa bwsate bodol simi se bebakni phan tongo tei bebak chap thanibo bohrokno chapo.

english: There are many advantages to democracy.
kokborok: Luku haphang kwbangma kaham tongo.

english: One advantage is that it allows for more freedom and expression.
kokborok: Kaisa kaham hwnkhe aro teisa yoksamung tongo tei sakni muchungma kokrok sa'ui mano.

english: People in democracies can vote for their leaders, speak out against the government, and start their own businesses.
kokborok: Lukurok lukuhaphango khe bohrokni twidulnaino saiwi nao, haphangni thani chao chaya kok tisa mano, tei bohrokni muchung mani samung khwlaiwi mano.

english: Another advantage of democracy is that it can lead to more economic prosperity.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lukuhaphangni kaham hwnkhe rangthongo teisa kuchuk ka'ui mano.

english: When people have a say in how their government is run, they are more likely to be invested in the country's success.
kokborok: Borokrok haphangni twidulmungno kok tisana cheng khe, bohrok teibo hakotorno naikol nani siwi phayo.

english: However, there are also some disadvantages to democracy.
kokborok: Phiyaba, lukuhaphango bo chaya le tongo.

english: One disadvantage is that it can be slow and inefficient.
kokborok: Kaisa chaya hwnkhe abo belai lerwi mano tei kulukya wngwi mano.

english: It can take a long time to make decisions in a democracy, and there is always the risk of gridlock.
kokborok: Jesa samungno khlaina thang thani lukuhaphango khe lerwi mano, tei aro kwbangma jwngjal phaiwi mano.

english: Another disadvantage of democracy is that it can be more vulnerable to corruption.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lukuhaphangni chaya hwnkhe aro manthaino kasowi chathogo.

english: When there are many different people involved in making decisions, it can be easier for special interests to buy influence.
kokborok: Kokchapthani borokrok bangkhe, borokni bwkhano paiwi bande na layo.

english: Dictatorships have some advantages over democracies.
kokborok: Baithangni haphang nibo kahamle tongo.

english: One advantage is that they can be more efficient.
kokborok: Kaisa kaham hwnkhe borok teisa kulugwi mano.

english: Decisions can be made quickly and without a lot of debate.
kokborok: Kokchapmanirok daktino chapwi mano tei kokbanglaiya wi.

english: The question of "who am I?" is one that has been asked by philosophers and thinkers for centuries.
kokborok: Ah swngmung "ang sabo?" wngkha kaisa je nukuansuksinai tei bisirarok bagwi wansuknairok swngjak phaimani.

english: There is no one answer that will satisfy everyone, as our sense of self is constantly evolving and changing.
kokborok: Aro wngkha mungsa kokphirokmung kwrwi je jottono no khasupung manya, ahaino chini sak sina samanwi wngkha kwnwjakya phijakma tei swlaijakmani.

english: However, there are some things that we can say about who we are.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro wngkha baksa manwirok bagwi je chwng saimanao chwng sabo wngkha.

english: We are all individuals, with our own unique thoughts, feelings, and experiences.
kokborok: Chwng jotto saichungrok wngkha, chini sakni manthokya wansukmungrok, wansukmani, tei saimanarok.

english: We are also part of a larger community, and our sense of self is shaped by our interactions with others.
kokborok: Chwng kaisa kotorma hoda bokcho wngkha, tei chini sak sinai simanwi wngkha chini swnamjak koksalaimaraok kubunrok bai.

english: We are all born into a particular time and place, and our experiences in this world help to define who we are.
kokborok: Chwng jotto kaisa chongjak jora tei thai bisingtwi achayo, tei chini saimanjakrok bising oh hayung chubama bwkhak chwng sabo wngkha hwnwi sukrupsama.

english: But what is the essential "I" that lies at the core of our being?
kokborok: Phiya ah nangnaai tamo wngkha "ang" je chini wngdok bwchwlwi kwlaijak?

english: Is it our thoughts?
kokborok: Omo chini wansukmarok da?

english: Our feelings?
kokborok: Chini wansukmani?

english: Our experiences?
kokborok: Chini saimanmarok?

english: Or is it something else entirely?
kokborok: Eba omo bebak mungsawk wngkha?

english: Perhaps the "I" is simply a collection of memories, experiences, and beliefs.
kokborok: Wngna ah "ang" khakeplengma kaisa mutiorok thummani, saimanmarok, tei poitorok.

english: Perhaps it is a narrative that we create about ourselves, in order to make sense of the world around us.
kokborok: Wngna omo wngkha kaisa sajakma je chwng chinisaksakrok bagwi swnamjak, chini yaksiyagra hayung sina simana'ui swnamna bagwi.

english: Or perhaps the "I" is something more ephemeral, something that cannot be pinned down or defined.
kokborok: Eba wngma ah "ang" wngkha mungsaswk teibo ephemeral, mungsawk je tola serupjak manya eba sukrupsakha.

english: Ultimately, the question of "who am I?" is a mystery that we may never fully understand.
kokborok: Phaithago "ang sabo?" hwnmani swngmungno chwn kukubuikhe tei kahamkhe bujimangwlak.

english: I walked into the church, and was immediately struck by the beauty of the architecture.
kokborok: Ang girjao bisingo himwi thang kha, hakhe ang aro achomsa naithok khe manwi swnamjak nugwi rwi kha.

english: The soaring arches and stained glass windows were breathtaking.
kokborok: Birsajak arches tei sajokjak glassni tailamrok belai kwmasingcha.

english: I sat down in a pew and closed my eyes, trying to take it all in.
kokborok: Khamplai kologo ang achugwi kha tei mukum kha, je nukmarogno bebak uansokna bagwi.

english: As I sat there, I began to think about the purpose of church architecture.
kokborok: Ang aro achuk kha, ang uansokna cheng kha girjani swnamjakrogno twywi.

english: What is it meant to do?
kokborok: Abobai tamo khwlainai hwnw?

english: Is it simply to create a beautiful space for worship?
kokborok: Abo khulumna bagwi thai swnam mani de?

english: Or is there more to it than that?
kokborok: Eba abono karwi teibo da tong kho?

english: I think that church architecture can be a powerful tool for communicating the message of the Gospel.
kokborok: Girjani manwi swnamjakrok kothoma kaham bai kwtha rwjaknai manwise wng khwna.

english: The soaring arches and stained glass windows can remind us of the vastness of God's love and the beauty of his creation.
kokborok: Birsajak arches tei sajokjak tailamrok chwngno muito khwlai rwphio Kaitorni hamjakmung kotor tei boni naithothok swnamjak manwirogno twywi.

english: They can also create a sense of awe and wonder, which can help us to connect with the divine.
kokborok: Abohrokbo borom tei kwmasingcha wngrwi mano, abo bai chwng Kaitor bai halok bothani chukrwi mano.

english: In addition, church architecture can be a place of refuge and comfort.
kokborok: Abohrokno khobwi, girjani swnamjak manwirok tongthai tei tongthok rwi mano.

english: When we are feeling lost or alone, we can come to church and find a sense of peace and belonging.
kokborok: jephuru chwng kwmajak tei saichung wngwi tongphru, chwng girjao phai mano tei aro khakchangma tei nini bebakno manwi mano.

english: The familiar surroundings and the supportive community can help us to feel at home.
kokborok: Tongjakuk mani tongthairok tei chubanai lukurok bai malai sakno nogo hai matongo.

english: Of course, not all church architecture is beautiful or inspiring.
kokborok: Au, bebak giraja le aswk naithok tei khangnai buya.

english: Some churches are simply functional buildings that do not have much to offer in terms of aesthetics.
kokborok: Baksa ni girja khe ba ahaino nok bachadropni nok se aswk naithok naijaknairogbo kwrwi.

english: A: I'm so itchy! I think I have lice.
kokborok: A: Ang aswkno motokjak! Ang wansukha ani thani thwk tongo hwnwi.

english: B: Oh no! That's terrible.
kokborok: B: Omah! Abo belai kirimasincha.

english: I know how to get rid of them, though.
kokborok: Tophano, ang saimano bohrokno bahaikhe hamrwi manai.

english: We can use a traditional remedy.
kokborok: Chwng kaisa sirisithi hambithi phwnang mano.

english: A: What is it?
kokborok: A: Amo tamo?

english: B: We'll need some olive oil, some lemon juice, and a few cloves of garlic.
kokborok: B: Chwng jotto kisa jolpui thok nango, kisa lebu bwtwi, tei kisa risum bokrarok.

english: A: Okay, I have all of that. What do we do with it?
kokborok: A: Ako, abo ani thani jotto tongo. Omo bai chwng tamo khlaiman?

english: B: First, we'll mix the olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic together.
kokborok: B: Puila, chwng thansa khlai ah jolpui thokni, lebu bwtwi, tei risumno sapulnai.

english: Then, we'll apply it to your hair and scalp.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, chwng omo nini khwnai tei khorok bukuro phulnai.

english: We'll let it sit for about an hour.
kokborok: Chwng amono damsani bagwi yakar toninani.

english: A: An hour? That sounds like a long time.
kokborok: A: Damsa? Abo kisa kolok jora nama hai ta.

english: B: It is, but it's worth it.
kokborok: B: Amono, phiya nasingmani bwthai mannai.

english: The oil will help to suffocate the lice and the lemon juice will help to kill them.
kokborok: Ah thok ah thwk no hama mwthakma bwkhak chubanai tei ah lebu bwtwi bohrokno bwtharna bwkhak chubanai.

english: The garlic will help to repel them.
kokborok: Ah risum bohrokno kasoma bwkhak chubanai.

english: A: Okay, I'll do it.
kokborok: A: Ako, ang amono khainai.

english: My friend, Abel, and I were walking home from school one day when we saw a blood drive being held at our local community center.
kokborok: Ani bayap, Abel, tei ang rwngnok ni simi salsa nogo himwi thangphuru aphuru chwng kaisa thwih chaluk wngma nukha chini hoda bokhwrwi'o.

english: We were both 17 years old, and we had never donated blood before.
kokborok: Chwng khoroknwi no omor bisi 17, tei chwng waisa phano swkango thwi bakjakya khu.

english: We decided to stop in and see what it was all about.
kokborok: Chwng bathakna hwnwi chapkha tei naikha omo jotto tamoni bagwi.

english: The process of donating blood was actually pretty simple.
kokborok: Ah thwih bakmani tangsep wngkha kubuino naithok khalepleng.

english: We both filled out a questionnaire and answered some questions about our health history.
kokborok: Chwng khoroknwi no ah swngjaknairok tei kokphirokmarok supung karikha baksa swngmungrok chini sakdukma laihbuma bagwi.

english: Then, we had our blood pressure checked and our veins were checked to make sure they were big enough.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, chwng chini thwi sepmung nairikha tei chini sirok nairikha oh wngkubui khlainani bohrok belai kotor da hwnwi.

english: Once we were cleared to donate, we each sat down in a chair and had a needle inserted into our arms.
kokborok: Waisa chwng bakna bwkhak sraisrai wngkha, chwng thangwi kaisa achukphang tola achukha tei chini yaptwirok bisingo suchi yorjakha.

english: The blood was collected in a bag, and the whole process took about 15 minutes.
kokborok: Ah thwi kaisa sola bising thumjakha, tei ah jotto tangsep 15 sotirok nakha.

english: It felt good to know that we were helping to save lives.
kokborok: Omo kaham wansukha bwkhak sikha chwng langmarok mwthangna bagwi chubamani hwnwi.

english: After we donated, we were given a juice box and a cookie to help us recover.
kokborok: Chwng bakmani ulo, chwngno kaisa bwtwi baksho tei kaisa cookie rwjakha chwng kaham wngwi chubama bwkhak.

english: We also received a thank-you card from the blood bank.
kokborok: Chwng kaisa hambai-nono bwlap bo mankha ah thwi khatinokni simi.

english: I'm glad that Abel and I decided to donate blood.
kokborok: Ang khatung khajak je Abel tei ang thwih bakna bwkhak chapkha.

english: It was a quick and easy way to make a difference in the world.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa dakti tei lama kaisa ah hayung juda juda khlai swnamna bwkhak.

english: I encourage everyone to consider donating blood if they are eligible.
kokborok: Ang jottono khatorwma rio thwih baknani gosima bwkhak tumungno boro chukjak wngkhe.

english: It's a simple act of kindness that can help save lives.
kokborok: Omo kaisa khakepleng khanangma samung je langrokno mwthangna chubai mano.

english: "Dude, I'm so heartbroken right now. My girlfriend of 2 years just broke up with me."
kokborok: "Kiching, ang tabuk markhe bwkha baijak. ani bwrwi no bisi 2 swkang ang bai kagwi thangkha."

english: "What happened?"
kokborok: "Tamo wngkha?"

english: "I don't know. She just said she wasn't feeling it anymore.
kokborok: "Ang bo saimanya. bo sakha je boni thani wansukphan kisaphano kwrwi kha hwnwi.

english: I'm so confused.
kokborok: Ang palamanliya.

english: I thought we were happy."
kokborok: Chwng kaham kwrwngno hwnwi ang wansukmani."

english: "I'm sorry, man.I know how you feel. Heartbreak sucks."
kokborok: "Nakardi, borok. ang saimano nwng bahai chongmao tong. bwkha baima hamya."

english: "It does. I don't know what to do."
kokborok: "Ahaino wngo. I saimanliya tamo khaina nang."

english: "Just give yourself some time.
kokborok: "Saksak no nwng kisaa jora rwdi.

english: Cry it out if you need to.
kokborok: Chirik kabwi nadi jodi nangkhe.

english: And then, when you're ready, start to move on.
kokborok: Hwnkhe tei, nwng buphuru tiyar wngnai, yapri sena chengkhe.

english: There are plenty of other fish in the sea."
kokborok: Aro twibom o kubuni ah kwbangma tongo.

english: "I know. But I don't know if I'm ready to date again yet."
kokborok: "Ang saimano. phiya ang saimanya aphrubo ang tei waisa date khaina tiyarda wngno."

english: "That's okay. You don't have to be ready right away. Just take your time and heal."
kokborok: "Bo thikno. nwng tabuk tiyar wngnani mungsa nangya. tak nini joranadi tei hamdi."

english: "Thanks, man. I appreciate it."
kokborok: "Hambai, borok. ang appreciate khayo."

english: "No problem."
kokborok: "Kunu wngya."

english: The view from the top of the mountain was breathtaking.
kokborok: Hapung saka simi naimung wngkha belai hamathakmani.

english: The sun was shining, the birds were singing, and the clouds were below us.
kokborok: Sal pohorwma wngkha, tokrok rwchapmani, tei chumuirok chini tolao.

english: I couldn't believe how high up we were.
kokborok: Ang poito khaimanya chwng bwswk kuchugo.

english: We had hiked for hours to get here, and it was worth every step.
kokborok: Chwng aro sogwina bagwi damrwi hiked khai thango, tei jotto yapri omo swk wngkha.

english: As we stood there taking in the view, a truck drove by.
kokborok: Chwng bachawui aro naimung nai tongphuru, kaisa truck lai thangkha.

english: It was a big, old truck, and it was covered in mud.
kokborok: Abo belai kotor, kwcham truck, tei omo harpek bai thukulubjak.

english: The driver was sticking his head out the window, and he was smiling.
kokborok: Ah chaluknai bini khorok tailam ni kariwui kwphajak, tei bo mwnwi tongo.

english: He must have been enjoying the view as much as we were.
kokborok: Bo naimung nai aswkno tongthogwi nai tongo aswkno chwng je nai tongmani hai.

english: We watched the truck drive away, and then we turned our attention back to the view.
kokborok: Chwng ah truck chaluk thangmani naitongkha, tei hwnkhe cheng guriwui chini skatongnai naimung bwkhak phirokha.

english: We stayed up there for a while, just enjoying the moment.
kokborok: Chwng swrapsa ni bagwi aro saka bathagwi tongkha, haino mukphiliksa tongthokmani twi.

english: It was a perfect day, and we were glad we had made the effort to hike up the mountain.
kokborok: Amo wngkha kaisa chasukjak sal, tei chwng belai khatung khajak chwng hapung saka hike chaitokma bwkhak swnamkha.

english: As we started to hike back down, we realized that the view was even better from below.
kokborok: Chwng hikhe kha tola phirokna chengphuru, chwng saimankha je tola ni simi teibo kahamkuk naimung nukjakha.

english: We could see the truck in the distance, and it looked like a tiny speck.
kokborok: Chwng hakchalni truck no nuk tongo, tei omo kaisa chikonsa speck haikhe nukjago.

english: It was amazing to think that we had just been up there, looking down at it.
kokborok: Omo mwlang chajak wansukma bwkhak wngkha je chwng aro haino saka sogwidrop, tola naisijak aro.

english: The hike down was easier than the hike up, and we made it back to our car in no time.
kokborok: Ah tola hike teisa kwlai saka hike khaimani slai, tei chwng chini malkhungo jora kwrwi sani phirogwi sogwikha.

english: The museum was a treasure trove of history, artifacts, and stories.
kokborok: Ah mukumukhatinok wngkha kaisa rangmai trove laihabuma, rikmamanwirok, tei kothokmarok.

english: From the ancient Egyptian mummies to the modern-day paintings, there was something for everyone to enjoy.
kokborok: Ah kwcham Egyptian mummies simi ah kwtal-sal lepamanirok bwkhak, aro jottonni tongthokma bwkha mungsaswk tongo.

english: One of the most interesting exhibits was the collection of old toys.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai khasrangjak phunukmark wngkha ah kwcham thwngmanwirok thumsa khlaimani.

english: There were dolls from the Victorian era, toy soldiers from the Civil War, and even a set of wooden blocks from the early 1900s.
kokborok: Aro ah Victorian jukni simi phutlarok tongo, thwngmanwi sengkwrakrok ah lukurok chobani simi, tei ahaino kaisa buphang phangkhorrok kaihma ah 1900s swkang simi.

english: Each toy had its own story to tell, and it was fascinating to see how they had changed over time.
kokborok: Twngmanwi thwgwi omoni sakni kothoma sana bwkhak tongo, tei omo nukna bwkhak mauni khlaima wngkha bahai boorg jora rwgwi swlaijakha.

english: One of the toys that caught my eye was a small wooden car.
kokborok: Kaisa ah thwngmanwirok je ani mokol romkha kaisa chikonsa buphangni malkhung wngkha.

english: It was made in the 1950s, and it was in perfect condition.
kokborok: Omo 1950s bising swnamma wngkha, tei omo chasukjak tonghalok bising wngkha.

english: The paint was still bright, and the wheels were still smooth.
kokborok: Ah lepama tabukbo kwchwngkhu, tei ah swkwirok tabukbo milik.

english: I picked it up and examined it closely.
kokborok: Ang omono khochai naikha tei omo ganakhai amjokkha.

english: It was a simple toy, but it was also very well-made.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa khakepleng thwngmanwi, phiya omo belai kaham-swnamma bo wngkha.

english: I wondered who had played with this car all those years ago.
kokborok: Ang uanamasingsa wngkha sabo oh malkhungbai thwngkha jotto ah bisirok swkang.

english: What were their dreams and aspirations?
kokborok: Bohrokni imangrok tei muchungjakmarok tamo?

english: What did they think the future held?
kokborok: Bohrok tamo wansuk ah thinang narakmao?

english: I put the car back in its display case and continued on my way.
kokborok: Ang malkhungno ungkulugo tonikha omo phunukma tonghalok bising tei choyawui ani lama sakao.

english: As I walked through the museum, I thought about all the things that had changed in the world since these toys were made.
kokborok: iko ang ah mukumukhatinok twih himwi thangkheno, ang jotto ah manwirokni bagwi wansukkha je ah hayungni bising swlaijak tongkha swkango oh thwngmanwi swnamma wngkha.

english: A brave little robin was flying through the forest when he saw a group of birds gathered around a large tree.
kokborok: Chikonsa kaisa robin bolong bisingtwi biriwui tongo bo nukha yaksigra kaisa kotorma buphango tok buthup kuthumlaimani.

english: He landed on a branch nearby and listened to what they were saying.
kokborok: Bo ganani bedego bikhwlaikha tei bohrok tamo salaitong abo khwnakha.

english: "We've been investigating this tree for weeks," said a raven.
kokborok: "Chwng hatibar romwi oh buphangno naitukphugwi tongmani", masa tokha sakha.

english: "We're not sure what's causing it to lean so precariously!" said a little sparrow.
kokborok: "Chwng wngkubui bwkhak wngyakhu tamoni bagwi aswkno khekma wngthotokungya!" chikonsa chwrwi masa sakha.

english: "But we're worried that it's going to fall and hurt someone!" cried an eagle.
kokborok: "Haiphano chwng wanjak je omo kwlaina bwkha thangtongo tei khoroksaswkno dukhumanwi mano!" toiling chirik kha.

english: The robin looked at the tree and saw that it was indeed leaning very heavily to one side.
kokborok: Robin buphangno naisikha tei nukha je kaisa digi bwkhak kubuino belaino hilikhe khekjak.

english: He knew that he had to do something to help, but he didn't know what.
kokborok: Bo saimano je bo chubana bagwi mungsaswk khaina nango hini, phiya bo saimanya tamono.

english: Suddenly, an idea came to him.
kokborok: Achumsa, kaisa biniro khakama phaikha.

english: He flew down to the ground and gathered a large load of leaves.
kokborok: Bo ha tolao bikhwlai thangkha tei poja kotorma bwlairokno thumkha.

english: He then flew back up to the tree and started to stuff the leaves into the hole where the roots were exposed.
kokborok: Bo hwnkhe phirogwi buphang saka biriwui thangkha tei bwlaino hakoro swkna chengkha je thayo yarwng nukjaktongmani.

english: The birds below watched in amazement as the robin worked.
kokborok: Tokrok tolao mwlangchalai nailai tonglaikha robin samung khai tongphuru.

english: They couldn't believe that such a small bird could have so much strength.
kokborok: Borok poito khaise manliya je aswk tok chikosa ni thani amswk phan tonganw hwnwi.

english: After a few hours, the robin had filled the hole completely.
kokborok: Kisa damrwini olo, robin hakorno muthubwi paikha.

english: The tree was now standing upright and stable.
kokborok: Buphang tabuk sakadigi tei seya khai bachawui tongo.

english: The other birds cheered and thanked the robin for saving the day.
kokborok: Kubuni tokrok chiroklaiwi tei sal bachirima bagwi robino hambai yapharkha.

english: Once upon a time, there was a beautiful young girl named Luna who lived in a small village on the edge of a forest.
kokborok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro khoroksa bwrwi sikli naithok Luna mungwi kaisa chikonsa kamio tongo bolongni buchu gana.

english: She was the subject of many poems and songs, and all the young men in the village were in love with her.
kokborok: Bo kwbangma kokloprok tei rwchapmung rogo sajaknai, tei jotto para ni chwla siklarok bini hamjakmao kwlwkjak.

english: But Luna's heart was set on someone else: the moon.
kokborok: Phiya Luna's bwkha teimasa ni oro se thepajak: tal o.

english: Every night, Luna would sit outside and gaze up at the moon, dreaming of one day being with him.
kokborok: Jotto horo, Luna phataro achugwi tei tal o saka naikolwi tongo, salsa bini logi tonganw hwnwi imang nugo.

english: She would write poems and songs about him, and she would often dance in the moonlight.
kokborok: Bo bini bagwi kokloprok tei rwchapmungrok swio, bo uramuram talpilala tola mwsao.

english: One night, the moon appeared to Luna in a dream.
kokborok: Kaisa horo, tal Luna ni imango pepla phayo.

english: He told her that he loved her too, and that he would one day come to her.
kokborok: Bo bono saka je bobo bono hamjago, tei je bo salsa bini oro phainai hwnwi.

english: Luna was overjoyed, and she could not wait to be with him.
kokborok: Luna belai tongthokjakma bara, tei bo bobai tongna bagwi naisingwi manya.

english: The next day, Luna went to the forest to meet the moon.
kokborok: Teini salo, Luna bolongo moon bai malaina thangkha.

english: She waited for him all night, but he never came.
kokborok: Bo bono sapung hor dwgwi naisingwi tongo, phiya bo twse phailiya.

english: Luna was heartbroken, and she did not know what to do.
kokborok: Luna belai bwkha baijakha, tei bo saimanliya tamo khainai.

english: The next day, Luna went back to the forest.
kokborok: Teini ssalo, Luna tei waisa bolongo thangkha.

english: She sat down under a tree and started to cry.
kokborok: Bo kaisa buphang tola achugwi tei kabna chengkha.

english: Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Luna," the voice said.
kokborok: Atumsma, bo kaisa khorag khwnakha. "Luna, " ah khorang sakha.

english: Luna looked up, and she saw the moon standing in front of her.
kokborok: Luna saka naisikha, tei bo nukha tal bini bwskango bachajak.

english: Books have been a source of entertainment and education for centuries.
kokborok: Bijaprok kaisa tongthokmung ni yaphang tei bisirarok rwngni bagwi wngkha.

english: In the past, books were hand-written and were very expensive.
kokborok: Ungthangjak bising, bijaprok wngkha yakbai swijak tei belai morokjak wngkha.

english: This made them a luxury item that only the wealthy could afford.
kokborok: Omo bohrokno kaisa tongphlai manwi swnamo je ah rangrigwnang rok simi naimano.

english: However, with the invention of the printing press in the 15th century, books became more affordable and accessible to the general public.
kokborok: Haiphano, 15th bisira bising ah sapukmani sapokkhol swnamjakha, bijaprok ah jotto lukuni bwkhak sogwima tei naimanai wngkha.

english: This led to a boom in literacy and education.
kokborok: Omo swikwrwngmung tei rwng dagima bwkhak hamkrai wngkha.

english: Books have played a major role in shaping culture and society.
kokborok: Bijaprok kaisa kotor tangmung thwngkha hukumu tei dopha swnammani bising.

english: They have been used to document history, spread ideas, and promote social change.
kokborok: Borok swijak laihbuma, wansukamarok auaima, tei hodarwk salai remtisama bwkhak phwnangjakha.

english: Some of the most influential books in history include the Bible, the Quran, and the works of Shakespeare.
kokborok: Baksa jottoni slai koboljakma bijaprok laihbumani bising Bible, Quran, tei Shakespeareni samungrok khobwi.

english: Today, books are still a major source of entertainment and education.
kokborok: Tini, bijaprok tabukbo kaisa kotor yaphang tongthokmung tei rwng bwkhak twi.

english: They are available in a variety of formats, including print, e-books, and audiobooks.
kokborok: Bohrok kaisa dalbidal swnammarok bising manthokma tongo, sapukma khobmani, e-booksm tei audiobooks.

english: Books can be found in libraries, bookstores, and online.
kokborok: Bijaprok bijapnokrok, bijapkhatinokrok, tei online manwi mano.

english: The future of books is uncertain.
kokborok: Bijaprokni thinang wngkha chongmanya.

english: Some people believe that e-books will eventually replace print books.
kokborok: Baksa borok poito khayo je e-books paithago sapokma bijaprok no norwimano.

english: However, there is still a strong demand for print books, especially among readers who prefer the physical experience of reading a book.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro tabukbo kaisa kwrak sanmung tongo sapokm bijaprokni bagwi, ahaino porinairokni kwcharo je ah sakno twywi saimanjak kaisa bijap porimani chajakkukma bai.

english: Whatever the future holds, books are sure to remain a vital part of human culture for many years to come.
kokborok: Thingango jesaphano khatijakrok wngthwng, bijaprok wngkubui wngkha torwkma bwkhak kaisa borok hukumuni lam bokcho kwbangma bisirok phaima bwkhak.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Grace who lived in a small village.
kokborok: Kiasa jorani kok, aro khoroksa bwrwi sikli Grace wngwi tongo je kaisa chikonsa kami bising tongo.

english: She was a kind and gentle girl, but she was also very shy.
kokborok: Bo wngkha khoroksa kaham tei kwchang bwrwi, phiya bo belai lachijago.

english: She didn't have many friends, and she often felt lonely.
kokborok: Bini kwbangma bayaprok kwrwi, tei bo uramuram saichung wansukha.

english: One day, Grace was walking in the forest when she came across a beautiful white flower.
kokborok: Salsa, Grace ah bolong bisingtwih himwi tongmani jephuru bo kaisa naithok khum kuphur bswkang phaikha.

english: She had never seen anything like it before.
kokborok: Bo swkango omo kahai jesa manwi waisaphano nukyakhu.

english: The petals were so delicate, and the fragrance was so sweet.
kokborok: Ah bubarlaih aswkno dugwnang tongjak, tei ah bahai wngkha aswkno kwtwi.

english: Grace was enchanted by the flower, and she decided to take it home with her.
kokborok: Grace ah khum bai hamjakrwma wngkha, tei bo omono bini logi nogo twlangna chongkha.

english: When she showed the flower to her parents, they were amazed.
kokborok: Jephuru bo ah khumno bini maphasongno phunukha, bohrok mwlangchakha.

english: They had never seen anything like it either.
kokborok: Bohrok jeba kaisa omo kahai jesa manwi waisaphano nukyakhu.

english: They told Grace that the flower was very special, and that it was a symbol of purity and innocence.
kokborok: Bohrok Grace no sakha je ah khum wngkha belai mahmlai, tei je omo wngkha kaisa mari kwthar tei chayakwrwi wngkha.

english: Grace was very proud of her flower, and she took great care of it.
kokborok: Grace bini khum bai belai kungchukma wngkha, tei omono kotor kuar naikani nahaka.

english: She watered it every day, and she made sure it was always in a sunny spot.
kokborok: Bo salbrumbrum amono twi rwkha, tei bo wngkubui swnamkha omo homnino kaisa sal thai bising tongo.

english: The flower grew and grew, and it soon became the most beautiful flower in the village.
kokborok: Ah khum torwi tongkha tei torwi tongkha, tei omo daktino ah kamini bising jottoni slai khum naithok wngkha.

english: One day, a young man came to the village.
kokborok: Salsa, khoroksa chwla sikla ah kami bwkhak phaikha.

english: He was a traveler, and he had come from a faraway land.
kokborok: Bo wngkha khoroksa berainai, tei bo kaisa hakchal hani simi paikha.

english: The importance of national integration cannot be overstated.
kokborok: Ah hodapharwk thumsakhaima nangukma overstated wngya.

english: A nation is made up of people from all walks of life, with different cultures, religions, and beliefs.
kokborok: Kaisa bosong wngkha borok bai swnamjakma jotto langma himmarok simi, juda juda hukumurok bai, tongtharrok, tei poitorok.

english: National integration is the process of bringing these people together and creating a sense of unity.
kokborok: Hodapharwk thumsakhaima wngkha ah khlaijak tongmung oh borokno thansakhe tubumani tei kaisa sinai simanwi thansa swnammani.

english: There are many benefits to national integration.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmrirok tongo hodapharwk thumsakhaima bwkhak.

english: For example, it can help to reduce crime, improve economic growth, and promote social harmony.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, omo tangsitra khaina bwhak chubai mano, rangthong kasama, tei hodarwk kwthamung remtisama.

english: A more integrated nation is more likely to be prosperous and successful.
kokborok: Kaisa teibo thumsakhajak bosong wngkha teibo talikha hamrwma tei khlaimanmung bwkhak wngo.

english: There are many ways to promote national integration.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kwbangma himlarok bwkhak hodapharwk thumsakhaima.
