kokborok: Chwng jephuru mungsaswk bai manjugo, chwng sasokma bai kasokmahai wngthango, tei jephuru kwmama eba chwng je nangma manwi manyakhe aphuru chwnwg jwngjalo kwlaiyo.

english: The Buddha taught that the way to end suffering is to let go of our attachments.
kokborok: Buddha chwngno phwrwngo jwngjalno mwthakna hwnkhe chwng jotto manjuma rokno rwi hona nango.

english: This is not easy, but it is possible through meditation and other spiritual practices.
kokborok: Amtwiya 1, phiya dhiyan khaima bai tei pholagwdaljak loi khwlaikhe abo gerebjak wngmano.

english: When we let go of our attachments, we become free from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and we can experience true peace and happiness.
kokborok: Chwng jephuru chini manjukma rwi howo, chwng aphuru gurima thani phiyokjago halok achaima, thwima, tei ayang maising, tei chwng kubui kwchangtotok tei tongthtok sijak wngmano.

english: One of the most important things to remember when trying to let go of our attachments is that we are not our possessions.
kokborok: Chini thani kaisa jottoni swlai muito naraknani nangkukmani manwi hwnkhe jephuru chini manjumano rwi hona chaitokphuru chwng je chini saksomani no ya.

english: We are not our ideas or beliefs.
kokborok: Chwng chini khakamung eba poito no ya.

english: We are simply beings who are experiencing the world through our senses.
kokborok: Chwng mohai khakeplengjak kwthang je chini sinai simanwi twi swngcharno sijagwi khai tongo.

english: When we can see ourselves in this way, it becomes easier to let go of the things that we think we need to be happy.
kokborok: Jephuru chwngno chwng omo haikhe nugo, aphuru manwi rwi honani belai kwlai wngthango chwng wansugo je chwng tongthokna nango hwnwi.

english: Letting go of our attachments does not mean that we have to give up everything.
kokborok: Chini manjuma rokno rwi horphano omo haiya je chwng chini jotto yakar rinai.

english: It simply means that we need to be able to let go of things when it is time.
kokborok: Omoni suja kokbwrwng hwnkhe je chwng chini manwi no rwi hona nango jephuru jora phaikhe.

english: We need to be able to let go of the things that are no longer serving us, and we need to be able to let go of the things that we are attached to out of fear or insecurity.
kokborok: Chwng mohai manwi rwi honani chukna nango je chwngno tei chubai manliya, tei chwng mohai manwino rwi howui chukha je chini naimwthang eba chini kirima bai manjuwi tongmano.

english: When we can let go of our attachments, we open ourselves up to a new world of possibilities.
kokborok: Chwng jephuru chini manjuma rwi howo, chwng aphuru kwtal swngchar halok wngmarokno chwngno khulugo.

english: We become free to live our lives in a way that is true to ourselves, and we become free to experience the joy and happiness that is our birthright.
kokborok: Chwng chini langmano mohaikhe tongwi thangnani hwnwi yokjak wngthango je omo chini bagwi kubui, tei chwng sijakna bagwi yogwi thango khaswrang tei thongthokma abo chini manthai.

english: While this may seem like a gross habit, it is actually quite beneficial to the pig.
kokborok: Jephuru omo kaisa bebak loi hai khakama wngmano, omo kubuino wakni bagwi belai manmarijak.

english: The mud helps to keep the pig cool and clean, and it also provides a natural sunscreen.
kokborok: Ah harpek wakno kwchang tei kwchwng khai chubao, tei omo haino kaisa habar satungriso bo manthokrio.

english: In addition, the mud helps to protect the pig’s skin from parasites and bacteria.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising, ah harpek wakni bukur no parasites tei bacteria thani katina chubao.

english: Some people believe that pigs are dirty because they eat garbage.
kokborok: Baksa borok poito khayo je wakrok wngkha letra patra tamni hinba bohrok khibijaknai manwi chao.

english: However, pigs are actually very clean animals.
kokborok: Haiphanom wakrok wngkha kubuino belai kwchwng malmatarok.

english: They only eat what they find in their environment, and they will not eat anything that is rotten or diseased.
kokborok: Bohrok abo chao je bohrokno bohrokni habar bising mano, tei borok mungsaphano chagwlak je sokjak eba bermajak.

english: In fact, pigs are often used to clean up garbage dumps because they are so good at eating trash.
kokborok: Kubui hwnkhe, wakrok wngkha uramuram bwkhak khibijaknai khipma hakorrok kwchwng khaima tamni hinmakhe bohrok wngkha aswk kaham erengmanwi chamani.

english: Pigs are also very intelligent animals.
kokborok: Wakrok wngkha belai siyankwrwng malmatarok.

english: They are able to solve problems and learn new things quickly.
kokborok: Bohrok kebengmungrokno solve khaimano tei kwtal manwirok daktino swrwng mano.

english: Pigs have been known to use tools, and they can even be trained to do tricks.
kokborok: Wakrok kolrokno phwnangna bwkhak sini jago, tei bohrokno phemloknarok khaina bagwi haino phwrwng mano.

english: Despite their reputation, pigs are actually very gentle and social animals.
kokborok: Bohrokni munggnang phano, wakrok wngkha kubuino belai kwchang tei hodarwk malamatarok.

english: They are very affectionate with their owners, and they enjoy being around people.
kokborok: Bohrok bohrokni bugrarok bai belaino hamjakjak, tei bohrok borokni yaksiyagra tong tongthokjago.

english: Pigs are also very curious animals, and they love to explore their surroundings.
kokborok: Wakrok wngkha haino belai simuchung malmatarok, tei bohrok bohrokni khopmani naitukberaima bwkha hamjago.

english: If you are looking for a loving and intelligent pet, a pig may be the perfect animal for you.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng kaisa hamjakmani tei uansukphan rwjak malmata naitongkhe, kaisa wak nini chasukjak malmata wngwi mano.

english: Pigs are easy to care for, and they make great companions.
kokborok: Wakrok wngkha 1 bwkhak naikani bagwi, tei bohrok kotorkuar logisongjak swnamo.

english: They provide a safe and supportive environment where former inmates can learn to live independently and avoid relapse.
kokborok: Bohrok khatijak tei twichuruma habar yapharo boro swkangni tongnairokno phiyokjagwi tongnani tei haya wngphimung katima swrwng mano.

english: Sober living homes typically offer a variety of services, such as counseling, job training, and addiction support groups.
kokborok: Kwchangtotok tongjaknai nokrok hainohai podrepod samungrok yapharo, ahaino kokchapmani, samung swrwngmani, tei loiungmani bodolrok twichuruma bai.

english: They also provide a sense of community and support, which can be invaluable for people who are reentering society after a period of incarceration.
kokborok: Bohrok hoda sinai simanwi tei twichuruma bago, je borokrokni bagwi marokjakya wngmano je jora bokjakl chobwi rwjak mani olo teiwaisa hodao habphimani.

english: There are many benefits to living in a sober living home.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmari tongo kwchangtotok tongjaknai nok tongkhe.

english: For one, it provides a structured environment where former inmates can learn to live independently.
kokborok: Masa ni bagwi, obo habar nokrakrok bagjago boro swkangni tongnairok phiyojak khai tongna swrwngmano.

english: They are expected to follow a set of rules and regulations, which can help them to develop good habits and routines.
kokborok: Bohrok raida thepama tei kerem khamungno je bohrokno kaham tongraida tei tangremrok hamkrai bwkhak chubai mano.

english: Additionally, sober living homes offer a variety of services that can help former inmates to get back on their feet.
kokborok: Jora rwmungo, kwchangatotok tongjaknai nokrok podrepod samungrok yapharo je swkngnai tongnairokno bohrokni yethego teiwaisa bachana bagwi.

english: These services may include counseling, job training, and addiction support groups.
kokborok: Oh samungarok kokchapmani khobwi mano, samung swrwngmani, tei loiungmani bodolrokno twichuruma bai.

english: The sense of community and support that is found in sober living homes can also be very beneficial.
kokborok: Oh hoda sinai simanwi tei twichuruma je kwchangthotok tongjaknai nokrok belai chubanai mankha.

english: Former inmates often feel isolated and alone after being released from prison or jail.
kokborok: Swkangni tongwi thangnairok uramuram chongo junda khai tongma tei saichung wngo along eba along ni phiyokjakma olo.

english: Living in a sober living home can help them to connect with others who are going through a similar experience.
kokborok: Kwchangtotok tongjaknai nogo tongmnai bohrokno tei kubuni bai kwrwngmano je mohai solai molai saimanjak gerebwi thangwi tongmani.

english: They can also receive support from staff and other residents, which can help them to stay on track with their recovery.
kokborok: Bohrok tangsong tei kubn tongnairokni thani twichuruma manwi mano, je bohrokno yaprimari tongnani bohrokno phiroktubuna bagwi.

english: If you are a recently released inmate, living in a sober living home can be a great way to transition back into society.
kokborok: Nwng jodi tabukno yoknai tongnai hwnkhe, kwchangtotok tongjaknai nogo tongmani obo kotorkuar lama bwkhak twi mung hoda phiroknani.

english: It can provide you with the support and structure that you need to succeed.
kokborok: Omo nono twichuruma tei swnamari bagwi mano je nwng tangmanma wngna nangnai.

english: There are many sober living homes available, so you can find one that meets your needs and budget.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma kwchangtotok tongjaknai nokrok manthogo, je nwngbo kaisa naituk mano, je nini nangmarok tei rangchongmungo malaimarok.

english: It is important to comply with the training requirements in order to ensure that you are properly prepared for the job.
kokborok: Nwng samung tangnani tiyar de tong abono sraisrai khwlaina bagwi loi phwrwngmungni nangmarokno rwksaui tongnani nango.

english: This includes attending all training sessions, completing all assignments, and following all instructions.
kokborok: Oboni bisingo tongo jotto loi phwrwngmung pandao manjakma, jotto samung chongjakno paihma, tei jotto dagimarokno rwksama.

english: It is also important to be receptive to feedback and suggestions from your trainers and supervisors.
kokborok: Nini loi phwrwngnai tei supervisorni thani chama chaya phirokmung tei kokbiti nahanabo nangkugo.

english: This will help you to improve your skills and knowledge, and it will also help you to develop a positive work ethic.
kokborok: Obo nono nini rwbai tei elem hamrwthani chubauano, tei obo nono samung kahamni uansukmung chasarwthanibo chubauano.

english: When you receive feedback or criticism, it is important to take it in a positive manner.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng chama chaya phirokmung eba sejamung mano, abono tongraida kahambai yachaknani nangkugo.

english: This does not mean that you have to agree with everything that is said, but it does mean that you should be open to hearing different perspectives.
kokborok: Oboni kokmang nono jesa sajakmani jotto kokno soinani nangnai abohaiya, phiyaba oboni kokmang wngkha obohaise je dalbidal naharmungtwi khwnana bagwi tiyar tongnani nanganw.

english: It is also important to be respectful of the person giving you feedback.
kokborok: Je borok nini chama chayano phirogmung rwui tongo bohno borom rwnabo nangkugo.

english: Remember, they are trying to help you, so it is important to listen to what they have to say.
kokborok: Muitu narwkdi, bohrok nono chubanani chaitogwi tongo, haini bagwi bohrokni sajakthai tongmano khwnani nangkugo.

english: Once you have received feedback, it is important to take some time to think about it.
kokborok: Nwng chama chayani phirokmung uaisa manpaikha hinkhe obono twywi uansukna bagwi kisaswk jora nanani nangkugo.

english: Consider what was said, and how you can apply it to your work.
kokborok: Uansugwi naidi tamo sajakha tei bahaikhe nwng obono nini samungo thepauiman.

english: If you have any questions, do not hesitate to ask your trainer or supervisor.
kokborok: Nini mungsaswk swngmung tongkhe, nini loi phwrwngnai eba supervisorno swngnani takwmamdi.

english: It is also important to be open to making changes to your work habits or procedures.
kokborok: Nini samungni loi eba tangraidao swlaimung tubuna bagwi khulokjak tongnabo nangkugo.

english: If you are not willing to change, then you will not be able to improve.
kokborok: Tumung nwng swlainani muchungjakya hinkhe nwng chasaui mangwlak.

english: By complying with the training requirements and responding in a positive manner to any suggestion or criticism, you will be able to improve your skills and knowledge, and you will also be able to develop a positive work ethic.
kokborok: Loi swrwngmungrokni raida rwksai tongmani bisingtwi tei jesa kokbiti eba sejamano tongraida kahambai yachagwi, nwng nini kwrwng tei elemno chasarwi manano tei nwng kaisa samung kahamni tangraidani hamkwrai khwlai manano.

english: This will make you a valuable asset to any team, and it will help you to achieve your career goals.
kokborok: Obo nono jesa bodolni bagwi kaisa mulaja gwnang rwbai khwlai tisauano tei obo nono nini tangmungni naharmung ajithani chubauano.

english: You have been waiting for this day for what feels like an eternity, and now it is finally here.
kokborok: Nwng oh salni bagwi naising tongmani tamo kaisa molbrumbrum kahai wansukmarok bagwi, tei tabuk omo paithago oro wngkha.

english: You can't wait to start your new life together as a family.
kokborok: Nwng nini kwtal langma thansa nukhung haikhe chengma bwkak naising mangwlak.

english: The adoption process can be long and arduous, but it is all worth it in the end.
kokborok: Ah sandaima tansep kolok tei kwrak wngmano, phiya omo wngkha jotto swk ah paithakni bising omo.

english: When you finally hold your child in your arms and say, "I'm your mom/dad now," you will know that it was all worth it.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng paithago nini chwraino romkha nino yaktwkrok bising tei sakha, "ang nini ama/baba tabuk, " nwng saimannai je omo wngkha jotto swk.

english: Adoption is a beautiful thing.
kokborok: Sandaima wngkha naithokma manwi.

english: It is the gift of giving a child a loving home and the opportunity to grow up in a safe and stable environment.
kokborok: Omo wngkha khroksa chwraino hamanai nok kaisa rwmung rwmani tei saka torna bwkhak sep kaisa katijak tei kwrak habar bising.

english: It is also a gift to the parents, who are given the chance to experience the joys of parenthood.
kokborok: Omo bo ah mapharokni bwkhak kaisa rwmung je ah sujug rwjak tongo ah maphawngjak tongthokrok simari bawkhak.

english: If you are considering adoption, I encourage you to do your research and find a reputable adoption agency.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng sandaima wansugwi tongkha, ang nono khatungrimung khaidi hino nini rutukrwk tei kaisa borom gwnang sandaima adong naitukna bagwi.

english: There are many different types of adoption agencies, so it is important to find one that is a good fit for you.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma juda juda sandaima adong sakpokthaihrok tongo, aswkno omo kaisa naitukna bwkhak nangkukma je nini bagwi kaisa kaham chukjak.

english: The adoption process can be complex, so it is important to have a good support system in place.
kokborok: Ah sandaima tangsep kutuk wngwi mano, aswkno omo wngkha nangkukma thaini bising kaisa kaham nangmani lam bwkhak tongo.

english: Adoption is a life-changing experience.
kokborok: Sandaima wngkha kaisa langma-swlaimani simari.

english: It is a journey that is filled with love, laughter, and tears.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa beraima je hamjakma, mwnwima, tei mwktwrwi bai supungjak.

english: But it is a journey that is worth taking.
kokborok: Phiya omo wngkha kaisa beraima je swk namani wngkha.

english: If you are considering adoption, I encourage you to take the leap.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng sandaima wansugwi tongkha, ang nono ah barma bwkhak khatungrimung khayo.

english: You will not regret it.
kokborok: Nwng omo dukhu mangwlak.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Alice who was very lazy.
kokborok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro khoroksa bwrwi sikli Alice mungwi tong je belaino seler.

english: She would never do her chores, and she would always skip school.
kokborok: Bo bini samungrok jesaphuru phano khaiya, tei bo homnino bini rwngnok karo.

english: Her parents were very worried about her, and they tried everything they could to get her to change her ways.
kokborok: Bini maphasong bini bagwi belai wanajak, tei jotto manwi chaitok naikha bohrok khaimatwi bini lamarok swlaida mano hwnwi.

english: But nothing worked.
kokborok: Phiya mungsaphano samung khailiya.

english: One day, Alice's parents decided to take her to see a therapist.
kokborok: Salsa, Alice's ni maphasong chongkha bono kaisa hamya nainai ni oro bono twlangna hwnwi.

english: The therapist talked to Alice about the importance of discipline, and she told her that if she wanted to be successful in life, she would need to learn to be disciplined.
kokborok: Ah hamya nainai Alice bai kok sakha ah nangkukma tongchapjak ni bagwi, tei bo bono sakha je tumungno nwng bini langmao tangmanjak wngna muchungkhe, bo tongchapjak swrwngna nango.

english: Alice was not happy to hear this, but she knew that her parents were right.
kokborok: Alice omo khwnai tongthok jakliya, phiya bo saimano je bini maphasosng chao hwnwi.

english: She decided to make a change, and she started to do her chores and go to school every day.
kokborok: Bo swlaina hwnwi chongwi nakha, tei bo bini samungrok khwlaina chengjakha tei sal thwigwi rwngnok bwkhak thangkha.

english: It was not easy at first, but she stuck with it, and eventually, she started to see results.
kokborok: Omo puilao 1 wngmaya, phiya bo omo bai kwchajak, tei phaithago bo abono bwthaihrok nukna chengkha.

english: She started to get better grades in school, and she made new friends.
kokborok: Bo rwngnok bising kaham remrok manna chengkha, tei bo kwtal bayaprok swnamakha.

english: She was even happier than she had been before.
kokborok: Boh ahaino tongthokjak wngkha bo swkang wngmani slai.

english: Alice learned that discipline is important for success in life.
kokborok: Alice swrwngkha je tongchapjak wngkha nangkukma langma khlaimanmung bagwi.

english: It is not always easy to be disciplined, but it is worth it.
kokborok: Omo homnino 1 tongchapjak wngma simiya, phiya omo morojak wngkha.

english: When you are disciplined, you can achieve anything you set your mind to.
kokborok: Nwng jephuru tongchapjak wngkha, nwng jesamanwi manwi mano nwng nini khorogo khaihmani.

english: The end.
kokborok: Awa toke.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Anna who lived in a small village.
kokborok: Adi nobar o, khoroksa sikli khungsa bwsate kami o tong jao bwmung Anna.

english: She was a kind and gentle soul, but she was also very unhappy.
kokborok: Bo belai maya gwnang tei bwkha kaham, phiya bo belai bwkha bo tongthok jak ya.

english: She longed for freedom, but she knew that she would never be able to leave her village.
kokborok: Bo yoksamung bahai sina muchungo, phiya bo saimano bo boni kami no yakarwi thangmaya hwnwi.

english: One day, Anna was walking in the forest when she came across a strange man.
kokborok: Salsa, Anna bolongtwi himwi tong phuru khoroksa siniya chwla bai malai kha.

english: He was tall and handsome, with long black hair and piercing blue eyes.
kokborok: Bo kolok tei chwla naithok, boni khwnai bo kolok tei naichomung gwnang mokol.

english: He introduced himself as Luka, and he told Anna that he was a traveler from a faraway land.
kokborok: Bo sakno Luka hwnwi sinimung rw kha, tei Anna no bo sakha bo khoroksa hakchalma ni phainai hwnwi.

english: Anna and Luka quickly fell in love, and they decided to run away together.
kokborok: Anna bai Luka daktino hamjak lai kha, tei bohrok kwnwi kharlai na bagwi kok chablai kha.

english: They traveled for many days, and they saw many amazing things.
kokborok: Bohrok sal kwdwkma romwi himlaijak, tei bohrok belai naithok naithok manwirok nuklaikha.

english: They met kind people and cruel people, and they learned a lot about the world.
kokborok: Bohrok borok kaham baibo malaikha tei borok hamya baibo malaikha.

english: Finally, Anna and Luka reached the sea.
kokborok: Paithago, Anna bai Luka twijwlango sogwi laikha.

english: They boarded a ship and sailed away, and they never looked back.
kokborok: Bohrok rung swnamlaikha tei chogwi thanglaikha, tei bohrok ungkuluk phirogwi bo naharliya.

english: They found a new home in a faraway land, and they lived happily ever after.
kokborok: Bohrok kwchalma hao kwtal tonthai manlaikha, tei aro bohrok tongthogwi tonglaikha.

english: Anna and Luka's story is a reminder that freedom is a precious thing.
kokborok: Anna bai Luka ni kothoma wngkha kaisa muito rwmani se yoksama bwswkse kaham hwnwi.

english: It is something that we should never take for granted.
kokborok: Abono chwng tongphlainai hwnwi bo uansogwi manya.

english: We should all strive to be free, and we should never give up on our dreams.
kokborok: Chwng bebakno yoksajakkhe tongnani masaktharnai, tei chwng chini naharmungno yakarthai kwrwi.

english: The Old Man and the Sea
kokborok: Chakra borok bai twiyung.

english: Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman, has gone eighty-four days without catching a fish.
kokborok: Santiago, khoroksa chakra Cuban ni ah romnai, bo charchi-bwrwi salromwi kaisa phano ah rommwi manyawui thangkha.

english: He is the oldest man in the village, and the youngest, Manolin, no longer wants to fish with him because the old man is unlucky.
kokborok: Boh kamini jottonislai chakra borok, tei chwraikuk, Manolin, bobai tak tei ah romna muchungjakliya tamni hinmale chakra borok belai talikha hamya.

english: One day, Santiago sets out in his skiff and hooks a giant marlin.
kokborok: Salsa, Santiago bini skiff twi ongkhor thangkha tei kaisa kotorma marlin no bosoi karkha.

english: The marlin is so big that it pulls the skiff far out to sea.
kokborok: Ah marlin aswkhe kotorma je abo skiff no hakchalo sotonwi twiyung bwkhak twlangkha.

english: Santiago fights the marlin for two days and nights, but he cannot bring it in.
kokborok: Santaigo salnwi tei hornwi jora marlin bai bulaikha, phiya bo amono tubui manliya.

english: The marlin is too heavy, and the old man is too tired.
kokborok: Ah marlin belai hilik, tei ah chakra borok belai lengjakha.

english: Finally, the marlin begins to tire.
kokborok: Paithago, ah marlin lengna chengkha.

english: Santiago is able to get a harpoon into the marlin, and he kills it.
kokborok: Santiago marlin no ahyung suhrma bwkhak mankha, tei bo omono bwtharkha.

english: But the marlin is so big that Santiago cannot bring it into the boat.
kokborok: Phiya ah marlin aswkhe kotor je Santiago omono rungo tubui manliya.

english: He ties the marlin to the side of the boat and begins to row back to shore.
kokborok: Bo ah marlin no rungni kuna khaka tei rukungo chogwi phirokna chengkha.

english: A school of sharks follows the boat, and they begin to eat the marlin.
kokborok: Sharkrokni bodol kaisa rungno rwtharkha, tei bohrok marlin no chana chengkha.

english: Santiago fights the sharks off, but he cannot stop them all.
kokborok: Santiago Sharkrokbai bulaikha, phiya bo bohrokno mwthak manliya.

english: By the time he reaches shore, only the head and the tail of the marlin are left.
kokborok: Bo rukungo sogwima jora, marlin ni khorok tei khitung amswk simino torok sio.

english: Freedom of the press is the freedom of communication and expression through mediums including printed media and the internet.
kokborok: Kokthuna yokmung wngkha manjumung tei muchung samung yokmung kwrwnglamrok twih sapokjak pinlam tei ah internet no khobwi.

english: It is a fundamental human right recognized by Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and reaffirmed in Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
kokborok: Omo kaisa nangthai borokni manthai 19 kerongbwkhak bai sinijakma ah hayungkhobwi sakhlaimani borokni manthairok tei gosi chongmani 19 kerongbwkhak hayung rwkjak kokchaplaimung luku tei thwngrwngrwk manthairok.

english: The right to freedom of expression is recognized as a necessary precondition for the enjoyment of all other human rights.
kokborok: Ah manthai yokmung bwkhak muchung samung sinijakma ahaino kaisa nangmani swkang tonghalok ah tongthokmani bagwi jotto kubun borokni manthairok.

english: Freedom of the press is essential for a healthy democracy.
kokborok: Kokthumnai yokmung wngkha kaisa sakdukma lukuchongraida bagwi nangnai.

english: It allows citizens to access information and to hold their government accountable.
kokborok: Omo habarokno kwbang kokthumjakmani gosimarok tei bohrokni hapang thikemung bwkhak romchrepmani.

english: It also helps to ensure that all voices are heard, and that the public is informed about important issues.
kokborok: Omo khasrai khwlaima bwkhak bo chubao je jotto khorangrok khwnajak thwng, tei je ah lukurok nangkukma ongkhormarok kokthumjak thwng.

english: In recent years, there have been growing threats to freedom of the press around the world.
kokborok: Laithangjak bisirokni bising, aro kwbangma sikrimungrok torwi tongo kokthumnai yokmung ah hayung yaksiyagra bwkhak.

english: Governments have been using laws to restrict the media, and journalists have been harassed and attacked.
kokborok: Haphangrok kerongrok phwnangwi tongo ah pinlam kasona bagwi, tei kokholnairok cheklekjagwi tei choprobjagwi tongo.

english: These threats are a serious concern, and they need to be addressed.
kokborok: Oh sikrimarok wngkha kaisa uansukrak uanama, tei bohrok tongthai bumungrok khaina nango.

english: We must all stand up for freedom of the press.
kokborok: Chwng haino jotto bachana nangnai kokthumnai yokmungni bagwi.

english: We must defend the right of journalists to report the news without fear of reprisal.
kokborok: Chwng ah kokhoknairokno saksoma bwkhak ah kokrikma koktunmarok kiriyawui sejana nangnai.

english: We must also support independent media outlets, and we must encourage people to read and share news from a variety of sources.
kokborok: Chwng yohkjak pinlam ongkhorlam rokno twichuruma makhainai tei chwng borokrokno porina bagwi khatorwma nangnai tei koktunmarok bakma simi kaisa dalbidal yaphangrok.

english: Freedom of the press is a precious right.
kokborok: Kokthumnai yokmung wngkha hamkukjak manthai.

english: We must all do our part to protect it.
kokborok: Chwng jotto yangtwi bokcho khaina nangno omono katirina bwkhak.

english: As the sun began to set, a young boy named Raman made his way home from school.
kokborok: Sal thangna chengkheno, chwrai omor kisa Raman mungwi rwngnok simi bini nok lama thangkha.

english: As he walked, he noticed a stray dog following him.
kokborok: Bo himwi thangphuru, bo khel khaikha lamakorokjak swi bono rwtharwitongo hwnwi.

english: The dog was dirty and skinny, but it had a friendly face.
kokborok: Ah swi leta-pata tei keram, phiya bini bayap wngna mwkhang tongo.

english: Raman felt sorry for the dog, so he decided to take it home with him.
kokborok: Raman oh swino khairokjakha, haini bagwi bo bono bini nogo twlangna hwnwi chongwinakha.

english: When Raman got home, he told his parents about the dog.
kokborok: Jephuru Raman nogo thangwi sogwikha, bo bini ma-phano swini bagwi sakha.

english: They were hesitant at first, but they eventually agreed to let him keep the dog.
kokborok: Bohrok puila'o sakphorkha, phiya bohrok paithago swirokno tonina hwnwi gosi'ui nakha.

english: Raman named the dog Buddy, and they quickly became best friends.
kokborok: Raman swino Buddy hwnwi mung rwkha, tei bohrok dakti kiching kaham wnglaikha.

english: Buddy was always there for Raman, no matter what.
kokborok: Buddy Ramanni bagwi homnino tongo, jesaphano wngthwng.

english: He was there to greet him at the door when he came home from school, and he was there to comfort him when he was feeling down.
kokborok: Boh bono lamsukna bagwi duklam bwskango tongo jephuru bo nogo rwngnokni kiphilwi phaiphuru, tei bo khasrangna bagwi bini logi tongo jephuru bo tola uansukphan wngphuru.

english: One day, Raman was playing in the park when he fell and scraped his knee.
kokborok: Salsa, Raman berailwngo thwngwi tongphuru boh kwlainai bini yasku kukkha.

english: He started to cry, and Buddy came running over to lick his wound.
kokborok: Boh kabna chengkha, tei Buddy bini gana khaprumwi phai bini kwsano swlakha.

english: The dog's gentle tongue helped to soothe Raman's pain, and he soon forgot all about his injury.
kokborok: Swini kwchang bwslai Raman no samani simi holirwna chubakha, tei bo daktino bini kukma pogwi thangkha.

english: Raman and Buddy shared many happy years together.
kokborok: Raman bai Buddy thansakhe kwbangma bisi romwi tongthoktokkhe tonglaikha.

english: They went on walks, played fetch in the park, and cuddled up on the couch together.
kokborok: Bohrok himna thangkha, berailwngo khitarmung thwnglaikha, tei thuyamo thansa khe kwbaklai tonglaikha.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young man named Rajiv who lived in a small village.
kokborok: Agi phuru, khoroksa sikla tongo bwmung Rajiv bo kaisa kami bwsatete'o tongjao.

english: He was a poor man, and he and his mother often went hungry.
kokborok: Boh bigra borokja, tei bo bai bini buma okhui'ui mangno matonglaijao.

english: One day, Rajiv decided to go into the forest to find some food.
kokborok: Salsa, Rajiv chamung rutukna bagwi bolongo thangnai hwnwi khao chabkha.

english: As he was walking through the forest, Rajiv came across a strange tree.
kokborok: Boh bolong bising twi himwi tong phuru, Rajiv phangsa siniya-nukya buphangno nukha.

english: The tree was covered in golden apples, and Rajiv had never seen anything like it before.
kokborok: Oh buphang rangchak ni apples bai kupulwng, tei omo twi buphangrokno waisa phano Rajiv nukya kho.

english: He reached up to pick an apple, but as soon as he touched it, the tree spoke to him.
kokborok: Boh apple khosana bagwi aro sogwi kha, phiya boh abono tangkheno, ah buphang bono kok sakha.

english: "Do not touch my apples," the tree said. "They are not for you."
kokborok: "Ani apple no tatang di" hwnwi a buphang sakha. "Aborok nini bagwya."

english: But Rajiv was hungry, and he didn't listen to the tree.
kokborok: Phiya Rajiv belai kheno okhuijak, tei boh ah buphangni kokno khwnaliya.

english: He picked an apple and took a bite.
kokborok: Boh ah apple no khosa'ui wakhakha.

english: As soon as he did, he felt a strange change come over him.
kokborok: Boh abo hai khlaikheno, boh bini sago swlaijakma hai matongkha.

english: He felt stronger and more powerful, and he knew that he had done something wrong.
kokborok: Boh bini sago belai phan kwrak phaijakmahai wngjakkha, tei saimankha bo mungsaswkle chaya khwlai kha hwnwi.

english: "I am the Golden Apple Tree," the tree said. "And now that you have eaten my apple, you will be cursed.
kokborok: "Ang wngkha Rangchakni Apple Buphang, " hwnwi ah buphang sakha. "Tei tabok nwng ani apple chamani, nwng swraimung mansinai."

english: You will never be satisfied with what you have, and you will always be searching for more."
kokborok: Je nini tongma bai nwng tei kha suksogwi mangwlak, tei nwng teibo manna bagwi rutukphwlai mangno matongnai."

english: And so it was.
kokborok: Aboni bagwino tabuk omo hai mangno wngwi matongkha.

english: The little girl stood on the street corner, shivering in the cold.
kokborok: Khoroksa chwraisa bwrwi lama baichingo bachajak, kwchangmani ba kwlwibrajak.

english: She had been trying to sell matches all day, but no one had bought any.
kokborok: Bo salni simino horkotra phalnani chaitokjak, phiya keba paiya.

english: She was about to give up when she saw a man approaching.
kokborok: Bo khoroksa chwla phaima nuhurwi yakarnase nai tongkha.

english: He looked like he was in a hurry, but he stopped when he saw the little girl.
kokborok: Bo belai dojak, phiya bo chwraisa bwrwino nugwi bathak kha.

english: "What are you doing out here all alone?" he asked.
kokborok: " Nwng oro saichung khe tamo khwlai?" bo swngkha.

english: "I'm trying to sell matches," the little girl said. "But no one will buy them."
kokborok: " ang horkotra phalnai nayo, " a chwraisa bwrwi sakha. " Phiya kebo abono paina se naiya."

english: "Well, I'll buy one," the man said "But you have to give me a rose in exchange."
kokborok: "Do, ang kaisa paisi wano, " a chwla sakha"phiya nwng ano gulap rwna nangnai aboni bodla."

english: The little girl was surprised, but she agreed.
kokborok: A chwraisa bwrwi wanajakha, phiya bo gosi kha.

english: She ran home and picked a beautiful rose.
kokborok: Bo nogo kharwi thang kha hakhe gulap naithokno kholwi tubukha.

english: Then she went back to the man and gave him the match and the rose.
kokborok: Hakhe bo a borokni aro phirogwi thang kha hakhe bono horkotra bai gulap yapharwi rwi kha.

english: "Thank you," the man said "You're a kind girl." He took the match and lit it.
kokborok: " Hambai, " a borok sakha "nwng belai maya gwnang bwrwi." bo horkotra na'ui mwchwng kha.

english: As the flame grew, the little girl saw that it was a magic match.
kokborok: Horjwlai torwi phaima bai, a bwrwi abono soidomni horkotra khe nukha.

english: It turned into a beautiful bouquet of roses.
kokborok: Abo kaisa naithok khe gulap bubarni motha se wngwi thangsio.

english: The little girl was so happy.
kokborok: A chwraisa bwrwi belai tongthok jakha.

english: Trains have been a vital part of transportation for centuries.
kokborok: Relmalkhungrok kaisa mal bokcho bisirarok karwi rwkajakamnai tongkha.

english: They are a safe, efficient, and reliable way to travel long distances.
kokborok: Bohrok kaisa katijak, pharinai, tei poitognang himla kolok chalmarok beraina bwkhak tongo.

english: However, the railroad industry requires regular updates to keep pace with the changing needs of passengers.
kokborok: Haiphano, ah rellama swnammung sabrumbrum updates nango yapri tonma bwkhak ah kaiberainai nangmarok swlaimani bai.

english: One of the most important updates that trains need is the installation of new safety features.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai nangkukma updates ah relmalkhung nangma wngkha ah kwtal katijakma mwkhangrok thepamani.

english: In recent years, there have been a number of high-profile train accidents, which have highlighted the need for better safety measures.
kokborok: Tabukni bisirok bising, aro kisa kuchuk-profile relmalkhung akabikarok tongkha, bomo ha phunukjakma tongo ah kaham katijakma sumarokni bagwi nangma.

english: New safety features such as positive train control (PTC) can help prevent accidents by automatically stopping trains that are traveling too fast or that are about to collide with another train.
kokborok: Kwtal katijakma mwkhangrok ahaino sosol relmalkhung kasomung (PTC) relmalkhung bathakmani saksak khaimanma akabikarok kasogra chubai manai je belal doui beraimani wngkha eba je kubun relmalkhung bai thutaima bagwi tongo.

english: Another important update that trains need is the installation of new technology.
kokborok: Teikaisa nangkukma update je relmalkhung nangma wngkha ah kwtal tangsep thepamani.

english: In the past, trains were powered by steam engines.
kokborok: Ah wngthang bisingm relmalkhungrok phap kolrok bai cholijakha.

english: However, steam engines are inefficient and pollute the environment.
kokborok: Haiphano, phap kolrok wngkha pharimanya tei ah habar sitra rwkha.

english: Today, most trains are powered by diesel engines or electric motors.
kokborok: Tini, jottoni slai relmalkhungrok wngkha diesel kolrok eba pherang loriwnai kolkrok bai chalukjakha.

english: These engines are more efficient and environmentally friendly.
kokborok: Oh kolrok wngkha teibo pharinai tei habarma bayapma.

english: In addition to safety and technology updates, trains also need to be updated to accommodate the needs of passengers.
kokborok: Jora rwmani bising katijakma tei tansep updates bwkhak, relmalkungrok bo updated wngna bwkhak nango ah kaiberainairokni nangmarok gothokrima bwkhak.

english: In recent years, there has been an increase in the number of passengers who travel by train.
kokborok: Tabukni bisirok bising, aro kaisa bangrwma tongkha ah lombor kaiberainairok je relmakhung bai berainai.

english: This has led to overcrowding on trains, which can make for a less comfortable and enjoyable experience.
kokborok: Omo railmalkhung sakao bwlai bohrokbangmani bwkhak dagi tongo, bomo kaisa kisa tongthotok tei tongthokma simari bagwi swnam mano.

english: My dear daughter, I know you've been wondering about the nature of light and darkness.
kokborok: Ani khapangni sajwkma, ang saimano nwng uanamansingsa wngjak ah habar pohor tei mwnakni bagwi.

english: It's a big question, and one that scientists have been trying to answer for centuries.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kotor swngmungrok, tei kaisa soisikwrwngrok bisirarok kwrwi kokphirokna bwkhak chaitongmani tongkha.

english: But I think I can give you a simple explanation that will help you understand it a little better.
kokborok: Phiya ani wansukmung ang nono kaisa khakepleng swbaisukrupmani rwi mano je nono buchina chubai mano kaisa kisa kaham bai.

english: Light is a kind of energy that travels in waves.
kokborok: Pohor wngkha kaisa phan prakar je twidurok bising beraimarok.

english: We can see light because it enters our eyes and stimulates the retina, which is a light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye.
kokborok: Chwng pohor nugwi mano tamni hinma omo chini mokolrogo habu tei ah retinano jolirwo, bomo wngkha kaisa pohor-bormanjak sakhanm ah mokolni ungkulugo.

english: The retina sends signals to our brain, which interprets them as images.
kokborok: Ah retina chini botomrok bwkhak phunukmari howu, bomo bohrokno mangpilirok haikhe kokswlaima wngo.

english: Darkness is the absence of light.
kokborok: Mwnakma ah kwrwisani pohor wngkha.

english: When there is no light, we can't see anything.
kokborok: Jephuru aro pohor kwrwi, chwng mungsaphano nukya.

english: Light and darkness are two opposites, but they're also two sides of the same coin.
kokborok: Pohor tei mwnakma wngkha kainwi judarok, phiya bohrok bo kainwi digirokni ah puisa ni solai wngo.

english: Light is needed for us to see, but darkness is also important.
kokborok: Chwngno phunuknani bagwi pohor nango, phiya mwnakma bo nangkukma wngkha.

english: Darkness helps us to rest and sleep.
kokborok: Mwnakma chwngno lenglana tei thuna bwkhak chubao.

english: It also creates a sense of mystery and wonder.
kokborok: Omo bo kaisa sinai simanwi bisingnikok tei uanamasingsa swnamo.

english: So next time you're outside at night, take a moment to appreciate the darkness.
kokborok: Aswkno teiwaisa jora nwng horo phataro phuru, kaisa mukphliksa nadi ah mwnama chajakma bwkhak.

english: It's just as important as light, and it has its own beauty.
kokborok: Omo haino pohor nangmaswk nangkukma, tei omo thani omo sakni naithong tongo.

english: Kindness is one of the most important virtues that a person can possess.
kokborok: Mayachamani abo wngkha borokni bisingo kaisa nangkukmani koboljaknai tongmung kaham.

english: It is the act of being considerate and thoughtful of others, and it is something that can make a real difference in the world.
kokborok: Abono khe bebak borokrokno gosi'ui nao tei uabo uansok rwo, tei abobaino mungsaya mungsle swngcharo swlaimung bo sok phayo.

english: A kind word, a smile, or a helping hand can go a long way to brighten someone's day and make them feel better about themselves.
kokborok: Mayachama kokthai, mwnwima, eba chubana bagwi yak pholokmani abohrok bai khoroksaswk ni sal chwngsa rwi mano tei bohrokni sak baithang khabacharwi mano.

english: There are many different ways to show kindness.
kokborok: Nini mayano phunuknani kwbangma dalbidal lama tongo.

english: You can volunteer your time at a local soup kitchen or homeless shelter, donate to a charity that you believe in, or simply be a good listener to someone who is going through a tough time.
kokborok: Nini kamini nokgantirogo bo jora rwimano eba nok kwrwirokni bagwi bo, nwng poito chamani abotwi ma-pha kwrwirokni tongthayo bo yapharwi mano, eba nwng bui tekto kotor manjaknairokni kokno bo ahaino khwna'ui tongwi mano.

english: No matter how big or small the act, kindness is always appreciated.
kokborok: Nini samung kotor eba kotoi phano wngthwng abo mungsa wngya, mayachamani khe jesa phuru phano kaham.

english: The world needs more kindness.
kokborok: Oh swngchar belai kheno maya nango.

english: It is a simple act that can make a big difference.
kokborok: Abo samung khe kotoise phiya belai kotor swlaimung tubui mano.

english: So next time you see someone who could use a little help, don't hesitate to reach out and lend a hand.
kokborok: Abobaino teisa phuru khe sabono chuba'ui man abono naitukdi, chubana muchungyarok tawngdi tei yak pholokna muchungyarok tawngdi.

english: You might just make their day.
kokborok: Nwng bohrokni salno kaham phano khwlaiwi mano.

english: One classic example of kindness is the story of the Good Samaritan.
kokborok: Kaisa maya chamani phunukmari khe Kaham Samaritan.

english: In this story, a man is beaten and left for dead on the side of the road.
kokborok: O kothoma o, khoroksa borok bujak kha tei thwitwtwi khe lamao yakarwi kwlangjak kha.

english: Two men pass by, but they do not help him.
kokborok: Khoroknwi borok laiwi thangkha, phiya bohrok bono chubaya.

english: However, a third man, who is a Samaritan, stops to help the injured man.
kokborok: Abobaino, waitham o sokphainai borok, bo wng kha Samaritan, a derajak borokno chubana bagwi bathak kha.

english: Organ donation is the process of giving organs or tissues to someone else after death.
kokborok: Sak bokocho yapharmung wngkha kaisa borok khoroksa sak manwi rwmani thwimani yak ulo.

english: It can save lives and improve the quality of life for people who are waiting for transplants.
kokborok: Obo sak manwi swlaina bagwi muchung tongnairokni bagwi lang thangcharwna tei hamcharwna samung kwlayo.

english: There are many different types of organs that can be donated, including kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, and pancreases.
kokborok: Dal bidal ni sakmanwi tongo aro baksa ba yapharwi mano romdi, kidney, liver, bwkha, lungs tei pancrease rok.

english: Tissues that can be donated include bone, skin, heart valves, and corneas.
kokborok: Bokobai rok yapharwi mano romdi, bekreng, bukur, bwkhani valve tei mokolrok.

english: There are many benefits to organ donation.
kokborok: Sak bokocho yapharthani dal bidal hamari manwi mano.

english: For the recipient, organ donation can mean a new lease on life.
kokborok: Yachaknaini bagwi sak bokocho manmani langmani kaisa kwtal langma manthai hai.

english: For the donor, organ donation can be a way to make a difference in the world and help to save lives.
kokborok: Yapharnaini bagwikhe sak bokocho yapharmani bisingtwi o hayungo khoroksa juda borok tei langma mwthangnai wngwi bachaui mano.

english: There are a few things to keep in mind if you are considering organ donation.
kokborok: Kisaswk bwkhao muitu narwkthai tongo tumung nwng sak bokocho yapharna muchungwi tongkhe.

english: First, you must be over the age of 18 and in good health.
kokborok: Puila, nwng umor bisi 18 ni swlai kwbang tei sak kaham tongna nangnai.

english: Second, you must have a valid driver's license or state ID.
kokborok: Ulnwio, nini kaisa gosijak driver ID tongna nangnai.

english: Third, you must sign a consent form to donate your organs.
kokborok: Ulthamo, nwng jesakhebo yasi mari ma rwnai sak bokocho yapharna bagwi.

english: If you are interested in learning more about organ donation, there are many resources available to you.
kokborok: Nwng tumung teibo swrwngna muchungwi tongkhe sak bokocho yapharmungno twywi, oro kwbang lam tongo nini bagwi.

english: You can visit the website of the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) at www.unos.org.
kokborok: Nwng o website o habwi mano United Netwrok for Organ Donation eba www.unos.org.

english: You can also contact your local organ procurement organization (OPO).
kokborok: Hayakheba nwng nini amchaini gana ginio Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) o.

english: Healthy food is not just about eating salads and avoiding junk food.
kokborok: Chathaini sakduk khali kwthwng chamung tei hamya chathai no karma simiya.

english: It's about eating a variety of foods that give your body the nutrients it needs to function properly.
kokborok: Omo juda-juda chathaino chamasiya nini sakni je bolimung tei bahai khe kahamkwrwngkhe samung khai.

english: This includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein.
kokborok: Oro bwthai, muikwthwng, jotto bwthai bwchwlwi tei hankwrwi protein khobjago.

english: There are many different ways to eat healthy, and what works for one person may not work for another.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma juda juda sadukni chakjaknai lama tongo, tei khoroksa borokni sago samung khaikhe tei khoroksa ni sago samung khaigwlak.

english: The key is to find what works for you and make it a part of your lifestyle.
kokborok: Surani mannakhe niniro tamkhe samung khainai tei nini tongmung chamung bwkhak swnamdi.

english: One way to make healthy eating easier is to cook at home more often.
kokborok: Kaisa lama sakdukni chajaknai kwlai khainakhe nogo teibo uramuram khe songdi.

english: This gives you more control over the ingredients in your food and allows you to make healthier choices.
kokborok: Oro nono teibo kaswkma rio nini chathai swraimanwi sakao tei nono sadukma saithani gosirio.

english: Another way to eat healthier is to make small changes to your diet.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lama sakdukjak chathani swnamna hwnkhe nini chamungo kisasa swlaidi.

english: For example, you could start by adding one serving of fruits or vegetables to your meals each day.
kokborok: Phunukamari karwi, nwng jora rwi chengwi mano kaisa bwthai sebugwi eba mwikwthwng nini chathayo salo waisa khobkhe.

english: Or, you could swap out unhealthy snacks for healthier options.
kokborok: Eba, nwng kulumgwnang chamung simi sakdukmano chongwi swlaimano.

kokborok: Paithago, hapang chuwainai rokni langma rokno kaham khaina bwkhak samung khai mano bohrokno swnamtoniwui kahamkum sakduknai bwkhak phiyogwi, phwrwngmani, tei kubun hodarwk samungrok.

english: Farmer suicides are a tragic problem, but they are one that can be solved.
kokborok: Chuwainai sakthwimungrok wngkha kaisa khanangma biyal, phiya aborok wngkha kaisa je kokpaihjak mano.

english: I have been considering the science of heredity and variation in living organisms.
kokborok: Ang ah bosong soisimung tei swlaimani malmata tongmani bising wansukukmani tongkha.

kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa kotor kuthuk hauar, tei kaisa bara koklam bising mankubui omo khaina bwkhak khajamung manya.

english: But I would like to share some of my thoughts on the subject, and perhaps spark a discussion.
kokborok: Phiya ang baksa banta khaina muchungkha ani wansukmungrok ah rwngdal, tei kaisa salaimani hopreng wngthothokrok bwkhak.

english: One of the most important things to understand about heredity is that it is not simply a matter of passing on genes from parents to offspring.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai nangkukma manwirok buchina bwkhak bosongni bagwi wngkha je omo khakeplenhya kaisa manwi genes sakao laimani wngkha ah mapharok bwsabwtwi bwkhak simi.

english: Genes are only one part of the story.
kokborok: Genes wngkha aswkno ah kothomani kaisa bokcho.

english: The environment also plays a major role in determining how an organism develops.
kokborok: Ah habar bo kaisa kotorma tangmung thwngkha khathonma bising bahaikhe kaisa malmata hamrwrwkrok wngkha.

english: For example, two identical twins may have the same genes, but they will not necessarily look or behave the same.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, kainwi sinijka ahpherok ah kosol genes tongwi mano, phiya borok nangmani naima eba ah baksa tongmung wngya.

english: This is because they will have been exposed to different environmental factors during their development.
kokborok: Omo tamni hinba bohrok juda juda habar kusungchwlwirok bwkhak phiyokma wngkha bohrokni hamkrai wngjora phuru.

english: The environment can affect an organism's development in a number of ways.
kokborok: Ah habar kaisa malmatani hamkrai kwbangma lamarok bising nangrwma mano.

english: It can influence the expression of genes, the way that genes interact with each other, and the way that the organism responds to its surroundings.
kokborok: Omo ah genes koksamung kobolmung mano, ah lama je genes khoroksa tei khoroksa bai jugajug khaima, tei ah lama je ah malmata hainohai wngmarok omo khopmanirok bwkhak.

kokborok: Swlaimani malmata tongmani bisng wngkha ah thaihmung kainwi bosong tei habar.

english: No two organisms are exactly alike, even if they are identical twins.
kokborok: Jesaphano kainwi malmata khoropsa kahai wngya, tumungno bohrok sinijak ahpherrok wngkha.

english: This variation is essential for evolution.
kokborok: Oh swlaima wngkha nangnai philjakmungni bagwi.

kokborok: Sengkrakrok wngkha kwrwng kwrwng thaini bodol ni borokrog, phiya bohrokni naharmung kaisa no: bohrokni langma no kaisa ari o yapharjak bohrokni hakotor no mwthang na bagwi.

kokborok: Bohrokni sakphang tei uansokma no belai kwrak khe tongna nango, tei bohrok dol thansa khe samung tangna rwngna nang wano.

kokborok: Tabok hai jora o, swlai jagwi thang kha.

kokborok: Bohrok kaisa sinai simana'ui hoda swnamna bwkhak chubao tei borok no teibo kwchagthotok tei boromjak uansukma swnamo.

english: There are many different types of good manners, but some of the most important ones include being polite, being respectful, being honest, being considerate of others, and being responsible.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kwbangma juda juda sapokthaihrok tongmung kahamrok, phiya baksa ah belai nangkukma kaisarok khobma tongkwchang wngdok, boromrwjak wngdok, tongkwthar wngdok, kubunrok larojak wnngdok, tei bojak.

english: This includes saying "please" and "thank you," holding the door open for others, and listening attentively when someone is speaking.
kokborok: Omo "khapur" tei "hambai nono," samani khobmarok ah duklam khulukma rommani kubunrokni bagwi, tei jephuru khoroksaswk koksai tongkha khunjukainai khwnamani.

english: Being respectful means treating others with dignity and respect, regardless of their age, race, gender, religion, or social status.
kokborok: Boromjak wngdok kokmarok kubunrokno saknangmani borom tei borom rwma bai, khauraya bohrokni omor, bosong, sir, tongthar, eba hodarwk tongborom.

english: This includes not making fun of others, not interrupting them when they are speaking, and listening to their opinions even if you disagree with them.
kokborok: Omo kubunrokno chengta khlaimai khobyawui, jephuru bohrok koksai tongphuru bohrokno kasuyawui, tei bohrokni khachongmarokno khwnamani ahaino tumung nwng bohrok bai gosiya phano.

english: Being honest means being truthful and sincere.
kokborok: Tongkwthar wngdok kokmarok kubuikuk tei sakthar wngdok.

english: This includes not lying or cheating, and being upfront about your intentions.
kokborok: Omo tala saya eba phemlokmani khobyawui, tei khachongmungrok bagwi sakbwskang wngdok.

english: Being considerate of others means being thoughtful and helpful.
kokborok: Larokjak wngdok kubunrok kokmarok wngdok wansukmung tei chubamung.

english: This includes being aware of the needs of others and doing what you can to make them feel comfortable.
kokborok: Omo saimanri wngdok khobmarok ah kubunrokni nangmarok tei nwng tamo bohrokno tongthotok wansukma swnamma bwkha khlaimani.

english: Teacher, I think friends are one of the most important things in life.
kokborok: Phwrwngnai, ang wansukha bayaprok wngkha kaisa belai nangkukma manwirok langmani bagwi.

english: They're the people who are there for us when we need them, who make us laugh, and who help us grow as people.
kokborok: Aro borok tongo je chini bagwi tongo jephuru chwng bohrokno nango, je chwngno mwnwi rio, tei je chwngno borok haikhe tornani chubao.

english: When I was younger, I was kind of immature.
kokborok: Jephuru ang chwrai phuru, ang kaisa torsukya hai.

english: I didn't really understand the importance of friendship.
kokborok: Ang kubuino buchiya bayapsong ni nangkukmano.

english: I thought it was all about having fun and doing things together.
kokborok: Ang wansukha omo jotto tongthok tongmani hwnwi tei thansa khai manwirok khailaimani.

english: But as I've gotten older, I've realized that friendship is so much more than that.
kokborok: Phiya ang haino torwi thangkha, ang saimankha je bayapsong wngkha aboni slai teibo kwbang.

english: It's about having someone to talk to who understands you, who you can trust, and who you can count on.
kokborok: Omo kaisa khoroksaswk kok sajaknai tongmani bwkhak je nono buchinai, je sabono nwng poito khaimano, tei nwng saboni sakao yakar mano.

english: My friends have been there for me through thick and thin.
kokborok: Ani bayaprok ani bagwi rwja tei kepher bisingtwih tongwi tongo.

english: They've seen me at my best and my worst, and they've always loved and supported me.
kokborok: Borok ano ani kahama tei hamya phuru nukjak, tei borok ano homnino hamjago tei twichurujak khayo ano.

english: They've helped me through tough times, and they've made me laugh when I've needed it most.
kokborok: Abo ano ani kutuk jorarogo twih chubakha, tei bohrok ano mwnwi rio jephuru ang omo kwbang nangjak tongphuru.

english: I know that I can always count on my friends.
kokborok: Ang saimano je ang hominino ani bayaprokni sakao yakar mano.

english: They're the people who I can be myself around, and who I know will always be there for me.
kokborok: Bohrok mohai borok je ang saksak yaksiyagra tongwi mano, tei je ang saimano ani bagwi homino tongnai.

english: I'm so grateful for their friendship, and I know that my life would be much poorer without them.
kokborok: Ang belai khatung khajak bohrokni bayapsongni bagwi, tei ang saimano je ani langma bohrok kwrwi khe kwrwikuk wngkhamu.

english: When my husband acquired his first computer, the technology was still in its infancy.
kokborok: Jephuru ani bwsai bini puila computer mankha, ah technology tabukbo omo chengjora bising siko.

english: The computer was a large, bulky machine that took up a significant amount of space in our living room.
kokborok: Ah computer kotor, hilikma kol je kwbangma thai nakha chini tongmani nokbisingo.

english: It was also very expensive, and we had to save up for several months to be able to afford it.
kokborok: Abo wngkha belai morokjak, tei chwng amono naimanna bwkhak dalbidal talrok romwi khatina nangkha.

english: My husband was very excited about his new computer, and he spent hours learning how to use it.
kokborok: Ani bwsai belai tongthokjak wngkha bini kwtal computer ni bagwi, tei bo damrwirok swrwngmanio jora lairio bahaikhe omo no phwnangna hwnwi.

english: He quickly became an expert in using the computer to do research, write papers, and play games.
kokborok: Bo daktino khoroksa kwrwng wngwi thangkha phwnangmani bising twi ah computer rutukrwk khaima bwkhak, laihrok swina, tei thwngmung thwngnarok.

english: I was not as interested in using the computer, but I did appreciate the convenience of being able to use it to pay bills and do other tasks that used to require a trip to the library or store.
kokborok: Ang aswk ol manjakya ah computer no phwnangmani bising, phiya ang ah suvidha ni bagwi chajakma wngjakha amo bo phwnangwi rwthairok rwi manma bwkhak tei kubun samungrok khaima je kaisa bijapnok eba khatinok bwkhak beraitongthok bwkhak phwnangjak.

english: As the years went by, computers became more and more affordable and accessible.
kokborok: Bisirok thangma bai, computer rok teibo naimanma tei sogwinani wngkha.

english: They also became smaller and more powerful.
kokborok: Borok chikonsa tei teibo phangwnang bo wngkha.

english: This made them more popular with people of all ages, including women.
kokborok: Omo bohrok no teibo jotto omorokni borok bai luku hamjakma swnamkha, bwrwima rokno khobwinai.

english: I eventually became interested in using computers to do things like create presentations for work and manage my finances.
kokborok: Ang paithago computerrok ni bising phwnangwi manwirok khainani iko samungni bagwi presentationrok swnamnani tei ani rangmairok naikol bwkhak ol manmung.

english: Today, computers and electronics are a part of our everyday lives.
kokborok: Tini, computers tei electronics wngkha kaisa bokcho chini sal thwngwi tongmarok.

english: We use them for work, school, entertainment, and communication.
kokborok: Chwng bohrokno samung, rwngnok, tongthokmung, tei kwrwnglaimani bagwi phwnango.

english: They have made our lives easier and more convenient in many ways.
kokborok: Borok chini langmarokno kwlaikuk tei teibo suvidha kwbangma lamarokni bising swnamkha.

english: Before the invention of the light bulb, people used candles and oil lamps to light their homes.
kokborok: Ah pohor phlikchati swnamjakmani swkang, borok homchang tei thok chati bohrokni nokrogo pohor rwma bwkhak phwnangkha.

english: These sources of light were not very efficient and they often produced a lot of smoke.
kokborok: Oh pohorni yaphangrok belai yaksrai wngya wngkha tei borok uramuram kwbang hoku thaihrwkha.

english: The invention of the light bulb changed everything.
kokborok: Ah pohor phlikchati swnamjakmani jottomanwi swlaikhak.

english: It allowed people to have more light at night and it also made it possible to work and play in the dark.
kokborok: Omo borokno yapharma bwkhak horo teibo pohor tongna tei omo samung wngmanma bwkhak swnamkha tei ah mwnak bising thwngkha.

english: One way to save electricity is to turn off lights when you leave a room.
kokborok: Kaisa lama phereng khatina bwkhak wngkha pohorrokno mwthakma jephuru nwng khotol yakaro.

english: Another way to save electricity is to use energy-efficient light bulbs.
kokborok: Teikaisa lama pherang khatima bwkhak wngkha yaksrai-phan pohor phlikchatirok phwnangma bwkhak.

english: Energy-efficient light bulbs use less electricity than regular light bulbs and they last longer.
kokborok: Yaksrai-phang pohor phlikchati rok sabrumbrum pohor phlikchatirokni slai kisa pherang phwnangjago tei bohrok kwdwk tikio.

english: Children can help save electricity by turning off lights when they leave a room and by unplugging appliances when they are not in use.
kokborok: Chwrairok pherang khati mano pohorrok mwthakmani bai jephuru bohrok kaisa khotol yakaro tei manwirok khakma wngma jephuru borok phwnangjakya.

english: They can also help by being aware of the amount of electricity they use.
kokborok: Bohrok ah thikemung pherang bohrok phwnangma sijak wngjora wngjak bai bo chubai mano.

english: Saving electricity is important because it helps to reduce our carbon footprint.
kokborok: Pherang khatimani wngkha nangkukma tamhinba omo chini hangar yaprimari khaina bwkhak chubamarok.

english: When we use less electricity, we produce less greenhouse gases.
kokborok: Jephuru chwng kisa pherang phwnango, chwng kisa nokkwkhwrang phap thaihmung.

english: Greenhouse gases are one of the main causes of climate change.
kokborok: Nokkwkhwrang phaprok wngkha kaisa ah kwchar phermarok nokbartwibar swlaima.

english: By saving electricity, we can help to protect the environment and we can also save money.
kokborok: Pherang khatimani bai, chwng ah habar mwthangma bwkhak chubai mano tei chwng rang bo khati mano.

english: Matchmakers in traditional societies played a vital role in bringing couples together.
kokborok: Horkathi swnamlaima jorao amchayo hiksongnwi thepa laimani samung belai kotor khe nukjago.

english: They were often respected members of the community, and their advice was highly valued.
kokborok: Bohrokni hodao bohrok belai borom rwjago, tei bohrokni khoraimarok bo belai yachakjago.

english: Matchmakers would consider a variety of factors when making a match, including the social status of the families involved, the financial situation of the couple, and their religious beliefs.
kokborok: Horkathi swnamnairok bebak phaising twi no yachajago, amchayo boni nukhung bomo hai, hiksongnwi ni ajemung bo, tei bohrok bo tongkwthar no poito khwlai abotwirog.

english: They would also take into account the personal qualities of each individual, such as their personality, education, and appearance.
kokborok: Bohrokni baithangni rwngmungno bo naijago, boni tongmung chamungrog, boni rwngrem no twywi bo, tei sakdukrok bo naijago.

english: The process of matchmaking could take months or even years.
kokborok: Horkathi swnam mani abo talnwi taltham phano nangwi mano eba khe bisi phano nangwi mano.

english: During this time, the matchmaker would get to know the couple and their families.
kokborok: O jora o, horkathi swnamnairok hiksongnwirok sini layo tei bohrokni nukhung no bo sinijago.

english: They would also arrange for the couple to meet each other on several occasions.
kokborok: Bohrok hiksongnwi malaijaknai jora bo rwjago jora kahamrogo khe.

english: If the couple felt that they were compatible, the matchmaker would then begin the formal negotiations between the families.
kokborok: Hiksongnwirok bohrok bataijak mahai wngjak khe, horkathi swnamnairok bohrokni nukhung bisingo salaina cheng layo.

english: Once a deal was reached, the couple would be married in a traditional ceremony.
kokborok: Waisa gosewi na khe, o kokrwlaijak hiksongnwirok kaijagwi mano bohrokni hukumu panda o.

english: Matchmaking in traditional societies resulted in lasting and fulfilling relationships.
kokborok: Horkathi swnam mani samungni bwthai abo amchayo chobo choro tei halog bolaithani swpwngo.

english: The couples were often well-suited to each other, and they had the support of their families and community.
kokborok: O hiksongnwirok bohrok kiching borok belaino gothoklayo, tei bohrokni nukhung tei hodasong bo gose bayo.

english: This helped to ensure that they would be able to weather any challenges that came their way.
kokborok: Abo baino bohrok gosesogwi mano bohrokni lama o jwngjal phaiwi bo.

english: While matchmaking is no longer as common as it once was, it still plays an important role in some traditional societies.
kokborok: Horkathi swnam mani puila phuru ni hai aswk khwlai jakliya, baksa buksu ni amchayo khe tabok bo wngwi tong kho.

english: While there are still challenges to be overcome, the potential benefits of nuclear energy are significant.
kokborok: Jephuru aro tabukbo baitaimarok bwkhak mechenrwma tongo, ah phangwnang manmarirok nuclear phan nangkukmani wngkha.

english: One of the biggest advantages of nuclear energy is its stability.
kokborok: Kaisa ah kotorma subhidarok nuclear phan wngkha omoni kwrakama.

english: Nuclear power plants can operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, regardless of the weather or other conditions.
kokborok: Nuclear phan phangrok 24 damrok kaisa salo chaluk mano, 7 salrok kaisa hatio, khaurarya ah salbar eba kubun tonghalokrok.

english: This means that they can provide a reliable source of electricity, even when other sources are unavailable.
kokborok: Omo kokmarok je bohrok kaisa pherangni puitgnang yaphang, haino jephuru kubun yaphangrok manthokya wngkhe.

english: Nuclear energy also has a relatively low carbon footprint.
kokborok: Nuclear phan kaisa solaima tongo bacher hangar yaprimari.

english: When compared to fossil fuels, nuclear energy produces much less greenhouse gas emissions.
kokborok: Jephuru tongrwk mari supungmungrok sujakma bwkhak, nuclear phan duna bwthaihrok belai kisasa nokkwkhwrang phap tikhlaimarok.

english: This makes it a more environmentally friendly option for generating electricity.
kokborok: Omo kaisa teibo habar bayapma saimung pherang achairwmani bagwi omo sanmarok.

english: Of course, there are also challenges to be overcome with nuclear energy.
kokborok: Aow, aro bo bataimungrok tongo mecherwma bwkhak nuclear phan bai.

english: The most significant of these is the issue of nuclear waste.
kokborok: Ah jottoni slai nangmani oh wngkha ah nuclear phiyakma swirwma.

english: Nuclear waste is radioactive and must be stored safely for many years.
kokborok: Nuclear phiyakma wngkha radioactive tei kwbangma bisirokni bagwi katimung khatijak wngna nango.

english: However, there are a number of promising technologies being developed to deal with this issue.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro kasa lombor swmaini tanseprok hamkrai wngjak tongo oh swirwma bai lenden bwkhak.

english: Despite the challenges, the potential benefits of nuclear energy are significant.
kokborok: Tophano ah bataimungrok, ah phangnang manmarirok nuclear phan nangkukma wngkha.

english: It is a clean, reliable, and efficient source of energy that can help us to meet our growing energy needs.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa kwchwng, tei kwrwng phan yaphang je chwngno malaima bwkhak chubai mano chini phan nangmarok tormani.

english: I think that the use of the word "mother" is often limited by our expectations of what a mother should be.
kokborok: Ang wansukmakhe haisi "buma" oh kokthai phwnangjakmani khe chini uramuram wansukma ari o buma tamo bahai wngnai hwnwi.

english: We expect mothers to be selfless, nurturing, and always putting their children first.
kokborok: Chwng wansugo bumarok belai sakthor, nurturing, tei homnino bohrokni slai swkang bwsarokno tonio.

english: This can be a very difficult role to live up to, and it can lead to mothers feeling guilty or inadequate if they don't feel like they're doing enough.
kokborok: Omo thangwi thangnani bagwi tangmung 3 wngwi mano, tei omo bumarokno uansukphan chaya khwlaimano, eba bangthayai bohrok uansuskyai bohrok belai khaitongmani.

english: I think it's important to remember that mothers are just people, and they're not perfect.
kokborok: Ang wansukha omo muitonarakna nangkukmani je kubuino bumarok bo borokno, tei bohrokbo aswk chasukjakya.

english: They're going to make mistakes, and they're going to have moments when they're not sure what they're doing.
kokborok: Bohrokbo chayarok khwlai mano, tei bohrokbo thangwi phliksa manwi mano jephuru bohrok wngnaino siyai bohrok tamo khai tong.

english: That's okay.
kokborok: Abobo wngo.

english: We all make mistakes.
kokborok: Chwng jottono chaya khwlayo.

english: What matters is that we learn from them and try to do better next time.
kokborok: Tamo matters khai hwnkhe je chwng bohrokni thani swrwngma bai tei waisa phuru teibo kahamkhe khaina hwnwi.

english: I also think it's important to remember that there is no one right way to be a mother.
kokborok: Ang hai hin wansukha omo muitonarakna nangkukma hwnkhe je aro mungsa juda kubui lama kwrwi buma wngna hwnkhe.

english: Every mother is different, and every child is different.
kokborok: Jotto buma no pherlayo, tei jotto chwrai rokbo pherlayo.

english: What works for one family might not work for another.
kokborok: Kaisa nukhungo samung khaiphano tei kubuniro khaigwlak.

english: So don't be afraid to experiment and find what works for you and your family.
kokborok: Hwnkhe takiridi experiment khainani tei naitugwi karidi nini bagwi tamo samung cha tei nini nukhungo.

english: Being a mother is a wonderful and rewarding experience, but it can also be challenging.
kokborok: Buma wngwi belai no uanamasingsa tei rwmnani saimanani, phiya omo bataimani bo wngmano.

english: Wild rabbits are a fascinating and often misunderstood species.
kokborok: Boijakya khorgo rok wngkha muani khlaimung tei uramuram buchimanya dahl.

english: They are found in a variety of habitats around the world, and their populations can fluctuate dramatically depending on the availability of food and water.
kokborok: Bohrokno hayungni yaksiyagra juda kaisa tongmarok naitukmano, tei bohrokni banagmarok ernai ninangwi thungnukmarok sakboknai chahthai bai twi manthokkhe.

english: One of the most interesting things about wild rabbits is their ability to adapt to their surroundings.
kokborok: Kaisa suk khasrangjak manwirok boijakya khorgoni bagwi bohrok khopmani bwkhak bohrok pharimung bwkhak naharmung.

english: They are able to survive in a wide range of climates, and they can eat a variety of foods.
kokborok: Bohrok wngkha kuar rem nobartwibar rogo thangwi mano, tei bohrok juda chamungrok chai mano.

english: This adaptability has allowed them to become one of the most successful mammals on the planet.
kokborok: Oh naharmungrok bohrokno oph hagirini jottoni swlai manjak abuktwi nwngnai mal hwnwi gosikha.

english: Unfortunately, wild rabbits are also a popular target for hunters.
kokborok: Talikhahamya, boijakya khorgorok wngkha sikarirokni bagwi kaichommung luku hamjakjak.

english: They are hunted for their fur, meat, and even for sport.
kokborok: Borok sikar khaijakmani hwnkhe bohrokni bikhumu, muihan, tei haino thwngma rokni bagwi.

english: This hunting has led to a decline in wild rabbit populations in some areas.
kokborok: Oh sikhar khaimani boiyjakya khorgoni bangmanirok khairwkha baksa ari bwkhak.

english: In addition to hunting, wild rabbits also face a number of other threats, including habitat loss, climate change, and disease.
kokborok: Sikari jora rwmung bai, boijakya khorgorok haino kubun sikrimung bai bwskang malayo, tongmanma kwmamano khobwinai, nobartwibar swlaima, tei bemar.

english: Habitat loss is a major problem for wild rabbits, as they need a lot of space to live.
kokborok: Tongmanma kwmama hwnkhe boijkaya khogorokni bagwi kaisa kotor biyal, tamni hwnkhe bohrok tongna bagwi kwbang thai nango.

english: Climate change is also a concern, as it is causing the habitats of wild rabbits to change.
kokborok: Nobartwibar swlaijakma bo kaisa wanamasinja, tamni khe omo boijakya khorgo rokni pherwi tongmani swlaijago.

english: Disease can also be a major problem for wild rabbits, as they are susceptible to a number of different diseases.
kokborok: Bemar kaisa boijakya khorgo rokni bagwi kotor biyal wngwi mano, bohrok wngkha khanagkrak juda juda bemarokni lombor bwkhak.

english: Despite all of these threats, wild rabbits are still a common sight in many parts of the world.
kokborok: Tophano jotto sikrimarok tongphano, boijkaya khorgorok tabukb hayungni kwbangma bwkhak nwnwi nukjago.

english: The coming season is a time for celebration and joy.
kokborok: Palaijaknai tei tongthokjaknai jora ni mol phaiwi tongo.

english: However, it is also a time for increased risk of illness.
kokborok: Haiphano, o jora o se kulum-kwsa wngkukmani bo jora.

english: By following some simple health and hygiene tips, you can help to keep yourself and your family healthy and safe.
kokborok: Kisisa sak hamkhwrai tei kwchwng khe tongjaknai raida no loi khwlaima bisingtwi, sakno tei sakni nukhungno kaham tei bermar ni phiyogwi mano.

english: One of the most important things you can do to stay healthy is to wash your hands frequently.
kokborok: Jotto ni swlai sak kaham tongna bagwi nangkuk mani wngkha yak su mani se.

english: This is especially important during the coming season, when cold and flu viruses are more likely to spread.
kokborok: Kuchuk-kongraini virusrok pirjagwi mano, aboni bagwi phainai mol o khe yak suna nangsogo.

english: Be sure to wash your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially after using the bathroom, before eating, and after being around sick people.
kokborok: Chakhwi budul tei twi bai yak su phuru Mukpli 20 swk jora nadi, abobo nwng khithai thangmani yagulo, chana swkang, tei kulumrok bai malaiwi phai mani yagulo.

english: You should also avoid touching your face, as this can spread germs.
kokborok: Nini mwkhang o ahai no tatang di yaksuya swkang, abo yong habwi mano.

english: If you do touch your face, be sure to wash your hands immediately.
kokborok: Nwng nini mwkhang no tangna khe, swkang yak suwi nagra di.

english: It is also important to get enough sleep.
kokborok: Mwktrwi kwpulung nana bo belai nango.

english: When you are tired, your immune system is not as strong, making you more susceptible to illness.
kokborok: Nwng lengwi tongphuru, nini bisingni phan aswk kwrakya, aboni bagwi nono teibo sak dera rw wi mano.

english: Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per night.
kokborok: 7-8 dam swk hor burumno thuna chaitok di.

english: Eating a healthy diet is another important part of staying healthy.
kokborok: Chamung kaham chamani bo tei kaisa nangkuk mani sak kaham tongna bagwi.

english: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can help to boost your immune system and keep you feeling your best.
kokborok: Bwthai manwi no kwbang chamani, mwikwthwngrog, tei mairok chamani nini sakno kwrak khwlayo tei omo se jotto ni swlai kahamkugo.

english: Studying abroad is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to immerse yourself in a new culture, learn a new language, and make lifelong friends.
kokborok: Kuchuk berem o pore mani abo langma o waisa se jora phayo sakno kwtal hukumu bai gwdalwi tongna bagwi, kwtal kok swrwngwi mano, tei langma kolok ni bagwi kiching swnamwi mano.

english: It's also a great way to boost your resume and set yourself apart from the competition.
kokborok: Abo wngkha kaisa sakni ni sinimungno kuchugo tisajaknai lamase tei sakno batailaimung ni yakni yogwi mano.

english: There are many different programs to choose from, so you can find one that fits your interests and budget.
kokborok: Kwbangma dalbidal lama saiwi najaknai tongo, aroni bisingo je nwng chajakmani tei chukmani abono kaisa rutugwi namano.

english: Whether you want to study in a major city or a small town, there's a program out there for you.
kokborok: Nwng dholi kotor o de swrwngna muchung eba dholi bwsa o de muchung, aro nini bagwi lama tongo.

kokborok: Alena bini logi a bwtwi no nogo twlangkha tei bini bupha no phunukha.

english: And I am grateful for the opportunities that I have had to travel, to meet new people, and to learn about different cultures.

kokborok: Thaichuk: Bwthaihrokni bubagra.

english: If there was one fruit that could be considered the king of fruits, it would be the mango.
kokborok: Tumungno aro kaisa bwthaih je ah bwthaihrokni raja gosijak wngwi mano, omo thaichuk wngwi mano.

english: This delicious and nutritious fruit is enjoyed by people all over the world, and for good reason.
kokborok: Oh kothok tei chahkohlom bwthaih jotto hayung saka rwgwi borok bai tongthojak, tei kaham karoni bagwi.

english: Mangoes are a good source of vitamins A, C, and E, as well as potassium and fiber.
kokborok: Thaichukrok wngkha kaisa yaphang kaham chahthaihphanrok A, C, tei E, iko haino postassium tei fiber.

english: They are also low in calories and fat, making them a healthy snack or dessert option.
kokborok: Bohrok calories tei bupham bising hacher, bohrokno kaisa sakdukma chahmung eba olo chahmung saimung bo wngo.

english: Mangoes are native to India, but they are now grown in many tropical and subtropical regions around the world.
kokborok: Thaichukrok Indiani achaiha wngkha, phiya bohrok wngkha kwbangma tropical tei subtropical bwkhakrok ah hayungni yaksiyagra bising tabuk torkha.

english: There are hundreds of different varieties of mangoes, each with its own unique flavor and texture.
kokborok: Aro thaichukrokni dalbidal juda juda rarok tongo, omo sakani solya thokmung tei taknai bai thwgwi.

english: Some of the most popular varieties include the Alphonso, the Kent, and the Haden.
kokborok: Baksa ah jottoni slai lukuk hamjakak dalbidalrok khobma wngkha Alphonso, Kent, tei Haden.

english: Mangoes are typically eaten fresh, but they can also be used in a variety of dishes, such as salads, smoothies, and curries.
kokborok: Thaichukrok hainohai kwthar chajakha, phiya bohrok kaisa dalbidal chahmarok, mwkhwihrok, smoothes, tei muirok bising phwnangjak bo mano.

english: They can also be dried, canned, or made into juice.
kokborok: Bohrok kwran, canned, eba bwtwi bising swnam bo mano.

english: Mangoes are a versatile and delicious fruit that can be enjoyed in many different ways.
kokborok: Thaichukrok kaisa kwbang sinai tei kothok bwthaih wngkha je kwbangma juda juda lamarok bising twih tongthokjak mano.

english: They are a healthy and nutritious snack or dessert option, and they can also be used in a variety of dishes.
kokborok: Bohrok wngkha kaisa sakdukma tei chahkohlom chahmung eba olo chahmung saima, tei bohrok kaisa dalbidal chahmarok bisingtwih phwnangjak bo mano.

english: If you have never tried a mango, I encourage you to do so.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng kaisa thaichuk waisa phano chaitok naiyakhukhe, ang nono khaina bwkhak khatungrimung rio.

english: Addiction: A Story of Hope and Recovery Addiction is a serious problem that affects millions of people around the world.
kokborok: Loi wngmani: Kaisa kothoma khajamung tei loi wngmani hamnani wngkha kaisaa kubui kebengmung je chirasairok borok ah hayung yaksiyagra nangrwmarok.

english: It can be a difficult and isolating experience, but there is hope for recovery.
kokborok: Omo kaisa 3 tei judakhai tonmani saimanma, phiya aro hamnami bagwi kajamung tongo.

english: In this article, we will tell the story of a person who struggled with addiction but was able to overcome it.
kokborok: Oh koksopn bising, chwng khoroksa borokni bagwi kothoma kaisa sanai je loi wngmani bai khapharjak phiya obono mechenma bwkwhak phaimankha.

english: We will explore the different factors that contributed to their addiction, the challenges they faced in recovery, and the things that helped them get through it.
kokborok: Chwng kwtal karima ah juda juda bwchwlwirok naiyanw je bohrokni loi wngmani bwkhak khanglaijak, ah bataimungrok bohrok hamani bising dadakdidik wngmani, tei ah manwirok je bohrokno omo bising twih mana chubachu khaimani.

english: Our story begins with a young woman named Sarah.
kokborok: Chini kothoma kaisa bwrwima sikli mung Sarah bai chengjago.

english: Sarah was a bright and talented student, but she struggled with anxiety and depression.
kokborok: Sarah wngkha kaisa kwchwng tei manphanjak rwngswrwngnai, phiya bo khapharjak khachuk-buchuk tei khakwbaimani bai.

english: She began using drugs and alcohol to self-medicate, and soon her addiction spiraled out of control.
kokborok: Bo kephekbithirok tei arak sak-bithi rwma bwkhak phwnangnani chengkha, tei daktino bini loi wngmani spiraled kaswkma baira wngthangkha.

english: Sarah lost her job, her relationships, and her home.
kokborok: Sarah bini samung kwmajakha, bini halokbokmarok, tei bini nok.

english: She was homeless and living on the streets when she finally decided to get help.
kokborok: Bo nokthai kwrwi wngkha tei lamarogo ma tongkha jephuru bo paithago kokchapkha bo chubama nanai hwnwi.

english: Sarah entered a treatment program, where she learned about the root causes of her addiction and how to cope with her emotions in a healthy way.
kokborok: Sarah kaisa saknaimung pandarem hapkha, aro bo swrwngkha bini loi wngmani yaphang bagwirok tei bahaikhe bini khanangjak no samung chokrwnai bwkhak kaisa sakduma lama bising.

english: She also made new friends who were supportive of her recovery.
kokborok: Bo kwtal bayaprok bo swnamkha je bini hamnani no twichuruma khayo.

english: After several months of treatment, Sarah was ready to start her new life.
kokborok: Saknaimung dalbidal talrok olo, Sarah bini kwtal langma chengna tiyar wngkha.

english: She got a job, moved into an apartment, and began to rebuild her relationships.
kokborok: Bo kaisa samung mankhaa, kaisa nokthai bisingo lorikha, tei bo bini chomimanirokno teisa tisana bwkhak chengkha.

english: One day, a group of animals were gathered at the watering hole, enjoying a few drinks.
kokborok: Salsa, kaisa malmatarokni motha ah twi hakor kuthumkha, kisa nwngmarok tongthogwi.

english: As the drinks flowed, the animals began to get competitive.
kokborok: Iko ah nwngmarok kochokheno, ah malmatarok bataina bwkhak chengkha.
