english: They started racing each other to see who could drink the most alcohol.
kokborok: Bohrok batai kachikmani chengkha kubun thwgwi naina bwkhak sabo jottoni slai arak nwngwi man.

english: The competition was fierce, and the animals were getting more and more intoxicated.
kokborok: Ah bataimani wngkha kirimasingsa, tei ah malmatarok teibo tei teibo phekrwjak manwi tongkha.

english: Finally, one of the animals, a deer, could drink no more.
kokborok: Paithago, khoroksa malmatarokni bising, kaisa mwnwi, tei nwngwi manliya.

english: He stumbled away from the watering hole and collapsed.
kokborok: Bo goirok thang ah twi hakorni tei lengkha.

english: The other animals laughed and continued to drink.
kokborok: Ah kubun malmatarok mwnwikha tei choyawui nwngkha.

english: But then, the deer started to convulse.
kokborok: Phiya hwnkhe, ah mwnwi jangrima bwkha chengkha.

english: He had alcohol poisoning, and he was dying.
kokborok: Bo arak thwima bithimani wngkha, tei bo thwina nai tongkha.

english: The other animals realized what they had done, and they were horrified.
kokborok: Ah kubun malmatarok termankha je bohrok tamo khaikha hwnwi, tei borok kirijakha.

english: They tried to help the deer, but it was too late.
kokborok: Bohrok ah mwswi no chubana bwkha chaithokha, phiya omo belai lerwi thangkha.

english: He died a few minutes later.
kokborok: Bo kisa swrapsa olo thwikha.

english: The animals were all very sad, and they vowed never to drink alcohol again.
kokborok: Ah malmatarok jotto belai mokjak wngkha, tei bohrok swmai thangkha bohrok tei arak nwngliya hwnwi.

english: Childhood games are a special part of our lives.
kokborok: Chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha chini langmarokni bagwi kaisa mahmlai bokcho,

english: They provide us with hours of fun and laughter, and they help us learn important life lessons.
kokborok: Bohrok chwngno thongthok tei mwnwimarok damrwirok bai bago, tei bohrok chwngno nangkukma langma poriremrok swrwngna bagwi chubao.

english: Some of the most popular childhood games include hide-and-seek, tag, jump rope, and marbles.
kokborok: Baksa ah belai lulu hamjajak chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha huijakma, dwkhwi buchukni budul, dwkhwi barsuma, tei marbels khobwi.

english: These games are simple to play and require very few materials, making them perfect for kids of all ages.
kokborok: Oh thwngmungrok wngkha khakepleng bwkhak thwngma tei belai kisa manwi-khwnwirok nangma, bohrokno jotto omorrokni bagwi chasukjak swnamani.

english: In addition to being fun, childhood games can also help children develop their social and motor skills.
kokborok: Jora rwmung bising tongthok wngjak bwkhak, chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok chwrairokno borokni hodarwk hamkrai tei motor yaksrairok bo chubai mano.

english: Hide-and-seek teaches children how to cooperate with others and how to follow directions.
kokborok: Huijakma chwrairokno phwrwngo bahai kubunrok bai chubalaima bwkhak tei bahai bwkhangrogo rwtharma.

english: Tag helps children develop their coordination and agility.
kokborok: Dwkhwi buchukni budul rok chwrairokno bohrokni raibaisamung tei agility hamkrayo chubamarok.

english: Jump rope helps children improve their balance and rhythm.
kokborok: Dwkhwi barsuma chwrairokno bohrokni ojon tei kokyapri hamrwma chubamarok.

english: And marbles teaches children how to compete and how to deal with winning and losing.
kokborok: Tei marbles chwrairokno bahai khe baitaina bwkhak phwrwngmarok tei bahaikhe jitimani tei harimani bai phaiphalmung bwkhak.

english: Childhood games are also a great way for kids to connect with their friends and family.
kokborok: Chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha kaisa kotorkuar lama chwrairokni bagwi bohrokni bayaprok tei nukhung bai kwrwngma bwkhak.

english: When you play a game with someone, you're creating a shared experience that can bring you closer together.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng khoroksaswk bai kaisa thwngmung thwngo, nwng kaisa saimanjak bakjak swnamani je nono thansa ganarwk khai tubui mano.

english: And when you play a game with your family, you're not only having fun, you're also learning how to work together and how to support each other.
kokborok: Tei jephuru nwng nini nukhung bai kaisa thwngmung thwngo nwng haino tongthok simi ya, nwng twbo swrwngmani bahaikhe thansa samung khainai tei bahai khoroksa tei khoroksa no twichuruma khainai.

english: Unfortunately, many of the classic childhood games that we grew up playing are no longer as popular as they once were.
kokborok: Talikhahamya kwbangma ah hamkuk chwrai phangsini thwngmungrok je chwng torwi thwngwi phaimani bohrok tabuk aswk luluk hamjajak wngya agi waisa wngwi phaima hai.

english: I am honored to be writing to you today.
kokborok: Ang nono tini swihormani bagwi boromjakha.

english: I am a huge fan of your work, and I was inspired by your essay "No Extra Movement", where you discuss the difference between cool weather and freezing cold weather.
kokborok: Ang nini samungni kotor bhokto, tei ang nini kokbwkhal bai khaswrango "kunu lorima bara kwrwi", jerw nwng pherlaimani salaima bisngtwi kwchang nobarhalok eba kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok.

english: I would like to share my own thoughts on this topic.
kokborok: Ang oh kokbwkhalo ani sak-sak wansukma bwkhak rina muchungo.

english: Cool weather is refreshing and invigorating.
kokborok: Kwchang nobarholok belai no swrangphirimani tei phanrimani.

english: It can be a welcome relief from the heat of summer, and it can create a sense of calm and tranquility.
kokborok: Kutung tungplama simi holirwmung lamsogwi mano tei omo sina simanwi siringsiring tei kwchangthotok swnam mano.

english: Freezing cold weather, on the other hand, is harsh and unforgiving.
kokborok: Kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok, tei kubun digi, belaino rakphereh tei nakarmung riya.

english: It can be dangerous, and it can make it difficult to stay warm and comfortable.
kokborok: Omo kirimasingsa wngmano, tei omo 3 takutung tei khasrangwi mano.

english: One of the biggest differences between cool weather and freezing cold weather is the way it affects our bodies.
kokborok: Kaisa kotorma pherlaimani bising kwchang nokbarhalok tei kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok wngkha mohai omo chini sakno khoti khayo.

english: When it is cool, our bodies are able to maintain their temperature relatively easily.
kokborok: Jephuru kwchango, chini sakrok kaham khai tonimano tei bohrokni temparature no kwlaikhe halogwi.

english: We may need to wear a sweater or jacket, but we can still stay active and comfortable.
kokborok: Chwng jampar eba jacket kanna nangwi mano, phiya chwng tangrak tei khsrangwi tongwi mano.

english: When it is freezing cold, our bodies have to work much harder to stay warm.
kokborok: Jephuru kwchang raksario, chini sakrok teibono teibo samung kwrak khaina ango kutung tongna khe.

english: We may need to bundle up in layers of clothing, and we may even need to stay indoors.
kokborok: Chwng richumung pola thumsa nanganw, tei chwng nokbising ma tonganw.

english: Another difference between cool weather and freezing cold weather is the way it affects our mood.
kokborok: Tei kaisa pherlaimani bising twi kwchang nokbarhalok tei kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok lama wngkha chini morji no gwdalrima.

english: Criticism is a necessary evil.
kokborok: Kokchirmani wngkha kaisa hamya nangmani.

english: It is the process of evaluating and judging the quality of something, and it can be a valuable tool for improving the work of art, literature, music, or other creative endeavor.
kokborok: Omo wngkha ah twtamani tansep tei dorbaphangmani ah mungsaswk tongham, tei omo kaisa morokjak kol ah rikmung samung charwmani bagwi, kokrwbai, rwchpmung, eba kubun swnamanma chaitokma.

english: However, criticism can also be destructive, tearing down what others have created without offering any constructive feedback.
kokborok: Haiphano, kokchirmani baikhrupmung bo wngmano, mungsa swnamani kokphirokma yapharmani karwi kubunrok tamo swnamkha abo tola swbaimani.

english: The perfect criticism is one that is both fair and helpful.
kokborok: Ah chasukjak kokchirmani wngkha kaisa je kainwi banik tei chubama wngkha.

english: It should be based on sound reasoning and evidence, and it should offer specific suggestions for how to improve the work in question.
kokborok: Omo khorang kanrokmani tei yakumu yaphang sakao wngna nango, tei bahai ah samung swngmani bising charwma bwkhak omo nangmani kokberamarok karwi yapharna nango.

english: The perfect critic is someone who is knowledgeable about the subject matter and who is able to articulate their thoughts clearly and concisely.
kokborok: Ah chasukjak kokchirma wngkha khoroksaswk je ah rwngdal manwi bagwi elemgnang wngma tei je bohrokni wansukmarok kwchwngma tei kothumma sraisrai bwkhak chukma wngkha.

english: Criticism is a skill that can be learned and improved with practice.
kokborok: Kokchirmani wngkha kaisa yaksrai je swrwngma tei charrwma loi khlaimung bai swrwng mano.

english: If you are interested in becoming a better critic, there are a few things you can do.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng khoroksa kaham kokchir wngmani bising ol manmung wngkha, aro kisa manwirok tongo nwng khlaimano.

english: First, read widely and develop a strong understanding of the different forms of art and literature.
kokborok: Puila, kuarmakhe poridi tei ah juda juda sakmang rikmung tei kokrwbai kaisa kwrak buchimani hamkrai khaidi.

english: Second, learn to think critically about the work you are consuming.
kokborok: Nwirem, dehrama wansukma bwkhak swrwngdi ah samung naitongmani bagwi.

english: Ask yourself questions about the author's purpose, the audience for the work, and the techniques used by the artist.
kokborok: Nwngsakbaithang swngmarok swngdi ah suinaini naimung bagwi, ah nainaini bagwi ah samung khlaima, tei ah seprok ah rikkwrwng bai phwnangjakma.

english: Third, be willing to share your opinions with others, even if they are not popular.
kokborok: Thamrem, kubunrok bai nini khakamungrok bakna bwkhak muchungmani wngkha, ahaino tumung bohrok luku hmjakjak wngya phano.

english: The best way to improve your critical skills is to practice them.
kokborok: Ah kahamkuk lama nini dehrama yaksrairok wngkha bohrokno loi khlaimani bwkhak charwma bwkhak.

english: The coffee shop was bustling with activity as people came and went, grabbing a quick cup of coffee or tea to start their day.
kokborok: Coffee phalnok tangmungni bai dosidopra wngjak iko borok phaima tei thangma bagwi, atomsa fatsa coffee cup eba cha borokni sal chengma bwkhak.

english: The baristas were working hard to keep up with the demand, but they were also taking the time to chat with their customers and get to know them.
kokborok: Baristas rok kwrak samung khlayo sanmarok saka tonina bagwwi, phiya bohrok koksana baagwwi jora naitongo borok ni painai borokrok bai tei bohrokno kahamkhe sinina bagwi.

english: One of the baristas, a young woman named Sarah, was particularly friendly and outgoing.
kokborok: Khoroksa baristas, bwrwima sikla mung Sarah, wngkha kiching hai tei phatarlamsoknai.

english: She loved getting to know her customers and learning about their lives.
kokborok: Bo bini painai borokrokno sinina hamjago tei bohrokni langmano twi swrwngo.

english: One day, a man came in who looked like he was having a bad day.
kokborok: Salsa, khoroksa chwla habphaikha nugwi khakamani bini sal hamya thang tongo hwnwi.

english: He was pale and his eyes were bloodshot.
kokborok: Bo uahrap thong wngjak tei bini mokolrok thwipojak.

english: Sarah could tell that he was sick, so she offered him a free cup of tea.
kokborok: Sarah saimano je bo kulum wngjak hwnwi, haini bagwi bo bono suta cha cup yapharkha.

english: The man gratefully accepted the tea and took a sip.
kokborok: Ah chwla kotorkuarkhai cha no yachakha tei kaisa khukthepama nakha.

english: He immediately started to feel better.
kokborok: Bo logilogi no kaham wansukma chengjakha.

english: He told Sarah that he had been feeling sick for a few days, but he hadn't been able to get to the doctor.
kokborok: Bo Sarah no sakha je bo kisa salrok romwi kulum kailajak, phiya bo saknainai ni oro thangwi manyakhu.

english: Sarah told him that he should go see a doctor as soon as possible, but she also offered to make him some more tea to help him feel better in the meantime.
kokborok: Sarah bono sakha bo saknainai ni oro jeswk dakti naijak mankhe chanai, phiya kaisadigi bo bono kaham wansukma khai chubana bagwi bono tei kisa cha swnamwi yapharkha.

english: The man ended up staying at the coffee shop for a while, drinking tea and talking to Sarah.
kokborok: Ah chwla paithago coffee phalnogo tongkha kisa jorani bagwi, cha nwngwi tei Sarah bai kok salai.

english: He told her about his job and his family.
kokborok: Bo bono bini samung tei nukhungni bagwi sakha.

english: It's an opportunity to help those in need and make a difference in the world.
kokborok: Omo nangmani bisingtwih aborokno chubama bwkhak kaisa sep, tei ah hayung pherlaima bisingtwih kaisa swnamma.

english: But sometimes, charity can have unexpected consequences.
kokborok: Phiya waisa-wuisu, daan wansukmanya thaihmungrok tongwi mano.

english: One of the most common unintended consequences of charity is that it can create a dependency on the giver.
kokborok: Kaisa jottoni slai daan thaihmungrok muchungjakya manthok wngkha je omo kaisa ah rwinaini sakao sakbokjkama swnam mano.

english: When people are given help without having to work for it, they can start to expect that help to continue.
kokborok: Jephuru borokno chubachu rijago omoni bagwi samung khaiya karwi, bohrok khakama bwkhak chengwi mano je choyai chubachu khaina.

english: This can lead to a lack of motivation and a sense of entitlement.
kokborok: Omo kaisa khangra babai tubumani tei sinai simanwi mung rwma.

english: Another unintended consequence of charity is that it can create a divide between the giver and the receiver.
kokborok: Tei kaisa daan thaihmungrok muchungjakya wngkha je omo kaisa khakma ah rwnai tei mannaini kwcharo swnam mano.

english: The giver may feel superior to the receiver, while the receiver may feel inferior or ashamed.
kokborok: Ah rwnai mannai ni slai kahamkuk wansuk mano, jephuru ah mannai hamsukya eba lachijak wansuk mano.

english: This can make it difficult for both parties to build a relationship based on mutual respect.
kokborok: Omo kainwi bodolrokni kwthalai borom rwma yaphang saka kaisa holokrung tangma bwkhak karwi 3 omo swnam mano.

english: Finally, charity can sometimes do more harm than good.
kokborok: Paithago, daan waisa-wuisu teibo chaya khlaimano kahamni slai.

english: If the help that is given is not appropriate or if it is not given in a way that is respectful, it can actually make the situation worse.
kokborok: Tumungno ah chubachu je rwjak wngkha gothokya wngma eba tumungno omo rwjakya wngkha kaisa lama bising je borom rwjak wngkha, omo kubuino ah tonghalok hamya swnam mano.

english: For example, giving food to a homeless person without also providing them with shelter or job training may only enable their homelessness.
kokborok: Phunukmari karwi, haino nokthaikwrwi borokno tongthai eba samung ni swrwngmani rwya karwi chahthaih bakmani bo haino bohrokni nokathaikwrwi tangrak khlaimanma.

english: Of course, these are just a few of the unintended consequences of charity.
kokborok: Ao, omo wngkha haino kisa ah daan wansukmanya thaihmungrok.

english: There are many other ways that charity can backfire.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kwbanga kubun lamarok je daan ulta nang mano.

english: When I went shopping for a new horse, I mentioned the colour I was looking for and asked the attendant if they had anything in stock.
kokborok: Kwtal korai nana bagwi hatio thang phuru, ang bo palino nanai sa'ui rohor kha tei aroni mwrwknai nobo swng kha abo hai toda tong hwnwi.

english: She showed me a few different horses, but none of them were quite right.
kokborok: Bo ano dalbidal korai phunuk kha, phiya abohrok bebakno ang chajakya.

english: Then, she mentioned that they had just received a new horse in that colour.
kokborok: Hakhe, bo sakha abotwi palini korai kwtal tabokno sok phaidrop.

english: I went to take a look and I was immediately smitten.
kokborok: Ang naina thang kha hakhe ang waisabai no chajak kha.

english: The horse was a beautiful chestnut mare with a long, flowing mane and tail.
kokborok: A korai damri naithokma kwchak kwtha'ui ni pali kolok khe, khitongni bikhumu tei khitong bo.

english: She was also very well-behaved and seemed to be quite intelligent.
kokborok: Bo belai tongna kwrwng tei kwbo kwrwng.

english: I decided to buy her and I'm so glad I did.
kokborok: Ang bono paina hwnwi khao chong kha tei paiwi na'ui bo belai kha swrwng kha.

english: She's been a wonderful addition to my family and I'm so happy to have her in my life.
kokborok: Bo masa chini nukhungni borok hai wngwi thang kha tei bono ani langma o manwi belai tongthok kha.

english: When I first brought her home, I took her to the vet for an inspection.
kokborok: Ang puila bono nogo tubu phuru, ang malmata naikwrwngrokni thanio boni sakham nairwna bagwi twlangwi thang kha.

english: The vet said that she was in good health and that she was a very sound horse.
kokborok: A malmata naikwrwng sakha bo bebak no kaham tongo hwnwi tei bo belai kwchang kwchang korai.

english: I was relieved to hear that she was healthy and I was excited to start riding her.
kokborok: Bo sak kaham tongo hwnwi khwna'ui ani uanama hamkha tei ang korai kanani belai tongthokjak.

english: I've been riding my horse for a few weeks now and I'm really enjoying it.
kokborok: Ang tabuk hatibar kisisa romwi korai kamani tei ang kwbwino tongthoksok kha.

english: She's a very easy horse to ride and she's very responsive to my commands.
kokborok: Kasana bagwi a korai belai kaham tei bo ani kok bo khwna o.

english: Getting your driver's license is a rite of passage for many teenagers.
kokborok: Nini chalokjaknai license mannani kwbangma chaslokjorarokni bagwi tongkthwter lama.

english: It signifies a new level of freedom and independence.
kokborok: Omo buchimanikhe kwtal mil yokmani tei phiyokjakmani.

english: However, getting behind the wheel of a car for the first time can also be daunting.
kokborok: Haiphano, malukung swikni ungkuluk thangmani puila jora sundrumahai wngwi mano.

english: There are so many things to think about, from the rules of the road to the different types of vehicles.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manwino twi wansuk thai, lamani raida simi juda juda malkhungrok sapokthaih.

english: One of the biggest challenges of learning to drive is dealing with the different road conditions.
kokborok: Kaisa kotorma bataimani chalukna swrwngmani hwnkhe juda juda lamani kaurwlaimung bokchono twi.

english: When you're first starting out, it's important to be aware of the different factors that can affect your driving, such as the weather, the time of day, and the amount of traffic.
kokborok: Nwng puila jephuru chengwi ongkhoro, nwng juda juda bwcwllwino saimana nangkukmani je nini chalukmano gwdalwi, ahaino nobarhalok, salni jora, tei thahnglaiso bangmari.

english: For example, driving in the rain is much different than driving on a sunny day.
kokborok: Phunukamari hwnkhe, watwio chalukmarok sal kutung chalukmani belai juda.

english: The roads are slicker and visibility is reduced, so you need to be more careful and slow down.
kokborok: Lamarok wngkha rimirwk tei nukmani khairio, haini bagwi nwng teibo naikani tei twrwk twrwk wngdi.

english: Another challenge of learning to drive is shifting gears.
kokborok: Teikaisa chalokma swrwngmani bataima hwnkhe gears sehmani.

english: This can be especially difficult for people who have never driven a manual transmission before.
kokborok: Omo kahamkhai borokni bagwi wngmano je swkango waisaphano yakbai tangjaknai rohormungno chalukjakyakhe.

english: It takes practice to get the hang of it, but once you do, it will become second nature.
kokborok: Omo loi khlaimannakhe khaichiwi nango, phiya jodi waisa khaikhe, omo nwirem tongraida wngwi thango.

english: As you get more comfortable driving, you'll start to feel closer to your car.
kokborok: Nwng teibo chaluknani khasrangma manwi mano, nwng nini malkungni ganarwkrwk khao nangma khainani chenganw.

english: You'll develop a better understanding of how it handles and how to control it.
kokborok: Nwng teibo hamraia kahamkhe buchinai bahaikhe handlekhai tei bahaikhe kaswkma khai.

english: My neighborhood is a quiet and family-friendly community located in the heart of the city.
kokborok: Ani nokarini kisa siringsiring tei hodani nukhung-bayap hai doyungni bwkhao chongma.

english: It's home to a diverse group of people, and there's always something going on.
kokborok: Omo bohrok buthup baksayani nok se, tei aro homnino mungsaswk choli tongo.

english: There are several parks, playgrounds, and community centers, making it a great place to raise a family.
kokborok: Aro dalbidal khumbahri tongo, thwngjaknai, tei hoda kwcharw, abo kotorkuar thai hwnwi swnamjakmani nukhung kaisa tisana bwkhak.

english: There are also plenty of restaurants, shops, and businesses, so you can find everything you need without having to leave the neighborhood.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma chahnok tongo, phalnokrok, tei paiphalnai, nokarini yakarya karwi nwng jottomanwi nangmani nwng aswkno manwi mano.

english: One of the things I love most about my neighborhood is the sense of community.
kokborok: Kaisa manwi ang belai hamjakmani ani nokarini bagwi hwnkhe hodani sinai simanwi.

english: Everyone knows everyone else, and there's always a sense of support.
kokborok: Jottono saimano jottono karwi, tei aro homnino sinai simanwi twichuruma tongo.

english: If you need something, there's always someone who is willing to help out.
kokborok: Nwng mungsamanwi nangkhe, aro homnino khoroksaswk tongo je muchungwi chubana bagwi.

english: I've lived in my neighborhood for over 10 years, and I've made some lifelong friends here.
kokborok: Ang ani nokarinio bisi 10 saka romwi tongwi phaimani, tei ang kisa langmakolok bayaprok swnamkha oro.

english: I also love the convenience of my neighborhood.
kokborok: Ang haiphano ani nokarini manmarino hamjago.

english: It's close to everything I need, and I can easily walk or bike to most places.
kokborok: Omo jottomanwi ang nangmani bai gana, tei ang kwlaikhai himwi mano eba jotto thaini bawkha saikel khaimano.

english: There's a public transportation stop right at the end of my street, so it's easy to get around without a car.
kokborok: Ani laharni pathai yagra digi aro kaisa lukuni laisunani bathakjaknai tongo, aswkno obo 1 bwkhak kaisa malkhung karwi yaksiyagra mano.

english: One of the drawbacks of my neighborhood is the lack of affordable housing.
kokborok: Kaisa ani nokarini kebengjakma hwkhe nokni biyalwi naimanya.

english: Many of the homes are older and in need of repair, and the prices are very high.
kokborok: Jotto nokrok kwcham wngkha tei swnamphina nangphiro, tei belai kuchuk morokuk.

english: Scott was a young scientist who had always been passionate about nature.
kokborok: Scott wngkha sikla soisikwrwng bo homnino habarni bagwi belai khamuchungjago.

english: He grew up in a small town near the mountains, and he spent his free time exploring the woods and fields.
kokborok: Bo chikonsa aoli hapung gana torwi phayo, tei bo bini jora yokphuru bolongo tei hauarrok naitukberayo.

english: He loved learning about the different plants and animals that lived there, and he was always eager to protect their habitats.
kokborok: Bo aro tongnairok juda juda buphang-uaphang tei malmatarokni bagwi swrwngnani hamjakago, tei bo bohrokni tongwimanthai no bachirina bagwi homnino muchungjak.

english: When Scott was in college, he studied environmental science.
kokborok: Jephuru Scott rwnwgkotoro wngkha, bo soisimung tongkhorno porijak.

english: He learned about the many threats facing the natural world, and he became determined to do something to help.
kokborok: Bo habarni hayungo bwskango kwbangma kirima bagwi swrwngkha, tei bo jephano kaisa chubachu khainani bwkhak khathonjak.

english: After graduating, he got a job with a conservation organization, where he worked on projects to protect endangered species and restore damaged ecosystems.
kokborok: Rwngthekani olo, bo kaisa khatimani motha o samung mankha, boro bo samungbwtango samung khayo komornai dahl no bachirinani tei rwphima piyakmung ecosystems.

english: One day, Scott was working on a project to restore a forest that had been clear-cut.
kokborok: Salsa, Scott kaisa samungbwtango samungkhai tongmani bolong rwphima bwkhak je sraisrai-tanjak mani.

english: He was surveying the area when he came across a group of people who were illegally logging the trees.
kokborok: Jephururu bo ario naikolwi tongphuru bo ayang naro thumsa borokbai malaikha je lamchaya khai buphangrok chirphangmani.

english: Scott confronted the group, and they threatened to attack him.
kokborok: Scott buthupno swkangbaiswkang malaikha tei bohrok bono choprona hwnwi sikrikha.

english: However, Scott stood his ground, and he eventually convinced them to leave.
kokborok: Haiphano, Scott hawo bachai tongkha, tei bo daktino bohrokno yakarna bagwi gosirikha.

english: Scott's actions that day inspired the other conservationists working on the project.
kokborok: Scott's ni tangmung ah salo kubuno samungbwtang khatinairokno khaswrang rwkha.

english: They were all inspired by his courage and determination to protect nature.
kokborok: Borok jotto bini khakrakno nugwi khaswrangjak tei khathonmani habarno bachirina bagwi.

english: They worked together to restore the forest, and they created a thriving habitat for the plants and animals that lived there.
kokborok: Bohrok bolongno rwphima khaina abwi thansakhe samung khlaikha, tei bohrok kaisa tongwimanai hamsama swnamkha buphang-uaphang tei malmatarok je aro tongnairok.

english: The city was abuzz with activity.
kokborok: Ah doyung wngkha samung-humung bai gundrijak wngkha.

english: People were rushing to and fro, all with their own destinations in mind.
kokborok: Borokrok ayang uyang tei domani bwkhak wngkha, jottono bohrokni sakni sogwina thairok khorok bising chongwi.

english: The air was thick with the smell of exhaust fumes and the sound of honking horns.
kokborok: Ah nokbar rwja wngkha ah malkhungni hoku dummarok bahai bai tei ah horns tammani khorang.

english: But even in the midst of all this chaos, there was a sense of humor to be found.
kokborok: Phiya ahaino jotto oh ubrumjabrum ah kwcharni bising, aro kaisa sinai simanwi naituk manna bwkhak wngkha.

english: One day, I was walking down the street when I saw a man sitting on a bench, reading a newspaper.
kokborok: Salsa, ang ah lama tola himwi thangphuru ang ohjora kaisa chwlano achukthai sakao achukmani nukha, kaisa koktunlaih porimani.

english: He was wearing a tuxedo and a top hat, and he had a monocle in his eye.
kokborok: Bo kaisa tuxedo tei thupi kolok kanajak, tei bini mokol bising kaisa monocle tongo.

english: He looked like he was straight out of a movie.
kokborok: Bo mohai nukjak tongkha je bo suja no kaisa tokeni ongkhor phai hai.

english: As I got closer, I saw that the man was actually reading a comic book.
kokborok: Ang ahaino ganarwk thangkha, ang nukha je ang chwla kubuio kaisa mwnwikothok bijap pori tongo.

english: He was laughing out loud, and I couldn't help but smile.
kokborok: Bo chirikhogwi mwnwi tongkha, tei ang mwnwiya karwi tongwi manliya.

english: It was so funny to see this man, who was dressed so formally, reading a comic book.
kokborok: Omo aswkno mwnwikothok ah chwla no nukhe, je raidatwi aswkno richumjak, kaisa mwnwi kothok bijap porimani.

english: It was like he was living in his own world, where anything was possible.
kokborok: Omo wngkha bo bini sakni hayungo tongwi tongo, boro jesaphano wngmano.

english: I continued on my way, and I couldn't stop thinking about the man in the tuxedo.
kokborok: Ang choyawui ano lama thangkha, tei ang ah tuxedo chwlani bagwi wansuknani mwthak se manliya.

english: He was a reminder that even in the midst of all the chaos of city life, there is always room for humor.
kokborok: Bo ano kaisa muitomanrikha je ahaino jotto oh ubrumjabrum ah kwcharni bising, aro homnino mwnwikothokni bagwi khotol tongo.

english: The woman stood at the podium, her voice clear and strong.
kokborok: Ah bwrwima ah podium o bachakha, bini khorang sraisrai tei phangnang.

english: "We are facing a global crisis," she said.
kokborok: "Chwng kaisa hayungrwgwi biyal malaimani wngkha, " bo sakha.

english: "Droughts are becoming more frequent and severe, and they are having a devastating impact on our planet.
kokborok: "Khoranrok wngkha teibo kwthajak tei kwrak, bohrok kaisa chini hagri sakao swabaimani sekrupma tongmani wngkha.

english: In the past year alone, we have seen droughts in Africa, Asia, and the Americas.
kokborok: Ah wngthahng bisi saichung bising, chwng Africa, Asia, tei Americas bising khoranrok nukha.

english: These droughts have caused widespread hunger, poverty, and displacement.
kokborok: Oh khoran kuarpisarjak okkhwi, bigra, tei norjakmung pherjak tongo.

english: We must act now to address this crisis."
kokborok: Chwng tabukno samung ma khainai oh biyal nikuma bwkhak."

english: The woman's words were met with a round of applause.
kokborok: Ah bwrwimani kokthairok kaisa yapha khoropma bai malaima wngkha.

english: She had been invited to speak at a conference on climate change, and she had used her platform to raise awareness of the devastating impact of droughts.
kokborok: Bo nokbartwibar swlaima sakao kaisa koklam pandao sana bwkhak kwcharjakha, tei bo ah swbaimani sekrupma khoranrok saimanrimani tisama bwkhak bini char phwnangkha.

english: She called on governments and businesses to take action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate the effects of climate change.
kokborok: Bo haphangrok tei beparirokno ringkha samung nana bwkhak nokkwkhwrang phab emissions lonma bwkhak tei ah nokbartwibar swlaima sekrupmarok holirwma wngkha.

english: She also urged individuals to make changes in their own lives, such as reducing their energy consumption and recycling.
kokborok: Bo saksakrokno bo koikha bohrokni sakni langrok biisng swlaimarok swnamna bwkhak, ahaino bohrokni baimani tei teiwaisa gurimani lonmani.

english: The woman's speech was a powerful reminder of the urgent need to address climate change.
kokborok: Ah bwrwimani koklam wngkha kaisa phangnang muitunarakna nokbartwibar nikuma bwkhak ah matangthai nangma.

english: Droughts are just one of the many impacts of climate change that we are already seeing, and they are only going to get worse if we do not take action.
kokborok: Khoranrok wngkha haino kaisa ah kwbangm kekrupmrok nokbartwibar swlaima je chwng swkango nukmani, tei bohrok aswkno hamya wngna bwkhak thangmani tumungno chwng samung nayakhe.

english: We must all work together to create a more sustainable future for our planet.
kokborok: Chwng jotto thansa samung makhaina teibo kaisa tikimannai thinang swnamna bwkhak chini hatingni bagwi.

english: My mother is a fantastic cook.
kokborok: Ani ama markhe songkrwng.

english: She has been cooking for our family for as long as I can remember, and her food is always delicious.
kokborok: Ang je muito manmani bo kwdwkma jora romwmi chini nukhungni bagwi songwi phaimani, tei bini muirok homnino kothok.

english: She is always experimenting with new recipes and techniques, and she is always willing to share her knowledge with others.
kokborok: Bo homnini no kwtal recipes tei sep bai amjokmung khayo, tei bo homnino bini elem bo kubunrokbai bakna gosio.

english: One of the things that makes my mother's cooking so special is the fact that she uses fresh, high-quality ingredients.
kokborok: Kaisa manwirok je ani ama songmani no belai mahmlai kubui khaimani khe bo kwthar, kuchuk-tongham sarimanwirokno phwnangwi.

english: She never uses processed or pre-packaged foods, and she always takes the time to cook her food properly.
kokborok: Bo waisa phano swnamjak eba swkang-chujak chathairok phwnangya, tei bo homnino jora nawui bini chathaino kahamkhe songo.

english: This attention to detail results in dishes that are full of flavor and nutrients.
kokborok: Oh saktongmani bwkhak sukhrubwi bwthaihrokni bising thokmung tei chahkohlom bai kupulung muirok.

english: Another thing that sets my mother's cooking apart is her ability to create dishes that appeal to everyone.
kokborok: Tei kaisa manwi je ani ama songmani bade khaima hwnkhe bini muirokno swnamwi manmani je jottono koima bwkhak twi.

english: She is always willing to accommodate different dietary restrictions, and she is always willing to experiment with new flavors.
kokborok: Bo homnino muchungjago kokrwnglaimung bai juda juda chahmungrok ujono toninani, tei bo homnino kwtal thokmungrok amjokmung bai muchungjago.

english: This makes her a great cook for large families or groups of people with different tastes.
kokborok: Omo bono kaisa kotor songkwrwng swnamo kotor nukhungo eba borok bodolo juda juda chaihnaima bai.

english: My mother's cooking is also a great way to bring people together.
kokborok: Ani amani songmani wngkha kaisa kotor lama borok rokno thansa tubunani.

english: When she cooks for us, it is a time for us to relax and enjoy each other's company.
kokborok: Jephuru bo chini bagwi songo, aphuru chwng lenglawui tei khoroksa tei khoroksa ni logisong bai jora katilayo.

english: We talk about our day, laugh, and share stories.
kokborok: Chwng chini sal bagwi kok salayo, mwnwilayo, tei kothomarok banta khayo.

english: These are some of my fondest memories, and I am grateful to my mother for creating them.
kokborok: Aro baksa ani chajakmani muitorok tongo, tei ang ani ama no belai hambai bohrokno swnamma bagwi.

english: The sun had been shining brightly for hours, and the birds were singing merrily in the trees.
kokborok: Ah sal damrwirok karwi kwchwng khai jilik jalak wng tongo, tei ah tokrok ah buphango tongthokjakkhe rwchapmani.

english: It was a perfect day for Eid, and everyone in the village was excited.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa chasukjak sal Eid ni bagwi, tei kamini jottono tongthokjak wngkha.

english: The children had been up early, getting dressed in their new clothes and eating a big breakfast.
kokborok: Ah chwrairok dakti phaijak, bohrokni kwtal richumrok kanjak manmani bising tei kaisa kotor phungbaili chamani.

english: Then they had gone to the mosque to pray, and now they were all gathered in the town square, waiting for the Eid celebrations to begin.
kokborok: Hwnkhe bohrok jotto mosque bwkhak surina thangkha, tei tabuk borok jotto aoli thekabwrwi bising kuthumkha, ah Eid palaijakmarok bwkhak chengma bagwi naisingmani.

english: The mayor of the village stepped up to the microphone and welcomed everyone.
kokborok: Ah kamini aolipha yakpri sehma bwkhak ah khorangkoktokol tei jottono lamsukha.

english: He spoke about the importance of Eid, and how it was a time for family and friends to come together and celebrate.
kokborok: Bo sakha ah Eid ni nangkukma bagwi, tei bahai amo wngkha kaisa jora nukhung tei bayaprokni bagwi thansa phai tei palaima bwkhak.

english: Then he led the crowd in a prayer of thanks.
kokborok: Hwnkhe bo ah kuthumjak no twlangkha kaisa surimung hambairokni bising.

english: After the prayer, the festivities began.
kokborok: Ah surimani olo, ah terrok chengkha.

english: There were games for the children, music and dancing for everyone, and plenty of food and drink to enjoy.
kokborok: Aro chwrairokni bagwi thwngmungrok tongo, rwchapmung tei mwsamani jottoni bagwi, tei kwbangma chathaih tei nwngwi tongthokna bwkhak.

english: The people of the village laughed and talked and ate and drank, and they all had a wonderful time.
kokborok: Ah kamini borok mwnwikha tei kok sakha tei chakha tei nwngkha, tei bohrok jottono kaisa uanamasingsa jora mankha.

english: As the sun began to set, the people of the village started to drift home.
kokborok: Ah sal hapna bwkhak chengkheno, ah kamino borokrok nogo thangna bwkhak chengkha.

english: They were tired, but they were also happy.
kokborok: Bohrok lengjak wngkha, phiya bohrok tongthokjak bo wngkha.

english: They had spent a perfect day celebrating Eid with their loved ones, and they knew that they would remember it for years to come.
kokborok: Bohrok kaisa chasukjak sal katikha Eid palaimani bohrokni hamjakma borokrok bai, tei bohrok saimano je bohrok omono bisirok phaima bwkhak muito khlaimano.

english: Afforestation is the process of planting trees on land that was previously not forested.
kokborok: Bolong swnamma wngkha mohai tangsep halogwi hao buphangrok kaijakmani je swkango bolong khajakya.

english: It can be done for a variety of reasons, such as to provide timber, to improve soil quality, or to create a habitat for wildlife.
kokborok: Omo podrepod karonrok paijakhe khai mano, ahaino timber manthogo, haisingni hammung chasama, eba bolongni langma tongthai kaisa swnamwi mano.

english: There are many benefits to afforestation.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manmarirok tongo bolong swnammani bwkhak.

english: Trees help to clean the air and water, they provide shade and shelter, and they can help to prevent soil erosion.
kokborok: Buphangrok twi bai nokbar no kwchwng khaima bwkhak chubao borok saklom tei lenglama swnamtonima rio, tei bohrok haising kochokmani kasogra o chubai mano.

english: They can also help to improve the climate by absorbing carbon dioxide.
kokborok: Bohrok carbon dioxide no monogwi nokbartwibar chasama khai thani chaubai mano.

english: One of the benefits of afforestation that I have experienced firsthand is the reduction in noise pollution.
kokborok: Kaisa manmari bolong swnamthani hwnkhe je ang manjakphaimani puilayak wngkhe khorang ebrumrwma khairimani.

english: When I walk through a wooded area, I can hear the birds singing and the wind rustling through the leaves.
kokborok: Jephuru ang buphang ari twi himphuru, ang tokrok rwchapmani khwnai mano tei bwlairok bai nokbar sibramwi phayo.

english: This is a very calming and peaceful experience, and it is something that I would not be able to enjoy if there were no trees.
kokborok: Omo kaisa belai siringsiring tei kwchangthotok manjakma, tei omo kaisamanwi je aro buphangrok jodi kwrwi hwnkhe ang tongthogwi mangwlak khamu.

english: In addition to the benefits that I have mentioned, afforestation can also help to improve the economy.
kokborok: Manmari bising jora rwmungrok je ang kok khurmani, bolong swnamani rangthong chasama bwkhak chubai mano.

english: Trees can create jobs in the forestry industry, and they can also help to attract tourists to an area.
kokborok: Buphangrok forestry swnammung samungrok swnam mano, tei bohrok berainai rokno khasotongwi ari bwkhak tubuthani chubai mano.

english: Overall, afforestation is a very beneficial practice.
kokborok: Bebagwi, bolong swnamani wngkha belai hamkraini loi khlaimung.

english: It has many environmental, economic, and social benefits.
kokborok: Oro kwbangma habar, rangthong, tei hodarwi manmarirok tongo.

english: If you are interested in learning more about afforestation, I encourage you to do some research on the topic.
kokborok: Nwng jodi teibo bolong swnamani bagwi swrwngnani muchungjak tongkhe, ang nono khatungrimung rwi kokkhak salaikok go kisa rutukrwk khaidi.

english: The spirit world is a place of many colors and shapes.
kokborok: Phola gwdaljak swngchar wngkha kwbangma pali tei goron ni haphar se.

english: It is a place where anything is possible.
kokborok: O hapharo bebakno khwlaiwi mano.

english: There are no rules, no limits, and no boundaries.
kokborok: Aro raida bo kwrwi, thakmung bo kwrwi, tei ari bo kwrwi.

english: In the spirit world, you can be anything you want to be.
kokborok: O swngcharo, je nwng muchung mani abono wngwi mano.

english: You can fly, you can breathe underwater, and you can even talk to animals.
kokborok: Nwng birwi mano, twiwi bisingo bo hama sosa'ui mano, tei nwng malmatarok bai bo kok sa'ui mano.

english: One day, a young woman named Abigail was walking through the forest when she came across a strange sight.
kokborok: Sala, khoroksa sikli mung Abigail bolong bisingtwi himwi tong phuru bo siniya-nukya abotwi manwi nukha.

english: There was a coach standing in the middle of the path, and it was unlike any coach she had ever seen before.
kokborok: Abo wngkha sola lama kwcharo bachajak, tei a sola kubun solrok hai wngya abono waisa bo nukya kho.

english: The coach was made of different parts of animals, and it was painted in bright colors.
kokborok: O sola dalbidal malmatarokni bukur bai swnamjak, tei abo kwchwng pali phuljak.

english: Abigail was curious about the coach, so she decided to take a closer look.
kokborok: Abigail a sola no nugwi belai sina muchungjak kha, hake bo teisa gana khe nainai hwnwi khao chong kha.

english: As she got closer, she saw that there was someone inside the coach.
kokborok: Bo aro gana sogwi ba, nukha a sola bisingo khoroksa tongo.

english: It was an old man, and he was sitting on a throne.
kokborok: Abo wngkha khoroksa bura, tei bo singhason o achukjak.

english: The old man had a long white beard, and he was wearing a robe that was made of leaves.
kokborok: A bura ni kuphur tei kolok khosai tongo, tei bo bwlaini lolang chumjak.

english: Abigail had never seen anyone like him before "Hello," said the old man "My name is Oden, and I am the guardian of the spirit world.
kokborok: Abigail bo hai borokno waisa phano nukya kho "Hoi" a bura sakha "Ani mung Oden, tei ang o swngcharni pholano mwrwknai se".

english: I love talking about childhood.
kokborok: Ang ani chwraiphangni bagwi koksanani hamjago.

english: It's such a special time of life, full of wonder and exploration.
kokborok: Abo kaisa langmani yakbahra jora, uanamasingsa tei naitukberaimani kuplung.

english: I remember when I was a child, I would spend hours playing outside, making up games with my friends.
kokborok: Ang muitomano ang chwrai phuru, ang damrwi romwi phataro thwngwi katio, thwngmani swnamo ani bayap songbai.

english: We would build forts in the woods, play hide-and-seek, and ride our bikes all day long.
kokborok: Chwng buphango sengkrakrok swnam tisao, huijak-tei-naitukma thwngo, tei sapung sal logwi chini saikelrok chalugo.

english: We didn't have any worries or concerns, and we just lived in the moment.
kokborok: Chini thani unamani eba uanamarok kwrwi, tei chwng haino kisisajorao thangwi tonglayo.

english: I think childhood is so important because it's a time when we learn about ourselves and the world around us.
kokborok: Ang khakamani chwraiphang belai nangkukmani tamni hinba obo kaisa jora jephuru chwng chinisaksakni bagwi swrwngma tei hayungo yaksiyagra naisikgwi.

english: We learn how to interact with others, how to solve problems, and how to deal with our emotions.
kokborok: Chwng kubunbai bahaikhe koksalai swrwngmano, bahai khe chini biyalno kokpairinai, tei chini khanangjakma bai bahaikhe bokcho khainai.

english: We also develop our imaginations and creativity.
kokborok: Chwng chini wansukmung rokno bo hamkrai tei tagwimano.

english: Childhood is a time of growth and development, and it's something that we should all cherish.
kokborok: Chwraiphang wngkha torwnani tei hamkrai ni jora, tei omo kaisamanwi je chwng jottono naikolnai.

english: If you have children, I encourage you to spend as much time with them as possible.
kokborok: Nini chwrairok tongkhe, ang khasrangrwma rio nono nwng jeswk jora mansak bohrokbai jora kwbang swbaidi.

english: Let them explore their world and learn from their mistakes.
kokborok: Bohrokno bohrokni swngcharno naitukberaidi tei bohrokni chayani simi swrwngdi.

english: Be there for them when they need you, and help them to grow into happy, healthy adults.
kokborok: Bohrokni bagwi tongdi jephuru bohrok nono nango, tei bohrokno tongthokna bagwi tisaridi, siklarokni sakdukma bai.

english: Childhood is a precious time, and it's something that we should all treasure.
kokborok: Chwraiphang belai nangmani jora, tei omo mohaimanwi je chini bagwi bebak rangmai.

english: When it comes to raising children, there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
kokborok: Jephuru omo chwrairokno pusinani phayo, aro wngkha tei mungsa kaisa-uarma-khropsarok-jotto gana thangma kwrwi.

english: Every child is different, and what works for one family may not work for another.
kokborok: Jotto chwrai no pherlayo, tei tamo kaisa nukhungni bagwi samungrok khaiphano tei kaisa ni bagwi khaigwlak.

english: However, there are some general principles that can help parents raise happy, healthy, and successful children.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro baksa sosol raidarok je mapharokno tongthok, sakdukma, tei khlaimanma chwrairokno pusinani chubaimano.

english: One of the most important things parents can do is to establish a strong relationship with their children.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jotto nangkukma manwirok mapharok khai manma wngkha kaisa kwrak halokbokma bohrokni chwrairokbai songchama bwkhak.

english: This means spending time together, talking to them, and listening to them.
kokborok: Omo wngkha thansa khe jora katilaimani, bohrokbai koksamani, tei bohrok bai khwnamani.

english: It also means setting limits and boundaries, and enforcing them consistently.
kokborok: Omoni kokmangrok tangbwtang arirok tei ari bomanirok, tei bohrokno kwthajak uwngrwmani.

english: When children know what is expected of them, they are more likely to behave appropriately.
kokborok: Jephuru chwrairok saimano borokni thani tamo khakajak, bohrok teibo ahaino tongraida gothokjak bwkhak wngkha.

english: Another important factor in raising children is to teach them about consent.
kokborok: Tei kaisa nangkukma bwchwlwi wngkhaa chwrairokni pusinani wngkha bohrokno khathansa kahai phwrwngma bagwi.

english: This means teaching them that they have the right to say no to anything they don't want to do, and that they should respect the rights of others to say no as well.
kokborok: Omo kokmanagrok bohrokno phwrwngnanai je bohrokni thani manthai tongo jesano phano ehe hinnani je bohrok nana muchungya no, tei bohrok ah kubunrokni manthairokno borom rina nango haino kaham khai ehe hwnwi sana bwkhak.

english: This is an important lesson that will help children protect themselves from abuse and exploitation.
kokborok: Omo wngkha khaisa nangkukma porirem je chwrairokno bohrok saksakno katirwna satokma tei samung phwnangmani simi.

english: Finally, parents need to be role models for their children.
kokborok: Paithago, mapharok bohrokni chwrairokni bagwi tangmung naidalrok wngna nango.

english: Children learn by watching the adults in their lives, so it is important that parents behave in a way that they want their children to emulate.
kokborok: Chwrairok siklarokno naimani swrwngo bohrokni langmarokni bising, aswkno omo wngkha nangkukma je mapharok tongraida kaisa lama bising je bohrok bohrokni chwrairokni bataima bwkha nango.

english: This means being honest, respectful, and responsible.
kokborok: Omo kokmangrok tongham, boromjak, tei bokjak wngjak .

english: Dance is a form of art that is expressed through movement.
kokborok: Mwsamung wngkha kaisa sakmang rikmung je ninangrimung twih swbaikhrubwi sama wngkha.

english: It can be performed solo or in groups, and it can be used to tell stories, express emotions, or simply to create a beautiful experience for the audience.
kokborok: Omo saichung eba bodolrokni bising khlai phaijak bo mano, tei omo kothomarok sana bwkha phwnangjak mano, khanangmarok swbaikhrubwi sama, eba khakepleng bwkhak kaisa naithok saimanma ah nainaini bagwi swnamo.

english: Dance has been around for thousands of years, and it has been practiced in every culture on Earth.
kokborok: Mwsamung sai bisrok karwi yaksiyagra tongwi tongo, tei omo hating sakao jotto hukumu bising loi khalajak phaikha.

english: There are many different types of dance, each with its own unique history and style.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma juda juda mwsamung sapokthaihrok tongo, omoni sak solya laihbuma tei tongdal bai thwgwi.

english: Some of the most popular types of dance include ballet, modern dance, hip hop, and tap dance.
kokborok: Baksa ha jottoni slai luku hamjakjak sapokthaihrok mwsama khobjakha ballet, kwtal mwsamung, hip hop, tei tap mwsamung.

english: Dance can be a physical activity, but it is also a mental and emotional one.
kokborok: Mwsamung kaisa sakno twywi tangmung wngwi mano, phiya omo kaisa khaphang tei khanangjakma bo wngwi manu.

english: When you dance, you are using your body to express yourself in a way that words cannot.
kokborok: Jephuru nwng mwsao, nwng nini sak no sakbaithang swbaikhrubwi sama kaisa lama bising je kokthairok manya bwkha phwnangmani wngkha.

english: You are also connecting with the music and the other dancers in a way that can be very powerful.
kokborok: Nwng ah rwchapmung tei kubun mwsanairok bai manjumani bo wngkha kaisa lama bising je belai phangwnang wngwi mano.

english: Dance can have many benefits for both the mind and the body.
kokborok: Mwsama kwbangma manmarirok manwi mano khorok tei sak kanwini bagwi.

english: It can improve your cardiovascular health, reduce stress, and increase your self-confidence.
kokborok: Omo nini cardiovascular sakdukma, mothok khairina, tei nini sak-khaberamung bangrwimano.

english: It can also be a great way to meet new people and make friends.
kokborok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama bwkhak kwtal borok tei bayaprok swnamma bwkhak bo mano.

english: If you are interested in trying dance, there are many resources available to help you get started.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng mwsama chaitokmani bising ol manjak wngkha, aro wngkha kwbangma bumukrok manthokma bwkhak nono chubana chengjak mano.

english: There are classes for all levels of experience, and there are also many books and DVDs that you can use to teach yourself.
kokborok: Aro wngkha rwngremrok jotto homanrok saimanjak bagwi, tei aro wngkha kwbangma bijaprok tei DVDs je nwng sakbaithang phwrwngma bwkhak phwnang mano.

english: Addiction is a complex condition that can have a devastating impact on a person's life.
kokborok: Loi hamya wngkha kaisa kutuk tongmung, abo khoroksa borokni langmao swbaithotok swlaimung tubuimanw.

english: It is characterized by a compulsive need to engage in a behavior or substance despite negative consequences.
kokborok: Oboni wngmung chaya haiphano kaisa tongraida eba manuio kubulnani nangsuknai aboni nangmabai yasi kaijago.

english: There are many different types of addiction, including drug addiction, alcohol addiction, gambling addiction, and sex addiction.
kokborok: Kephek manuini loihamya, chuarakni loihamya, yapha bumani loihamya, tei sakmotokni loihamyano khobwi kwbangma dalni loi hamya tongo.

english: Addiction can develop in anyone, regardless of age, race, gender, or socioeconomic status.
kokborok: Loi hamya jeba borokni bisingo nukjagwimanw, boh jesa umor, bosong, sir eba hoda ranghalok tongmungni phano wngthun.

english: However, there are certain factors that can increase a person's risk of addiction, such as genetics, mental health problems, and environmental factors.
kokborok: Haikhe, obohai kisaswk pher tongo jebo khoroksa borokni loi hamyani kiringmung bangrwimanw, romdi bosong rwgwi, khapangni bemar, tei tongkhorni pher.

english: Addiction is a chronic disease, and there is no cure.
kokborok: Loi hamya wngkha kaisa kuduk bemar, tei oboni mungsa hammung kwrwi.

english: However, there are effective treatments available that can help people to overcome their addiction and live healthy, productive lives.
kokborok: Haikhe, borokrokno bohrokni loi hamyani yokthani tei sakhalok kaham, kaham kwrwngkhe thangwi tongthani chubaui mannnai abohai saknaimungni chajak lambo tongo.

english: The most effective treatment for addiction is a combination of medication and therapy.
kokborok: Loi hamyani bagwi saknaimungni jottonisai chajak lam wngkha bithi tei therapy-ni dalokjak lam.

english: Medication can help to reduce cravings and symptoms of withdrawal, while therapy can help people to address the underlying issues that led to their addiction.
kokborok: Bithi, muchungma tei karmungni sinimarino holirwthani simi chubauimanw, yang therapy hinkhe borokrokno loi hamya phaising twlangnai abohai jwngjalrokno paiswkmungo chubauimanw.

english: Recovery from addiction is a lifelong process, and there will be times when people struggle.
kokborok: Loi hamyani simi hamwi phaimung wngkha langma kwrwngwini samung, tei obohai jorabo phayo jephuru borokrok choba khwlainani nang thango.

english: However, with the right support, it is possible to overcome addiction and achieve a healthy, happy life.
kokborok: Haikhe, kaham chubachuni bisingtwi, loi hamyano mechenwi, kaham kwrwng, tongthok chahthokni langma ajiuimanw.

english: If you or someone you know is struggling with addiction, there is help available.
kokborok: Tumung nwng eba nini sinijak kebo loi hamyabai choba khwlai tongkhe, chubachu manthogo.

english: Please reach out to a professional for help.
kokborok: Chubachuni bagwi khoroksa tangdal kwrwngbai gwdaldi.

english: Happiness is a state of well-being and contentment.
kokborok: Tongthokmungungka kaisa tongrem kaham-wngjak tei khapungmung.

english: It is often associated with positive emotions such as love, joy, and gratitude.
kokborok: Omo uramuram kubui khanangjakrok bai gwdaljak wngkha ahaino hamjakma, tongthok, tei hansuthai.

english: There are many things that can contribute to happiness, including relationships with loved ones, meaningful work, and a sense of purpose.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je tongthokmung, hamjakma borokrok bai runghalokrok khobmani, kokmang samung, tei kaisa sinai simanwi naimung bwkhak rwui mano.

english: However, it is important to note that happiness is not always a constant state.
kokborok: Haiphano, omo mari bwkhak nangkukma wngkha je tongthokmung homnino kaisa tongphinai tongremya.

english: It can fluctuate depending on our circumstances and experiences.
kokborok: Omo ninangjakmano chini tonghalokrok tei simarirok sakbokmani sakao.

english: That is why it is important to find ways to cultivate happiness in our lives, even when things are tough.
kokborok: Haini bagwi chini langmarokni bising tongthokmung chuaima bwkhak lamaarok naitukna bwkhak omo nangkukma wngkha, ahaino jephuru manwirok kuthuk wngo.

english: One way to do this is to focus on the things that are important to us and that make us feel good.
kokborok: Kaisa lama omo khaina bwkhak wngkha manwirok sakao naisikma bwkhak je chini bagwi nangkukma tei chwng kaham wansukma swnamna bwkhak.

english: Another way is to be grateful for what we have and to appreciate the people in our lives.
kokborok: Tei kaisa lama wngkha hamsuthai wngma bwkhak chini thani tamo tongma tei chini langmarok bising borok chajakma karwi.

english: Finally, it is important to find ways to make a difference in the world, even if it is something small.
kokborok: Paithago, oh hayung bising kaisa pherlaimung swnamma bwkhak lama naitukna bwkhak omo nangkukma wngkha, ahaino tumung omo mungsaswk chikon wngkha.

english: When we feel like we are making a difference, it can give us a sense of purpose and meaning, which can contribute to our overall happiness.
kokborok: Jephuru chwng wansukma kahai kaisa pherlaimung swnammani wngkha, omo chwngno kaisa sinai simanwi naimung tei kokmang rwimano, bomo chini jottoi tongthokmung bwkhak bagwi mano.

english: In the context of a work environment, a boss can play a significant role in contributing to employee happiness.
kokborok: Kaisa samung habar bising ah kokmwkhang wngkha, khoroksa daginai kaisa nangkukma tanmung tangwimano sebukrokno tongthokmung rwnani bwkhak.

english: A supportive and understanding boss can create a positive work environment where employees feel valued and respected.
kokborok: Kaisa nangmani tei buchinai daginai kaisa kubui samung habar swnammano borok sebuk thinang morokma tei borom rwjak wansukmano.

english: This can lead to increased productivity and job satisfaction, which can in turn contribute to employee happiness.
kokborok: Omo thaihmung bahngrwma tei samung khapungmung bwkhak dagimano, amo sebuk tongthokmug bwkhak samung tangwimano.

english: "What is the meaning of becoming a queen?" asked the young woman.
kokborok: "Khoroksa isri wngmani kokmung tamo?" ah bwrwima sikli swngkha.

english: "It is to learn to accommodate all that is," said the old woman.
kokborok: "omo wngkha kokrwnglaimung bwkhak swrwngma wngkha abo jotto wngkha, " ah bwrwichwk sakha.

english: "To hold in your heart the beauty and the pain, the joy and the sorrow, the light and the darkness.To see the world as it is, and to love it nonetheless."
kokborok: "Nini khani bising romchrepma bwkhak Naithok tei ah sakdukhu nini bwkhak bising romchrepma, ah tongthok tei khanangma, ah pohor tei ah mwnakma. Ah hayungno amo haikhe naisikma bwkhak, tei omono haiphano hamjakma bwkhak."

english: "But how can I do that?" asked the young woman. "The world is so full of suffering."
kokborok: "Phiya ang abo bahaikhe khai mannai?" ah bwrwima sikli swngkha. "Ah hayung wngkha aswkno dukhumanmani kuplung."

english: "Yes, it is," said the old woman.
kokborok: "In', omo wngkha, " ah bwrwichwk sakha.

english: "But it is also full of beauty. And it is our task to find the beauty in the suffering, and to let it transform us.
kokborok: "Phiya omo bo naithok kuplung wngkha. Tei omo ah dukhu manma bising ah naithok naitukma bwkhak chini samung wngkha, tei omo chwngno swlaina rwkha.

english: "When you become a queen, you will have power.
kokborok: "Jephuru nwng khoroksa isri wngo, nini thani phan tongnai.

english: But power is not a thing to be used for your own gain.
kokborok: Phiya phan kaisa manwiya je nini sakni manna bagwi phwnangjakma wngo.

english: It is a responsibility to be used for the good of others.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisa bokjakmung ah kaham kubunrokni bagwi phwnangjakma wngo.

english: You must learn to use your power to heal the world, not to harm it.
kokborok: Nwng nini phanno phwnangna bwkhak swrwngna nango ah hayung hamrwna bwkhak, amono chaya khaiya bwkhak.

english: You must also learn to be humble.
kokborok: Nwng kwchangtoktok wngna bwkhak bo ma swrwngnai.

english: A queen is not above others, but she is also not below them."
kokborok: Khoroksa isri kubunrokni sakao boya, phiya bo bohrokni tolao boya."

english: The young soldier lay on the battlefield, bleeding from a wound in his side.
kokborok: Ah sengkrak sikla ah chobaha sakao kwlaijak, bini babai bising kaisa kwsani simi thwi kurukmani.

english: He looked up at the sky and saw the clouds scudding past, and the sun shining down on him.
kokborok: Bo ah nokha sakha naisikha tei ah chumuirok buprai laima, tei bini sakao sal chwngmani.

english: He thought of his home town, and the food he would never eat again, and the people he would never see again.
kokborok: Bo bini aoli bagwi wansukkha, tei ah chahthai bo pogwi phano teisa chaliya, tei ah borok bo teisa nukliya.

english: He closed his eyes and said a prayer.
kokborok: Bo bini mokolrok kholobakha tei kaisa surimung sakha.

english: A moment later, he heard a voice "Are you all right" The soldier opened his eyes and saw a woman standing over him.
kokborok: Kaisa swrapsa olo, bo kaisa khorang khwnakha "nwng kaham da" ah sengkrak bini mokol khulukha tei khoroksa bwrai bini sakao bachamani nukha.

english: She was tall and slender, with long black hair and green eyes.
kokborok: Bo kuchuk tei steni kolok wngkha, khwnai kosom kolok tei kwkhwrang mokolrok bai.

english: She was wearing a leather tunic and leggings, and she had a sword at her side "I'mI'm okay," the soldier said "You're hurt," the woman said "Let me help you" The woman helped the soldier to his feet.
kokborok: Bo kaisa bukur chumri tei leggings kanjak wngkha, tei bini babai digi kaisa bini seng tongo "ang ang theekno, " ah sengrak sakha "nwng dukhu manjak, " ah bwrwima sakha "ano nono chubana rwdi" ah bwrwima ah sengrakno bini yethek bwkhak chubakha.

english: She took off her cloak and wrapped it around him to stop the bleeding.
kokborok: Bo bini dulai karikha tei bini yaksiyagra amo khlopma ah thwih kurukma mwthakna bwkhak.

english: Then she led him to a nearby town.
kokborok: Hwnkhe bo bono kaisa aoli ganabai bwkhak twlangkha.

english: The town was small and quiet.
kokborok: Ah aoil chikon tei siring wngkha.

english: The people were friendly, and they gave the soldier food and a place to stay.
kokborok: Ah borokrok bayapjakma wngkha, tei bohrok ah sengkrakno chahthai tei tongna bwkhak kaisa thaih rwkha.

english: The woman stayed with him, and she helped him to heal.
kokborok: Ah bwrwima bobai tongkha, tei bo bono hamrwna bwkha chubakha.

english: In the forests of gold, there lived a people who were skilled in the ways of science.
kokborok: Rangchakni bolongo, kubuisimungni samung kwrwngrok tongbayo.

english: They had learned to harness the power of the sun and the wind, and they used their knowledge to build reliable structures that would withstand the elements.
kokborok: Bohrok sal tei nobarni phan no yachagwi narwkna rwngo, bohrok bohrokni ukti no elements no phanpainai abotwi samungo chuknai manwi swnamlayo.

english: One day, a young woman named Lawita was walking in the forest when she came across a strange object.
kokborok: Salsa, bwrwi sikli mung Lawita bolongo himwi thang tongphuru bo siniya-nukya manwi kaisa nukha.

english: It was made of gold, and it was unlike anything she had ever seen before.
kokborok: Abo rangchakni swnamjak, tei abo kubun manwirogbai kisa phano solya.

english: She took it home with her, and she showed it to her elders.
kokborok: Bo nogo twlangwi thangkha, hakhe bo boni okrarogno phunugwi kha.

english: They were puzzled by the object, but they agreed that it was something of great importance.
kokborok: O manwi no nugwi bohrok pal manjak liya, phiya bohrok gosewi nalai kha abo belai samungo chuknai manwi se hwnwi.

english: They decided to send Lawita to the city to find someone who could tell them more about it.
kokborok: Bohrok Lawita no dholi o rohor kha o manwino twywi saiman nai abotwi borokno rutukna bagwi.

english: Lawita traveled to the city, and she met with a wise man named Thoth.
kokborok: Lawita dholi o thang kha, hakhe bo khoroksa elem gwngang borok bai malai kha mung khe Thoth

english: Thoth was able to tell her that the object was a tool that could be used to harness the power of the stars.
kokborok: Abo wng kha athukirini phan no yachagwi man nai abotwi manwqise hwnwi Thoth sa'ui khwna rw kha.

english: He told her that it was a gift from the gods, and that it was meant to be used for good.
kokborok: Abo wngkha kaisa mwtaini hiyali se hwnwi Thoth bono sakha, tei samung kaham o thepajaknai manwi se hwnwi.

english: Lawita was honored to receive such a gift, and she vowed to use it wisely.
kokborok: Lawita belai tonthokjak kha amohai hiyali no manwi, tei bo swmai tang kha abobai hus khe samung tangnani.

english: She returned to her people, and she taught them how to use the tool.
kokborok: Bo boni borokrokni thani khiphilwi thang phi kha, hakhe bo bohrokno phwrwng kha bahai khe o manwi bai samung tangnai.

english: Nelson Mandela is a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary, political leader, and philanthropist who served as the first black president of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
kokborok: Nelson Mandela wngkha khoroksa South African anti-apartheid pekhrupnai wngkha, thwngrwngrwk ojama, tei bohrok hamajaknai je puila South Africa kosom kasku naikani khainai wngkha 1994 simi 1999 jora.

english: He is widely regarded as one of the most significant figures in world history.
kokborok: Bo kaisa jottoni slai nangkukma sakdukrok hayung laihbuma bising kotorma nahartongjakma wngkha.

english: Mandela was born in 1918 in Mvezo, South Africa.
kokborok: Madela 1918 o Mvezo, South Africa bising achaikha.

english: He grew up in a rural village and was educated at a Methodist mission school.
kokborok: Bo kaisa kamini bising torkha tei bo kaisa tongkhthar raida pinnok rwngnok bwkhak rwngjak wngkha.

english: After high school, he studied law at the University of Fort Hare.
kokborok: Kuchuk rwngnokni olom bo ah Rwngnokyung Fort Hare bwkhak kerong porikha.

english: In 1944, he joined the African National Congress (ANC), a political organization that was fighting against apartheid.
kokborok: 1994 o, bo ah African National Congress(ANC) manjukha, kaisa thwngrwngrwk motharok je apartheid kebengwi bulaimani chobakhaimani wngkha.

english: Mandela was arrested for his political activities in 1962 and sentenced to life in prison.
kokborok: Mandela bini thwngrwngrwk samung-humung bagwi 1962 o romjakha tei along bising langma paithak jora chopjakha.

english: He spent 27 years in prison, during which time he became a symbol of the anti-apartheid movement.
kokborok: Bo alongni bising 27 bisirok katikha, bobo wngjora bo kaisa mari wngkha ah anti-apartheid ninangrimung babai.

english: In 1990, Mandela was released from prison and elected president of South Africa in 1994.
kokborok: 1990 o, Mandela alongni simi phiyokjakha tei 1994 o South Africa ni kasku chongjakha.

english: As president, Mandela worked to unite South Africa and promote reconciliation between blacks and whites.
kokborok: iko kasku, Mandela South Africa no thansa khaina bwkhak samung tangkha tei kosomrok tei kuphurokni kwcharo millirwphinani remtisamung wngkha.

english: He also oversaw the end of apartheid and the transition to a democratic government.
kokborok: Bo ah paithak apartheid bo naikolkha tei kaisa lukuchongraidarwk haphang bwkha swlaijakmani tongo.

english: Mandela is a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and has been awarded numerous other honors.
kokborok: Mandela khoroksa borokkoto kwchangtotok yakpai boromgnang koklopnai wngkha tei gilama kubun boromrok sokat rwjakha.

english: The city was a vast, sprawling metropolis, full of life and energy.
kokborok: Doyung wngkha belai kuar, sahorjak rajakhor, langma bai tangphan kupulung.

english: It was a place where anything was possible, and where dreams could come true.
kokborok: Abo mohai thai wngkha aro jesaphano wngmano, tei jotto imang mukthang khaimano.

english: But for every person who found success in the city, there were many more who struggled to make ends meet.
kokborok: Haiphano jotto borokni bagwi je doyungo khwlaimanjak hai naituk manmani, aro teibo kwbangma tongo je biyalwi swnamjagwi paithago malaimani.

english: These people lived in the slums, in tiny apartments that were often overcrowded and in disrepair.
kokborok: Mohai borokrok bosti o tongo, chikon nokbwsao je uramuram belai keseplai tei swnam manya thayo tongjao.

english: They worked long hours for low pay, and they often had to go without basic necessities like food and healthcare.
kokborok: Bohrok kwdwkma tamwi samung khwlayo hacher rwmabai, tei bohrok yaphang nangmani bade chamung tei sakham naikini khainai karwi uramuram khe ma thango.

english: One such person was a young woman named Amelia.
kokborok: Sikli bwrwi borok khoroksa mung Amelia hwnwi tong.

english: She had come to the city with big dreams, but she quickly found that reality was much different than she had imagined.
kokborok: Bo imango kotor nugwi doyungo ma phaikha, haiphano bo daktino saimankha je bo wansukmani abo kubuio belai juda.

english: She worked as a waitress in a small diner, and she could barely make enough money to pay her rent.
kokborok: Bo kaisa chikonsa diner o waitressni samung khwlayo, tei bo bini nokchorai suna bagwi bebabagwi nangmaswk rang ajio.

english: She often went to bed hungry, and she was always worried about her future.
kokborok: Bo uramuram khe oakhui bisna thangjao, tei bo homnino bini thinangno twi wanachinta wngjak.

english: One day, Amelia was walking home from work when she saw a man sitting on a bench.
kokborok: Salsa, Amelia bini samungni nogo himwi thangphuru bo khoroksa chwla no achuthayo achujak nukha.

english: He was homeless, and he was holding a sign that said, "Will work for food." Amelia felt sorry for the man, and she decided to buy him a sandwich.
kokborok: Bo tongthai sara, tei bo kaisa mari romjak je sao, "Chwng chamung ni bagwi samung khwlayo." Amelia ah chwla ni bagwi markhe khairokjak, tei bo bono sandwich pairinai hwnwi chongwi nakha.

english: As she was talking to the man, she learned that his name was Charlie.
kokborok: Bo ah chwla bai kok sai tongphuru, bo bini mung Charlie hwnwi saimankha.

english: Unsolved mysteries have captured the public's imagination for centuries.
kokborok: Kokpaihjakya bisingkokrok ah lukuni wansukmani bisirarokni bagwi romjak tongkha.

english: From the disappearance of Amelia Earhart to the identity of Jack the Ripper, these cases have left us wondering what really happened.
kokborok: Amelai Earhart kwmamani simi ah Jack the Ripper sinirwma bwkhak, oh dorbakamungrok chwngno uanamasingsa bai yakarkha kubuio tamo wngkha.

english: While some of these mysteries may never be solved, they continue to fascinate us because they offer a glimpse into the unknown.
kokborok: Jephuru baksa oh bisingnikokrok ulo phano kokpaihjakya wngmano, bohrok choyai chwngno muani khlaima bwkhak tamnihinba bohrok kaisa philiksa yapharo ah siniyani bising.

english: One of the most famous unsolved mysteries is the disappearance of Amelia Earhart.
kokborok: Kaisa jottoni slai mungkoto kokpaihjakya bisingkorok wngkha ah Amelia Earhart kwmamani.

english: Earhart was an American aviator who became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.
kokborok: Earhart wngkha khoroksa American aviator je puila bwrwima saichung birinai wngkha ah Atlantic twijlang naro.

english: In 1937, she set out on an around-the-world flight with navigator Fred Noonan.
kokborok: 1937 o, bo khaisa ah-hayung-yaksiyagra birmung saka phatar kaihma phunuknai Fred Noonan bai.

english: The pair disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, and their fate remains unknown.
kokborok: July 2, 1937o ah Pacific twijlang sakao mangnwi kwmakha, tei bohrokni talika tongmarok saimanyakhu.

english: There are many theories about what happened to Earhart and Noonan.
kokborok: Earhart tei Noonanni logi tamo wngkha aboni bagwi kwbangma kokbwkrairok tongo.

english: Some believe that they crashed into the ocean, while others believe that they were captured by the Japanese.
kokborok: Baksa poito khayo je bohrok ah twijlang bising baikhrubkha, jephuru kubunrok poito khayo je bohrok ah Japanese rokbai romjakha hwnwi.

english: Still others believe that they deliberately disappeared in order to escape the public eye.
kokborok: Tabukbo kubunrok poito khayo je bohrok uansuksukma kwmakha lukuni mokolni bising yokna bwkhak.

english: The mystery of Earhart's disappearance has been the subject of books, articles, and documentaries.
kokborok: Oh Earthart ni kwmamani bisingkok ah yaktoljak bijaprok, koksoprok, tei swijakphunukmarok wngkha.

english: In 2017, a team of researchers announced that they had found evidence that Earhart's plane crashed on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean.
kokborok: 2017 o, khoroksa rutukrwk thwngdolrok sakhlaikha je bohrok yakumu mankha je Earhartni plane baikhrubkha kaisa hachal twihathaih ah Pacific twijlang bising.

english: Vimes was having a headache.
kokborok: Vimes khorok mihimjagwi tongmani wngkha.

english: It was the kind of headache that made you want to tear your hair out, or at least write a strongly worded letter to the makers of whatever it was that had given you the headache in the first place.
kokborok: Omo wngkha ah khorok mihimma kahai je nono nini khwnai chirna bwkhka muchungma swnamop, eba mukhuisa kaisa sakkrwrakma kokthaima koktun ah swnamarok bwkhak jesaphano omo wngkha je nono khorokmihima rwkha ah puila thaini bising.

english: In this case, the headache was the result of a particularly trying day at work.
kokborok: Oh tonghalok bising, ah khorok mihima kaisa chongjakma samung bwkak chaitokmani sal thaihmung wngkha.

english: Vimes had been investigating a series of robberies, and he was starting to feel like he was getting nowhere.
kokborok: Vimes kaisa bwtang kwbang khokmungni bagwi naitukmung khlaitongmani, tei bo matongkha boh mungsathayo sowgwiliya hwnwi.

english: He was tired, he was frustrated, and he just wanted to go home and sleep for a week.
kokborok: Boh lengjakha, bo khabaihjakha, tei boh haino nogo thangna tei hatibarsa ni bagwi thuna muchungjakha.

english: As he was walking back to his office, Vimes passed a small stationery shop.
kokborok: iko bo bini tangkhor bwkhak phirogwi himwi thangkheno, Vimes kaisa chikonsa switwi akorok phalnok laikha.

english: In the window, he saw a sign that said "Best Letters in the City".
kokborok: Ah tailamni bising, bo kaisa mari nukha ha sakha "kahamkuk koktunrok ah doyungni bising".

english: Vimes stopped and stared at the sign for a moment.
kokborok: Vimes bathakkha tei kaisa mukphliksani bagwi mari bai chengkha.

english: He thought about his headache, and he thought about all the letters he had to write.
kokborok: Bo bini khorok mihimma bagwi wansukha, tei bo jotto ah koktunrok bo swina bwkhak nangma bagwi wansukkha.

english: He sighed and went into the shop.
kokborok: Bo hamakolo nakha tei ah phalno bising thangkha.

english: The shop was full of all sorts of stationery supplies.
kokborok: Ah phalnok wngkha jotto rwngremrok switwi akorok yaktummarok bai kuplung wngkha.

english: There were pens, pencils, paper, envelopes, stamps, and even a few typewriters.
kokborok: Aro swikongrok, phangswikongrok, tei swilaih, kholopnairok, stamprok, tei ahaino kisa taipni kolrok tongjak.

english: It is true that there exist in this world situations that defy all explanation, events so strange and wondrous that they seem to be the stuff of dreams or nightmares.
kokborok: Obobo Kubui kok o hayungni tonghalok kwthang tongkho je jottonino chermung bata'ui sana nayo, wngmungrokbo aswkse kirimasingsa tei wanamasingsa abohrok imang hamya rogo nukjakphayo.

english: Such is the case with the story I am about to tell you, a tale of supernatural forces and the strange events that unfolded when they were unleashed upon the world.
kokborok: Obohaino kaisa kothoma ang norokno sanani nayo, kaisa wanaphan tei kaisa siniya-nukya wngma abo khulukjak sinai jephuru bohrok hayungni bwskango pehel rwjaganw.

english: It all began one night, when a group of friends were gathered together for a party.
kokborok: Obo jottono horsani bisingono chengkha, jephuru kaisa kiching bodol kuthumlayo kaisa tongthokmungni bagwi.

english: They were drinking and laughing, enjoying each other's company, when suddenly the lights went out.
kokborok: Bohrok aphuru nwnglaiwi tei mwnwilaiwi, thongthoklaiwi kaisa tei kaisa tongmani atomsa chati thwi paikha.

english: The room was plunged into darkness, and the only sound was the sound of their own breathing.
kokborok: Ah nok khotol mwnakbai koboljak wngwi thangkha, tei kaisa khorang hama nalaima simino khwnaui tongsio.

english: Then, in the darkness, they saw it: a strange, glowing light.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, mwnak bisingo, bohrok kaisa wanamasingsa pohor chwngsaui tongma nukha.

english: It seemed to be coming from nowhere, and it was growing brighter and brighter.
kokborok: Obo ganaginino phaikhwna hwnwi tongkha, tei obo chwngma teibo se chwngprabwi phayo.

english: The friends were terrified, but they were also curious.
kokborok: Kichingsong kirijaklaikha, phiya bohrok sinanibo muchungjago.

english: They wanted to know what this light was, and where it was coming from.
kokborok: Bohrok sinani muchungjagkha o pohorle tamo tei obo boroni phai hwnwi.

english: Slowly, they approached the light.
kokborok: Twrwk twrwk, bohrok pohorni ganao thanglaikha.

english: As they got closer, they could see that it was coming from a small, glowing sphere.
kokborok: Jephuru bohrok ganao sogwio, bohrok nukha obo kaisa chikonsa holong kwchwngni se pohor phayo.

english: The sphere was hovering in the air, and it was surrounded by a faint aura.
kokborok: Ah holong nobaro uriui tongo, tei obo chwnamung bai kitingjak.

english: Funny pictures and videos are a dime a dozen these days, but some of them stand out from the rest.
kokborok: Mwnwi kothok mangpilirok tei videos wngkha kaisa dime chwnwi oh salrogo, phiya baksa haino bohrok kubunrokni slai juda khai nukjago.

english: These are the ones that are so relatable or absurd that they make us laugh out loud.
kokborok: Omo wngkha kaisarok je aswkno solaijak eba khapchaya je bohrok chwng chirikgwi mwnwi rio.

english: One example is a recent video that went viral of a cat trying to fit into a small box.
kokborok: Kaisa phunukmari thangnai video je viral thangmani kaisa aming bakso chikonsa wo habna chaitok tongmani.

english: The cat is clearly struggling, but it keeps trying, and the whole thing is just so funny.
kokborok: Ah aming sraisrai khai kaphramung wngwi tongo, phiya omo chaitogwi tongo, tei jotto manwi wngkha haino aswkno mwnwi kothok.

english: Another example is a picture of a dog wearing a hat that is way too big for it.
kokborok: Tei kaissa phunukmari wngkha kaisa mangpili kaisa swi thupi kanmani je omoni bagwi belai kotorma.

english: The dog looks so ridiculous that it's impossible not to laugh.
kokborok: Ah swi aswkno mwnwijaknaai nukjak tongo je omono mwnwina bwkhak wngmaya.

english: These types of funny pictures and videos are often shared on social media, and they can quickly become a "meme" A meme is a humorous image, video, or piece of text that is copied and shared online.
kokborok: Omtwi sapukthaih mwnwi kothok mangpilirok tei videos wngkha uramuram hodarwk pinlam bakjago, tei bohrok daktino kaisa "meme" wngwi mano meme wngkha kaisa mwnwikothok mangpili, video, eba soibijap ni lapsa je solaijak tei online o bakjakmani.

english: Memes often use familiar images or phrases, and they can be used to express a wide range of emotions.
kokborok: Memes uramuram sinijak mangpilirok eba kokthaihthuprok phwnangjakma, tei bohrok swbaikhrubwi sama bai kuar bwtrang khanangjakrokni bwkhak phwnangjak mano.

english: One thing that must happen when a funny picture or video goes viral is that it is shared with others.
kokborok: Kaisa manwwi je ma wngnai jephuru kaisa mwnwi kothok mangpili eba video viral wngo je amo kubunrokbai bakjakmani.

english: This is what makes memes so popular.
kokborok: Omo ni bagwi memes belai luku hamjakma swnamjago.

english: People see a funny picture or video, and they want to share it with their friends so that they can laugh too.
kokborok: Bohrok nugo kaisa mwnwi kothok mangpili eba vidio, tei bohrok abono bohrokni bayaprok bai bakna muchungjago aswkno je bohrok bo mwnwi manai hwnwi.

english: This is why memes can spread so quickly across the internet.
kokborok: Haini bagwi memes daktino internet ayang naro auaima wngmano.

english: In a time long past, there lived a blind beggar who made his living by demonstrating the art of soil sculpting.
kokborok: Kaisa jora kolok wngthahng bising, aro kaisa mokolnukya bikha birnai tongo je ah haching takmani rikmung kubui phunukmani bai bini tongmani swnamo.

english: He would sit on the street corner, surrounded by his tools and materials, and invite passersby to watch him work.
kokborok: Bo ah lahar kuna o achugo, bini kolrok tei manwi-khwnwirok bai kitingjak, tei laithangnai rokno kwcharo bono samung khaima naima bwkhak.

english: With his deft fingers, he would mold the soil into intricate shapes, creating animals, plants, and even entire landscapes.
kokborok: Bini kwrwng yasirok bai, bo ah hachingsa no supungma bisingo kubuljak banokmarok, malmatarok swnammani, buphang uaphangrok, tei haino jotto hakungmanirok.
