english: Digital messaging across the internet, mobile phones, and other computer networks, such as email, voicemail, and messaging services, has revolutionized the way we communicate.
kokborok: Digital koktunmani ah internet nar bwkhak, mobile phonerok, tei kubun computer networkrok, ahaino email, khorangmail, tei kokkwcharmani sebukrok, chwng manjulaima haikhe lama pekhrubjakmung tongma.

english: In the past, sending a message meant waiting for a letter to arrive by snail mail, or hoping that your recipient would be available to answer their phone.
kokborok: Ah wngthahng bising, kaisa kokkwcharma kokma naisingmani karwi kaisa koktun sokphaima bwkak totobak mail bai, eba khajamani je nini yachaknai bohrok phone bwkhak manthoma wngwi mano.

english: Today, we can send messages instantaneously, regardless of time or location.
kokborok: Tini, chwng kokcharmarok dowui tangjakma howui mano, tongma thai eba khauarya jora.

english: This has had a profound impact on our lives, making it easier to stay in touch with friends and family, conduct business, and access information.
kokborok: Omo kaisa kuthukuk sebrupma tongo chini langmarokni sakao, omono kwlaikukma khai kwrwngwi tongna bwkhak swnamani bayaprok tei bukungni bohrok bai, bepar lamsoma, tei kothum sogwima.

english: However, the speed and convenience of digital messaging has also come with some challenges.
kokborok: Haiphano, ah domung tei digital kokkwcharmani chajakma bo phaikha baksa bataimung bai.

english: One of the most pressing concerns is the issue of data privacy.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai sekrubmani uanamarok wngkha ah sijakrwnai huijakthaino swirwma.

english: As more and more of our personal information is transmitted online, it is becoming increasingly important to protect ourselves from identity theft and other cybercrimes.
kokborok: Chini saksakni kokthuma wngkha online rwhorjakma iko kwbangma bai kwbangma, omo belai nangkukma wngwi tongmani wngkha chinisaksarok katima bwkhak sinrwma khokjakma tei kubun cybertangsitra simi.

english: Another challenge is the problem of spam.
kokborok: Teikaisa bataima wngkha ah spamni kebengmung.

english: Unwanted messages, often containing malicious software or fraudulent links, can be a nuisance and even a danger to our devices and our data.
kokborok: Nangnungya kokwcharmarok, uramuram hamyasutunai software eba thokaimung sordukungrok tongmani, kaisa akarmung tei ahaino kaisa akocho wngmano chini kolmanwirok tei chini sijakrwnai bwkhak.

english: Despite these challenges, digital messaging remains an essential part of our lives.
kokborok: Tophano oh bataimungrok, digital kokwcharmani torwkmarok chini langmarokni bagwi kaisa nangnai bokcho.

english: It is a powerful tool that we can use to connect with others, learn new things, and make our lives more convenient.
kokborok: Omo kaisa phangwnang kok wngkha je chwng kubunrok bai kwrwngna bwkhak phwnang mano, kwtal manwirok swrwngma, tei chini langmarokno teibo chajak swnamma.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Yvonne who lived in a small village.
kokborok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro khoroksa bwrwima sikli Yvonne mungwi tongo je kaisa chikonsa kamio tongo.

english: She was a talented blacksmith, and she loved to work with precious metals.
kokborok: Bo wngkha khoroksa suargnang sortaknai, tei bo mulakaknangkuk kwrakmanwirok bai samung khaina bwkhak chajago.

english: One day, she was working on a new design for a necklace when she had an idea.
kokborok: Salsa, bo kaisa kwtal rikma kaisa ganthi ni sakao samung khai tongman jephuru bini oro kaisa uansukma tongo.

english: She decided to create a necklace that would be made entirely of stones, but she would use a new technique to ensure that the stones were held securely in place.
kokborok: Bo kaisa ganthi swnamna bwkhak kokchapkha je abo jottowui holongrokni bai swnamjago, phiya bo kaisa kwtal tangsep bwkhak khasrai khlaima phanango je ah holongrok no naimwthangjak thai bising tonjakha.

english: Yvonne worked on her necklace for many weeks, and when she was finally finished, she was thrilled with the results.
kokborok: Yvonne bini ganthi sakao samung khaikha kwbangma hatibarok karwi, tei jephuru bo paithago paikha, bo ah thaihmungrok bai saktwikarjak wngkha.

english: The necklace was beautiful, and it was unlike anything anyone had ever seen before.
kokborok: Ah ganti naithoksukha, tei amo swkango waisaphano nujak haya.

english: Yvonne decided to call it the "Innovative Necklace". Yvonne took her necklace to the market, and she was immediately met with a flurry of excitement.
kokborok: Yvonne omono "Innovative ganthi " ringna bwkhak kokchapkha. Yvonne bini ganthi no ah hati bwkhak twlangkha, tei bo daktino malaikha kaisa sundruma tungphalrwjakma bai.

english: Everyone wanted to know where she had gotten such a unique and beautiful necklace.
kokborok: Jottono saimanna muchungjakha bo boro amswk kaisa manthokya tei naithok ganthi mankha.

english: Yvonne told them about her new technique, and she soon had many orders for more necklaces.
kokborok: Yvonne's bohrokno sakha bini kwtal tngsepni bagwi, tei bo daktino kwbangma dagimung mankha teibo ganthirokni bagwi.

english: Yvonne's innovative necklace was a huge success, and she quickly became one of the most famous blacksmiths in the land.
kokborok: Yvonne's innovative ganthi kaisa kotor khlaimanmung wngkha, tei bo daktino khoroksa ah ha ni bising jottoni slai sinikukjak sortaknairokni wngkha.

english: She used her newfound wealth to help her village, and she soon became known as a kind and generous woman.
kokborok: Bo bini kwtalmanma rangmaino bini kamino chubana bwkhak phwnangkha, tei bo daktino kaisa kaham tei khakaham bwrwima hwnwi sinijak wngkha.

english: Superstition is the belief in supernatural forces that can influence events and be influenced by human actions.
kokborok: Mwnakpoito wngkha kaisa siya nukya phan gwnang swbgcharni phan abo khoroksaswkno kobolmano tei borokbai phano koboljak mano.

english: This is often based on folklore and tradition, and can vary widely from culture to culture.
kokborok: Oborok homanino kerong kothoma tei hukumu rokbai mangno kwrwngjak wngo, kaisa tei kaisa hukumu bai pherlayo.

english: Some common superstitions include avoiding walking under a ladder, breaking a mirror, and spilling salt.
kokborok: Baksa nuk kukmani mwnakpoito wngkha yakhili tolatwi himmung, mangnuk swbaimung tei som sarmung.

english: Superstitions can have a significant impact on people's lives, causing them to avoid certain activities or objects out of fear of bad luck.
kokborok: Mwnakpoito borok rokni langmao kaichomwi potaliui mano, tei bohrokno saijak samungrok khwlaithani konorwi mano talikha hamya eba chaya wngnao kiriui.

english: They can also lead to irrational beliefs and behaviors, such as the belief that a certain charm or ritual can bring good luck.
kokborok: Kosolya poito tei tongmungrogo wansukthani luku raidao gosijak talikha hamya hwnwi phano chongwi mano.

english: There is no scientific evidence to support the existence of supernatural forces, and many people believe that superstitions are simply a way for people to cope with uncertainty and fear.
kokborok: Abo soisimungni mungsa mari kwrwi siniya-nukya phan rokni, tei kwbang borokno poito khwlayo mwnakpoito wngkha borok rokno sikriui sak chana naimase.

english: However, superstitions can be harmful, as they can lead to anxiety, stress, and even self-harm.
kokborok: Haiphano, mwnakpoito derarwnai phano wngmano, wanamung, kesep tei saksakno dukhu rwnarok sudano muchungmano.

english: It is important to be aware of the potential dangers of superstitions and to be able to challenge them when they arise.
kokborok: Mwnakpoito no kasuna bagwi obono nangkukmani sichamung tongna nangnai je oborok bangrwrwgwi tongkhe kasuna nangnai.

english: If you are struggling with superstitions, there are a few things you can do to help yourself.
kokborok: Nwng tumung mwnakpoito bai kubulwi tongkhe, nwng saksakno yoknani bagwi kisaswk lam tongo.

english: First, try to identify the sources of your superstitions.
kokborok: Puila, mwnakpoito boroni phai abono sinina naidi.

english: Are they based on your culture, your family, or your own personal experiences?
kokborok: Aborok nini hukumu bai gwdaljak da gwdaljak ya, nini nukhung eba saksani bujimabai.

english: Junk food is a type of food that is high in calories, fat, and sugar, and low in nutrients.
kokborok: Hamya chahthai wngkha kaisa sapokthaaih chamung je kuchuk calories, bupham, tei chini, tei bolimung kom.

english: It is often made with processed ingredients and is typically consumed in large quantities.
kokborok: Omono uramuram tangraida swraimanwi swnamjago tei hainohai kotorma ujunwi chajago.

english: Junk food can be addictive, and it can lead to a number of health problems, including obesity, heart disease, and type 2 diabetes.
kokborok: Hamya chahthai loi wngwi mano, tei omo sakduk lombor biyalwi sorphurwi mano, kuphung khobwinai, bwkhani bemar, tei 2 swtwibemar sapokthaih.

english: There are many different types of junk food, including candy, chips, soda, and fast food.
kokborok: Aro kwbangma juda juda sapokthai hamya chahthai tongo, candy no khobwi, chips, soda, tei dophre chathai.

english: These foods are often brightly colored and heavily marketed to children.
kokborok: Oh chahthai wngkha uramuram chwngsarwi palirwi tei chwrairokno naisikgwi hatio karijago.

english: They are also typically very cheap, which makes them a popular choice for people on a budget.
kokborok: Bohrok wngkha hainohai belai kwlai, bohrokni kaisa rangchongmung abo borokni bising lukuk hamjakjak chongwi swnamjago.

english: Junk food can be a problem for people of all ages, but it is especially harmful to children.
kokborok: Hamya chahthai jotto omor ni borokni bagwi biyal wngwi mano, phiya chwrairokni bagwi teibo hamya wngwimano.

english: Children who eat a lot of junk food are more likely to be overweight or obese, and they are also more likely to develop health problems later in life.
kokborok: Chwrairok je kwbangma hamya chahthai chanairok teibo belaihilikma eba kuphung wngwimano, tei bohrok langmani olo chwrwma sakduk biyalwi teibo kwbang bwkhak wngwimano.

english: There are a number of things that can be done to help reduce the consumption of junk food.
kokborok: Aro lombor manwi wngkha je hamya chahthaino chamani khairwi chubachu khaimano.

english: Parents can talk to their children about the importance of eating healthy foods, and they can make sure that healthy foods are available in the home.
kokborok: Mapharok bohrokni chwrairokni bagwi nangkukma chamani sakdukma chahthaini bagwi salai mano, tei bohrok wngkubui swnam mano je sakdukma chahthai nogono manthogo.

english: Schools can offer healthier options in their cafeterias, and they can educate students about the dangers of junk food.
kokborok: Rwngnokrok bohrokni cafeterias wo teibo sakdukmani saimung kokyapharwiw mano, tei bohrok rwngswrwngnairokno phwrwng mano hamya chahthai kebengmungni bagwi.

english: Arranged marriages have been a part of the Indian culture for centuries.
kokborok: Gothokrwjak kailaimungrok ah Indian hukumu bisirarokni bagwi kaisa bokocho wngkha.

english: While they are often seen as a relic of the past, they are still practiced by a significant portion of the population today.
kokborok: jephururu bohrok haino kaisa baikhrupjak wngthangjak uramuram nukjago, bohrok tabukbo loi khlaijago kaisa ah bohrok bahngma tini bo kaisa nangjakma bokcho bai.

english: There are many reasons why people choose to have an arranged marriage, including the desire to find a partner who shares their values and beliefs, the need to secure financial stability, and the desire to avoid the social stigma associated with being single.
kokborok: Oro kwbangma karonrok tong tangwi borokrok gothokrwjak kailaimung, ah muchungma kaisa logisong naitukma bwkhak khobwinai je bohrokni swkrok tei poitorok bagmarok, tei ah muchungma katima bwkhak ah hodarwk mungsitramung gwdaljak bai saichung tongjak bai.

english: In recent years, arranged marriages have come under fire from some critics who argue that they are outdated and discriminatory.
kokborok: Wngwi thangjak bisirok bising, gothokrwjak kailaimungrok hor ni tola phai tongkha baksa critics simi je tokra rio bohrok wngkha kwchamjak tei khakjakmani.

english: However, proponents of arranged marriage argue that they can be a positive way for two people to find happiness and fulfillment.
kokborok: Haiphano, gothokrwjak kailaimung tokra twichurumarok je bohrok kaisa kubui lama borok khoroknwi bagwi tongthokma tei khlaimanma naitukma bwkhak wngwi mano.

english: Ultimately, the decision of whether or not to have an arranged marriage is a personal one.
kokborok: Paithago, ah chongmani jesaba eba haiya kaisa gwdaljak kailaimung wngkha kaisa sakbaithang ni oro se.

english: There is no right or wrong answer, and what works for one person may not work for another.
kokborok: Aro mungsa chaya tei chanai kokphirokmung kwrwi, tei khoroksa borok ni bagwi tamo samung wng abo tei khoroksa ni bagwi samung wngya.

english: One anecdote that illustrates the complex and nuanced nature of arranged marriages is the story of Anju and Amit.
kokborok: Kaisa kokduma je kok swbaikhurmarok ah kutuk tei habar swrwngjak gwdaljak kailaimungrok wngkha ah kothoma Anju tei Amit ni.

english: Anju was a young woman from a small village in India.
kokborok: Anju wngkha khoroksa bwrwima sikli India ni kaisa chikonsa kami ni simi.

english: She had always dreamed of finding a husband who loved her for who she was.
kokborok: Bo homnino imang nugo kaisa bwsai kaham naituknani je bono hamjaknai je jetwi tongmani haikhe.

english: However, her parents had other plans for her.
kokborok: Haiphano, bini mapharok bini bagwi kubun chapmarok tongo.

english: Droughts and crop failure can have a devastating impact on food security, livelihoods, and the economy.
kokborok: Khoranrok tei bwthaih bethaya kaisa swbaimani sekrupma chathaih naimwthang, tangchamungrok, tei rangthong sakao tongwi mano.

english: In recent years, the world has experienced a number of severe droughts, which have led to crop failures and food shortages.
kokborok: Laithangma bisirok bising, ah hayung kwbangma kwrak khoranrok simari tongo, bomo bwthaih bethayarok tei chathaih kulukyarok bwkhak dagima tongo.

english: These droughts have caused widespread fear and anxiety, as people worry about how they will feed their families.
kokborok: Oh khoranrok kuarpisrarjak kirima tei uanma pherjak tongo, iko borokrok bahaikhe bohrok bohrokni nukhungno chahrwna bagwi unajak.

english: In some cases, governments have been forced to take drastic measures to address the impact of droughts.
kokborok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, haphangrok kwrak sumarok nama bwkhak tangphan tongkha ah sekrupma khoranrok nikuma bwkhak.

english: For example, in 2011, the government of Ethiopia declared a state of emergency in response to a severe drought that had caused widespread crop failure.
kokborok: Phunukmarki karwi, 2011 o, ah Ethiopia haphang kaisa haste naigramung sakhlaikha kaisa kwrak khoran bwkhak siphirokma bising je kuarpisarjak bwthaih bethaya pherjak tongo.

english: The government provided emergency food aid to millions of people, and it also implemented a number of measures to help farmers cope with the drought.
kokborok: Ah haphang chirasairok borokno naigramung bwkhak chahthai chubama manthokrikha.

english: These measures included providing seeds and fertilizers, and building irrigation canals.
kokborok: Oh sumarok bwchwlwirok tei phasrok, tei twilumung twilahrok tisamani manthokmani khobjak.

english: Despite these measures, the drought had a devastating impact on the country's economy.
kokborok: Tophano oh sumarok, ah khorak ah hakotorni rangthong sakao sekrupma swbaimani tongkha.

english: The agricultural sector was severely affected, and many farmers were forced to abandon their land.
kokborok: Ah hukba kitingkhak kwrakma nangrwjak wngkha, tei kwbangma chuainairok bohrokni ha no yakarna bwkhak tangphan wngkha.

english: The drought also led to a sharp increase in food prices, which made it difficult for many people to afford food.
kokborok: Ah khoran bo chahthai swkrok bising kaisa kubuk bwkhak dagima tongo, bomo borokni bagwi chahthai manma bwkhak omo 3 swnamo.

english: The impact of droughts and crop failure is not limited to the countries that are directly affected.
kokborok: Ah sekrupma khoranrok tei bwthaih bethaya ah hakotorok bwkhak paithak ari wngya je sakphangma nangrwjak wngkha.

english: The AIDS crisis has had a devastating impact on communities around the world.
kokborok: Ah AIDS biyal kaisa ah hayung yaksiyagra hodarokni sako swbaimani sekrupma nakha.

english: In the United States, it is estimated that more than 650,000 people have died from AIDS since the epidemic began in the 1980s.
kokborok: Ah Unites States bising, omo lekhajakma je 650, 000 borok slai teibo thwi tongkha AIDS simi ah 1980s bising chacharara chengna swkang.

english: The disease has also had a significant impact on the social and economic fabric of communities.
kokborok: Ah bemar karwi bo tongo kaisa nangkukma sekrupma ah hodarwk tei rangthong swnamma hodarok.

english: Many people living with HIV/AIDS have lost their jobs, their homes, and their loved ones.
kokborok: Kwbangma borok HIV/AIDS bai tongmani bohrokni samungrok, bohrokni nokrok, tei bohrokni hamjakma borokrok kwmajak tongkha.

english: The epidemic has also led to increased stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV/AIDS.
kokborok: Ah chacharara selengmung bangkha tei khakamung borok kebengwi HIV/AIDS bai tongmani dagima bwkhak bo tongo.

english: Despite the challenges, there is a growing sense of community among people living with HIV/AIDS.
kokborok: Tophano ah bataimungrok, aro kaisa tormani wngkha sinai simanwi hoda bohrok bisingo tongmani HIV/AIDS bai.

english: This community is based on a shared experience of living with the disease, as well as a shared commitment to fighting for a cure.
kokborok: Ah hoda wngkha kaisa simari banta ah bemar bai tongmani yaphang sakao, aboni logi kaisa swmai tangmung banta kaisa hammung bagwi bulaimani bwkhak.

english: People living with HIV/AIDS have come together to support each other, to advocate for their rights, and to raise awareness about the disease.
kokborok: Borok HIV/AIDS bai tongmani thansa phaikha kubun thwgwi nangmani bwkhak, bohrokni manthairokni bagwi sualphang bwkhak, tei ah bemarni bagwi saimanrima tisama bwkhak.

english: This community has been instrumental in making progress in the fight against AIDS.
kokborok: Oh hoda sakmanwi swnammani bising ah AIDS no kebengwi bulaim bising chasamung wngkha.

english: One example of this community is the AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power (ACT UP).
kokborok: Kaisa phunukmari oh hoda wngkha ah AIDS kwthamung phang phiyokma (ACT UP) bwkhak.

english: ACT UP is a grassroots organization of people living with HIV/AIDS and their allies.
kokborok: ACT UP wngkha kaisa yaphangyarwngrok motha bohrok HIV/AIDS bai tongmani tei bohrokni kwthamarok.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Alice who was very interested in ethics.
kokborok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro kaisa bwrwima sikli Alice mungwi tong je belai khlaithai koknorok bising ol manjak.

english: She wanted to learn more about the different ethical theories and how they could be applied to everyday life.
kokborok: Bo tebi swrwngna muchungjakma bwkha ah juda juda khlaithi kokma kokbwrairok tei bahaii bohrok salbrumbrum langma o thepai man.

english: One day, Alice was walking through the forest when she came across a small cottage.
kokborok: Salsa, Alice ah bolong twih hwnwi tongmani jephuru bo kaisa chikonsa nokbwsa twih phaikha.

english: The cottage was owned by an old woman named Eda, who was a wise and respected member of the community.
kokborok: Ah nok chikonsa khoroksa bwrwichwk Eda mungwi bai naharjak, je belai sijala tei hoda songni bising boromjak.

english: Alice knocked on the door and Eda invited her inside.
kokborok: Alice ah duklam tokkha tei Eda bono bisingo ringkha.

english: Alice told Eda about her interest in ethics, and Eda asked her a few questions to get a better understanding of her background.
kokborok: Alice Eda no sakha bini khlaithai kokrok ol manmung bising, tei Eda bono kaisa kokswngmungrok swnkha kaisa kahamkuk buchimanai bini hatlai manna bwkhak.

english: Then, Eda told Alice about a story from her own life.
kokborok: Hwnkhe, Eda Aliceno kaisa kothoma sakha bini sakni langmani bagwi.

english: Eda said that when she was young, she was a very talented artist.
kokborok: Eda sakha je jephuru bo sikli phuru, tei bo wngkha belai manphanjak swnamkwrwng.

english: She loved to paint and draw, and she was always coming up with new ideas.
kokborok: Bo pali rikna tei agukma bwkhal, tei bo homnino saka phaimani wngkha kwtal khachongmarok bwkhak.

english: One day, Eda was working on a painting of a beautiful landscape when she realized that she could make a lot of money by selling it.
kokborok: Salsa, Eda kaisa pali rikani sako samungkhaimani wngkha kaisa naithok hakung mari jephuru bo saimankhaa je bo kwbang rang swnam mano amono phalmani bai.

english: Eda was tempted to sell the painting, but she knew that it would be wrong to do so.
kokborok: Eda ah pali rikmani no phalna bwkhak lugrijak wngkha, phiya bo saimano je amo khaimani chaya wngwi mano.

english: Coming of age is a time of great change and self-discovery.
kokborok: Omor horwi phaima jorarok saksakno swnamnani tei kotor swlaimung jora.

english: It is a time when we begin to learn who we are and what we want out of life.
kokborok: Obono swrwngmani jora tei chini langmao wngna muchungma rokbo.

english: It is also a time when we learn to take responsibility for our own actions and to make our own decisions.
kokborok: Ojorao no chwng saksakni khwlaithai rokno khwlayo sak sakni chongmung tei samungbai.

english: The journey of coming of age is not always easy.
kokborok: Omor horwi phaimani jora abo dalsa thayo tongya.

english: There will be times when we feel lost, confused, or alone.
kokborok: Aro ahai jorabo tongo chwng jorao kwmajago, pal manya wngo eba saichung susuru khakao.

english: But it is also a time of great opportunity and growth.
kokborok: Phiyaba obo kotor sep bo hwnwi mano hamchanani bagwi.

english: We can learn to become more independent, more confident, and more resilient.
kokborok: Chwng teibo khakwrak wngnani bagwi teibo swrwngna mano, teibo kharagwi thonjak wngwi mano.

english: We can learn to live our lives with purpose and meaning.
kokborok: Chwng chini langmano teibo swrwngwi kahamkhe tongwi thangmano langmani kokmangrokno teibo swrai swraikhe siniui.

english: If you are currently in the process of coming of age, know that you are not alone.
kokborok: Nwng tumung tabuk omor hormani jorao phaiwi sokphaikhe, saimandi nwng saichunglia hwnwi.

english: Many people have gone before you, and many will go after you.
kokborok: Kwbang borokno nini swlai swkang thangkha, tei teibo kwbang borok thangnai nini ulobo.

english: The journey of coming of age is a universal one, and it is one that we all must take.
kokborok: Thangsuk langma him mung abo hayungo kaisano, tei obo kaisa chwng jottono salsa yachagwi ma nanai.

english: Conservation of natural resources is essential to the survival of humans and all other life on Earth.
kokborok: Hapharni manwi khwnwi khatimung borol munuisu tei jotto kwthang tongnairokni bagwi belai nangkukmani.

english: Natural resources are the materials and energy sources that humans rely on for survival, such as water, air, soil, minerals, and plants.
kokborok: Borok munuisu thangwi tongna bagwi hapharni manthokma manwibai gwdalwi kwrwngwi ma tongsogo romdi, nobar, twi, ha, hani manwi tei buphang waphangrok.

english: When we conserve natural resources, we are using them wisely and preventing them from being wasted or depleted.
kokborok: Chwng jephuru hapharni manthokma manwino khatio, chwng ah manwino kahamkhe chabwi samung phwnangma kwlayo eba mosogwi rohorya.

english: One way to conserve natural resources is to reduce our consumption.
kokborok: Hapharni manwino khatinani hwnkhe bono samungo phwnangmani ma khochor rwnai.

english: We can do this by buying less stuff, using less energy, and wasting less water.
kokborok: Chwng kisa kisakhe khochorwi manwi paimani bisingtwi, kesep khe hapharni phan tei twirok kisakhe samung phwnangmani bisingtwi.

english: We can also recycle and compost, which helps to reduce the amount of waste that goes to landfills.
kokborok: Chwng recycle tei ha kosok swnamwi panthor ha rogo teisa samung phwnang manphinai.

english: Another way to conserve natural resources is to invest in renewable energy sources.
kokborok: Tei dalsa lamtwi hapharni phan rokno khatina hwnkhe paiphlaiya hapharni phan no samungo ma thepanai.

english: Renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, do not produce greenhouse gases, which contribute to climate change.
kokborok: Paiphlaiya haphar phan romdi, saltung tei nobar ni phan, aborok green house gas rokno swnamya abagwi nobar twibarbo swlaijakya.

english: They are also a sustainable way to generate electricity, as they do not rely on finite resources like fossil fuels.
kokborok: Aborok paiphlaiya chwng chwng pherang swnambo mungsa hapharno dera rwya thok kosom sokmungni slai.

english: Conservation of natural resources is important for both the present and the future.
kokborok: Hapharni phan manwi khatimung obo tabuk tei thinang jorani bagwi nangkugo.

english: By taking steps to conserve now, we can ensure that future generations will have access to the natural resources they need to survive.
kokborok: Step namani bisingtwi tabukni simino hapharni phan no ma khatinai thinang jorani borokni bagwi bohrok kha kwchangkhe langma thangsuk manna twi.

english: Obesity is a major public health problem that affects people of all ages, races, and ethnicities.
kokborok: Kuphung kotor wngmani jwngjal wngkha bebak bisi ni borokrogo no manjago.

english: In July 2023, the World Health Organization (WHO) released a new report on obesity, which found that the number of obese people worldwide has tripled since 1975.
kokborok: 2023 bisi ni Taltuk o, World Health Organization(WHO ) kaisa kwtal awaimung rwkha kuphungtor ma no twywi, 1975 bisi ni simi rwgwi naijakmani manjak kha kuphung kotor wngmani abo yakhilik engtham jora twi kasajak.

english: The report also found that obesity is now the fifth leading cause of death globally.
kokborok: Awaimung o manjak kha swngchar gwnangwi kuphung torwi thwimani tabok jora twi yakhilik engba o kasajak.

english: There are many factors that contribute to obesity, including genetics, diet, and physical activity.
kokborok: Kwbangmani bisingtwi kuphung torwi mano, bosong rwgwi thwi o solo mani no khobwi, chamani bai bo, tei phan ni samung bai bo.

english: However, the environment also plays a role.
kokborok: Aro bising, chwng tongmani tongkhor bo belai samung kotor khwlayo.

english: For example, many people live in areas where healthy food is expensive and inaccessible, and where there are few opportunities for physical activity.
kokborok: Phunukmari , kwbangkuk borokrogno kaham chamung morok tei abono paiwi chamaya abotwi thai o tongnairok tongbayo, tei aro phan ni samung bo aswk ma khwlaiya.

english: Obesity can have a number of negative health consequences, including heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, and some types of cancer.
kokborok: Kuphung tormani abo bwsakni bagwi kwbangma no hamya khwlayo, bwkha ni bemarno khobwi, stroke, types 2 diabetes, tei cancer manjak manirog.

english: It can also lead to social isolation and discrimination.
kokborok: Kuphung tormani bai amchairogo norjagwi mano tei cherjakya bo wngwi mano.

english: There are a number of things that can be done to address the problem of obesity.
kokborok: Kuphung tormani jwngjal no twywi kaisa kainwi khwlaijaknai tongo.

english: These include making healthy food more affordable and accessible, providing more opportunities for physical activity, and changing the way we think about obesity.
kokborok: Abohrok wngkha chamung kaham no teibo manthok rwdi tei morokya khwlai di, phan ni samungno teisa jora rw di, tei kuphung tormano twywi uansok marogno swlaina nango.

english: In July 2023, the U.S. government released its first ever National Strategy for Childhood Obesity.
kokborok: Taltuk talni 2023 o, U.S. ni haphang awaimung khwlai kha boni pwilani National Strategy for Childhood Obesity no.

english: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Alice who was very good at math.
kokborok: Jora kaisao, Alice mungwi bwrwi sikla khoroksa lekhamung kwrwng tongmani.

english: She loved to solve problems and come up with new solutions.
kokborok: Bo lekhamung rokno kwtal twtalkhe chapnani belaino hamjago.

english: But when she went to college, she quickly realized that she was one of the only women in her math classes.
kokborok: Phiya bo jephuru rwngnok kotoro thango aphuru wansukma phayo bo simise saichung bwrwi lekhamung khwlainai.

english: The other students were often surprised to see her there, and they would sometimes make comments about her gender.
kokborok: Juda swrwngnairok bono nugui wanajago tei bono alaidakhe bwrwi hwnwi khagwi tonlayo.

english: One day, Alice was working on a problem in the library when a group of male students came up to her.
kokborok: Salsa, Alice bijapkhoro kaisa problemno twywi samung khwlai tongphuru kaisa chwla bodolrok bini ganao phaikha.

english: They started making fun of her for being a woman in math, and they told her that she would never be able to succeed.
kokborok: Bwrwi saichung lekhasimung wngmabai bohrok bono phatra khwlai layo, tei bohrok bono hai hwnwi sao nwng nini langmao mungsa khwlai manglak.

english: Alice was very upset, but she didn't let them get to her.
kokborok: Alice aphuru belaino wanajago, phiya bo bwkha baya.

english: She knew that she was good at math, and she wasn't going to let anyone tell her otherwise.
kokborok: Bo sio bo lekhamungno belai kaham, tei bo kebono sana muchungjakya.

english: Alice continued to study hard, and she eventually graduated from college with honors.
kokborok: Alice thakphlaiyakhe samung kwrak khwlaikha, tei phaithago rwngborom bwlaibo mankha.

english: She went on to get a Ph.D. in math, and she became a successful mathematician.
kokborok: Bo lekhamungo Ph.D khwlai rwngkwrwngbo wngkha.

english: She proved that she was just as good as any man, and she showed the world that gender discrimination is no match for a woman who is determined to succeed.
kokborok: Bo kubuikhe phunukha chwlabai baksano lekhamung kwrwng, tei o hayungno phunugwi rwkha chwla bwrwi khaklaimung tongphano khagwi manya je kwplai wngnani chaitoknai borokno.

english: If I could stop aging, I would do so many things.
kokborok: Tumungno ang omor wngmani bathak mankhe, ang kwbangma mawirok khlaikhamu.

english: I would travel the world, visiting all the places I've always dreamed of seeing.
kokborok: Ang hayung beraikhamu, jotto thairogo naina thangwi ang homni imang nugwi tongmani.

english: I would learn new languages and cultures.
kokborok: Ang kwtal kokrok tei hukumurok swrwngkhamu.

english: I would spend more time with my family and friends.
kokborok: Ang tei ang nukhung tei bayaprokbai teibo jora katikhamu.

english: I would make a difference in the world.
kokborok: Ang hayungni bising kaisa juda juda khai swnamkhamu.

english: But I know that aging is a natural part of life.
kokborok: Phiyia ang saimano je omor wngma wngkha kaisa habar langma ni bokcho.

english: It's a process that we all go through, and it's something that we should embrace.
kokborok: Omo kaisa tangsep je chwng jotto twih thango, tei omo mungsamanwi je chwng lamsokna nango.

english: As we age, we gain wisdom and experience.
kokborok: Chwng omor wngo, chwng simung tei saimanma mano.

english: We become more resilient and compassionate.
kokborok: Chwng teibo khongkwlai tei khayokjakma.

english: We learn to appreciate the simple things in life.
kokborok: Chwng swrwngna bwkhak chajakma ah khakepleng manwirok langma ni bising.

english: So, while I may not be able to stop aging, I can choose to make the most of it.
kokborok: Aswkno, jephuru ang omor wngmani no bathak mangwlak, ang saima bwkhak swnam mano ah jottono.

english: As a driver, I've seen firsthand the effects of poverty in India.
kokborok: Khoroksa chaluknai wngwi, ang nukha puilayak ah bigra sago kwlaima India bising.

english: Every day, I drive past people living in slums, begging on the streets, and working in dangerous and unhealthy conditions.
kokborok: Sal thwigwi, ang nokchukhrurok tongmani borok lai chaluk phaiyo.

english: It's heartbreaking to see so many people struggling to survive.
kokborok: Aswk kwbangma borok thangma bwkhak kaphramani nukma bwkhak bwkhabaimani omo.

english: Poverty is a complex problem with no easy solutions.
kokborok: Bigra wngkha kaisa kutuk kebengmung 1 gwdalmungrok bai.

english: It's caused by a variety of factors, including lack of education, lack of opportunity, and social and economic inequality.
kokborok: Omo pherkha kaisa dalbidal kusungchwlwirok bai, rwng kwrwi khobmani, sep kwrwi, tei hodarwk tei rangthong thansaya.

english: The government is working to address poverty, but it's a slow process.
kokborok: Ah hapang bigra sakhlaima bwkhak samung khaimai wngkha, phiya omo kaisa keler tangsep.

english: There are many challenges to overcome, including corruption, bureaucracy, and a lack of resources.
kokborok: Aro kwbang bataimungrok tongo mechenma bwkhak, coruuption, haphangtanglam, tei kaisa bumukrok kwrwi.

english: In the meantime, people living in poverty are struggling to make ends meet.
kokborok: Omon bisingtwih, borok bigra bising tongmani wngkha kaphramani malaima paithakrok swnamma bwkhak.

english: They often have to make difficult choices, such as choosing between food and medicine.
kokborok: Bohrok uramuram 3 saimarok swnamma bwkhak tongo, ahaino chaithai tei bithi kwcharo saimani.

english: Poverty is a serious problem, but it's not impossible to overcome.
kokborok: Bigra wngkha kaisa kubui kebengmung, phiya omono mechenma bwkhak wngmanya wngya.

english: With hard work, dedication, and a commitment to social justice, we can create a world where everyone has the opportunity to live a full and prosperous life.
kokborok: Samung kwrak bai, saktharma, tei kaisa hodarwk mankubui bwkhak swmai tangmani, chwng kais hayung swnam mano boro jottono ah sep tongna bwkhak kaisa kuplung tongma tei talikha hamrwmani langma bai.

english: In the past, people did not know the importance of exercise.
kokborok: Agio, borokrok saimanya ah sakswnam nangkumarok.

english: They thought that it was only for athletes and people who wanted to lose weight.
kokborok: Bohrok wansukha je amo aswkno thwngnairok ni bagwii simi tei borok je hilikmung khairina muchungjakma bwkhak.

english: However, science has shown that exercise is important for everyone.
kokborok: Haiphano, soisimung phunukha je sakswnam wngkha jottoni bagwi nangkukma.

english: It can help to reduce the risk of heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, and some types of cancer.
kokborok: Omo kaisa bwkha bemar khapharmung khainani bwkhak chubama mano, ayukmuyuk, sapokthaih 2 swtwibemar, tei baksa cancer sapokthaihrok.

english: It can also help to improve mood, sleep, and energy levels.
kokborok: Omo moji , mwtwrwi, tei tangphan hasmairok chasama bwkha chubai mano.

english: If you are not used to exercising, start slowly and gradually increase the amount of time and intensity of your workouts.
kokborok: Tumungno nwng sakswnamnai bwkhak phwnangya hwnkhe, twrwk-twrwk chengma tei remrem khai jora tei nini kwbangkukma samungkarimarok bangrwimano.

english: There are many different ways to exercise, so find something that you enjoy and that fits into your lifestyle.
kokborok: Aro wngkha kwbangma juda juda sakswnam bwkhak lamarok, aswkno mungsaswk naitukna je nwng tongthok tei je nini tongdal no khropsa khaima bisingtwi.

english: You can walk, run, bike, swim, lift weights, or do yoga.
kokborok: Nwng himwi, kharma, bike, twi yohkma, hilikmung tisama, eba yoga khaima.

english: Just make sure to get at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week.
kokborok: Haino wngkubui swnamma bwkha mukhisa 30 srapsarok nadi 2-kwbangkuma sakswnam ah hatibar jottoni slai salrok twi.

english: Exercise is one of the best things you can do for your health.
kokborok: Sakswnam wngkha kaisa kahamkuk manwirok nwng nini sakduk ni bagwi khai mano.

english: It can help you to live a longer, healthier life.
kokborok: Omo nono tei kisa kolokuk, sakdujakma langma tongna bwkhak chubai mano.

english: The wide variety of natural resources available on Earth has been the subject of much scientific research and speculation.
kokborok: Hayungo manthoknai habarni dalbidal rwbai kwbangma soisimatwi amjok naitukmung tei khachongmungni bothoma tongmani.

english: Some of the most commonly referenced resources include water, air, soil, minerals, and energy.
kokborok: Kisaswk khursathai rwbaini bisingo tongo twi, nokbar, ha, habising manwi tei pherang.

english: The availability and distribution of these resources varies widely around the globe, and this has a significant impact on the development of human societies.
kokborok: Oh rwbairokni manthokmung tei bakmung hayung gwnangwi belaikhe swlaijakha tei obo borok hodani hamkwrayo kaisa khursathai swlaimung khikwlaikha.

english: For example, some regions of the world are rich in natural resources, while others are relatively poor.
kokborok: Phunukmarini bagwi, hayungni kisaswk amchai habarni tangdalbai kupulwng, taisa kubunrok hinkhe aswk kwrwi.

english: This can lead to significant differences in the standard of living between different countries and regions.
kokborok: Obo judajuda hakotor tei ha-bwkhakni bisingo tangwi chahmungni marino twywi nangmani pher chongwimanw.

english: It can also lead to conflict and competition over the control of natural resources.
kokborok: Obo habarni rwbaino yaphao tonmano twywi ualaimung tei bataimungbo wngwimanw.

english: The use of natural resources has also had a significant impact on the environment.
kokborok: Habarni rwbaino samungo phwnangmung tongkhorni sakaobo khursathai swlaimung khikwlaikha.

english: The extraction and processing of natural resources can pollute the air, water, and soil.
kokborok: Habarni rwbaino kariui tubumung tei samungo thepamung nokbar, twi tei ha sitrarwimanw.

english: It can also lead to the depletion of natural resources, which can have a devastating impact on ecosystems.
kokborok: Obo habarni rwbaino chamrwimanw, jebo tongkhor raidani sakao deramungni swlaimung khikwlaimanw.

english: As the world's population continues to grow, the demand for natural resources is also increasing.
kokborok: Hayungni borok bangmari bangmabai baksa habarni rwbai nangmabo bangwi tongo.

english: This is putting a strain on the Earth's resources, and it is important to find ways to use natural resources more sustainably.
kokborok: Obo hayungni rwbaini sakao phanbai sinklugwi tongo tei habarni rwbaino teibo kwrakkhe samungo phwnangnani lam naituknani belai nangkugo.

english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are a language, a means of communication between cook and food.
kokborok: Ah gadgets tei ah nokgantini twkrok wngkha kaisa kok, kaisa kokmarok gwdalaimani songma tei chathaih ni bising.

english: The whisk, the tongs, the ladle, the spatula - each has its own meaning, its own purpose.
kokborok: Ah bupranai, ah yakheprok, ah tharukrok, ah spatula - thwgwi omoni sakni kokmang tongo, omoni sakni naimung bai.

english: To use them well is to understand the language of cooking, to season the dish with the flavors of experience and skill.
kokborok: Bohrokno kaham khai phwnangma hwnkhe ah songmani kok buchina bwkhak wngma, ah thokmungrok saimanjak tei yaksrai bai ah mui no season khaima bwkhak.

english: The whisk is a whisk, the tongs are tongs, and the ladle is a ladle.
kokborok: Ah bupranai wngkha kaisa bupranai, ah yekheprok wngkha ah yekheprok , tei ah tharuk wngkha ah thahruk.

english: But in the hands of a skilled cook, they become something more: they become extensions of the cook's own body, tools that allow him or her to express creativity and passion.
kokborok: Phiya kaisa yaksrai songnai ni yago, bohrok mungsaswk teibo wngo: bohrok ah songnaini sakni bwsak phuarmarok wngo, manwirok je bono eba bono sraisrai khai sama bwkhak swnamkwrwng tei khamuchung gosio.

english: With a whisk, the cook can whip up a frothy batter or emulsify a delicate sauce.
kokborok: Kaisa bupranai bai, ah songnai kaisa sobomma battery eba kaisa naithok sauce emulsify dukalatha saka khai mano.

english: With tongs, he or she can flip a steak or turn a roast.
kokborok: Yekheprokbai, bo eba bo kaisa steak no yohrmung eba kaisa yohkma pakok mano.

english: With a ladle, he or she can ladle out a steaming bowl of soup or sauce.
kokborok: Kaisa tharuk bai, bo eba bo kaisa muthungmani khuri muitwi eba sauce tharuk kari mano.

english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are more than just tools.
kokborok: Ah gadgets tei twkrok ah nokganti haino manwirokni slai teibo wngkha.

english: They are a means of expression, a way to create something beautiful and delicious.
kokborok: Bohrok wngkha kaisa kokmarok kok samung, naithok tei kothok mungsaswk kaisa lama bwkhak swnamma.

english: The wind howled through the trees, and the rain beat down on the roof of the old cabin.
kokborok: Ah nokbar ah buphangrok twih sokromkha, tei ah watwi ah kwcham nokbwsa nukhung sakao tola buwo.

english: Inside, a young woman sat by the fire, knitting.
kokborok: Bisingo, khoroksa bwrwima sikli ah hor bai achukjak, khachropmani wngkha.

english: She was alone in the cabin, save for the cat curled up at her feet.
kokborok: Boh ah nokbwsa bising saichung wngkha, ah aming bini yapha tola kitingjakni bagwi mwthangma.

english: The woman sighed and looked out the window at the storm.
kokborok: Ah bwrwima tailkha tei tailamni phatar bankundri no naisikha.

english: She had been living in this cabin for many years, and she had grown used to the noise of the wind and the rain.
kokborok: Boh kwbangma bisirok karwi oh nokbwsa bising tongwi tongkha, tei bo ah nokbarni khorang tei ah watwi bwkhak loi wngwi torwi phaikha.

english: But tonight, the noise seemed different.
kokborok: Phiya tini horo, ah khorang khakama juda.

english: It was louder, and it seemed to be coming from closer by.
kokborok: Omo khorangkotorma wngkha, tei omo khakama ganarwk bai simi phamani bwhak wngkha.

english: The woman stood up and went to the window.
kokborok: Ah bwrwi bachakha tei ah tailam bwkhak thangkha.

english: She peered out into the darkness, but she could see nothing.
kokborok: Bo ah mwnakma bising phatar naisonkha, phiya boh mungsaphano nukliya.

english: She turned away from the window and went back to her knitting.
kokborok: Boh ah tailamni simi hakchalo philkha tei bini khachropmani bwkhak phirok thangkha.

english: Freshwater lakes are home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, from microscopic algae to large fish and mammals.
kokborok: Twikwchwng twikhungrok wngkha kaisa kuar daldidal flora tei faunani nok, mukhinukkhol algae simi ah kotor tei abuktwi nwngnai mal jora.

english: The unique environment of freshwater lakes provides a variety of habitats for these organisms, and the interactions between them are complex and fascinating.
kokborok: Ah manthokya habar twikwchwng twikhungrok kaisa oh malmatarokni bagwi dalbidal tongthairok manthomarok khayo, tei ah bohrokni kwcharo jugajugrok bai kuthuk tei muani khlaima hai wngkha.

english: One of the most striking features of freshwater lakes is the presence of a distinct zonation of plant life, which is determined by the depth of the water and the amount of sunlight that reaches the bottom.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai twikwchwng twikhungrokni bumani wngkha ah kaisa pherjak amchoima buphang-uaphang langma wngtongmung wngkha, bomo ah twi ni thukma bai khathonma wngkha tei ah salpohorni thikemung je ah tola sogwimarok.

english: In shallow areas, where there is plenty of light, a dense mat of rooted plants known as a "macrophyte bed" forms.
kokborok: Thena kholarok bising, boro aro pohor kwbangma wngkha, kaisa kwthajak yampra buphang-uaphangrok yarwngjak kaisa "macrophyte thuyam" kayamayarok hwnwi sinima wngo.

english: This provides a habitat for a variety of invertebrates, fish, and amphibians.
kokborok: Omo kaisa dalbidal bekreng kwrwirok bagwi kaisa tongthai manthokmarok wngo.

english: In deeper areas, where there is less light, the water column is dominated by phytoplankton, which are microscopic algae that float freely in the water.
kokborok: Kuthuk kholarokni bising, boro aro kisa pohor wngkha, ah twi thong phytoplankton bai kolopjakma wngkha, bomo mukhinukkhol algea wngkha je ah twini bising phiyokjakhe kuphungma tongo.

english: These organisms are the primary producers in the lake ecosystem, and they are the basis of the food chain.
kokborok: Oh malmatarok wngkha ah remswkang bwthaihrok ah twikhung habarlam bising, tei bohrok ah duisa chahthai gurima tongo.

english: The fauna of freshwater lakes is also diverse, and includes a wide variety of fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
kokborok: Ah malmata twikwchwng twikhungrok solya bo ugkha, tei kaisa kuar dalbidal ah, twibaihapongbairok, makhokmalnairok, tokrok, tei abuktwi nwngnai mal khobmarok wngkha.

english: Fish are the most abundant vertebrates in freshwater lakes, and they play a vital role in the food chain.
kokborok: Ah wngkha jottoni slai gila durukung jorarok twikwchwng twikhungrok bising, tei bohrok kaisa ah chahthai jorarwma bising mal tangmung thwngo.

english: Some of the most common fish species in freshwater lakes include trout, bass, pike, and perch.
kokborok: Baksa ah twikwchwng twikhungrokni bising jottoni slai manthokma ah dahlrok wngkha trout, bass, pike, tei perche khobwi.

english: Fatima Messaoudi: I'm an actor and a furniture designer. I'm also passionate about flowers, especially those that bloom in the winter.
kokborok: Fatima Messaoudi: ang wngkha gain khwlaina kwrwng tei buphangni manwi takna kwrwng. Ang khumrogno twywi belai chajaksogo, abo bo masingo barnai no se.

english: Interviewer: What drew you to acting and furniture design?
kokborok: Amjoknai sa: Nwng gain khwlai mani tei buphang ni manwi tak mani tamono uansogwi khwlai kha?

english: Fatima Messaoudi: I've always loved performing and creating things.
kokborok: Fatima Messaoudi: Ang jesa phuru phano gain khwlai nani tei manwi taknarok no hamjago.

english: Acting allows me to express myself creatively, and furniture design allows me to use my creativity to make something beautiful and functional.
kokborok: Gain khwlaimani abo ani kha bising ni kokrogno sakhwlai rwo, tei buphangni manwi tak mani khe bwkha bisingni rwngmani abono naithok tei samungo chuk rwnai abotwi manwirogno swnam rw o.

english: Interviewer: What are some of the challenges you've faced as an actor and a furniture designer?
kokborok: Amjoknai sa: Bobo twi kenbeng mungrok manjak kha nwng khoroksa gain khwlainai tei buphangni manwi twkna kwrwng wngwi?

kokborok: Fatima Messaoudi: Khoroksa gain khwlaina kwrwng wngwi kebeng mung manjakuk mani khe aro kubun dophani borokno khe aswk mokol kaijak ya.

english: I've often been told that I'm not the right type for a role because of my race or ethnicity.
kokborok: Ang sajak wi mangno tongo bohrok bai nwng gain khwlaiwi gothokya hwnwi tamni hwkhe ang kubun dophani borok bla.

english: As a furniture designer, I've faced the challenge of breaking into a male-dominated industry.
kokborok: Ang khoroksa buphangni manwi takna kwrwng wngwi, kebeng mung phaijak mani khe abo kaisa chwlarokni samung o khopjakma bagwi.

english: Interviewer: How have you overcome these challenges?
kokborok: Amjoknai sa : Nwng bahai khe o kebeng mungrogno kate wi man kha?

kokborok: Fatima Messaoudi: Ang a samung no bwkha rosogwi samung khwlaima bagwi tei a samung no yakarya khe tongma bagwi ang omo hai kebeng mungni yakni katewi man kha.

english: I've always wondered what they're made of and how far away they are.
kokborok: Ang homnino uanajak bohrok tamo bai swnamjak tei bwswk hakchalo bohrok wngkha.

english: Mother: Well, the stars are actually huge balls of gas that are very far away from us.
kokborok: Buma: kahamno, ah athukirirok wngkha kaisa kotor gas ni budulrok je chini oroni simi belai hakchalo wngkha.

english: The closest star to us is the Sun, and it's about 93 million miles away.
kokborok: Ah athukiri chwngbai ganarwk wngkha Sal, tei omo 93 chisrai muk hakchalo.

english: The other stars are much farther away, and some of them are so far away that it takes light years for their light to reach us.
kokborok: Ah kubun athukirirok wngkha belai bwskang hakchalo, tei baksa wngkha aswkhe hakchal je omo pohor bisirok nango bohrokni pohor chini bwkhak sokphainani.

english: Son: Wow, that's amazing! I can't even imagine how far away that is.
kokborok: Bwsla: paah, abo mlangchamani! ang wansuk phano manya je amo bwswk hakchalo wngkha.

english: Mother: It is amazing. And the stars are so important to us.
kokborok: Buma: omo wngkha mlangchamani. Tei ah athukirirok wngkha chini bagwi nangkukma.

english: They provide us with light and heat, and they help us to grow crops.
kokborok: Bohrok chwngno pohor tei kutung manthok rio, Tei borok chwngno muithaih-bwwthaihrok tor rithani chubao.

english: Without the stars, we wouldn't be able to live on Earth.
kokborok: Ah athukirirok kwrwi hwnkhe, chwng hating sakao tongwi mangwlak khamu.

english: Son: So the stars are really important to us.
kokborok: Bwsla: aswkno ah athukirirok chini bagwi kubuino nangkukma.

english: Mother: They are. And they're also beautiful.
kokborok: Buma: In' bohrok. tei boro wngkha belai naithokma.

english: Once upon a time, there were two pilots who were very good friends.
kokborok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro khoroknwi birkhung chaluknai tongo borok belaino kaham kichingkumar.

english: They loved to fly together and share funny stories.
kokborok: Bohrok thansa khe birilayo tei mwimwikothok kothomarok salayo.

english: One day, they were flying over the ocean when they saw a large fish jump out of the water.
kokborok: Salsa, bohrok jephuru twiyung saka twi biriwi tongphuru bohrok ah kotorma twi sakatwi barjak nukha.

english: The pilot on the left said, "Did you see that big fish?"
kokborok: Debra digi ni birkhung chaluknai sakha, "nwng ah kotor da nukha?"

english: The pilot on the right said, "Yes, I did! It was huge!"
kokborok: Yagra digi ni birkhung chaluknai sakha, "In', ang nukha! abo belai kotorma!"

english: They laughed and continued on their flight.
kokborok: Bohrok mwmwilai tei choyai bohrokni birima chaluk thangkha.

english: As they were flying, they passed by a large airport.
kokborok: Bohrok birilai tongphuru, bohrok kotorma birkhungkhola twi laithangkha.

english: The pilot on the left said, "I wonder how many people are at that airport right now."
kokborok: Debra digi ni birkhung chaluknai sakha, "ang wanao je borok bwswk bangno birkhungkhola tak."

english: The pilot on the right said, "I don't know, but it must be a lot."
kokborok: Yagra digi ni birkhung chaluknai sakha, "angbo saimanya, phiya kwbangno wnganw."

english: They laughed again and continued on their flight.
kokborok: Bohrok teiwaisa mwmwikha tei choyai bohrokni biriwi chaluk thangkha.

english: Law and government are two closely related concepts that are often used interchangeably.
kokborok: Kerong tei haphang wngkha kainwi ganarwi halok hokjak wansukmungrok je uramuram kubunthayo phwnangjak tongo.

english: However, there is a key difference between the two: law is a set of rules that govern society, while government is the body that enforces those rules.
kokborok: Haiphano, aro wngkha kaisa berepkong pherlaimung ah kainwi kwcharo: kerong wngkha kaisa raidarok kaihma je dopha sashon khainai wngkha, jephuru hapang wngkha sakmang je ah raidarokno phanbai khlaimarok.

english: Laws are created by governments in order to maintain order and protect the rights of citizens.
kokborok: Kerongrok haphang bai swnamjak tongo dagimung tonima bising tei habohrokrok mwthangma bwkhak tonima.

english: They can be either written or unwritten, and they can be enforced through a variety of means, such as fines, imprisonment, or even death.
kokborok: Bohrok jebakaisa swijak eba swijakya wngmano, tei bohrok kaisa dalbidal kokma rok thwih phanbai khlaima wngmano, ahainno, jurimana, alongchopjakma, eba haino thwimung.

english: Governments are responsible for interpreting and enforcing the law.
kokborok: Haphangrok kokswbai sama tei ah kerong phanbai khlaimani bagwi bojak wngkha.

english: They also create policies that are designed to promote the general welfare of society.
kokborok: Bohrok bo chaplamrok swnam mano je remtisama ah jottoni hoda hamkrai bwkha rikjak wngkha.

english: Governments can be either democratic or authoritarian, and they can range in size from small villages to large countries.
kokborok: Haphangrok lukuchongraidarwk eba bubagra jebakaisa wngwi mano, tei bohrok torma bising bwtrang mano chikonsa kamirokma simi kotor hakotorok jora.

english: The relationship between law and government is a complex one.
kokborok: Ah runghalok kerong tei haphang kwchar kaisa kutuk wngkha.

english: Laws can influence the way that governments operate, and governments can influence the way that laws are created and enforced.
kokborok: Kerongrok ah lama kolopmung khlaimano je haphangrok chalukma bai, tei haphangrok ah lama kolopmung khlaimano je kerongrogrok swnamjak tei phanbai khlaijak mano.

english: This relationship is constantly evolving, and it is an important part of understanding how society functions.
kokborok: Oh runghalok loriya tormani wngkha, tei omo wngkha kaisa nangkukma buchimani bokcho haikhe dopha samung khai.

english: Charles Darwin was a British naturalist who is best known for his contributions to the science of evolution.
kokborok: Charles Darwin wngkha khoroksa British habarrwk je ah soisimung philjakmung bwkhak bini khangmarokni bagwi kaham sinikukjak wngkha.

english: In his book On the Origin of Species, he proposed the theory of natural selection, which states that organisms that are better adapted to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce.
kokborok: Bini bijap bising ah aichaiphang Dalhrok, bo koktisakha ah kokwkwrai habar saimani twih, bobo swisamarok je malmatarok bohrokni habar bwkhak kaham naharmung tongo bohrok ahaino teibo thangna tei achirwma bwkhak tongo.

english: This theory revolutionized the way we think about life and has had a profound impact on the history of science.
kokborok: Oh kokbwkrai pekhrupmungkha ah lama chwng langmani bagwi wansukma tei ah soisimung laihbuma sakao kaisa kuthukuk sekhrupma tongwi tongkha.

english: One of the most interesting aspects of Darwin's work is that he was inspired by his observations of marine life.
kokborok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai khasrangmani Darwin ni samung mangrok wngkha je bini ah twibom langma naikolmungrok bai bo khasrangjak wngkha.

english: While traveling on the HMS Beagle, he spent a great deal of time studying the animals and plants that he encountered on his journey.
kokborok: Jephuru ah HMS Beagle o berai tongphuru, bo kaisa kotor lenden ah malmatarok tei buphang-uaphangrok porimani jora bai lairwkha.

english: He made detailed observations of the different species that he saw, and he began to notice that there were patterns in the way that they were distributed.
kokborok: Bo ah juda juda dahlrok je bo nukmani naikolmungrok pholokjakrok swnamkha, tei bo naisikma bwkhak chengkha je aro ah lamarok bising naidalrok wngkha je borok bakjak wngkha.

english: He also noticed that some species were better adapted to their environment than others.
kokborok: Bo naisikha je baksa dahlrok kubunrokni slai bohrokni bwkhak kahamkhe naharkha.

english: These observations led Darwin to develop his theory of natural selection.
kokborok: Oh naikolmungrok Darwin dagikha bini habar saimani kokbwkrai hamkrai bwkhak.

english: He argued that the organisms that are best adapted to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce.
kokborok: Bo tokra rwkha je ah malamatrok bohrokni habar bwkhak kahamkuk yapharjak wngkha borok tei bo ahaino thangna tei achairwma bwkhak.

english: This means that over time, the populations of organisms will change as the environment changes.
kokborok: Oh kokmarok je jora rwgwi, iko ah habar swlaimarok wngkheno ah malmatarokni bahngmarok swlaijaknai.

english: Earthquakes are a natural phenomenon that can cause widespread damage and loss of life.
kokborok: Bangla phaima wngkha habarni patimung jebo belaikhe baikhrupma tei langma chomani pher wngwimanw.

english: They are caused by the sudden release of energy in the Earth's crust, and can range in size from minor tremors to major catastrophes.
kokborok: Oborok hatingni bukur kwrakni bisingni simi atomsa phan yakarjakma bagwi wngo tei obo ha kisakhe kwlwimani simi kotorkhe kwlwima joratwi wngwimanw.

english: The largest earthquakes can cause entire cities to be leveled, and can even trigger tsunamis and other secondary hazards.
kokborok: Jottonislai kotor bangla phaimabai jotto aulirok hamil wngwimanw tei abobai Tsunami tei kubun kotor deramung wngwimanw.

english: Earthquakes are a major threat to human life and infrastructure, and can have a devastating impact on economies and societies.
kokborok: Bangla phaima borokrokni langma tei bekherepni bagwi kaisa kotor uanamung, tei ranghalok tei hodao kirimung rwuimanw.

english: There are a number of factors that can contribute to the severity of an earthquake, including the depth of the earthquake, the proximity to population centers, and the type of soil or rock that the earthquake occurs in.
kokborok: Obohai kwbangma pher tongo jebo banglani phan-o logirwo, oro banglani thukmung, borok bangmari gwnang thaibai ganamung tei je thayo bangla phayo aroni ha eba holongni dal tongwimanw.

english: Earthquakes can also be triggered by human activity, such as the construction of dams or the injection of fluids into the ground.
kokborok: Borokrokni samung humung, romdi ha theui twi mwthakma eba ha bising kwlwi manwi damabaibo bangla phaiuimanw.

english: The scientific study of earthquakes is known as seismology.
kokborok: Bangla phaimano twywi soisimatwi swrwngmung seismology mungwi sinijagw.

english: Seismologists use a variety of tools to study earthquakes, including seismographs, which measure the ground shaking caused by an earthquake.
kokborok: Bangla soisikwrwngrok bangla phaimano twywi swrwngna bagwi dalbidal manui khunui samungo phwnago, oboni bisingo tongo seismograph, jebo bangla phaimabai ha kwlwima marino suo.

english: Seismologists also use computer models to help them understand the causes and effects of earthquakes.
kokborok: Bangla soisikwrwngrok bangla phaimani pher tei wngmungno saimanthani borokno chubana bagwi computer model samungo phwnango.

english: The early warning systems that are used to alert people to impending earthquakes are based on the information that seismologists collect from seismographs.
kokborok: Bangla phaithotokno twywi borokrokno hojak khwlaina bagwi swkang-swkang hojak khwlainani je yapri romjago abo wngkha bangla soisikwrwngrok seismographani simi thumjak kokthumno rwgwi swnamjago.

english: A good mattress is essential for getting a good night's sleep.
kokborok: Horo mwktrwi kaham man na khe thuyam o bomani mattress kaham wngna nang nai.

english: A comfortable mattress can help to relieve pain, improve sleep quality, and boost your mood.
kokborok: Thuyam o bomani mattress kaham hwnkhe se nini bwsak ruwaimarok no swra rwo, mwktrwi kaham bo man rwo, tei nini tongma chamarogno kaham wng thanio bo chuba rwo.

english: The first mattresses were developed in ancient Egypt, where they were made from straw, reeds, and other natural materials.
kokborok: Thuyam o bomani mattress no pwila sirisiti ni simi Egypt ha o tong bo nai borokrogse swnam na chengsa grao, aphuru a bohrok chwkab ni, bata ni, tei kubun manthok mani jabrarok ni se swnam jagrao.

english: In the Middle Ages, mattresses were made from wool, feathers, and other animal products.
kokborok: Kwchar ni bisirogo khe, mattressrok mera bikhumu ni swnam jago, bwkrang ni, tei kubun malmatarokni bisingtwi manthok mani manwirok bai swnam jago.

english: In the 19th century, mattresses began to be made from springs and other metal components.
kokborok: Bisi 19th centuryrogo khe, mattressrok springs ni swnamjak na chengsa kha tei kubun manthok mani sorni manwirok bao bo swnam jak kha.

english: The type of mattress that is best for you depends on your individual needs and preferences.
kokborok: Bobo hai mattress no nwng chajak tei nangjak abo nini thani o se.

english: Some people prefer a firm mattress, while others prefer a soft mattress.
kokborok: Baksa borok khe ba kwrak mattress no chajago, tei kubunrok khe ba sophong wngnai jat abotwi mattressrok no chajago.

english: It is important to find a mattress that provides you with the support you need and that is comfortable for you to sleep on.
kokborok: Nwng chajak mani mattress no nwng nanse nango, hakhese nwng aro thu wi khakchangma manai.

english: A good mattress can help to protect you from serious health problems, such as back pain, neck pain, and headaches.
kokborok: Mattress kaham baibo nini sakni bemar belai hamya wngmarogno kasowi mano, sing samarog, godwna samarog, tei khorok samarogno kasowi mano.

english: It can also help you to get a better night's sleep, which can improve your mood, your energy levels, and your overall health.
kokborok: Horo nwng thu phuru kaham mwktrwi manrw o, abo nini tongma chamano bo kaham phaisingo twlango, nini phan no bo bang rwo, tei bebak nini sak hamkhwrai o samung chuk rwo.

english: Water is a vital resource for life on Earth.
kokborok: O ha saka o kwthang tongna bagwi mamwlai nangkuk mani khe twi se.

english: It is used for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and many other purposes.
kokborok: Abo nubo nungjago, subo sungjago, kwchwng khwlai thani bo, tei kwbangma tongo.

english: The chief use of water is for irrigation, which accounts for over 70% of global water consumption.
kokborok: Mamwlai twi no nangkukmani wngkha panthoro al-chuaina bagwi twi chom mani, abobai hagwnangwi 70% twi habo.

english: Other major uses of water include industrial production, domestic use, and power generation.
kokborok: Tei kaisa kotor khe twino samungo phwnang jakmani khe industry production ni bagwi, chini salbrum ni samung ni bagwi, tei chwngpherang khwlaina bagwi.

english: The cost of water varies depending on the source and location.
kokborok: Twi ni morokmung pherwi thango aboni manthokmani tei thaino rwgwi.

english: In some areas, water is relatively cheap and plentiful, while in other areas, it is scarce and expensive.
kokborok: Kaisa-kuisu amchairogo khe, twi belai kwlai tei kwbang, phiya kubun amchairogo khe, manthokya tei morok.

english: The cost of water can also be affected by factors such as pollution, drought, and climate change.
kokborok: Twi ni morokmung pherwi mano jephuru twi-sitra, watwi kwlaiya, tei mol swlaijakma bisingtwi.

english: The many uses of water make it a valuable resource.
kokborok: Twi no jesphru phano samung nangmani bagwi se twi wngkhe nangkukma manwi hwnjago.

english: However, water scarcity is a growing problem in many parts of the world.
kokborok: Phiya, twi manthokya ni jwngjal kwbangma hayungni thayo no wngwi tongo.

english: It is important to use water wisely and to conserve water whenever possible.
kokborok: Twi no belai hus khe samungo phwnangna nangnai tei mankhe twino khatina bo ma sakthar di.

english: John was a young man who had always been fascinated by the way things worked, and he was always eager to explore new areas.
kokborok: John wngkha khoroksa chwla sikla je homnino maunai khlaijakma hai wngjak ah lama samungrok samung khaima baii, tei bo homnino muchungwi kwtal khorarok bwkhak naitukberima wngkha.

english: One day, John was hiking in the woods when he came across a strange sight.
kokborok: Salsa, John ah bolong bisingtwih yakung bai himwi thangkha ahjora bo kaisa siniya nuijaknai phai malaikha.

english: There was a large hole in the ground, and it seemed to be leading to a vast underground cavern.
kokborok: Aro ah ha bisingo kaisa hakor kotorma tongo, tei omo kaisa kotorma habsingo goirang bwkhak dagimani bwkhak khakama khayo.

english: John was curious about what was inside, so he decided to climb down into the hole.
kokborok: John bisingo tamo tong bagwi simuchungjak wngkha, tei bo chongkha ah hakor bising tola onghkorna hwnwi.

english: As John descended, he was amazed by what he saw.
kokborok: John tola ongkhorkheno, bo mwlangchakha bo tamo nukma bai.

english: The cavern was filled with strange and wonderful creatures, and it was clear that this was a place unlike any other.
kokborok: Ah goirang siniya tei unamansingsa malmatarokbai bai kuplung wngkha, tei amo wngkha kwchwng je oh wngkha kaisa thai jesa kubun haiya.

english: John spent the next few days exploring the cavern, and he learned a great deal about the processes that were at work there.
kokborok: John tei kisa salrok ah goirang naitukberaimani bai katikahm tei bo swrwngkha kaisa kotor kuar lenden ah tanseprok bagwi je aro samungo tongjak.

english: He also learned a lot about himself, and he realized that he was more capable than he had ever thought possible.
kokborok: Bo binisaksakni bagwi bo kwbang swrwngkha, tei bo saimankha je bo aboni slai teibo chukjak bo jottojora wngman wansukmung wngkha.

english: When John finally returned to the surface, he was a changed person.
kokborok: Jephuru Johna paithago saka phirokha, bo khoroksa borok slaijak wngkha.

english: He was no longer content to simply observe the world around him.
kokborok: Bo tabuk khakwchang kwrwikha bini yaksa yaksiyagra hayung khakeplengma naikolma bwkhak.

english: An earthquake is a sudden and violent shaking of the Earth's crust that can cause great damage.
kokborok: Kaisa hakwlwima wngkha atomsa tei phankhai jangrimani ah hating habukurno je kotor piykamung pher mano.

english: The most common cause of earthquakes is the movement of tectonic plates, which are large pieces of the Earth's crust that ride on top of the molten rock beneath the surface.
kokborok: Ah jottoni slai chwrokni hakwlwimarok pher wngkha ah tectonic sisileprokni ninangrimung, bomo wngkha kotor bokchorok ah hating habukur je buchuk saka kama ah gelejak sothaih ah sakani tolao.

english: When these plates move past or collide with each other, they can cause the Earth's crust to break and produce seismic waves.
kokborok: Jephuru oh sisleprok wngthang sehma eba khoroksa tei khoroksa bai thutaima wngo, bohrokh ah hatingni habukru swbaima bwkhak pher mano tei seismic twidurok thaihrwo.

english: These waves travel through the Earth and can cause the ground to shake.
kokborok: Oh twidurok ah hating twih berayo tei ah ha jangrima bwkhak pher mano.

english: The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale, which ranges from 0 to 9.
kokborok: Ah hakwlwima kotorma ah Ricter scale sakao sujakha, bomo 0 simi 9 remrok wngo.

english: The higher the magnitude, the more powerful the earthquake.
kokborok: Ah kotorma jeswk kuchukma, ah hakwlwima teibo phangwnang.

english: Earthquakes can cause damage in a variety of ways, including ground shaking, landslides, tsunamis, building collapses, fires, and loss of life.
kokborok: Hakwlwimarok kaisa dalbidal lamarok bising piyakmung pher mano, ha jangrimani khobmani, hakuakmanirok, tsunamis, nokktor kuakmarok, horrok, tei langma kwmamma.

english: Earthquakes can also trigger other hazards, such as avalanches.
kokborok: Hakwlwimarok kubun atomsa wngmung bo khili mano, ahaino avalanches.

english: The damage caused by an earthquake depends on a number of factors, including the magnitude of the earthquake, the distance from the epicenter, the type of soil, and the construction of buildings.
kokborok: Ah piyakmung kaisa hakwlwi bai pherjakma kwbangma kusungchwlwirok sakao sakbogo, ah hakwlwi babai kotorma khobmani bai, ah chalmung ah epicenterni simi, ah hachingni sapokthaih, tei ah nokkotorok tangmani.

english: This is because we are all created in God's image, and God is the essence of rationality and order.
kokborok: Omo wngkha tamhinba chwng jotto mwtaini mangpili bising swnamjakma wngkha, tei mwtai wngkha ah uansukkwrwima biphring tei dagimung.

english: When we live in accordance with our true nature, we are able to experience peace and harmony.
kokborok: Jephuru chwng chini kubui habar bai omotwi bising tongma, chwng kwchwngtotok tei kwthamung simari bwkhak chugo.

english: However, when we allow our thoughts and actions to become chaotic and inconsistent, we experience inner conflict and turmoil.
kokborok: Haiphano, jephuru chwng chini wansukmarok tei samungrok gosima bwkhak ubrumjabrum tei kwthajakya, chwng bisingni nanglaimung tei oroiporoi simari wngo.

english: There are many ways to achieve internal consistency.
kokborok: Bohrok kwbangma himlarok tong bisingni kwthajakma manma bwkhak.

english: One way is to live according to our values.
kokborok: Kaisa lama wngkha chini mulajarok bwkhak omotwi tongma.

english: When we know what is important to us and we make choices that are consistent with those values, we feel a sense of purpose and direction.
kokborok: Jephuru chwng saimano chini bagwi tamo nangkukma tei chwng chini saimungrok swnamo je ah mulajarok bai kwthajak wngkha, chwng kaisa sina simanwi naimung tei phunukma.

english: Another way to achieve internal consistency is to be honest with ourselves about our strengths and weaknesses.
kokborok: Bisingni kwthajakma manma bwkhak tei kaisa lama wngkha chinisaksak bai kubui tongnani chini phanrokno tei belmungrokno twywi.

english: When we are aware of our true selves, we can make choices that are in alignment with our authentic nature.

english: The river was also a popular spot for humans to swim, fish, and relax.
kokborok: Ah twima bo kaisa luku hamjajak thai twi yokma, ah, tei lengrwma bwkhak borokrokni bagwi.

english: One day, a young girl named Lily was playing near the river when she saw a turtle caught in a fishing net.
kokborok: Salsa, khoroksa bwrwi sikli Lily mungwi ah twima gana thwngwi tongo jephuru bo kaisa kasing nukha kaisa ah rommani jaal bising romjak.

english: Lily knew that she had to help the turtle, so she ran home to get her father.
kokborok: Lily saimankha je bo ah kasingno chubana nangnai, haini bagwi bo nogo kharwi thangkha bini bupha no naharna bwkhak.

english: Lily's father helped her to free the turtle, and the two of them returned to the river.
kokborok: Lilyni bupha bono chubakha ah kasingno phiyokna bwkhak, tei bohrok khoroknwi ah twima bwkhak phirokkha.

english: The turtle thanked Lily for saving her life, and Lily promised to always be kind to animals.
kokborok: Ah kasing Lilyno hambai rwkha bini langma mwthangmani bagwi, tei Lily swmai tangkha bo homnino malmatarokno kaham wngnai hwnwi.

english: Lily continued to visit the river often, and she always made sure to look out for any animals that might be in danger.
kokborok: Lily choyawui ah twima bwkhak uramuram thango, tei bo homnino wngkubui swnamo phatar naima bwkhak jesa malmata karwi je akocho wngwi mano.

english: One day, Lily saw a group of boys throwing rocks at the fish in the river.
kokborok: Salsa, Lily kaisa chwlarokni buthupno ah twima bisingni ah no holongrok khitarmani nukha.

english: Lily knew that she had to stop them, so she ran up to the boys and told them that what they were doing was wrong.
kokborok: Lily saimano je bo bohrokni mwthakna nango, haini bagwi bo ah chwlarokni bwkhak kharkah tei bohrokno sakha je bohrok tamo khlai tongmani abo chaya hwnwi.

english: The boys were surprised to hear this from Lily, but they listened to her and stopped throwing rocks.
kokborok: Ah chwlarok uananjak Lily simi omo khwnama bwkhak tongjak, phiya bohrok bono khwnakha tei holongrok khitarmni mwthakkha.

kokborok: Oh sebuk wng chasukjak genealogists ni bagwi je kaisa sirwkjak thumani tongmarirok naitongnaini bagwi.
